Against the GPU control and §1's thresholds:

- **Generation is no longer the limit.** With its queue full the planet generates 67 to 126 chunks a second on the GPU
  (the 80° runs lowest, as the control on the same circle: 59 to 82), against 29 on the CPU (Phase 1's rate, reproduced in
  this batch) and the control's 70 to 107 on its straight route. The CPU planet in this
  batch catches up as in §15.2 (1.72 s and 20.43 s against 1.77 and 20.09), so the batch's machine state matches Phase
  1's.
- **Catch-up: met on the equator and at 45° at both speeds** (0.17 s and 0.17 s at v1500 against the control's 0.17; 0.18
  s and 0.41 s at v3000 against 0.48). Phase 1 missed it on every route.
- **Catch-up on the 80° circle: 0.70 s at v1500 and 0.87 s at v3000**, against the straight control's 0.17 and 0.48, and
  the control on the same circle's 0.37 to 0.41 and 1.15. The repeat gives the same 0.69. The cause is where the route
  ends: the viewer enters a new chunk 11 uu before the stop (y crosses −9,600 between the last two samples, the route
  ending at y −9,611), which runs the load decisions at the stop and queues the new row of columns in the shell window:
  78 chunks appear in one frame (tracked 1,087 to 1,165) and take 0.55 s to generate at the GPU's rate. The control's
  circle is offset by its `WorldOrigin` and ends mid-chunk. Both speeds stop at the same point, so both carry it; on
  the circle at v3000 the planet still catches up faster than the control. Not a planet cost.
- **Frame and manager P95: within the thresholds on every route.** Frame P95 is 4 to 22% below the straight control's,
  but for 80° at v3000 (+4%, against the circle control's 34.0 ms −6%); manager P95 is 6 to 18% below, but for 80° at
  v3000 (+6%, against the circle control's 10.0 ms −12%).
- **Peak loaded chunks within +6%** (1,165 to 1,265 against 1,163 and 1,212), **peak voxel MB and systems MB within +25%**
  (the most, 45° at v3000: 848 and 1,097 MB against 699 and 891, +21% and +23%). The planet's peak voxel memory rose
  from §15.2's 292 to 330 MB to 754 to 848 MB: the GPU keeps up, so more chunks are resident uncompressed at once, as for
  the control (699 to 808).
- **D3: met.** Systems memory peaks at 988 to 1,097 MB while streaming (at most 1.5 GB) and is 382 MB settled (at most
  0.6 GB; Phase 1: 383). The residency audit finds 0 on every run.

**Things to know.**

- The GPU's parity is not bit-exact on a planet as it nearly is near the origin: positions 250,000 uu out cost the cave
  noise about 0.03 uu, and density at a cave's edge rounds the other way in a few hundred voxels a land chunk (above).
  The mesh differs by about 10 triangles in 450,000; terrain, coasts and caves look the same.
- `FVoxelDownLines` is the one definition of the lines along local down; the CPU and GPU passes cannot drift apart.
- The parity harness logs counts and a CRC32 of the GPU data per case: a shader change that must not move heightmap
  voxels can be checked against the previous build's log.
- Saves are unaffected (`PlanetGenerationVersion` stays 2): the GPU generates the CPU's planet.

**Left for later.**

- **G18** (§14.1): the heightmap branch still ignores the cave configuration's biome overrides and `UnderwaterMinDepth`,
  which the demo uses, so GPU heightmap worlds carve caves under the sea and in the Ocean biome that CPU worlds do not.
  The planet branch's `GpuPlanetCaveCarve` shows the port; it moves GPU heightmap terrain, so it needs a decision on
  `GenerationVersion` (it would refuse every heightmap save). *Fixed in §16.3 (2026-10-17), `GenerationVersion` 2.*
- The ore `Rarity` hash at absolute positions (SP-H3, Phase 4) and large planets (SP-H1, P2).
- Walking (Phase 3), systems (Phase 4) and places (Phase 5) as before; nothing here changed them.

### 16.3 G18: the heightmap GPU caves take the biome overrides and the underwater minimum depth (2026-10-17)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#100, `fix/g18-heightmap-gpu-caves`, base `c13ae7d`, main after spherical Phase 2; the
parent's gitlink and doc map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#111). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor with background throttling off.

**Decision.** D10 (§8): `FVoxelWorldModeFactory::GenerationVersion` goes to 2, so every save made before is refused.

**What changed.**

- `GenerateVoxelDensity.usf`: the planet's `GpuPlanetCaveCarve` became `GpuCaveCarve`, shared by every world mode,
  with its overrides lookup (`GpuCaveBiomeOverride`) and `ApplyCaveCarve` beside it. Each layer samples its noise at
  `GpuCaveSamplePos`: `VerticalScale` along Z in the heightmap modes, along local up on a planet (`PlanetScaleAltitude`,
  moved over unchanged). The heightmap branch now runs in the CPU's order: the biome blend (`SampleGpuBiomeBlend`, the
  dominant biome and its ore range), then the caves with that biome and `bUnderwater` (water on and the column's terrain
  height under `WaterLevel`), then the blended material with the underwater variant, height rules, the cave-wall
  override on the scaled, clamped carve, ores. Before, it carved first with every layer at scale 1 and the layer's own
  minimum depth.
- Gone with it: `CalculateDepthFade` (`CaveGeneration.ush`) and `ComputeBiomeMaterial` (`BiomeMaterial.ush`), whose
  only caller was the old heightmap block.
- The planet branch calls the same function with the same arguments, so its output did not move (below).
- `GenerationVersion` 2; comments in `VoxelGPUNoiseGenerator.cpp` no longer call the parameters planet-only.

**Tests.** `VoxelWorlds.Generation.GPUvsCPUCavesParity` keeps its core case (no overrides, water off, chunk (3, 1, 0))
and adds four, each at LOD 0/1/2 with the default thresholds. Without continentalness every column samples
continentalness 0, where Ocean wins the blend by priority, so the chunk is Ocean; the test
reads the chunk's biome and gives it the override under test, every other default biome a different one, and a second
entry for the chunk's biome after them (the first match must win), so a wrong lookup would carve differently.

| Case | Overrides on the chunk's biome | CPU, non-vacuous probe | Old shader (density within 2 / metadata) | New shader: voxels differing (by > 2), material, metadata |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| Caves (core) | none | 439 cave-air voxels | 99.9% / 100% (CRC 295b2d48) | 24 (6), 0, 0; CRC 295b2d48 as before |
| Caves biome overrides | scale 1.25, minimum depth 8 | 261 cave-air voxels (439 without) | 87.3% / 95.3%: **fails** | 17 (3), 0, 0 |
| Caves biome scale 0 | scale 0 (the demo's Ocean) | 0 cave-air voxels | 82.7% / 86.6%: **fails** | 5 (2), 0, 0 |
| Caves biome scale 0.5 | scale 0.5 | 740 voxels softened, none carved to air | 83.3% / 86.6%: **fails** | 21 (2), 0, 0 |
| Caves under the sea | scale 1.25, minimum depth 8; water level 800, `UnderwaterMinDepth` 25 | chunk (0, 0, −1): 1,054 cave-air voxels without the underwater minimum depth, 450 with it (the rest lie deeper than 25 voxels) | 65.3% / 85.9%: **fails** | 26 (10), 2, 0 |

The differences left are the float-against-double boundaries every heightmap case has (the core case's 24 voxels).

**Every earlier parity case is bit-identical.** The 63 lines of the other `GPUvsCPU*Parity` cases (the heightmap ones
and the nine planet sites, each LOD) report the same counts and the same CRC32 of the GPU output as before the change,
in a baseline run of the same build with the old shader and in spherical Phase 2's final log: the planet branch and
every heightmap case without overrides or `UnderwaterMinDepth` did not move.

**Suites.** Headless (`-nullrhi`) VoxelWorlds + VoxelWorldSave + VoxelCharacter: 299 of 299 (13 GPU tests skip
there). In the editor (D3D12): 299 of 299, the GPU tests running (only the two retired GPU DC interior tests skip),
and the 75 parity lines the same as in the run above.

**Live look.** `VoxelDemo` with `DemoSmoothWorldConfig` (GPU generation, water at −1,500, `DemoCaveConfig`), fresh
worlds. The pawn spawns on a coast: the seabed falls from the waterline at y −1,000 to 2,100 uu deep at y −10,000, south
of the spawn. Five fixed cameras along x 0: two in the water above the seabed (y −2,000 and −4,500), three just inside
the ground looking down (at the waterline, and 200 to 400 uu under the seabed at y −4,500 and −7,000). Each was shot
three times: the GPU with the old shader (swapped back for the run), the GPU with the new one, and the CPU
(`voxel.GPUGeneration.Enable 0`). Pixel differences (share of pixels off by more than 40 of 255):

| Camera | New GPU against the CPU | Old GPU against the CPU |
|--------|------|------|
| In the water, y −2,000 and −4,500 | 0.0%, 0.0% | 0.0%, 0.0% |
| At the waterline, inside the ground | 0.2% | 0.7% |
| Under the seabed, y −4,500 and −7,000 | 0.0%, 0.0% | 5.6%, 3.7% |

No cave opens in this seabed with either shader: the demo's cave layers start too deep to reach it. What the old shader
got wrong was underneath: the differing pixels are the cave walls nearest the seabed, which the old shader carved where
the CPU keeps the ground solid (within the underwater minimum depth of 25 voxels). The deeper caves under the sea are
the CPU's own and stay. Screenshots:
`Saved/Screenshots/Claudius/g18_{old,new,cpu}_{a..e}.png` in the worktree (not committed).

**Things to know.**

- GPU and CPU heightmap worlds now carve the same caves under the sea and in biomes scaled to 0. The demo's GPU world
  loses the caves it had under the sea within 25 voxels of the seabed and everywhere in the Ocean biome.
- `GenerationVersion` 2 refuses every earlier save, planet saves included (their terrain did not move; the version is
  shared). A refused save stays on disk until the next explicit save overwrites it.
- The CPU's legacy fallback (biomes on without a biome configuration) still picks biomes from `FVoxelBiomeRegistry`, which
  the GPU has no twin for (the GPU uses biome 0 and the legacy materials there, in every world mode). A separate,
  older gap, not G18; not changed here.

## 17. Spherical Phase 3: walkable (2026-10-17)

The requirements doc's Phase 3 ([SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md](SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md) §4): SP-F1 to SP-F5,
SP-C4, SP-B11 and SP-E1 to SP-E3. Phases 1 and 2 give a correct planet, generated on the GPU by default (§15, §16), but
nothing walks on it: gravity is world −Z, the pawn spawns walking on the seabed 1,900 uu under the north-pole sea (the
water depth is measured from the Z-plane `WaterLevel`, so it never swims), and `vox.TP` to latitude 45 holds it 57,600 uu
above the ground at latitude 54.9 until its settle times out, then re-settles it there for ever (the heightmap settle reads
the legacy equatorial radius as a Z). Exit check: walk and swim around the planet (poles, 45°, the equator, a cube corner)
with no fall-through, the per-frame capture (`vox.Debug.Capture`) showing no READY→NOT-READY transition under the feet.
Heightmap worlds must behave exactly as before.

Bases: VoxelWorlds `c444759`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `a04c1aa`, InteractionPlugin `071f005`, UE5_PluginDev `4ccd735`.
Live checks on `PlanetTest` with `/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride` (R 250,000,
water at `WaterRadius` 249,500, shell ±6,500, voxel 75, chunk 64, GPU generation), as in §15 and §16.

**Design (written before building).**

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Gravity | `UVCMovementComponent::PerformMovement` calls `SetGravityDirection(−GetUpVectorAt(location))` before the engine's movement, on a planet only (the world's bounds are a shell). The engine's `UCharacterMovementComponent` does the rest: walking, falling, floors, steps, jumps, input constraint and the rotation upright (`PhysicsRotation`) run in gravity space since 5.4. Simulated proxies take the engine's replicated gravity direction (`ACharacter::ReplicatedGravityDirection`). Heightmap worlds never call it | `PerformMovement` is where every move is simulated: the server's replay of a client move, the client's prediction and its replays, the standalone tick and NPCs. Gravity is a pure function of the position at the start of the move, so prediction and authority agree without new replicated state. The engine skips the update for changes under about 1e-4 (25 uu of travel on this planet) |
| Which Z uses become gravity-relative | Every one in `UVCMovementComponent`: the swim ascend and descend accelerations, the passive buoyancy, the surface damping and cap, the vertical speed clamp, the dive's floor probe; the floor-normal and landing-spot line traces and the grace probe; the shore climb's ledge test, probe sweep (the capsule along local up), "steep" test and feet heights; the terrain context's feet and upper-body samples; the head point for breath; the embed resolve's headroom scan and snap; the sprint's ground speed. Each uses the engine's gravity-space helpers (`GetGravitySpaceZ`, `SetGravitySpaceZ`, `ProjectToGravityFloor`, the gravity transforms) | With gravity −Z these reduce to the old arithmetic exactly (the dot product with (0, 0, 1) is Z, the plane projection zeroes Z), so heightmap worlds compute the same numbers |
| Camera and control rotation | The control rotation stays in world space. On a planet, `AVCPlayerController::UpdateRotation` first turns it by the change in gravity since the last frame (the view stays put relative to the ground as the pawn walks over the curve), converts it to gravity space, lets the camera manager add the input and clamp the pitch, zeroes the roll and converts back. `AVCCharacterBase::FaceRotation` takes the control rotation's gravity-relative yaw (first person) and keeps the body upright. Ground input moves along the gravity-relative yaw; swimming keeps the full control rotation. The camera modes rotate their offsets by that yaw and lift the eye height along local up; so do the camera collision pivot and the interaction trace origin; the anim instance reads speed, direction and aim in gravity space. Without custom gravity each falls back to the old code | Epic's custom-gravity pattern; only frame-independent things are done in gravity space (pitch from the horizontal, roll about the view axis), so the gravity frame's own twist (`FindBetweenNormals` from +Z, which spins near the south pole) never shows. At the north pole the gravity is −Z and the old path runs |
| Spawn and the settle hold | By direction: on a planet `FVCVoxelNavigationHelper::FindSpawnablePosition` takes the direction from the planet centre to the requested position, the terrain surface along it (`GetSurfacePointAt`: noise, continentalness), and accepts it above the sea; under the sea it searches rings of directions around it, one chunk of arc apart in 8 bearings, as the heightmap search walks rings in XY. The terrain wait requests the chunks under a grid in the tangent plane (and the one under the feet along local down), the final trace runs along local up, and the pawn is stood upright before it moves. SP-B11's spawn point is `UVoxelChunkManager::GetPlanetSpawnPosition`: the configured direction's surface plus `PlanetSpawnAltitude` along up (the configuration's version, without the world mode, is the datum's) | `GetSurfacePoint` is the analytic surface generation matches within 0.81 uu (§15.2), so it needs no loaded chunks, as `GetTerrainHeightAt` does for the plane. The chunk grid in X and Y at one Z misses the ground at mid latitudes, where the surface crosses chunk layers diagonally |
| `vox.TP` by latitude and longitude | `vox.TPLatLon lat lon [altitude=0] [settle=1]`: the direction (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) from the planet centre, `altitude` over the datum; settle as `vox.TP` (by direction now). `vox.TP X Y Z` on a planet settles by the direction of (X, Y, Z). `vox.Planet` logs the radius, shell, sea radius, horizon, KillZ and the pawn's latitude, longitude, altitude, ground altitude, sea depth, gravity and how far its up is from the radial. `vox.AutoRun` on a planet follows the great circle through the pawn along the given direction (the axis fixed at the start), so one command walks pole to equator | SP-F4 and the two SP-I5 commands Phase 3 needs to be checked; a fixed world heading on a sphere would converge on the point where it is radial |
| KillZ | On a planet the chunk manager lowers the world's KillZ to below the planet (`Centre.Z − OuterRadius − one chunk`) when it lies above that, and logs it; otherwise it stays. The character's out-of-world rule (WM-I4) is radial on a planet: deeper than `OutOfWorldDepth` inside the shell's inner radius | The engine's KillZ is a Z plane: on planets over about 1,040,000 uu it would cut the southern hemisphere off. Below the planet it never touches the surface, and bodies still on world −Z gravity (physics props, SP-F7 in Phase 4) are still removed once they leave it. Turning bounds checks off would let them fall for ever |
| Where the world-item pool parks | `UWorldItemPoolSubsystem` gets a `ParkingLocation` (default (0, 0, −100,000), as before) and `SetParkingLocation`, which moves the parked items too; `AWorldItem::ResetForPool` parks at the pool's spot. `AVCGameModeBase` sets it to the planet centre once the voxel world is up (a planet only). InteractionPlugin knows nothing of voxels | The centre is 250,000 uu under the surface, inside the core, which never streams; parked items are hidden and have no collision, so nothing reaches them and they are never relevant to a player |
| The collision cook lead | `ForcePathCoverage` takes the focus's local up from the chunk manager: the second sample half a chunk along −up, the look-ahead along the velocity's tangential part, and "descending" (also cover the chunk below each look-ahead point) from the velocity along up | With up (0, 0, 1) these are the old expressions exactly; at the equator the old "below" sample was beside the pawn, and a pawn walking toward a pole had its look-ahead cut by its world-Z component |
| One sea | `FVoxelSeaSurface` gets `GetDepth(Position)`: the signed depth below the surface (plane: `PlaneZ − Z`; sphere: `Radius − |P − C|`). Heightmap water consumers disagree on the plane: generation, scatter, the map and PCG compare with `WaterLevel`; navigation, the character and the NPC spawner with `WaterLevel + WorldOrigin.Z`. They agree whenever `WorldOrigin.Z` is 0 (every configuration in the project: the demo's origin is (12,345, 54,321, 0)). The second convention is kept as a factory, `FromConfigOriginRelative`, so each consumer keeps its plane; on a planet both are the sphere of `WaterRadius` around `WorldOrigin`, generation's own. The chunk manager exposes `GetSeaSurface` and BlueprintPure `GetSeaDepthAt` | Every consumer then asks one type the same question, and on a planet gets the radius generation floods with. Unifying the two plane conventions would move water in any world with `WorldOrigin.Z` ≠ 0, which is not this phase's business; the difference is recorded as G19 |
| Swimming, breath, the spawn search | The character's water depth is `GetDepth` at the position, clamped at 0, wherever a water-flagged voxel was found (as before); swimming starts and ends by that depth; the head is under when its depth is above 0; the spawn search's "above water" is `GetDepth(surface) < 0` | Radial depth on a planet; on the plane the same subtraction as before |
| The ocean shell | `FVoxelPlanetOcean` (VoxelStreaming, pure geometry, like `FVoxelFarOcean`): a cube sphere of `WaterRadius` around the centre with the tangent warp (the surface coordinate's mapping), its resolution chosen so a quad's middle sags at most 4 uu under the sphere (between 32 and 160 quads along a face edge), UVs in voxels along each face (as the water tiles' world XY over the voxel size), the water material id in UV1 as the tiles have it, normals radial. Two sections: the top (faces outward) always, the underside (inward) only while the viewer is inside the sea radius. The chunk manager builds it at world start on a planet with water on and a `WaterMeshMaterial`, positions relative to the centre; `voxel.World.PlanetOcean 0` hides it. `AVoxelWorldTestActor`'s sphere goes | The configured water material (`M_Water`) is one-sided and translucent, so from outside the far hemisphere is culled and no ray crosses the near one twice: the light and dark halves of §15.2 came from the test actor's two-sided `MI_Ocean`. From inside a sphere every ray meets it once, so the underside alone is right there; the island's far ocean shows its undersides the same way. A static mesh needs no rebuild as the viewer moves. The ocean then belongs to the world, not to one test actor |
| Underwater camera and post-process | `UVCUnderwaterPostProcess` keeps its test (the camera in a water-flagged voxel); the immersion that darkens it is the radial depth through the terrain context | The flags are generation's radial fill (SP-B8); only the depth was Z-based |
| Things that stay Z-up this phase | NPC AI movement and auto-jump (SP-F6), world-item drop traces and the placeable slope (SP-F7), the edit brush axis (SP-F8), scatter's surface extraction, PCG, the map and navigation grids (SP-G*), the item drop and chop aim points, the sky and clock (Phase 4) | Phase 4's list; NPCs do get planet gravity, since they use `UVCMovementComponent` |
| Heightmap worlds unchanged | Planet-only code runs only when the world's bounds are a shell (gravity, KillZ, the pool, the ocean, the spawn search, the debug commands' planet branches); everywhere else the gravity-relative expressions reduce to the old ones exactly with gravity −Z and up (0, 0, 1), and each sea consumer keeps its plane. Checked by the existing suites (the character tests, the far ocean, the streaming and water tests), heightmap cases in the new tests that compare against the old formulas bit for bit, and a live regression pass on `VoxelDemo` with the capture on | — |

**The debug tooling, two fixes (G20, §14.1).** The first exit-check run found two artefacts of the tools, not of walking.
`vox.TP`'s settle re-requested the target chunk's collision every half second, also once it was cooked, and a request
for a cooked chunk re-cooks it: a READY→NOT-READY "re-cook" under a pawn already standing there. And the capture compared
the frame after a teleport with the frame before, so every teleport onto ground not streamed yet logged a "fall-through
signature" for a pawn the settle was holding (mode 0, no velocity): five in the trial run, each one frame after a
teleport, at its exact target. The settle now requests only chunks without collision, and the capture restarts its state
after a jump of more than a chunk in one frame and while the settle holds, so it compares only frames where the pawn
moved under its own power. Both are game-module changes, so heightmap play is untouched; `vox.TP` on a plane benefits
the same way.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter` on the final build: **310/310 in the
editor** (274 VoxelWorlds, 2 VoxelWorldSave, 34 VoxelCharacter; the GPU tests ran, among them every
`Generation.GPUvsCPU*Parity`, `Generation.GPUNoiseGeneratorAsync` and `Meshing.MarchingCubes.CPUvsGPU`; only the retired
GPU DC interior test skips, as before) and **310/310 headless** (`-nullrhi`: the GPU tests skip themselves, 13 skip
messages). The 11 new tests pass in both.

**The exit check.** **Met.** One PIE session on the final build, `vox.Debug.Capture 1` at 0.25 s for all of it (6,466 capture
lines): 0 fall-through signatures (READY→NOT-READY under the feet), 0 re-cooks under the feet, 0 out-of-world
recoveries, 0 settle timeouts.

| Site | Start (`vox.TPLatLon`) | Landed | Walk | Swim, dive, climb out | Upright |
|------|------------------------|--------|------|-----------------------|---------|
| Spawn | PlayerStart over the north pole (sea) | ring 3, lat 86.696°, 99 uu over the ground | — | — | 0.004° |
| North | 90°, 0° | ring 3 (14,400 uu of arc), lat 86.70° | east 10 km into the sea | swim north, dive to −606, up, ashore in 9 s | ≤ 0.007° |
| 45° | 45°, 45° | ring 0 | east, north (a ridge, 966 over the datum) | dive to −988 (166 uu/s down), up at 199 uu/s, swim 2.4 km, ashore in 33 s | ≤ 0.007° |
| Cube corner | 35.26°, 45° | ring 2, lat 36.80° | east into the sea | swim, dive to −1,020, up, ashore in 15 s | ≤ 0.009° |
| Equator | 0°, 45° | ring 0 | east 9 km, north 10 km | dive to −847, up, ashore in 19 s | ≤ 0.010° |
| South | −90°, 0° | ring 1, lat −88.90° | east, north 15 km (1,366 over the datum) | dive to −798, up, ashore in 19 s | ≤ 0.009° |

Each site: stand, jump and land (the fall along the radius), walk east and north with `vox.AutoRun` along great circles,
drop into the sea with `vox.TP … 0`, swim, dive (crouch), surface (jump), swim to land and walk out; screenshots
`p3f_<site>_stand`, `_swim`, `_under`, `_ashore`. Then **one continuous walk from 89.5° to the equator** along longitude
45° (`vox.AutoRun` along the meridian, `vox.SetSpeed 1500` on land): 1,239 s, about 210,500 uu walked and 185,600 uu
swum in seven stretches of sea, each left by climbing out onto the next land; blocked once on land at 45.84° and over
it with one jump, no sidestep; the gravity at most
0.014° off the radial, the body at most 0.090° off it (the moment it reached a 1,500 uu/s slope at the equator, 0.013°
otherwise); 4,901 capture lines, no fall-through, no re-cook. The capture's `feetCol=0` appears twice, both the
`settle=0` drop into the polar sea (no ground under the feet in the water); its 186 `feetBody=0` lines are swimming over
chunks with no surface (open water above the seabed).

**Heightmap play: `VoxelDemo` against the base build.** **Unchanged.** The same scenario on the feature build
and on the base build (the worktree checked out at the bases above and rebuilt), with the capture on and the surface NPCs
off (`vox.NPCDensity 0`): PIE start with no save, stand, walk +Y for 40 s, jump, walk −Y off the spawn's coast into the
sea, swim, dive (crouch) and surface (jump), swim back to the coast and walk up it. Three runs on each build; the first
base run was an earlier version of the script with the NPCs on.

Every run spawns on the same point by the same path (`FindSpawnablePosition` finds (0, 0) above water at −609, the
resume trace hits `VoxelCollision_-3_-12_-1` and places the pawn at −502). Base 3 and feature 3 walk, swim, dive and climb
out within a few tens of uu of each other. **Three runs (base 2, features 1 and 2) stopped dead for a minute on land:**
the walker hit an obstacle square on and pushed into it. In base 2 a probe at the stall found the capsule against a scatter
spruce (`HISM_Spruce03_2`, contact at (20, 16169)); feature 1 stopped beside the same tree, at (23, 16167); feature 2 at
(82, 2287), not identified (the probe was added after it), and a later walk through the same point did not stop.
Whether a run meets a trunk depends on where the first contact deflects the walker (its X at the first sample is −16 or
−45 on either build). That is the auto-walker against scatter collision, on both builds; heightmap walking, swimming,
spawning and the capture are the same.

**Things to know.**

- Gravity is a function of the position; nothing new replicates (the engine's replicated gravity direction serves
  simulated proxies). NPCs use `UVCMovementComponent`, so they fall toward the centre too, but their AI still steers in
  world yaw (SP-F6, Phase 4).
- The gravity frame is the engine's (`FindBetweenNormals` from +Z), which spins near the south pole; only
  frame-independent operations are done in it, and the south-pole site behaves like the others.
- Swimming is drag-limited at about 171 uu/s (`SwimmingMaxAcceleration` 256 over `SwimmingDragCoefficient` 1.5), as on
  the plane; `vox.SetSpeed` raises walking only.
- Trees and other scatter still stand along world Z on a planet (SP-G1): at mid latitudes they lean, and the auto-walker
  can walk into a trunk (the trial walk stopped at a spruce at 50.66° until a jump).
- The sky, clouds and sun are a Z-up layer (SP-G7, SP-G8): the equator and the south pole read as night, the cloud layer
  crosses the view diagonally at mid latitudes.
- The ocean shell is a sphere: in a dry cave below sea level it shows inside the cave (a per-chunk radial water surface
  would be the fix if it matters).
- G19 (§14.1): heightmap water consumers keep two plane conventions (generation, scatter, the map and PCG at
  `WaterLevel`; navigation, the character and the NPC spawner at `WaterLevel + WorldOrigin.Z`), now named in
  `FVoxelSeaSurface`. They agree whenever `WorldOrigin.Z` is 0, as in every configuration here.
- `vox.DeleteSave` in the editor (no PIE) does nothing; run it in PIE, or delete the worktree's
  `Saved/SaveGames/Worlds/World_PlanetTest_*` files. An old auto-save put the pawn 57 km over the planet (where a pre-Phase
  3 `vox.TP` had left it); the terrain wait timed out after 60 s and recovered to the planet spawn point, as designed.

**Left for later.** Phase 4 (systems): `GetTerrainHeightAt` (SP-A3), scatter, PCG, map, navigation and NPC AI on the
surface parameterisation and local up, world-item drops and the placeable slope (SP-F7), the edit brush axis (SP-F8),
the clock, sun and sky. Phase 5: POIs and campsites.

## 18. Spherical Phase 4: systems (2026-10-17)

The requirements doc's Phase 4 ([SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md](SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md) §4): SP-A3, SP-A4,
SP-D1 to SP-D3, SP-F6 to SP-F8, SP-G1 to SP-G4, SP-G7 to SP-G9, SP-H2, SP-H3 and SP-I4, plus SP-A6 and SP-I5, which are
already done (below). Phase 3 made the planet walkable (§17), but every other system that reads the surface still assumes
+Z is up: trees stand along world Z, the map draws both hemispheres onto one XY grid from the legacy height query (a
radius read as a Z), navigation and the NPC spawner sample that same query and steer in world yaw, the sun is one
world-frame direction (the equator and the south pole read as night), and world items snap along world −Z. Exit check:
the QA plan's world, NPC, map and save rows (`VoxelWorldPOI/Documentation/QA_TEST_PLAN.md`) pass on the planet; the
table at the end of §18.1 maps them to rows. Heightmap worlds must behave exactly as before.

Bases: VoxelWorlds `fab8fa3`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `e51cc77`, InteractionPlugin `99cc023`, WorldClockPlugin `e0919ab`,
UE5_PluginDev `a5948c1`. Live checks on `PlanetTest` with `/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through
`voxel.ConfigOverride`, as in §15-§17.

**Already done.** SP-A6: every planet params build from a configuration goes through
`FVoxelWorldModeFactory::MakePlanetParams` (the chunk manager, the generation request, the LOD strategy, and through
`Create` the map, POI placement and the field viewer); nothing else fills `FSphericalPlanetParams` from a configuration
(code survey, 2026-10-17). SP-I5: `vox.TPLatLon` and `vox.Planet` exist since Phase 3 (§17).

**What the code survey found (2026-10-17)**, beyond Appendix A of the requirements doc:

- 14 production callers of `GetTerrainHeightAt`, and two chunk-manager wrappers over it (`QueryEditMergedSurface`,
  `GetGeneratedSurfaceHeight`), feed the map, PCG, navigation, the NPC spawner, POI placement, campsite levelling, tree
  injection, the bench and three debug commands. Only scatter's cover check and the spawn search have a planet branch.
- The face type that runs is computed in the vertex conversion (`FVoxelLocalVertex::FromVoxelVertex`: the normal's Z
  against 0.7) for every mesh on the custom vertex factory, not in `VoxelMaterialCommon.ush`, which no shader includes.
  Planets mesh with Dual Contouring (the demo's), so the two marching-cubes sites (SP-D1, SP-D2) run only on an MC planet.
- Scatter's live path scans voxel columns along world Z. The mesh-vertex extractor is dead code; the GPU extractor is off
  by default, LOD 0 only, and not deterministic (an atomic claim per grid cell).
- Map tiles, explored tiles, edit overlays, NPC kill ids and dungeon records all key on world-XY cells. The save's
  fingerprint already carries a planet-only version (`PlanetGeneration` in its shape).
- The clock is one global hour. `ADayNightController` sets the sun's world rotation and never touches the SkyAtmosphere
  (at engine defaults in both maps: the planet's top at the world origin, an Earth-sized radius), the clouds or the sky
  sphere.
- `APawn::GetPawnViewLocation` adds the eye height along world Z (engine code), so at the equator NPC sight traces and
  the player's melee trace start beside the head.
- POI placement samples the legacy height, so on a planet POIs, their claims and dungeon stamps land above the northern
  hemisphere or inside it.

| P4.2 Scatter and PCG | WM-SY6, WM-SY7 | VoxelWorlds | Trees stand on local up at every site with a uniform density; the PCG grid tests pass; heightmap scatter and PCG unchanged |
| P4.3 Map and save keys | WM-SY8 to WM-SY10 | VoxelWorlds, VoxelCharacterPlugin, parent | The minimap and the world map show the planet; exploration and overlays save and load by surface key |
| P4.4 Navigation and NPCs | WM-SY11 to WM-SY13 | VoxelWorlds, VoxelCharacterPlugin, parent | Paths on the sphere; deer and wolves spawn, wander, flee, chase and jump in the local frame |
| P4.5 Clock and sky | WM-SY14, WM-SY15 | WorldClockPlugin, parent | A day side and a night side; local time in the HUD, the NPC spawner and sleeping; the sky centred on the planet |
| P4.6 Items, brush, bench, tooling | WM-SY16 to WM-SY19 | InteractionPlugin, VoxelCharacterPlugin, VoxelWorlds, parent | Drops and placing along gravity; the great-circle bench; the debug commands on a planet |
| Exit | WM-SY20 to WM-SY22 | all | The exit check met; suites green headless and in the editor; the heightmap A/B unchanged |

Order: P4.1 first (everything after it uses its queries), then P4.2 and P4.6 (independent of the rest), P4.3, P4.4, and
P4.5 as the decisions below allow. Waiting on a decision: WM-SY9's world map (D11), WM-SY14 and WM-SY15 (D12), and the
version bump in WM-SY5 and WM-SY10 (D13). PRs: VoxelWorlds in two, stacked (P4.1 and P4.2; then the rest with these docs),
InteractionPlugin, VoxelCharacterPlugin, WorldClockPlugin, then UE5_PluginDev (VoxelWorldPOI, VoxelWorldSave, the game
module, the setup script, the gitlinks and the doc map). ItemInventoryPlugin is not touched: the placeable slope test gets
the normal in the gravity frame (WM-SY16).

**Design (written before building).** P4.1, terrain queries, meshing and precision:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| The legacy query on a planet | `GetTerrainHeightAt(X, Y)`: the direction from the centre to (X, Y, Centre.Z + √(R² − ρ²)), ρ the distance of (X, Y) from the centre's vertical clamped to R; the terrain along it (`SampleRadialDisplacement`); its world Z. A warning the first time in a process, naming SP-A3. After this phase no planet path calls it; the warning catches strays | The requirement's fallback: a legacy caller then places on the northern hemisphere's surface instead of at a radius in the sky |
| Altitude bounds | `GetAltitudeBounds(Min, Max)`: by default `GetTerrainHeightBounds` mapped through `GetAltitude` (Z − SeaLevel on the plane and the island); a planet's is its shell, −MaxTerrainDepth to +MaxTerrainHeight. The planet's `GetTerrainHeightBounds` becomes Centre.Z ± OuterRadius, what its `GetWorldBounds` reports. The LOD strategy's vertical cull stays heightmap-only and unchanged; the map shades by the altitude bounds | A conservative superset in the planet's own terms, as `GetTerrainHeightBounds` is for the plane; the ±1e9 default made the map special-case planets |
| The edit-merged surface on a planet | `QueryEditMergedSurfacePoint(WorldPos, FVoxelSurfaceHit&)` starts from the analytic point along the direction (`GetSurfacePoint`) and walks a digital line along local up one chunk either side: steps along the axis nearest up, sideways shifts rounded as in `FVoxelDownLines`, one edit-merged voxel read per step as in the column scan. It takes the topmost solid voxel with air above it, interpolates the crossing along the true up direction, takes the normal from the edit-merged density gradient flipped toward local up, and the slope as the angle to local up. It returns false when the estimate's chunk is not loaded, as now. Heightmap modes: `QueryEditMergedSurface(X, Y)`, with (X, Y, H) | A planet query then costs what a plane query costs and stays exact on the voxel grid; generation's own underground and water passes walk the same lines (§15.1) |
| Material and biome at a planet surface point | `QuerySurfaceConditionsAt`: temperature, moisture and continentalness at the datum-sphere point (`GetNoiseSamplePoint`), the biome blend, height rules by altitude, the underwater variant when the terrain radius is under `WaterRadius`: the functions `GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet` calls, in its order | The map's colours and PCG's material attribute then equal what generation writes at that surface voxel (tested at sample points) |
| The MC material scan on a planet | The meshing request carries `LocalUp`, the chunk centre's (+Z in heightmap modes). The scan walks K = 0 to 8 along the digital line in that direction, and "highest" means farthest along it. Exactly +Z runs the old loop | The scan's purpose, grass over dirt at the surface corner, is along local up; the chunk centre's up is within 0.6° of the true up anywhere in a 4,800 uu chunk on this planet |
| The MC geomorph on a planet | Morph along the axis A nearest the chunk's local up (±X, ±Y or ±Z): `ComputeCoarseSurfaceZ` generalised to a coarse line along A, the steepness gate on \|N·A\| as today, on the CPU and the GPU (the GPU MC mesher is idle at runtime but kept in step). A = +Z is the old arithmetic | The surface lies mostly across one axis away from the cube's edges, and the gate already skips vertices more than 60° off it, as it skips steep slopes on the plane: the morph acts where it is valid and nowhere else. A radial morph would need a coarse lattice sampled along an arbitrary line, and the requirement allows the simpler course |
| The face type | `FChunkRenderData` gains `FaceUp` (the chunk centre's local up, +Z by default); `FromVoxelVertex(V, FaceUp)` classifies by N·FaceUp against 0.7, and with +Z it is the old Normal.Z comparison. The tangent's reference axis stays world Z | The custom vertex factory recomputes the face type for every vertex, so this is the site that runs. Smooth materials are triplanar on world axes, which works in any orientation, and read the face type only in the cubic atlas path, which planets do not use (SD3) |
| The ore hash on a planet | `Hash32(planet-relative voxel index) / 2³²` against `Rarity`: the index is round((ChunkWorldPos − Centre) / VoxelSize), computed in double, plus the local voxel index; one integer hash (PCG style) shared by C++ and HLSL. Heightmap modes keep `frac(sin(…))` | Planet-relative is what SP-H3 asks, but with `WorldOrigin` 0 the old hash already was: its trouble is `sin` of an argument near 10⁷, which the GPU's float and the CPU's double round differently. An integer index hash is exact at any radius and equal on both sides, so the parity test can run with `Rarity` < 1 |
| The radius ceiling (SP-H2) | Documented in `WORLD_MODES.md` and `TRAVERSAL_LIMITS.md`: absolute float vertex positions in the scene proxy have a ULP of about 0.06 uu at 10 km and 1 uu at 100 km, where seams and collision start to show; past that, origin rebasing would have to separate the planet centre from the chunk grid's origin, both of which `WorldOrigin` is today | — |

P4.2, scatter and PCG:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Scatter extraction on a planet | Lines along the chunk's local up over the same voxel data (edit-merged where edited), started on a stride grid across the axis nearest up (`FVoxelDownLines`'s geometry, moved to VoxelCore's public headers). Along each line the column's state machine: every solid voxel with air above it along the line, "not the topmost" makes it underground, the next voxel along the line answers "air above is water"; the crossing interpolated along the line; the density-gradient normal. Each point records its local up (radial at the point) and its altitude. Heightmap worlds keep `ExtractSurfacePointsFromVoxelData` as it is | Same data, same flags (generation's underground flag is radial since SP-B7), same determinism; the heightmap function is not touched, so heightmap scatter is unchanged by construction. The mesh-vertex extractor gives positions and normals but none of the voxel flags, and the GPU one is non-deterministic and LOD 0 only |
| Density on a planet | A line bundle across axis A with spacing s meets the surface at a density of 1 / (s² cos θ), θ the angle between up and A (up to √3× at a cube corner), so each point's spawn probability is scaled by cos θ | Trees per area then match the plane's at every latitude (measured in the test) |
| Classification on a planet | Face type and slope against the point's local up; the elevation filter compares the altitude (heightmap modes: world Z, as documented today); the underwater test is the sea (already); the cover check stays heightmap-only | The rules read "up" and "height" in the world's own frame |
| The instance transform | `FVoxelSurfacePoint::LocalUp` (default +Z). Without `bAlignToSurfaceNormal` the instance's Z axis is local up and the random yaw turns about it (`FindBetweenNormals(+Z, Up)` then the yaw); with it, the surface normal as now. Jitter in the tangent plane, from the same two random draws. Up exactly +Z runs the old expressions | Trees stand along gravity; the heightmap branch keeps the old rotator arithmetic bit for bit |
| The harvest exclusion box | The box's frame turned to local up, its centre along up from the base; the id from the base position as now | A felled tree's volume covers its trunk on a planet, and the save keeps it |
| GPU extraction | `WantsGPUExtraction` is false on planets | Its gates are along +Z; it is off by default anyway |
| The PCG grid on a planet | The bounding shape's box gives the faces and UV ranges it touches (its corners and centre through `WorldToSurface`). Per face, cells of du = Spacing / (R·π/4), so a cell is about Spacing across; each cell's centre gives the surface point along it (edit-merged near, analytic far), kept when inside the box; the seed from (face, iu, iv); rotation to local up (or the normal); the attributes as now, the slope against local up. The cell walk is a pure function, tested on its own. Heightmap modes: the XY loop unchanged | Points then cover a volume placed anywhere on the planet without gaps or doubles (each surface point belongs to one face) at the configured spacing, the tangent warp keeping cell areas within 1.38× |
| PCG water | `FVoxelSeaSurface::FromConfig` | On the plane it is `WaterLevel`, so nothing changes; on a planet the sphere. The configuration's water warning then names no consumer |

P4.3, map and save keys:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| The tile key on a planet | N tiles along a face edge, N = ⌈(π/2)·R / ChunkWorldSize⌉ (82 on `Review_Planet`: 6 × 82² = 40,344 tiles, a tile about 4,800 uu across and a pixel about 75 uu, as on the plane); the atlas coordinate (Face·N + TU, TV). Every container, the store, the queue, the budgets, the save blob and `PruneExploredOutsideWorld` (on a planet: inside the atlas) keep working on `FIntPoint` keys | No new key type: heightmap keys stay (chunk X, chunk Y) and their code paths are not touched |
| Tile pixels on a planet | Pixel (px, py) → UV → direction → the analytic surface point (`GetSurfacePoint`); material and biome from `QuerySurfaceConditionsAt`; water where the sea sphere is above the terrain, shaded by sea depth; elevation shading by altitude over `GetAltitudeBounds`; the hillshade's normal in the local frame (east, north, up) with the plane's light vector. The one-pixel apron through the neighbouring UV, across a face edge through the 3D direction | Each pixel is the plane's computation in the local frame; conditioning does not apply on planets yet (SP-B10) |
| Exploration on a planet | `RequestTilesInRadius`: the tiles whose centres lie within the radius (3D) of the position, gathered outward from the position's tile through UV neighbours (across face edges through the direction). `OnChunkGenerated` marks the tiles the chunk's surface patch touches (its corners and centre through `WorldToSurface`) | The explored set means "seen around the player", as on the plane, and the two hemispheres no longer share tiles |
| Edit overlays on a planet | The overlay's columns become the tile pixels' up-lines: `GatherOverlayInput` collects the edited chunks the tile's patch passes through, and the worker walks each pixel's line through their snapshots (WM-SY2's line walk), storing altitudes instead of world Z (`FVoxelMapEditOverlay::FormatVersion` 2 for planet overlays; the plane's stay version 1) | Digs show on the planet's map as they do on the plane's (W-05, W-06) |
| The minimap on a planet | The texture is the tangent plane at the player in a north-up frame: east = +Z × up normalised (at a pole the face's axes), north = up × east. Each texel's ground point → (face, UV) → tile pixel, through a 16 × 16 grid of exact control points with bilinear UV inside cells that stay on one face, exact per texel in cells that cross a face edge; rotated by the camera's heading against north, as now; markers projected into the frame | Heading-up like the plane's minimap. It costs a few ms per refresh instead of a blit, so it redraws only when the player has moved a texel, turned, or a tile arrived |
| The world map on a planet | D11 (below) | — |
| Map markers | `FVCMapMarker` gets `WorldLocation` (3D; the 2D field stays for heightmap providers) and the planet views project it. POIs are not placed on planets until Phase 5 (WM-SY3), so the planet's maps show no markers yet | The plumbing is ready for Phase 5 |
| Save keys | The save keeps the same blobs: planet worlds write atlas keys and version-2 overlays, and old planet saves are refused by D13's bump, so no format sniffing is needed. NPC kill ids pack the planet cell (WM-SY13) | Heightmap documents unchanged, byte for byte |

P4.4, navigation and NPCs:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Navigation on a planet | Regions are cells of the surface coordinate's grid, about four chunks (19,200 uu) across. A search uses the frame of the region its start lies in: origin O, the region centre on the datum sphere; up there; east and north from the face's axes projected onto the tangent plane. Frame coordinates (x, y) map to the world through the direction of O + x·E + y·N from the centre (a gnomonic projection: on `Review_Planet` the search radius stays within 7° of O, cell sizes within 2% of `CellSize`). The pathfinder is the existing `FVoxelSurfacePathfinder` over (x, y): its "height" is the cell's altitude (`QueryEditMergedSurfacePoint` along the direction, the analytic surface as the fallback), its water a plane at altitude `WaterRadius − PlanetRadius` (exactly the sea sphere's depth), its output (x, y, altitude) turned back into world points. One tile cache per region frame, frames dropped after 60 s unused. Blocked boxes become 3D boxes and temporary blocks 3D spheres (heightmap: the old cell set); invalidation by each cached tile's 3D bounds; `ProjectToSurface` and `IsWalkableAt` along local up | SP-G4 says a per-request tangent grid is enough, and one canonical frame per region keeps the plane's cache across requests. The pathfinder and its tests stay as they are, so the plane's navigation is unchanged by construction |
| NPC AI | Helpers in the controller over `FVCGravityFrame`: the offset across local up between two points, its length and direction, a yaw-only facing rotation. Every `Dist2D`, `GetSafeNormal2D`, `FVector(…, 0)` and world-yaw `FRotator` in the AI goes through them; auto-jump's feet, knee start, top probe and rise along local up; wander goals at an angle in the tangent plane at the leash origin; flee directions rotated about local up. Without planet gravity each helper returns the old expression | The engine already walks, falls and turns NPCs in gravity space (Phase 3); only the AI's own geometry is Z-up |
| Eye height | `AVCCharacterBase` and `AVCNPCCharacterBase` override `GetPawnViewLocation`: the location plus local up × `BaseEyeHeight` on a planet, the engine's otherwise | The engine adds it along world Z, so at the equator every eye trace (sight, melee, auto-aim) starts beside the head |
| The NPC spawner | On a planet, cells are the face UV grid at `CellSize` on the surface, atlas-coded like the map (they fit the id's 20-bit cell fields); plans and groups as now, with offsets in the tangent plane at the cell's surface; distances in 3D (heightmap modes 2D, as now); the collision and feet probes along −up; `SpawnCreature` stands the creature on local up and calls `UpdatePlanetGravity` / `SnapUprightToGravity`; the corpse topple sinks along −up and rolls about the body's own forward axis; loot bursts along local up | Herds keep their cells and ids across visits (F10-07, F10-08) on a planet too |

P4.5, the clock and the sky (if D12 is decided as recommended):

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| The sun's direction | With a planet frame set (centre C, axis the world's +Z through C), the sun's world direction turns about the axis by the hour angle of longitude 0, at declination 0 (a `SunDeclinationDegrees` setting left for a later axial tilt); the directional light points along −sun. The local solar hour at P is the global hour plus longitude(P) / 15. Phases, the HUD text, sleeping and the NPC spawner use the local hour, with the plane's hour rules; the light curves (sun, sky light, exposure) use a daylight value from the sun's elevation at the viewer, a ramp that equals `DaylightForHour` on the equator | A fixed sun over a turning planet is the same thing seen from the ground; the terrain cannot turn, so the sun does. Hour-based phases keep every consumer's rules; elevation-based light is what the sky shows (at a pole the sun stays low all day) |
| Who tells the clock | `UWorldClockSubsystem::SetPlanetFrame(Centre, Axis)` / `ClearPlanetFrame`; a VoxelWorldPOI world subsystem sets it once the chunk manager reports a shell. WorldClockPlugin keeps its engine-only dependencies | As the world-item pool learns its parking spot (§17) |
| Sleeping | `NextMorning` in local time at the campsite: the global time moves so that the campsite's local hour is sunrise | "Sleep until dawn" means dawn where you sleep |
| The sky | The controller, which already finds the lights, also finds the SkyAtmosphere. With a planet frame: `TransformMode = PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform`, the component at the centre, `BottomRadius` the sea radius (the datum without water) in km; the atmosphere's height and scattering stay the engine's, an Earth-like sky from the ground. The Z-up sky sphere actor (tagged by the setup script) and any height fog are hidden; the volumetric clouds follow the atmosphere's planet (their layer altitude lowered for a small planet in content); the sky light keeps its real-time capture | The engine's sky is already a sphere around a planet; it only needs to be told where the planet is |

**Decisions for the user** (asked and decided 2026-10-17, each as recommended; recorded in §8):

| ID | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|----|----------|---------|----------------|
| D11 | The world map on a planet (SP-G3) | (a) **A globe:** an orthographic view of the planet around a view direction, dragged to turn it and zoomed with the wheel (a local map when zoomed in), opening centred on the player with north up. (b) **An unfolded cube:** the six faces laid out as a cross, panned and zoomed as on the plane | **(a), the globe.** It reuses the minimap's sampler and has no cut edges (a route never jumps across the cross). (b) is cheaper to draw (tile images blitted per face) but tears the world along seven of the cube's twelve edges and is up to 1.38× distorted |
| D12 | How the sun and sky work on a planet (SP-G7, SP-G8) | (a) **A world-fixed sun** turning about the planet's axis once a day: a day side and a night side, local solar time by longitude for the HUD, the NPCs and sleeping, the poles always in a low sun (no axial tilt). (b) **A sun in each player's local frame:** the clock's hour lights every place the same way, there is no night side, and nothing else changes | **(a)**, as SP-G7 describes, with no axial tilt for now, phases by the local solar hour, light by the sun's real elevation, and the SkyAtmosphere at the engine's Earth values. `PlanetTest`'s PlayerStart over the north pole then spawns in a permanent low sun; QA moves to mid latitudes with `vox.TPLatLon`, and the pole stays as it is |
| D13 | Does Phase 4 bump `PlanetGenerationVersion`, the planet-only version in the fingerprint's shape? | Bump 2 → 3: every planet save is refused (planet saves hold only test data); heightmap saves keep loading (`GenerationVersion` stays 2). Or no bump, with a map key-format field that drops old planet exploration at load | **Bump.** SP-H3 changes which voxels are ore wherever an ore's `Rarity` < 1, and on planets the explored tiles, the overlays and the NPC kill ids change keys: a pre-Phase 4 planet save would put ores and exploration in the wrong places. Not bumping needs the key-format field and still loads stale ores |

Pass: every row as above, no fall-through in the capture, and nothing in the log beyond the known Phase 5 notices.

**Heightmap worlds unchanged.** Planet-only code runs only when the world's bounds are a shell (or the clock has a planet
frame); where bit-identity matters each new helper branches to the old expression for up +Z rather than rewriting it.
Checked by the existing suites, the "Unchanged" tests above, and a live A/B on `VoxelDemo`, base build against feature
build, one script on both: `voxel.Map.Capture` at the spawn (identical PNG), a scatter digest at the spawn (instance
counts and a CRC of the transforms per type, the new `voxel.Scatter.Digest`), `vox.NavPath` to three fixed points (the
same nodes and length), `vox.NPCs` after 60 s at a fixed hour (the same creatures in the same places), `vox.Clock`, and
the QA W, F6, F9 and F10 rows played briefly.

SP-G5, SP-G6, SP-G10; the WM-SY3 guard holds them off until then); the far-terrain band (SP-C5); the ocean shell showing

  respawn rotations from world yaw, so away from the north pole the view pointed into the ground or the sky; near the
  pole, where the first spawn is, it was 3° off and went unnoticed. Every possession now marks the view
  (`AVCPlayerController::bLevelViewInGravity`, set in `OnPossess` and `AcknowledgePossession`), and the first frame in a
  planet's gravity zeroes its pitch relative to local up, keeping the heading. Rechecked: 0.0° at the first spawn and
  after a respawn at 43°.
- **G22: world items lay in the world's frame.** The mesh is `AWorldItem`'s root, so the placeholder's zero and the
  WorldDisplay fragment's lying pose (`SetRelativeRotation`) replaced the pool's upright rotation. The new
  `AWorldItem::ApplyRestingPose` applies the pose on top of the upright rotation with a gravity centre and is the world

## 19. Spherical Phase 5: places (2026-10-17)

The requirements doc's Phase 5 ([SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md](SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md) §4): SP-B10 and
SP-G5, then SP-G6 and SP-G10. Phase 4 made every system that reads the surface work in the local frame (§18) but held
POIs, generated campsites, dungeons and claims' conditioning off on planets (`UPOIPlacementSubsystem::IsHeldForPlanet`,
WM-SY3), because placement samples the heightmap height and its cells are world-XY squares. Exit check: POIs and campsites
sit on the planet's surface, and dungeons too if scope decision SD4 includes them in this phase (D14 below); the table at
the end of §19.1 maps the QA rows to planet checks. Heightmap worlds must behave exactly as before.

Bases: VoxelWorlds `0fed9a0`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `8465d26`, InteractionPlugin `b941201`, WorldClockPlugin `0ce2ce2`,
ProceduralDungeonPlugin `fb4bd6b`, WorldClaims `cafde48`, UE5_PluginDev `e9d8ff0`. Live checks on `PlanetTest` with
`/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride` (R 250,000, water 249,500, shell ±6,500), as in
§15-§18.

**What the code survey found (2026-10-17)**, beyond Appendix A of the requirements doc:

- Conditioning is heightmap-only on both paths: an `FVoxelConditioningZone` is an XY disc with a world-Z target, the
  chunk manager gathers zones by a chunk's XY square (`GatherConditioningZonesForChunk`), the CPU generators blend the
  column height before the SDF, and the GPU's heightmap branch does the same (`GpuApplyConditioning`). The planet's CPU
  generator and its GPU branch (`SphericalPlanet.ush`) skip zones with a comment naming SP-B10. Nothing on a planet's
  analytic side would see a zone either: `GetGeneratedSurfacePoint`, the map's planet tiles, `QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions`,
  scatter's line top (the crossing at a chunk's upper face is put on the analytic surface, `ExtractSurfacePointsAlongUp`),
  the PCG sampler's far points and the planet spawn point all read the world mode's own surface.
- POI placement is a pure function of (seed, cell): one candidate per `CellSize` square (64,000 uu), a position inside it,
  a weighted type pick among the types whose surface filter accepts the centre, a 29-sample site survey (`SurveySite`:
  centre, two rings of 8 on the footprint, 12 on the falloff edge) judged against the water line, a relief limit and a cover
  rule for dungeons, and a pad at the survey's median height. On a planet every one of these steps reads `GetTerrainHeightAt`
  (the legacy query: the upper hemisphere's Z) and world XY.
- Everything a POI spawns is composed on its pad transform, `FTransform(ZeroRotator, (Centre, PadHeight))`: claims
  (`AWorldClaimVolume`), structures (`RelativeTransform * LayoutYaw * Pad`), the campsite spawner's campsite, the dungeon's
  origin. Only the pad transform and the terrain samples are Z-up; the composition is already transform-relative.
- Claims are already oriented boxes where it matters: `UWorldClaimComponent::ContainsPoint`, the edit validator
  (`FClaimEditValidator` bakes the component transform) and scatter's claim suppression (`FScatterExclusionVolume`, frame
  plus half extent) all invert the actor's transform; the registry's box query is an AABB of the oriented box
  (conservative). The map markers query claims as a world-Z ±1e9 box and dedupe in 2D (`UPOIMapMarkerSubsystem`), and
  nothing binds the 3D marker query Phase 4 added (`UVCMapMarkerRegistry::OnGatherMarkersNear`).
- Dungeons are translation-only end to end: the stamper writes each open cell's world AABB on the voxel lattice
  (`UDungeonVoxelStamper::StampDungeon`, faces ±X ±Y ±Z, stairs measured along world X/Y/Z), the entrance stitcher finds
  the surface by a world-Z sweep from +10,000 to −10,000 when the world is not a heightmap (on a planet it finds nothing and
  returns 0), the passage plan is a list of axis-aligned columns over a `float(X, Y)` surface, the tile mapper outputs
  `GridToWorld + WorldOffset` with yaw-only rotations, and `ADungeonActor` adds its instances in world space (an actor
  rotation would be cancelled). The POI side keeps scalar world Zs and world points in `FPOIDungeonEntranceInfo`
  (`EntranceFloorZ`, `PassageBottomZ`, room floors, `DungeonBoundsWorld` as an FBox), which the enemies, the objective,
  the chests, the elevator and the grid path build on with world-Z arithmetic.
- Save: dungeon records (`FPOIDungeonRecord`) are keyed by the placement cell (an `FIntPoint`), and import merges only the
  player-driven states and the cleared flag, so the saved geometry is never read back; player-placed campsites are saved
  as placed actors with their full transform (rotation-safe); seed-placed POIs are not saved (they are the seed's).
- Two heightmap readers of the analytic surface skip conditioning: scatter's buried-chunk test
  (`ExtractSurfacePointsFromVoxelData`, `ChunkTopWorldZ < GetTerrainHeightAt − 1.5 voxels`) and the PCG sampler's far
  points (`FVoxelSurfaceQuery::SampleSurface`). In a POI's falloff ring, where conditioning moves the ground, the first can
  flag a surface chunk as buried and the second puts far points at the natural height. Recorded as **G23** (§14.1); it is a
  heightmap behaviour, so Phase 5 does not change it (the A/B must stay identical), and the planet versions are written
  condition-aware from the start (WM-PL4).
- `ADungeonActor::SetTileInstanceHidden` writes the instance's world transform with `bWorldSpace=false`, so a hidden
  instance moves by the actor's location; it is only ever hidden (scaled to zero, F5-06's broken crate), so nothing shows.
  The local-space instances of WM-PL12 remove it.

**Design (written before building).** P5.1, conditioning on a planet:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| The zone's shape on a planet | A cap on the datum sphere: weight by the great-circle distance from the zone's direction, `s = R · atan2(|D × Dz|, D · Dz)`, `Strength` inside `InnerRadius`, the heightmap's smoothstep across `FalloffWidth`, 0 beyond (D15) | The plane's disc, measured on the surface; atan2 is well conditioned at small angles in float on the GPU (about 0.03 uu at 4,500 uu on this planet) |
| What it flattens | The terrain's altitude along each direction: `A' = lerp(A, TargetAltitude, w)` per zone in order, so the radius `R + A'` replaces `R + A` before the SDF, as `ApplyToHeight` replaces the column height | A pad is then level in gravity (constant altitude) everywhere on it; the heightmap's "TargetHeight is a world Z" becomes "an altitude", the planet's height everywhere else (SP-A1) |
| A planet zone's fields | `Direction` (FVector, zero on heightmaps) beside the 2D `Center`; one struct, so the request, the chunk manager's static list and Blueprint keep one type. A zone with a direction is a planet zone; heightmap code never looks at it | The heightmap struct's layout and every heightmap path stay as they are; a planet zone placed in a heightmap world (or the reverse) contributes nothing, with a warning at `AddConditioningZone` |
| Gathering on a planet | The chunk's cap: its centre's direction and the angle its half-diagonal subtends from the planet centre (everything, for a chunk around the centre). A zone meets it when the angle between them is at most the cap's angle plus the zone's angular radius `(InnerRadius + FalloffWidth) / R`. The conditioner answers the same cap query (`GatherConditioningOnSphere`) | Conservative and cheap (one dot product per zone and chunk); it gives the generator exactly the zones whose influence can reach the chunk, as the XY square does on the plane |
| The GPU | The same zone buffer and count; the planet branch reads `[Dx, Dy, Dz, Inner][Falloff, Target, Strength, 0]`, uploaded that way when the request's world mode is the planet; the weight and blend in `SphericalPlanet.ush` after the radial height, before `PlanetShellSignedDistance` | No new shader parameter; the heightmap packing, branch and CRCs are untouched |
| Who reads the generated surface | Every planet consumer that reads the world mode's analytic surface as "the ground": `GetGeneratedSurfacePoint`, the line walk's start in `QueryEditMergedSurfacePoint`, `QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions` / `SampleSurfacePoint` (with zones), the map's planet tiles, scatter's line top, PCG's far points, the planet spawn point and search. `GetSurfacePointAt` stays the world mode's (natural) surface, as `GetTerrainHeightAt` is on the plane; POI placement reads the natural surface on purpose | One rule, "the generated surface is the natural surface plus the zones", applied wherever a planet reader means the ground the generator makes. On the plane G23 is the same rule broken; it stays a heightmap follow-up |

P5.2 and P5.3, POIs, campsites and claims:

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Cells on a planet | The cube-sphere grid with `N = CellsPerEdgeFor(R, CellSize)` (7 a face edge on `Review_Planet` at the default 64,000: 294 cells, each at most 64,000 uu across), keyed by atlas coordinate; `HashCell(Seed, Atlas.X, Atlas.Y)` and the same draws for existence, position, radius and type; the position is the cell fraction 0.15-0.85 along U and V | The heightmap rule on the planet's own 2D coordinate; the atlas key is face-qualified, so streaming, dungeon records and the POI seed (`MakePOISeed`) keep their `FIntPoint` |
| Which cells a cap query visits | `GatherWithinAngle` from the cap's direction with the cap's angle plus the largest POI influence and a cell's angular half-diagonal; a POI is returned when its influence cap meets the query cap | Every caller (conditioner per chunk, streaming, markers, search) gets the same POI for a cell whatever cap it asks with: a pure function of (seed, cell) |
| The site survey | `SurveySite`'s pattern in the tangent plane at the centre (east and north from `FVoxelCubeSphere::GetTangentFrame`): a sample at distance r and heading a is the direction `D cos(r/R) + (E cos a + N sin a) sin(r/R)` (r along the surface), its natural altitude (`GetSurfacePoint` of the configured world mode). Water line: the sea's altitude, `WaterRadius − R` (−500 on `Review_Planet`), when water is on, else 0 | The plane's rules read in the planet's own height (altitude) and distance (along the surface) |
| Pad space | Each POI has a pad space: on a heightmap the world itself (identity); on a planet the tangent frame at the datum point under its centre, x east, y north, z local up (`C + D·R` the origin), so the pad is at (0, 0, PadAltitude). Every piece of POI code that composes things on the pad (claims, structures, layout yaw, the campsite, and in P5.4 the dungeon) works in pad space with its existing arithmetic and converts at the boundary: `PadToWorld` when it spawns an actor or writes a voxel, `WorldToPad` when it reads the world | One idea in place of a frame argument in each consumer: the plane's code is the planet's code in pad space, and the plane runs it with the identity, so its arithmetic does not change |
| Structures on the cap | A structure's world transform is `Relative * LayoutYaw * Pad` mapped to the world, then draped: moved along its own up line to the pad's altitude plus its height above the pad, and turned from the pad's up to its own local up | The pad is level in gravity, not a plane: a building 3,000 uu from the centre of a pad on `Review_Planet` would otherwise float 18 uu above it and lean 0.7° off its gravity |
| Claims | The pad claim and the deep dungeon claim spawn at their pad-space transforms mapped to the world (rotated boxes); extents as now (z along local up) | Their consumers already invert the actor's transform; the registry's AABB query stays conservative |
| Streaming and search on a planet | Distances in 3D between the viewer and the pad's world point (the claim band, the structure band, despawn); `FindNearestPOIs` from a world position by expanding caps (1 km, doubling up to the cap); `poi.Find` prints latitude, longitude, altitude and a `vox.TPLatLon` line | On a 2.5 km planet a 2D distance is meaningless; the bands stay straight-line distances, as on the plane |
| Generated campsites | The spawner is a draped structure; the campsite spawns at its transform (upright); `GetRespawnTransform` lifts along the actor's up and faces the fire across it (identity on the plane: the old expression) | F8-04 to F8-08 at a generated campsite |
| Runtime levelling (`PlaceCampsite`) on a planet | The core's mean natural altitude over voxel-spaced points of the tangent plane; then every voxel in the world box of the cap's radial band: its direction, its distance from the centre along the surface, the profile (flat core, the parabolic apron to the natural altitude), density from the radial signed distance `(R + Surface) − |P − C|` with the plane's grading and depth materials; the claim in pad space | The plane's pad and apron in the planet's height; the edits stay on the voxel lattice |

P5.4, dungeons (if D14 includes them):

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| The dungeon's frame | Pad space (no layout yaw, as the plane's grid is never yawed): the grid origin in pad space is computed exactly as today from the pad at (0, 0, PadAltitude), so `WorldOffset` and every recorded point keep their meaning in pad space | The dungeon is rigid (flat floors, straight halls); over its 8,000 uu its floor stays within 2° of the local gravity on `Review_Planet` |
| Stamping a rotated grid | With a non-identity frame the stamper takes the world box of the rotated grid (plus the lining and margin), enumerates its lattice samples once, classifies each by its frame-space position (open cell, lining face, outer seal, stair step), writes it with a density graded by the signed distance to the nearest open-cell box face (DC then meshes a plane at any angle) and one voxel more carve margin and lining (an oblique plane aliases by up to √3/2 voxel on the lattice). Identity frame: the existing per-cell loops, unchanged | A rotated box on an axis-aligned lattice cannot be written per cell AABB; graded densities are what the generator writes, and keep VoxelCarved walls smooth |
| The entrance | The passage plan built in frame space (offset zero) over a surface function: the frame-space height where the frame's vertical line through (x, y) meets the generated surface (a few bisection steps on the altitude along it); the stitcher writes its columns, cave opening and collar in frame space through the same per-sample classification | The plan is already pure and offset-linear; only its surface function and its writes were world-Z |
| The tile actor | Spawned at the frame; `MapToTiles` with a zero offset; instances added relative to the actor; openings, fixtures and props returned through the actor's transform (identity frame: the world-space path) | The mapper is rigid and pure, so composing with the frame is exact, and the interactables keep their ids (cell, face and kind) |
| Dungeon gameplay | `FPOIDungeonEntranceInfo` stays in pad space (world on a heightmap) plus a C++-only `PadToWorld` transform (not a UPROPERTY, so heightmap save documents stay byte for byte); each consumer computes in pad space as today and converts its final transforms (doors, torches, containers, traps, chests, the boss, enemies, the elevator car's axis, loot bursts along local up); the objective's inside test and the enemies' grid map world positions into pad space first | The consumers' Z-up arithmetic becomes correct by construction in pad space; the import never reads the geometry, so saves need no new field |
| Dungeon records on a planet | Keyed by the atlas cell (as streaming); `WorldOffset` saved in pad space; nothing else changes | Import merges states and the cleared flag only |

**Decisions for the user** (asked and decided 2026-10-17, each as recommended; recorded in §8):

| ID | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|----|----------|---------|----------------|
| D14 | Are dungeons (SP-G6) part of Phase 5? SD4 put them last because they need rotated stamping on an axis-aligned grid | (a) **Yes, as Phase 5's last milestone (P5.4)**, in its own PRs, with dungeon types held on planets until it lands; the exit check covers the dungeon rows (F3, F4, F5, F7's dungeon rows, F9-03, F9-04). (b) **No:** Phase 5 is surface POIs and campsites; dungeon types stay held on planets and P5.4 becomes Phase 6's first item. (c) **Axis-snapped dungeons:** stamp unrotated, only where local up is within a few degrees of a world axis (near the six face centres) | **(a).** The survey shows most of the work is mechanical once pad space exists (the mapper is rigid, claims are oriented, saves need nothing new); the real cost is the rotated stamp and the entrance. (c) is cheap but puts dungeons only near the six face centres (about 1% of the surface within 5° of them), tilted by up to the snap angle |
| D15 | The conditioning zone model on a planet (SP-B10) | (a) **A radial cap:** the footprint a cap on the datum sphere (great-circle distance), the target an altitude, so a pad is level in gravity; structures draped onto it. (b) **A tangent plane:** the pad is the plane tangent at the centre, so it rises toward its rim by r²/2R (40 uu at 4,500 uu on `Review_Planet`) and leans up to 1° off gravity there, and rigid layouts sit flush without draping | **(a).** It is the plane's rule in the planet's height, one weight function on the CPU and the GPU, and "flat" means what the player and the physics feel; the cost is draping structures, a few lines in the bridge |
| D16 | Does Phase 5 bump `PlanetGenerationVersion` (refusing planet saves only)? | Bump 3 → 4: every planet save from before Phase 5 is refused and kept on disk; heightmap saves keep loading (`GenerationVersion` stays 2). Or no bump: an old planet save loads onto terrain that is now flattened under POIs, with its edits where they were | **Bump.** Planet generation changes wherever a POI conditions the ground, and planet saves hold only test data. `GenerationVersion` does not move: no heightmap terrain changes |

registration line (placed of candidates, rejections), `poi.Find` for each type (positions, pad heights), the dungeon stamp
lines (seed, rooms, voxels, grid top), `voxel.Map.Capture` at the spawn (identical PNG), `voxel.Scatter.Digest`, NPC
spawns, three `vox.NavPath` paths, `vox.Clock`, and a dungeon visit (`vox.TPPOI Tiled`, `vox.TPRoom Boss`, `vox.Enemies`).

**Left for later.** G23 (heightmap readers that skip conditioning); claim-driven conditioning (a claim volume flattening
ground by itself; today only POI placement feeds the conditioner, on the plane too); World Partition for planets;
replicated world items (§18.2.6).

All of WM-PL1 to WM-PL15 is built, each with its tests, and the exit check is met on `Review_Planet` (§19.2.3): POIs,
generated campsites and both dungeon representations' stamps sit on the planet's surface, and the tile-dressed dungeons
play there as on the plane. Heightmap worlds are unchanged: the suites pass, the identity frames are bit for bit, the GPU
parity lines are identical by CRC, and the `VoxelDemo` A/B against the base build matches (§19.2.4). The live check found
two things, both recorded rather than fixed: G24, voxel-carved dungeons do not hold pawns on a smooth world (on the base
build too), and G25, faint shading lines on a flattened pad.

and `claude/spherical-p5-places-39c52a` in UE5_PluginDev.

Adjustments to the plan (§19.1's design and "How each is verified"):

- WM-PL11 writes the rotated stamp with the same air and solid `Set` edits as the identity path, not densities graded by
  the distance to the cell boxes: a carved or lined plane at an angle to the lattice then steps by up to √3/2 voxel (on a
  tile-dressed dungeon the tiles hide it; a voxel-carved dungeon's walls show it). The extra half voxel of margin and voxel
  of seal apply to tile-dressed stamps only; the voxel lining keeps its thickness, since its surface is the floor content
  stands on and a slab a voxel thick has a sample on every lattice line through it. `FDungeonEntrancePassagePlan::Build`
  did not need a frame: it is pure and offset-linear, so the stitcher builds it in frame space over a frame-space surface
  function (`DetectFrameSurfaceHeight`, a few Newton steps on the altitude along the frame line, not bisection).
- WM-PL13's lookups are by cell (`GetCellAt` maps a world point to its cell in any world mode) rather than an
  `…AtLocation` family; `IsDungeonCleared` already took a cell. The planet markers read the cleared flag by cell.
- `PCG.Planet.ConditionedFar` is part of `Streaming.Planet.ConditionedSurface` (the far points read the same generated
  surface through `SampleSurfacePoint`).
- `POI.Planet.Streaming` and `POI.Planet.MapMarkers` no longer test a held type: dungeon types stream and show markers on
  planets since WM-PL13.
