### 19.3 G23: heightmap scatter and PCG far points read the generated surface (2026-10-17)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#105, `fix/g23-heightmap-conditioning`, base `2fd32fc`, main after spherical Phase 5; the
parent's gitlink and doc map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#115). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor
beside the user's (Claudius on 8081), background throttling off. For every `VoxelDemo` run `DemoSmoothWorldConfig`'s
`bUseGPUScatterExtraction` was set false in memory, never saved (GPU scatter extraction is not deterministic).

**The rule.** "The ground the generator makes" is the natural height with the terrain conditioning zones layered on
(`FVoxelTerrainConditioning::ApplyToHeight`), as on a planet since Phase 5 (WM-PL4). Two heightmap readers that meant
that ground read the natural height (`GetTerrainHeightAt`): scatter's buried-chunk test and the PCG sampler's far points.
POI placement keeps surveying the natural height on purpose.

**Tooling** (kept): `voxel.Scatter.ConditioningAudit [maxLines] [drawSeconds]` audits every cached scatter chunk a zone
reaches: points on the generated ground classified underground (`groundUnder`), the column scan's top-face row under the
ground (`edge`, see G26), surface points in chunks the generated test buries (`rockSurface`), the largest
natural-against-generated gap at a ground point (`farErr`), with a CSV in `Saved/VoxelAudit` and optional debug points.
`voxel.Scatter.ConditioningAudit scan [radiusKm]` judges every zone within a radius analytically ("lost" columns: the
generated ground lies in a chunk the natural test buries). `voxel.Scatter.Digest file` writes one line per chunk
(count, CRC) so two builds compare chunk by chunk.

**Reproduction** (the base build with the audit added, behaviour unchanged).

- The scan over 40 km around the demo spawn: 275 of 1,766 zones have lost columns (86,667 columns on a 150 uu grid),
  394 have raised ones. Most are pads whose target sits a little under a chunk layer's top (Z 0 in the demo, whose
  terrain is near sea level) cut into ground rising over it.
- The Village at (−104,312, 331,034), 3.9 km from the spawn (pad −169, natural −30 at the centre, inner radius 4,609,
  falloff 2,000): 4,969 scatter points on the generated ground classified underground in six chunks; chunk
  (−25, 57, −1) holds ground in all 4,096 columns, 1,839 of them underground. Screenshots `g23_base_village_{1,2}.png`
  (red: those points).
- A second village at (−138,416, 26,779), pad raised over the natural ground: 5,315 points classified open surface in
  chunks the generated test buries (the top faces and cave floors of the chunks under the raised pad).
- Not G23: the Tower at (−204,430, −46,859) showed 850 "ground" points underground, all of them the top-face row of
  layer −1 under a pad 23 uu above it, which the natural test happened to bury (G26).
- PCG: a `PCGVolume` over the Village running `PCG_VoxelScatterTest` (300 uu spacing, the sampler's edit-aware band off in
  memory, so every point is a far point): 900 cubes, a median 346 uu off the ground (p90 774): 362 more than 150 uu above
  it, 333 more than 150 uu under it. Screenshots `g23_base_village_pcg{,_side}.png`.

**What changed.**

- `FScatterExtractionContext::ConditioningZones` (was `PlanetZones`) carries the chunk's zones in every world mode, from
  `UVoxelScatterManager::SetConditioningGatherer` (was `SetPlanetConditioningGatherer`): the chunk manager gathers by the
  chunk's XY footprint on a heightmap (`GatherConditioningZonesForRegion`, what generation gathers) and by the cap its
  box subtends on a planet, as before. `FScatterExtractionContext::GetGeneratedTerrainHeight` is the natural height plus
  those zones; the column scan (`ExtractSurfacePointsFromVoxelData`), the cubic scan (`ExtractSurfacePointsCubic`) and the
  GPU path's classifier (`ClassifySurfacePointsUnderground`) compare the chunk's top with it.
- `FVoxelSurfaceQuery::SampleSurface` takes optional zones: the height, the four gradient samples and the material's
  water and height rules on the generated surface; `SampleSurfacePoint` forwards them on heightmaps; the Voxel Surface
  Sampler gathers the zones over its bounds (`UVoxelChunkManager::GatherConditioningZones`).
- Generation does not change (no `GenerationVersion` bump). Without zones every path computes exactly what it did.
- Test seams: `UVoxelScatterManager::ExtractHeightmapSurfacePoints`; `ClassifySurfacePointsUnderground` is public.

**Tests.**

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.Conditioning.CutPadAndRing` | A hillside (natural height 0.6 X) with a pad cut into it; chunks made with the generator's SDF from the generated height; every heightmap path (column scan, cubic scan, GPU classifier) over the zone's 216 chunks | 0 of 59,226 ground points underground (13,119 of them where the ground is cut below the natural height); against the natural height 6,200 in 20 chunks |
| `Scatter.Conditioning.FilledPad` | The chunk under a raised pad with a cave pocket at its top, every path | the pocket floor (49 points) and the top face (975) underground; against the natural height all open surface |
| `Scatter.Conditioning.ManagerWiring` | A cut chunk through the manager's own pipeline (`OnChunkMeshDataReady`, the context built with the gatherer) | 1,018 ground points, 0 underground; without the gatherer all 1,018 |
| `PCG.FarPointsOnConditionedSurface` | Real terrain from the CPU generator with a cut and a raised pad on a chunk manager; 72 points around each (pad, ring, beyond) with the zones the sampler gathers | within 0.4 uu of the generated isosurface (0.3 on the cut); `SampleSurfacePoint` the same; pads flat; nothing changes beyond the ring; at the natural height up to 2,867 uu off |

Each test fails on the base build's behaviour. Suites: headless VoxelWorlds + VoxelWorldSave + VoxelCharacter + WorldClock
+ InteractionPlugin + Dungeon 509 of 509 (Phase 5's 505 and the four above); in the editor (D3D12) 509 of 509 with the GPU tests running (only the two retired GPU DC interior tests skip), the 87 GPU parity lines identical to Phase 5's by CRC.

**The fixed build on `VoxelDemo`.** At the Village: 0 ground points underground (4,969 before); at the second village 0
surface points in buried chunks (5,315 before). The PCG probe's 900 far points: on the 859 under which a trace finds the
terrain, a median 0.4 uu off (p99 1.9); the three outliers stand over an opening in the pad (the trace drops 1,500 to
2,700 uu), which no analytic surface knows, and the other outliers are traces that hit the two lookout towers.
Screenshots `g23_fix_village_{1,3}.png`, `g23_fix_village_pcg{,_side}.png` (in the worktree's
`Saved/Screenshots/Claudius`, not committed). At this village the visible scatter change is small: most of the ground
that was underground is the pad's gravel and the claimed structures' area, where no grass grows either way.

**A/B against the base build.** Six runs of one script: the spawn (60 s), then `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower, the
second village and a City (−146,871, 175,956) with 45 s each, streaming frozen for a per-chunk digest and the audit.

- `voxel.Map.Capture 6` at the spawn: the same PNG, byte for byte, in all six runs. The spawn's digest: identical
  (246 chunks, 18,502 points).
- Within 200 m of the five stops, 824 chunks are in every run's digest. 15 differ between runs of the same behaviour

| Village | (−26, 57, −1), (−26, 58, −1), (−25, 56, −1) | 66 → 147, 494 → 507, 667 → 933 | the cut pad's ground is surface again (1,356, 464 and 564 ground points were underground) |
| Tower | (−46, −22, −1), (−45, −22, −1), (−45, −21, −1) | 689 → 1,110, 109 → 439, 1,426 → 1,479 | layer −1's top-face row under the pad is surface, as everywhere on natural terrain (G26) |
| Second village | (−33, −6, −1), (−33, −5, −1), (−32, −7, −1), (−32, −5, −1), (−31, −7, −1) | 96 → 85, 3,350 → 3,343, 1,095 → 513, 677 → 539, 1,231 → 1,167 | surface points inside the ground under the raised pad are underground (844, 208, 2,292, 395 and 812 of them) |

- Over every cached chunk (no distance limit, 3,547 chunk-stops), 17 differ between the behaviours: the 11 above and the
  Village's two cut chunks again, still cached at the three later stops; nothing outside a zone.

**G26 (new, open).** The column scan takes the voxel above a chunk for air, so a chunk whose top face lies within 1.5
voxels under the ground makes a row of points on that face, and the buried test's 1.5-voxel margin keeps them as
surface: a second copy of the surface scatter up to 1.5 voxels under the ground along every contour where the terrain
crosses a chunk layer's top, and under a whole pad that sits just above one (the Tower's, 2,185 points). The natural
height used to bury some of them under cut pads; with the generated height a pad behaves like natural terrain there.
A fix (drop such a crossing when the generated surface continues above the chunk, as the planet's line top does, or
narrow the margin) moves heightmap scatter along every chunk-layer contour and needs its own A/B (§14.1).

**Things to know.**

- The cubic world's voxel trees (`FVoxelTreeInjector`, generation time) still stand at the natural height in a pad or
  ring; cubic is terrain-only (D1), and fixing it would change generation (`GenerationVersion`).
- The planet scatter test and the chunk manager use the renamed API (`ConditioningZones`, `SetConditioningGatherer`);
  planets behave as before (`Scatter.Planet.*` green).

### 19.4 G26: the voxel over a heightmap chunk's top layer (2026-10-17)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#107, `fix/g26-top-face-rows`, on G23's head `c21700d`, in main since G23 merged; the
parent's gitlink and doc map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#117). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8`
in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8081), background throttling off, `DemoSmoothWorldConfig.bUseGPUScatterExtraction` set
false in memory for every run but the GPU check, never saved.

**The bug.** The voxel over a chunk's top layer is the chunk above's bottom voxel, which the chunk's own data cannot show.
The column scan (`ExtractSurfacePointsFromVoxelData`) and the cubic scan (`ExtractSurfacePointsCubic`) took it for air.
Where the ground continues into the chunk above, the chunk's top voxel and the voxel over it are both solid, yet the scan
made a crossing between them: a copy of the surface on the chunk's top face, up to 1.5 voxels under the real surface,
which the chunk above extracts. The buried-chunk test (`ChunkTop < GeneratedHeight - 1.5 * VoxelSize`) let the copy
through as open surface wherever the ground lies within 1.5 voxels over the top: along every contour where the terrain
crosses a chunk layer's top, and under a whole pad just above one. Where the ground lies inside the top voxel cell (the
crossing is the real surface), interpolating against density 0 put the point up to half a voxel low.

**The GPU path does not have it.** The GPU extraction (`ScatterSurfaceExtraction.usf` and `ClassifySurfacePointsUnderground`)
reads the chunk's interior mesh, which since seam ownership has no vertex in the cells along the chunk's boundary (they
are the seams'). Live at the Tower with GPU extraction on (the asset's setting): the chunks extracted on the GPU (LOD 0)
have no point at all in their top voxel cell, and the chunks at LOD > 0 (the CPU fallback) match the CPU run chunk for
chunk. The Tower's chunk (−46, −22, −1): 1,033 copies and 81 real crossings on the CPU path, neither on the GPU path. No
copy, but no real crossing either (G27).

**Tooling** (kept): `voxel.Scatter.TopFaceAudit [maxLines] [drawSeconds]` audits every cached scatter chunk's top-face row
(the points on its top layer: inside the top voxel cell, or on the top face in cubic) against the chunk above's
edit-merged bottom voxel over each point's column (`GetEditMergedSnapshot`):

- `under`: that voxel is solid, so the point is a copy under the ground; `underSurface` counts those classified surface (G26).
- `open`: that voxel is air (the real surface, or a cave floor).
- Whether the generated height predicted the voxel: `bandDropReal` (in the 1.5-voxel band but the voxel is air), `deepDropReal` (deeper, but air), `keepFake` (under the top, but solid).
- Spawn points on the top layer under the ground, by type (surface types / underground-only).

It logs the chunks with the most copies with a `vox.TP` to each, writes `Saved/VoxelAudit/TopFaceAudit_<world>_<time>.csv`,
and draws, in front of the terrain: the copies (magenta), the band's underground copies (blue) and the surface spawns under
the ground (white).

**Reproduction.** The fixed build had a temporary switch that restored the old behaviour (`voxel.Scatter.G26Legacy 1`),
removed before the commit. With the switch on, G23's audit counted exactly G23's 2,185 at the Tower. The A/B below shows
the switch's runs equal the G23 build's own runs.

- At the Tower (−204,430, −46,859), over the 230 cached surface chunks: 9,326 copies classified surface, carrying 2,552
  spawn points of surface types under the ground. All are in layer −1 (top Z 0, the demo's lowland), in 37 chunks. The
  Tower's chunk alone has 1,033 copies and 681 surface spawns under the ground. Screenshots `g26_legacy_{pad,wide,top}.png`
  (in the worktree's `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius`, not committed) show the pad filled with copies and their spawns, and
  the copies following the Z 0 contour over the hills.
- Every A/B stop has copies, natural terrain included: the spawn 3,144 copies (271 surface spawns under the ground), the
  Village 7,298 (2,035), the Tower 9,250 (2,258), the second village 11,056 (1,515), the City 8,594 (349).
- `bandDropReal` was 0 at every stop. Inside the band the generated height never calls the voxel above solid where it is
  air (no cave, edit or dungeon reaches it in the demo), so the rule below loses no real crossing.
- `deepDropReal` was 2,743 to 8,522: under deeper ground the voxel above is air at real cave floors on a chunk boundary.
  That is why the rule stops at the band.
- `keepFake` was 7 to 36: the generated height a fraction of a uu under the top while its voxel is solid. This is the
  signed distance's rounding (solid from 0.29 uu under the sample). The rule reads the voxel's own density, so it drops
  these too.

**What changed.**

- `FScatterExtractionContext::GetVoxelAboveChunk` returns the voxel over a chunk's top layer as the heightmap generator
  makes it (`SignedDistanceToDensity` of the generated height at the chunk's top), with the chunk above's edit there
  applied. `FScatterExtractionContext::AboveLayerEdits` holds that chunk's edits on its bottom layer, copied by
  `UVoxelScatterManager::MakeExtractionContext` from the chunk manager's edit layers (`SetEditLayerSource`).
- The column scan reads that voxel where the generated ground lies at most 1.5 voxels over the chunk's top (the band the
  buried test lets through):
  - solid: the top voxel is no surface and is dropped, and the rest of the column is covered (lower crossings underground, as before);
  - air: the crossing interpolates against its density, as the mesher does, and the point lands on the surface (before, up to half a voxel low);
  - deeper than the band, the buried test covers the column and a cave can open the voxel above, so it is still taken for air.
- The cubic scan makes the same decision for the block over the top layer (sampled at the column's corner), with the band
  judged at the corner or at the block's centre (the buried test's height).
- The GPU path, planets and generation do not change; no `GenerationVersion` bump.

Edits: the analytic height alone is edit-blind. A live player edit only clears scatter (cleared volumes, nothing regrows
until the chunk reloads). On reload the extraction reads the chunk's edit-merged voxels and, now, the chunk above's
bottom-layer edits. A dig through the chunk above's bottom layer exposes the lower chunk's top face, which is open
surface again; a build over a top face that was the surface covers it. Both are tested. Deeper digs keep the buried
test's edit-blindness, as before: a floor dug more than 1.5 voxels under the generated ground stays underground.

**Tests.**

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.TopFace.Contour` | Planes rising and falling through a chunk layer's top (inside the lower chunk, its top cell, the band, past it; on the falling one a column's corner lies 3 uu past the band and its centre 3 uu inside), every heightmap path over the lower chunk and the one above | Every column has exactly one open point, on the surface (0.00 uu off), and the lower chunk's top layer has no point under the band's ground. Taking the voxel above for air makes 384 copies (12 columns × 32) |
| `Scatter.TopFace.FlatGround` | Flat ground from 0.9 voxels under the top to 3 voxels over it, every path | One open point per column, 0.00 uu off; the top cell's crossing 0.00 uu off, against 42.3 uu low with an assumed-air voxel |
| `Scatter.TopFace.EditsAbove` | The chunk above's bottom layer dug over a patch (ground in the band) and built over a patch (ground in the top cell), every path; the manager's own pipeline with and without the edit layer source | Dug: the exposed top face is open surface (64 of 64 columns), none without the edits. Built: one open point (the build's top), two without the edits. Pipeline: 64 with the source, 0 without |

Each test fails on the old behaviour. Suites: headless VoxelWorlds + VoxelWorldSave + VoxelCharacter + WorldClock + InteractionPlugin + Dungeon 512 of 512
(G23's 509 and the three above); in the editor (D3D12) 512 of 512 with the GPU tests running (only the two retired GPU DC
interior tests skip), the 87 GPU parity lines identical to G23's by CRC.

**The fixed build on `VoxelDemo`.** At the Tower: 0 copies (9,326 before), 0 surface spawns under the ground (2,552), and
G23's audit `edge` 0 (2,185). Screenshots `g26_fixed_{1,2,3}.png`.

**A/B against the G23 behaviour.** Six runs of one script, three per behaviour, interleaved, all in the fixed build: the
switch on for the old behaviour, off for the new. Each run: the spawn (60 s), then `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower, the
second village and the City with 45 s each, and at each stop streaming frozen for the per-chunk digest and both audits.

- `voxel.Map.Capture 6` at the spawn: the same PNG, byte for byte, in all six runs.
- The switch is the G23 build: the old-behaviour runs equal the G23 session's three fixed runs (§19.3) on all 809 chunk-stops
  stable in both.
- Within 200 m of the five stops, 788 chunk-stops are in every run. 16 differ between runs of one behaviour (capture
  timing, as in §19.3). Of the 772 stable ones, 61 differ between the behaviours: 60 whose top-face row had copies, and
  one, (−2, −10, −1) near the spawn, whose row had only real crossings in the top cell (they moved onto the surface; 1,239
  → 1,236 spawn points). None for any other reason.

| Stop | Stable / changed chunks | Spawn points in the stable chunks (old → new) |
|------|------|------|
| Spawn (natural terrain) | 173 / 8 | 15,834 → 15,563 |
| Village | 143 / 16 | 51,569 → 49,487 |
| Tower | 148 / 11 | 49,296 → 47,036 (its chunk 1,110 → 429) |
| Second village | 151 / 19 | 32,946 → 31,445 |
| City | 157 / 7 | 32,908 → 32,607 |

- The 61 changed chunks lose 6,415 spawn points, and the audit counted 6,360 surface spawns under the ground in them: the
  change is the scatter that stood on the copies. The rest comes from the audit's spawn test, which takes the nearest
  column, and from the moved real crossings.
- Rows that did not change: of the 247 chunks whose top-face row had only real crossings, 243 had only deep ones (cave
  floors under deeper ground, unchanged by design). 43 chunks with copies kept the same digest because no spawn stood on a
  copy.

**G27 (new, open).** The GPU path never had the copy, but it has no point at all in a chunk's boundary cells, real
crossings included. That is a strip without scatter wherever the surface crosses a chunk's top cell (and presumably its
side cells, not measured) at LOD 0 with GPU extraction on, the demo asset's setting. To measure, then extract the chunk's
owned seams too, or keep extraction on the CPU (GPU extraction is also nondeterministic).

**G28 (new, open, low).** Under ground more than 1.5 voxels over a chunk's top, the voxel above is still taken for air (a
cave can open it there, so the generated height cannot decide), so a buried chunk's whole top face carries underground
copies inside the rock. Around the Tower: 374,928 points in 223 chunks, on which underground-only scatter puts 306 spawn
points (inside the rock: invisible unless a cave floor lies just above). 1.5% of those crossings are real (5,736). The
voxel above could be decided with the cave carve there (analytic) or with the chunk above's own data. Fixed in §20.21 (the cave carve).

**G29 (new, open): planets.** The brief named the planet's line top (`ExtractSurfacePointsAlongUp`) as the model rule. It
drops a crossing whose voxel above lies outside the chunk only when the crossing is more than 1.5 voxels off the analytic
surface, and otherwise puts it on that surface. So where the ground continues up to about a voxel into the chunk the line
came from, both chunks make the point: no sunken copy, but two points on the surface. A temporary probe (not committed)
over the planet scatter tests' 27-chunk sites counted 605 (45°), 676 (equator) and 325 (cube corner) pairs of open points
from different chunks within half a voxel, 3 to 7% of the open points, and none at the pole. The same voxel-above
decision would fix it; it changes planet scatter, so it needs its own `Review_Planet` A/B. Fixed in §19.6.

### 19.5 G27: scatter reads voxels only; GPU scatter extraction retired (2026-10-18)

draquel/VoxelWorlds#108 (`fix/g27-gpu-scatter-boundary`, on main `8edb23b` after G26 merged); the parent's gitlink and doc
map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#118. Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor
(Claudius on 8081), background throttling off. `DemoSmoothWorldConfig.bUseGPUScatterExtraction` is true in the asset; the base-build runs set
it in memory (true for the GPU runs, false for the CPU run), never saved; the fixed build's runs left the asset as it is.

**The bug.** With `bUseGPUScatterExtraction` (the demo asset's setting) a chunk meshed at LOD 0 took its surface points
from its mesh on the GPU (`FVoxelGPUSurfaceExtractor`, `ScatterSurfaceExtraction.usf`: the first vertex in each 50 uu
world cell), then had them classified against its voxels (`ClassifySurfacePointsUnderground`). The mesh handed to scatter
is the chunk's interior mesh. Since seam ownership (`Research/SEAM_OWNERSHIP_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1) that mesh holds the
cells 0 to ChunkSize - 2 on each axis; the cell layer against each max face (+X, +Y, +Z) belongs to the chunk's seams.
So every chunk the GPU extracted had no point in those three layers, real crossings included. The column scan reads
voxels and covers every cell layer.

**Tooling** (kept): `voxel.Scatter.BoundaryAudit [maxLines] [drawSeconds]` audits how every cached scatter chunk's points
cover the cell layers along its six faces, against the edit-merged voxels of the chunk and its +X, +Y and +Z neighbours.
For each face it compares the boundary layer (local cell 0 on a min face, ChunkSize - 1 on a max face) with the layer next
to it: floor cells (one of the cell's four vertical edges goes from solid below to air above, the crossing scatter
extracts), points in them, spawn points of surface types, and the ratio of points per floor cell. A gap face has 8 or
more floor cells and no point; a strip chunk has every max face with floor a gap (the GPU path's signature). It logs a
summary per face and the chunks with the most floor cells on gap faces with a `vox.TP` to each, writes
`Saved/VoxelAudit/BoundaryAudit_<world>_<time>.csv`, and draws those cells red. (A first version counted every cell with a
sign change and every point: G28's copies inside the rock then inflated the +Z layer, and wide flat cavity ceilings at about
Z 0 (Things to know, below) read as gaps a column scan never fills.)

**Measured on the base build** (G26's head with the audit), the A/B route of §19.4 (the spawn after 60 s, then `vox.TP` to
the Village, the Tower, the second village and the City with 45 s each, streaming frozen at each stop for the digest and
the audits), two runs with GPU extraction on and one with it off:

- 11 to 18 chunks per stop of about 160 were extracted on the GPU, the chunks meshed at LOD 0 when they first came into
  the scatter radius: around where the player spawns or teleports. Walking, chunks enter the 250 m radius at LOD 1 or 2
  and took the CPU path. Every GPU-extracted chunk is a strip chunk: point ratio 0.00 on +X, +Y and +Z, 0.92 to 1.09 on -X
  and -Y. The CPU-extracted chunks: 0.98 to 1.02 on every side face.
- A second defect: the extractor's output buffer held 4,096 points (sized for 32³ chunks). The demo's 64³ chunks
  overflowed it in 60 of 75 GPU extractions (run 2), and which points were dropped depended on GPU thread order; some
  strip chunks lost whole min-face layers too.
- The same chunks, GPU run against CPU run: 38,272 against 55,503 spawn points (-31%).
- Visible: bare bands in the grass along the +X and +Y chunk borders and along the contour where the terrain crosses a
  chunk layer's top (Z 0 in the demo's lowland). Screenshots at the Tower (in the worktree's `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius`,
  not committed): `g27_tower_obl3.png` (GPU) and `g27_tcpu_obl3.png` (CPU, the same camera: denser, continuous),
  `g27_tower_obl3_red.png` and `g27_tower_top_red.png` with the gap cells drawn.
- Cost (a temporary timing log, not committed): the CPU extraction 3.7 ms mean, 5.9 ms P95 per 64³ chunk on a worker
  (1,180 chunks); the GPU path 31 ms from dispatch to result, a synchronous readback on the render thread (each chunk's
  three graphs lock their staging buffers right after `Execute`), then 1.8 ms to classify and place on a worker.

**Decision D25** (§8, the user, 2026-10-18): retire GPU scatter extraction, as GPU DC interior meshing was: keeping it
would mean feeding it each chunk's owned seam meshes (which depend on the neighbours and rebuild on LOD changes) and a
dynamic output buffer, for a path that stays nondeterministic and makes a different point set from the column scan that
extracts about 90% of chunks.

**What changed.**

- `UVoxelScatterManager` extracts every chunk from its voxels on the thread pool (the column scan, the cubic scan or, on
  a planet, the scan along local up). Deleted: the GPU branch of `LaunchAsyncScatterGeneration`,
  `ProcessCompletedGPUExtractions` and its queue and maps, `ClassifySurfacePointsUnderground`, `WantsGPUExtraction`, the
  mesh arrays in `FPendingScatterGeneration`; `FVoxelGPUSurfaceExtractor` and `ScatterSurfaceExtraction.usf`
  (VoxelMeshing); the uncalled mesh-vertex path `GenerateChunkScatter` and `FVoxelSurfaceExtractor`.
- `OnChunkMeshDataReady(ChunkCoord, VoxelData, ChunkSize, VoxelSize)`: the LOD and the mesh are no longer passed. The chunk
  manager's hand-off is otherwise unchanged (edit-merged voxels, before the renderer submit).
- `bUseGPUScatterExtraction` stays so assets load, marked deprecated (`AdvancedDisplay`, `DeprecatedProperty`) and
  ignored; the scatter manager logs once at initialisation when it is set. The bench report's `run.gpuScatterExtraction`
  is now `run.gpuScatterExtractionConfigured`.
- Generation, meshing and the CPU extractors do not change; no `GenerationVersion` bump.
- Docs: `SCATTER_SYSTEM.md` (architecture, the retired paths), `UNDERGROUND_CLASSIFICATION.md` (classification is the
  extractors'), `PERFORMANCE_TARGETS.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PHASES.md` (7D-2 retired).

**Tests.**

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.Boundary.EveryCellLayerCovered` | A plane tilted along X and Y (0.13, 0.11) through 3 × 3 × 2 chunks, crossing the two layers' shared plane; every chunk through the column scan with the world mode in the context | 2,304 of 2,304 columns with exactly one open point, at most 0.37 uu off the plane; every boundary layer holds the points of every column whose surface lies in it (144 on each side face, 133 on -Z, 203 on +Z) |
| `Scatter.Boundary.ManagerIgnoresGPUFlag` | A slope through one chunk through the manager's own pipeline, with `bUseGPUScatterExtraction` set and without, and a second manager with it set | 256 points each, the same point for point; 16 points in the +X boundary column and 16 in the +Y one |

The G23 and G26 tests (`Scatter.Conditioning.*`, `Scatter.TopFace.*`) lose their "GPU classifier" path with the function
it ran; `Scatter.Cubic.CPUExtractionOnly` loses its `WantsGPUExtraction` checks and keeps the cubic chunk with no
interior mesh, now with the flag set. Suites: headless VoxelWorlds + VoxelWorldSave + VoxelCharacter + WorldClock +
InteractionPlugin + Dungeon 514 of 514 (G26's 512 and the two above); in the editor (D3D12) 514 of 514 with the GPU
tests running (only the two retired GPU DC interior tests skip), the 87 GPU parity lines identical to G26's by CRC.

**The fixed build on `VoxelDemo`**, the asset as it is (the flag set): no gap face and no strip chunk at any stop of the
three A/B runs (15 audits of 221 to 249 surface chunks; 11 to 18 strip chunks per stop with GPU extraction on).
Screenshot `g27_tfix_obl3.png` (the Tower camera above): the same grass as the CPU run from that camera
(`g27_tcpu_obl3.png`), no bare bands.

**A/B.** Three runs of the §19.4 route on the fixed build with the asset as it is (the flag set), against the base build
with GPU extraction on (two runs) and against the CPU behaviour (the base build's run with it off and G26's three fixed
runs, the same behaviour in the G26 build, which differs from the base build only by the audit command).

- Against the CPU behaviour: within 200 m of the five stops, 788 chunk-stops are in every run. 4 differ between the fixed
  runs and 5 between the CPU runs (capture timing, as in §19.3). Of the 780 stable in both, none differs: the flag no
  longer changes anything.
- Against GPU extraction on: of the 526 and 527 chunk-stops stable in the fixed runs and present in each GPU run, 59 and 61
  differ. 58 and 60 are strip chunks in that run's audit. The other is the Village's (-24, 56, 0) in both runs (77 → 69
  spawn points), which has no floor on its max faces, so the audit cannot call it a strip chunk; its CRC differs between
  the two GPU runs, as a GPU extraction's does. Nothing else differs.
- Spawn points over the stable chunks: 160,297 and 158,614 with GPU extraction on, 178,365 fixed; over the strip chunks
  that differ, 42,735 → 60,811 and 45,107 → 64,866 (+42% and +44%).

**G30 (new, open).** `UVoxelScatterManager::RemoveChunkScatter` (on unload) clears the chunk's caches with
`SurfaceDataCache.Remove(...) > 0 || ScatterDataCache.Remove(...) > 0`: when the surface cache held the chunk, the
short-circuit skips the scatter cache, so the chunk's spawn points stay cached after it unloads. When it streams back in,
its extraction is taken for a supplemental pass: the new spawn points are appended to the stale ones and its surface data
is not cached again (the distance spawn and the audits then skip it). Found by `Scatter.Boundary.ManagerIgnoresGPUFlag`'s
first version (resubmitting a chunk after `OnChunkUnloaded` left no surface data); the test now uses a fresh manager.
Not fixed here: it changes what a reloaded chunk renders and needs its own check. Fixed in §19.7.

**Things to know.**

- Near every stop the audit's first version found wide flat ceilings at about Z 0, the chunk layers' shared plane: under
  hills whose ground lies around Z 1,350, the layer below's top voxels are air and the layer above's bottom voxels solid
  (in chunk (-45, -24, 0) near the Tower, 1,700 such cells). Scatter rightly puts no point on a ceiling. Whether a cavity
  that flat and that exactly on a layer boundary is meant (the cave configuration) was not checked.

### 19.6 G29: a planet chunk's line top reads the neighbour's voxel (2026-10-18)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#109, `fix/g29-planet-line-top`, on main `7f60551` after G26 and G27 merged; the parent's
gitlink and doc map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#119). The work and the live runs were on G26's head `bc085d6`; rebased
onto G27, which leaves planet extraction as it was (planets never extracted on the GPU), the suites ran again (below).
Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8083), background
throttling off. Live runs on
`PlanetTest` with `/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride` (R 250,000, chunk 64, voxel 75,
water 249,500, shell ±6,500, GPU generation); planets extract scatter on the CPU.

**The bug.** A planet chunk's scatter lines (`ExtractSurfacePointsAlongUp`) step along the axis nearest local up and
drift sideways with the up's slope. At a line top whose voxel above lies outside the chunk (over the upper face, or on a
side the line drifts in through) the chunk's data cannot show that voxel. The old rule kept the crossing whenever its
interpolation against an assumed-air voxel lay within 1.5 voxels of the analytic surface, and put it on that surface.
Where the ground continues into the neighbour, that voxel is solid and the neighbour makes the point itself, so along
every band where the surface crosses a chunk face the surface got two points (on it, not sunken like G26's copies).

**Reproduction.**

- The tests' 27-chunk sites (the CPU generator, R 250,000, voxel 75, chunk 32): pairs of open points from two chunks on
  one up-line (closer than half a voxel across local up, within two voxels along it), with a temporary switch for the
  old rule: 0 at the north pole, 374 at the south pole, 605 at 45°, 676 at the equator and 325 at the cube corner. The
  last three are the §19.4 probe's numbers exactly. The probe reported none "at the pole": the north pole has none (its
  surface crosses no chunk face in the band inside the 27 chunks), the south pole has 374.
- `Review_Planet`, five stops (`voxel.Scatter.LineTopAudit`, below): 4,147 pairs at the spawn (86.7°N), 10,807 at 45°N
  0°E, 5,275 at the equator (0°, 90°E), 10,961 near the cube corner (36.8°N 43.1°E, where `vox.TPLatLon 35.264 45` settles)
  and 8,080 at 59.9°S 115.6°W: 2.3 to 4.6% of the open points take part in a pair.

**What changed.**

- `FScatterExtractionContext::GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk` returns a voxel just outside the chunk as
  `GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet` makes it: the generated altitude along its direction (the context's conditioning zones
  applied), the shell's signed distance to it, `SignedDistanceToDensity`. The neighbour's edit there is applied on top
  (`FScatterExtractionContext::TouchingEdits`, keyed by the voxel's coordinate in the chunk's frame, gathered by
  `UVoxelScatterManager::GatherPlanetTouchingEdits` from the chunk manager's edit layers, `SetEditLayerSource` as G26).
- The neighbours it reads (`UVoxelScatterManager::GetPlanetLineTopNeighbours`): over the upper face, and its edges and
  corner where a line's step before its first voxel is shifted; the sides the lines drift in through and their edge. One
  at the poles and the equator, three at 30°, seven at a cube corner.
- Within the band (the 1.5-voxel check is unchanged): a solid voxel above drops the line top and covers the rest of the
  line, as the neighbour makes the point; an air one keeps it on the generated surface, as before, or interpolated
  against the voxel where an edit changed it. Outside the band nothing changed (a cave can open that voxel there).
- The voxel above a line's first voxel is now the line's own step before it (shifted sideways by its slope), where it
  was the voxel straight over it along the stepping axis. Before, that voxel only seeded the snap onto the surface; now
  it decides. Taken straight over, it dropped real line tops wherever the lines drift half a voxel a step or more: strips
  without points along the upper faces at 45° (412 of 10,803 samples under 0.8 in the local density below), and more at
  every site with a steep slope (the table below).
- Heightmap paths, generation and the GPU path are unchanged; no `PlanetGenerationVersion` change (scatter only).

**Tooling** (kept): `voxel.Scatter.LineTopAudit [maxLines] [drawSeconds] [densityRadius]` counts, over every cached scatter
chunk's open points, the pairs from two chunks on one up-line, logs the chunks with the most and a `vox.TP` to each,
writes `Saved/VoxelAudit/LineTopAudit_<world>_<time>.csv` (open points and pairs per chunk) and draws the paired points.
With a radius it also measures the open points' local density on the generated surface around the pawn: at samples every
half voxel, the spawn weights under a Gaussian of one voxel across local up, per the column scan's one point per voxel
square. A kernel as wide as the lines' spacing is flat over any regular sampling (a disc count of 1.5 voxels is not: a
square lattice gives 0.57 to 1.27 by where the sample falls), so a doubled strip shows as samples over 1.2 and a strip
without points as samples under 0.8. The tests use the same measure.

**Tests.**

The old rule's decision (an all-air touching layer) as the sensitive case | Pairs 0, 0, 0, 0 and 3 (the corner, G31); over 1.2: 0 everywhere; under 0.8: 0, and 398 at the corner. The all-air layer: 1,793 pairs and 2,786 samples over 1.2 over the sites |

The all-air layer: every column has two at 0.3, 0.7 and 1.0 voxels over the face |

With the temporary switch on (the old rule) all three fail. `Scatter.Planet.DensityPerArea` stays within its 10%: the

  spawn 372 / 7,679 → 372 / 79; 45°N 3,934 / 4,822 → 4,175 / 128; equator 288 / 3,345 → 288 / 0; corner 3,598 / 1,802 →

  points grow by 1,788, most of it at the south stop, whose slopes (0.25 and 0.53 voxels a step) are G31's worst case.
  With the voxel straight over a line's first voxel (one more pass, the switch's third setting) the gaps are larger at
  45° (5,259) and at the corner (6,048): 15,191 bad samples against 11,891 as built and 30,597 under the old rule. The
  372 at the spawn and 288 at the equator under 0.8 are the same in every behaviour, so not the lines'.

**G31 (new; fixed in §19.9).** Each planet chunk takes its lines' stepping axis and slope from local up at its own centre, so
neighbouring chunks' lines do not continue into each other: across the cube's diagonals they step along different axes,
and everywhere their drift rounds differently where the slope differs between the two centres (most where it is near
half a voxel a step). At such a face a line top whose ground continues into the neighbour is dropped (correctly by its own
line) while the neighbour's lines pass that spot with their crossing on this side of the face, so a strip gets no point;
rarely both chunks make it (the 3 residual pairs at the test corner: in each, one point is an interior crossing of one
chunk's lines and the other a line top that found air over it). The old rule's doubles had covered most of these strips:
`Scatter.Planet.DensityPerArea`'s corner read 99.7% with them and 96.5% without. A fix would give a crossing to the chunk
that contains it (each chunk keeping the crossings of its own lines that lie inside it, and reading the voxels just past
its faces as G29 does), or share one line family across a region.

### 19.7 G30: an unloaded chunk's scatter stays cached (2026-10-18)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#111, `fix/g30-scatter-cache-reload`, on main `cfd94c7`; the parent's gitlink and doc map
in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#121). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor
(Claudius on 8085), background throttling off.

**The bug.** `UVoxelScatterManager::RemoveChunkScatter` (called by `OnChunkUnloaded`) removed the chunk's caches with
`SurfaceDataCache.Remove(...) > 0 || ScatterDataCache.Remove(...) > 0`. A chunk with surface data (every chunk scatter
had extracted) kept its spawn points cached after it unloaded. What followed:

- **The reload was an append.** When the chunk streamed back in, `ProcessCompletedAsyncScatter` found its spawn points
  cached and took the extraction for a supplemental pass: the new spawn points were appended to the stale ones (every
  point twice) and the surface data was not cached again.
- **No surface data afterwards.** The distance spawn (which reads the surface cache) never added the distance-limited
  types there again, the exclusion regrow skipped it, and the audits (`voxel.Scatter.*Audit`, which skip a chunk without
  surface data) did not see it.
- **Rendered twice on the next re-render.** The unload had released the chunk's instances and the append rendered only
  the new points, so the chunk looked right until something re-rendered it from the cache: a cleared radius (a dig), an
  exclusion volume (a harvest, a claim), each of which replaces a type's instances with the cached survivors, two per
  point.
- **Alternating.** At its next unload the chunk had no surface data, so the `||` reached the scatter cache and removed
  it; the following reload was right again, the one after that doubled.
- **Leaked.** Every chunk unloaded with surface data stayed in the scatter cache until it was reloaded and unloaded again:
  `GetScatterChunkCount`, `ComputeScatterDigest`, the audits' chunk lists and the scatter memory the streaming bench
  reports (`peakScatterMB` / `endScatterMB`, from `GetTotalMemoryUsage`) included them.

**A second way a chunk rendered twice** (found while checking what a reloaded chunk renders).
`UVoxelScatterRenderer::ReleaseChunkScatterType`, which the distance spawn's out-of-range cleanup calls, released the
chunk's instances of a type but left its adds still queued for the per-frame budget. Flushed after the release, they
landed in the pool for a type the chunk no longer tracked, and `RemoveChunkInstances` (the unload) releases only the
tracked types: those instances stayed in the world across the unload, and when the chunk came back the type was added
again over them. (`UpdateChunkTypeInstances` and `RemoveChunkInstances` drop the queued adds themselves; the cleanup
was the one caller that did not.)

Live (`VoxelDemo`, the runs below): at 14 of 36 `vox.TP` stops (six runs), one to three chunks 137 to 234 m from the
stop had taken distance-limited types (`SpawnDistance` 10,000 and 12,000 uu) in their first pass: they were submitted
while the viewer (the camera) was still within 100 m of them, not yet at the stop. The next distance check released
those types while their adds still waited behind the arrival's backlog (about 50,000 adds at 2,000 a frame). Where the
chunk kept other types (its trees), the adds were then flushed untracked: 351 to 902 instances over the chunk's 12 to 30
spawn points, in two of the six runs with the cache fix alone. The Tower's (-44, -17, 0) held 371 such bush, grass,
plant, flower and young spruce instances, and the same 371 were there at the next visit to the Tower, after the chunk had
unloaded and come back.

**What changed.**

- `RemoveChunkScatter` removes both caches.
- `OnChunkUnloaded` also drops a queued exclusion regrow (the reload's first pass reads the current volumes), so an
  unloaded chunk keeps no scatter state at all.
- `ReleaseChunkScatterType` drops the queued adds for the chunk and type.
- Tooling (kept): `voxel.Scatter.Digest` logs a second line, `caches:` (`UVoxelScatterManager::ComputeCacheResidency`):
  chunks with spawn points, chunks with surface data, chunks with spawn points but no surface data (`scatterOnly`, 0 since
  the fix), spawn points against the renderer's instances (`UVoxelScatterRenderer::GetChunkInstanceCount`, queued adds
  included) with the chunks where they differ (`instanceMismatch`; up to five logged per type, `<id>:<spawn
  points>/<instances>`, `!` where the renderer does not track the type; `file` writes all to
  `Saved/VoxelAudit/ScatterCaches_<world>_<time>.csv`), and spawn points that repeat another of their chunk
  (`duplicates`). `UVoxelScatterManager::GetScatterRenderer`, `UVoxelScatterRenderer::GetChunkScatterTypes`.
- Checked, unchanged: supplemental passes (a deferred one is dropped on unload; a reload is now a first pass); the
  distance spawn (reads the surface cache, which the reload fills again); stale in-flight results (an extraction's is
  dropped through `AsyncScatterInProgress`, a distance stream's through the surface-cache check, which an unloaded chunk
  fails until its reload has been extracted, long after a placement-only task finishes); `RegenerateChunkScatter` (an
  edit) already dropped both caches; the audits, the digest and the stats iterate the scatter cache and now see every
  loaded chunk and no unloaded one.
- Generation, extraction and placement do not change; no `GenerationVersion` or `PlanetGenerationVersion` bump.

**Tests** (`Source/VoxelScatter/Tests/VoxelScatterReloadTests.cpp`, through the scatter manager's own pipeline as the
G27 and G26 harnesses: `OnChunkMeshDataReady`, the async extraction, `Update`; a tilted heightmap plane of grass with
every third column dirt; the default definitions given the engine cube so the renderer holds real instances, trees at
density 0.3):

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.Reload.SameAsFresh` | Four chunks; one unloads and reloads three times. After each unload no cache and no instance holds it and no chunk has spawn points without surface data; after each reload its surface data is cached and equals the first extraction's, its spawn points equal the first load's (no duplicate), it renders each once, and the digest equals the first load's, chunk by chunk. Then a cleared radius on the reloaded chunk against a manager that never unloaded it | 256 surface points, 136 spawn points (57 trees), 136 instances, the digest `types=3 chunks=4 points=547` at every cycle; after the cleared radius 118 spawn points and 118 instances on both |
| `Scatter.Reload.DistanceSpawn` | The chunk loads with the viewer 40,000 uu off (past the trees' 20,000 and their release at 22,000), the viewer comes near, goes away, the chunk unloads and reloads far away, the viewer comes near again | 83 spawn points far, 126 with 43 trees near, 83 again far; after the reload 83 far and 126 with 43 trees near, the same points; one instance per point at every stop |
| `Scatter.Reload.ReleaseBeforeFlush` | The viewer moves away before the extraction's result is taken, with every `Update` running the distance check, so the trees are queued and released in the same `Update`; then the chunk unloads and reloads near | No tree instance after the release, none of the chunk after the unload, 126 instances for 126 spawn points after the reload |

With the temporary switch (`voxel.Scatter.G30Legacy`, removed before the commit) at 1, the old code, all three fail:
after an unload the chunk's 136 spawn points stay cached (`scatterOnly=1`); the reload holds 272 spawn points (136
unique), no surface data and 136 instances, and the digest says `points=683`; cycle 2 is right again and cycle 3
doubled (the alternation); after the cleared radius the reloaded chunk renders 236 instances where the other renders
118; reloaded far away the chunk has 166 spawn points and no surface data, and near it gets no tree. At 2 (only the old
release) `ReleaseBeforeFlush` alone fails: 43 tree instances with no tree spawn point after the release, still there
after the unload, and 169 instances for 126 spawn points after the reload. The G27 test
`Scatter.Boundary.ManagerIgnoresGPUFlag` keeps a fresh manager per run (its point is determinism across managers); its
comment now points here. Suites: headless VoxelWorlds + VoxelWorldSave + VoxelCharacter + WorldClock
+ InteractionPlugin + Dungeon 520 of 520 (main's 517 and the three above); in the editor (D3D12) 520 of 520 with the GPU
tests running (only the two retired GPU DC interior tests skip), the 87 GPU parity lines identical to G29's by CRC.

**Live: `VoxelDemo`.** A round trip: the spawn (60 s), then `vox.TP` to the Village (-104312, 331034), the Tower
(-204430, -46859) and the City (-146871, 175956), then the same three again, 60 s at each stop; at each, streaming frozen
for `voxel.Scatter.Digest file` (the per-chunk digest and the `caches:` line). The stops are 1.6 to 3.9 km apart and the
view distance 400 m (chunks 4,800 uu), so every stop's chunks unload before its second visit. A throwaway run first;
then three runs on the old code (the temporary switch at 1) interleaved with three on the cache fix alone, three more
on the cache fix alone with a temporary log of releases with queued adds (the second bug's evidence above), and three
on the fix.

- **Round trip on the fix**: over the chunks stable in every run of one build (the same digest line in all three) at
  both visits, none differs between the first and the second visit: 245 at the Village, 215 at the Tower, 230 at the
  City (46,605, 47,357 and 31,333 spawn points both times). Every stop of every run: `scatterOnly=0`, `instanceMismatch=0`,
  `duplicates=0`; the chunk count stays 223 to 249. (The cache fix alone gives the same round trip on its stable chunks;
  its `instanceMismatch` was the second bug.)
- **Round trip on the old code**: of the chunks loaded at both visits and stable, 69, 77 and 75 have spawn points; 43, 57
  and 57 of them come back with exactly twice their points (8,114 → 16,228 at the Village), 10, 7 and 8 with a few more
  (up to 2.5%). At the second visits no loaded chunk has surface data (`surfaceChunks` 0 to 7 of 480 to 952).
- **The leak on the old code**: the chunks of every stop left behind stay cached: 246 after the spawn, about 495 at the
  Village, 718 at the Tower, 950 at the City, where 64,094 to 82,957 spawn points are cached against about 36,000
  rendered; `instanceMismatch` 49 to 262 per stop.
- **First visits** equal on both builds: 247, 215 and 230 stable chunks in both, none differs (the old code's extra
  chunks are the unloaded ones).
- Run-to-run variance, both builds: a few chunks near the villages and the City (for instance (-25, 55, 0): 2,980 or
  2,203 spawn points) differ between runs at both visits alike, so they are not stable and not counted; earlier A/Bs
  reported the same capture timing (§19.3, §19.5).

**Live: `Review_Planet`** (`PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride /Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet`; R 250,000,
chunk 64, voxel 75, the demo's scatter configuration). The same round trip with `vox.TPLatLon`: the spawn (86.7°N), then
45°N 0°E, 0° 90°E and 60°S 120°W (which settles at 59.9°S 115.6°W), then the same three again, 60 s each; the stops are
3.9 to 6.2 km apart along the surface. A throwaway run, then three on the fix and three on the old code (the temporary
switch at 1), interleaved.

- **Round trip on the fix**: 183, 172 and 182 chunks are stable at both visits. Clear of the distance spawn's bands
  (within 100 uu of a `SpawnDistance`, 10,000 or 12,000 uu from the stop, or between it and 1.1 times it, where the
  distance spawn neither adds nor releases; or within 500 uu of the 25,000 uu scatter radius) none differs: 148, 148 and
  157 chunks. In the bands 3 of 35 differ at 45°N and 4 of 25 at the south stop, each the same way in all three runs and
  on the old code: which types such a chunk holds depends on where the viewer was when it was submitted (for instance
  (-10, -23, -47), 12,094 uu from the south stop: 4 spawn points at the first visit, 2,492 at the second; the old code
  has 4 and 2,496, the stale 4 plus the same 2,492). Every stop of every run: `scatterOnly=0`, `instanceMismatch=0`,
  `duplicates=0`.
- **Round trip on the old code**: of the chunks loaded at both visits and stable, 45, 37 and 67 have spawn points; 37, 31
  and 61 of them come back exactly doubled (5,231 → 10,462 at 45°N, 6,446 → 12,892 at the south stop). The second visits
  hold 426 to 27,230 duplicate spawn points (in 41 to 76 chunks) and 1 to 5 chunks with surface data; the stale chunks
  grow from 155 after the spawn to 704 at the third stop.
- **First visits** equal on both builds: 184, 177 and 186 stable chunks in both, none differs.

**Things to know.**

- A chunk submitted in the seconds after a teleport can take its definitions with the viewer (the camera's position, as
  the chunk manager passes it) not yet at the destination: chunks 137 to 234 m from a `vox.TP` stop took the 100 m and
  120 m types and released them at the next distance check. The release is right; only that first pass's work is wasted.

### 19.8 G24: voxel-carved dungeons hold pawns (2026-10-18)

PRs open: draquel/ProceduralDungeonPlugin#30 (`fix/g24-voxel-carved-floors`: the stamp and its tests), this section in
draquel/VoxelWorlds#110 (`docs/g24-voxel-carved-floors`, docs only) and draquel/UE5_PluginDev#120 (`claude/g24-voxel-carved-dungeon-floors`: VoxelWorldPOI, the
game module's `vox.TPRoom`, the gitlinks and the doc map), all on main (VoxelWorlds `cfd94c7`, UE5_PluginDev `89f0455`).
Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8084), background
throttling off. Live runs on `VoxelDemo` with its `DA_POIType_DungeonTiled` switched to `VoxelCarved` in memory (never
saved), and on `PlanetTest` with `/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride`, the same switch.

**The bug.** Two causes, neither in meshing or collision cooking, and neither particular to smooth worlds:

1. *The lining filled the rooms.* `CarveUnderground` lined every closed face from inside its cell (`PlaceBoundary`),
   `WallThickness` voxels deep. The demo's voxel config (`DA_DungeonVoxelConfig_POIDemo`, shared by both demo dungeon
   types) has `WallThickness` 3 at voxel 75, 225 uu, on 400 uu cells: a one-storey cell's floor slab [0, 225) and ceiling
   slab [175, 400) cover all of it, and a one-wide hallway's walls likewise, so every room and hallway was stamped solid
   (only a two-storey room keeps a band of air). A pawn put on the "floor" stood in rock: the capture showed the chunk under
   its feet loaded and cooked (`feetLd=1 feetCol=1 feetBody=1`) and the pawn fell through it all the same, since that
   chunk's collision has no surface there; from the boss room's centre a camera sees no dungeon at all, and traces down
   from it find nothing where the floor should be. The tile-dressed type has the same config, but `CarveOnly` writes
   `WallThickness` as the outer seal, outside the cell, so its rooms were never filled. A cubic world fills them the same way.
2. *The boss could not wait for its floor.* With a walkable lining (`WallThickness` 1 in memory) the boss still fell in a
   fresh world: it spawns when its POI's structure band streams in, before the voxel floor under it has collision
   (collision cooks only near a player), and an NPC has no terrain wait. The floor's collision also goes when the player
   walks out of the collision radius (20,000 on `VoxelDemo`) while the structure band (the view distance, 40,000) keeps
   the boss. Tile floors are actor collision and exist from the start. `vox.TPRoom` had the same gap on a fresh arrival
   (no settle, "tiles carry collision").

**Reproduction** (`VoxelDemo`, the base build, the dungeon at cell (3, −2)): the stamp 118,387 + 4,950 voxels (§19.2.4's
numbers); the boss spawned at z −5,086 was at −136,476 half a minute later; `vox.TPRoom Boss` with the capture lands the
pawn at −5,105 over a cooked chunk and it falls straight through. With `WallThickness` 1 in memory the boss stands at
−5,250 and the player too where the floor was already cooked; in a fresh world the boss falls again (−146,907 after 30 s).

**What changed.**

- ProceduralDungeonPlugin: the voxel-lined modes (`CarveUnderground`, `ReplaceRegion`, `MergeAsStructure`) line each closed
  face with `UDungeonVoxelConfig::InnerLiningLayers` (one layer) inside the cell, the surface content stands on, and wrap
  it with the jacket's other `WallThickness` − 1 layers from outside through the outer seal (`PlaceOuterSeal`: never into
  another open cell). A voxel of lining from each side still walls a room off from a hallway beside it, and stacked
  hallways keep their floors. `GetInnerLiningLayers`, `GetOuterJacketLayers`, `GetInnerLiningThickness`. `WallThickness` 1
  stamps exactly as before. `FVoxelDungeonWorldMode`'s SDF lines by the inner lining too (outside its open cells everything
  is solid already). A warning when a cell is under two linings and a voxel (a one-storey cell keeps an air sample only
  from three voxels up).
- VoxelWorldPOI: the floor heights (`EntranceFloorZ`, the room floors the chests and the boss stand on, the side tunnel's
  lift) take the inner lining (`GetInnerLiningThickness`), not `WallThickness * VoxelSize`.
- VoxelWorldPOI: `FPOIVoxelFloorHold` holds a character (`MOVE_None`: no gravity, velocity zero) while no floor lies under
  its feet and releases it onto its default movement mode once one does; a free character is held again when its floor
  goes with the terrain's collision (a voxel chunk at its feet has none). A floor gone over cooked terrain is a real fall
  and is left alone. The probe sweeps most of the capsule's radius down through world-static and world-dynamic objects
  (voxel collision; tiles, the elevator's car, crates), so a tile floor is a floor from the start: a first version that
  read world-static objects only held the tile-dressed boss until the rock under its tiles cooked. `APOIDungeonObjective`
  polls it for the boss every 0.25 s.
- Game module: `vox.TPRoom` holds the player the same way (`UVoxelDebugSubsystem::TeleportPawnToFloor`).
- The tile-dressed stamp (`CarveOnly`) is unchanged: the same seal, written the same way.

**Tests.**

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|

### 19.9 G31: planet scatter samples one family of radial rays (2026-10-18)

PRs open (draquel/VoxelWorlds#112, `fix/g31-planet-line-families`, on main `48f9b82` after G30 and G24 merged; the
parent's gitlink and doc map in draquel/UE5_PluginDev#122). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8085), background throttling off. Live runs on `PlanetTest` with
`/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride`, as in §19.6; planets extract scatter on the
CPU.

**The bug** (§19.6). Each planet chunk walked digital lines along local up at its own centre: stepping along the axis
nearest up, started on a stride grid across it, drifting sideways by the rounded slope. Neighbouring chunks' lines did
not continue into each other. Across the cube's diagonals they stepped along different axes, and elsewhere their drift
rounded differently where the slope differs between the two centres. Along such a face a line top whose ground
continues into the neighbour was dropped while the neighbour's lines passed the spot with their crossing on this side
of the face, so a strip got no point; rarely both chunks made it. The staircase rounding also thinned the points inside
a chunk on some slopes: at 30°N 40°E 116 of its 230 thin samples lay 4 voxels or more from any face.

**Decision D26** (§8, the user, 2026-10-18): **one family of radial rays on the cube-sphere grid**, over giving each
crossing of a chunk's own lines to the chunk containing it. Ownership alone keeps each chunk's staircase (the interior
gaps above) and still has a line decide whether the neighbour's line makes the point at a face; with one family for
every chunk there is nothing to decide.

**What changed.**

- `UVoxelScatterManager::ExtractSurfacePointsAlongUp` casts one ray from the planet's centre through the centre of each
  cell of `FVoxelCubeSphereGrid` whose face-centre cells are the point spacing across (`CellsPerEdgeFor(PlanetRadius,
  Stride * VoxelSize)`), the same grid for every chunk. The cells the chunk spans come from its corners' directions
  (`GatherSpanned`); each ray's span in the box [0, ChunkSize]³ is walked down cell by cell (a 3D DDA). In a cell whose
  corners change sign the trilinear density is sampled five times along the ray (a cell whose corners agree has one sign
  throughout); a rise through the threshold going down is a floor, the first on the ray open and the rest underground,
  and every floor of a ray that enters the chunk in the ground is underground. The chunk keeps the floors that lie in its
  own box, [0, ChunkSize) on each axis, so every crossing has one owner. A cleared volume stops the ray, as it stopped a
  line.
- The point: position on the ray, local up = the ray, normal = the trilinear gradient, material, biome, AO and the
  underground and water flags from the solid and air corners nearest the crossing, altitude by the world mode. Its spawn
  weight is the cell's solid angle × r² over the column scan's area per point: at most 1 on the datum (a face centre's
  cell) and (r / R)² over it. The grid's cells shrink to 0.71 of the area at an edge's midpoint, so the rays meet the
  surface up to 1.42 times as often as the column scan's columns (the old lines up to √3 times, at a cube corner).
- **Past the faces.** The cells against the +X, +Y and +Z faces reach the voxels past them, which the chunk's data
  cannot show; they are G29's `GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk` (the planet generator's voxel there, the neighbour's edits on
  top), each computed the first time a ray needs it (`FPlanetRayField`). The neighbours whose edits it reads
  (`UVoxelScatterManager::GetPlanetShellNeighbours`, replacing `GetPlanetLineTopNeighbours`) are the seven on those sides
  wherever the chunk is; `GatherPlanetTouchingEdits` no longer takes the up. Fractions within 1e-7 of a cell face snap to
  it, so both chunks read a point on a face from the same four voxels: a voxel at exactly the threshold there read
  126.9999 from one side and 127 from the other, and neither chunk kept the crossing.
- A chunk wholly under or over the shell (`GetAltitudeBounds`, two voxels' margin) is skipped.
- `FVoxelCubeSphereGrid::GatherSpanned` is linear: it no longer scans its output for duplicates (a cell lies on one
  face, so none can repeat), which cost 5 ms per chunk at the rays' cell counts.
- `FPlanetScatterLines` (G29's lines) is deleted; `FVoxelDigitalLine` stays (the MC mesher's material walk and the chunk
  manager's edit-merged surface query use it). Heightmap paths and generation are unchanged; no `PlanetGenerationVersion` change (scatter only).
- `voxel.Scatter.LineTopAudit` is unchanged; it now measures that the rays leave no pairs and no thin strips.

**Tests.** The planet line-top tests now judge per ray (`RayGrid`, `PadRays`): each ray of the grid should carry one open
point. Real chunks from the CPU generator (R 250,000, voxel 75, chunk 32), the 27 around each site.

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.Planet.LineTop.Duplicates` | Ten sites: both poles, 45°, the equator, a cube corner, slopes of half and a quarter voxel a step (26.57°N and 14.04°N 0°E, where the lines rounded worst), 30°N 40°E and the live corner and south stops. Pairs on one up-line from two chunks (none), none within one chunk, the local density (no sample under 0.8 or over 1.2). The shell taken for air as the sensitive case | Pairs 0 everywhere; every site 0 under 0.8 and 0 over 1.2, mean 0.989-0.990. The shell taken for air doubles 7,694 crossings over the sites (19,123 samples over 1.2) |
| `Scatter.Planet.LineTop.FlatPad` | A pad at the north pole from 0.9 voxels under a chunk face to 3 voxels over it (12 heights): every ray over the pad has one open point, on the pad, and the lower chunks' top layer none where the pad lies over the face | 2,244 of 2,244 at every height, worst 0.23 uu off the pad, no top-layer point. The shell taken for air: two or more on 45 to 2,243 rays from the face up |
| `Scatter.Planet.LineTop.Edits` | The seven shell neighbours (components 0 or 1); the voxel past the faces against the neighbour's generated, edit-merged voxel at five sites; a dig through the upper chunk's bottom layer and a build over a face, through the context and the scatter manager's pipeline | 7 neighbours, 0 of 3,169 touching voxels (638 edited) disagree; dig and build: 36 of 36 rays with one open point (0.22 uu), the other 2,144 rays one each; 0 without the edits (the build: two on some); the pipeline 36 open points over the dig with the edit layer source, 0 without |

`Scatter.Planet.DensityPerArea`: 100.5%, 100.8%, 100.2%, 101.0% and 100.5% at the north and south poles, 45°, the equator
and the cube corner (the old lines 100.0%, 100.0%, 99.3%, 100.0% and 96.5%; a disc of 20 points' radius counts within
