### 19.10 G32: collision re-cooks when a neighbour arrives (2026-10-19)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `2dc80ac`, UE5_PluginDev `5f6a8f2` (P6.5 merged; built and measured on P6.4's, `6b35d64` and
`e6691f1`, then rebased: the suites re-run on the rebase). Branches `fix/g32-stale-collision-strips`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g32-stale-collision-strips` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program
Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8089), background throttling off.

**The bug** (§19.8's observation). Collision cooks a whole chunk from its own voxels and its 26 neighbours'
(`PrepareCollisionMeshRequest`, `VoxelNeighborSlices::Extract` on a worker), and the mesher reads a neighbour without
data as air; its comment still expects the neighbour's arrival to "trigger a remesh". The render path did that once
(`QueueNeighborsForRemesh`, deleted with the legacy whole-chunk path in M5, §14.9); nothing ever did it for collision.
The decision sweep cooks a chunk as soon as it is loaded, and a chunk's mesh never waits for its neighbours, so most
cooks run before some neighbour has data. Where the ground crosses the face toward such a neighbour, the boundary cells
are built against air: a voxel-wide strip along the face where the surface bends down into a wall and down-traces miss
the ground. Where both sides are solid, a wall stands along the face inside the rock.

How common: `voxel.Collision.AuditNeighbors` (new) counts the cooks that read as air a neighbour that has data now. With
the old behaviour, `VoxelDemo` at the spawn: 217 of 244 cooked chunks; after `vox.TP 60000 20000 9000`: 240 of 240;
after a 40,000 uu bench traverse: 60 to 75 of 240 to 290. `Review_Planet` (the small planet) at the spawn: 203 of 208;
after `vox.TPLatLon 45 20`: 241 of 244. Most of those neighbours are the layers over and under the terrain, whose
boundaries carry no ground; the strips are where the ground crosses a face.

**What changed** (VoxelStreaming):

- `PrepareCollisionMeshRequest` reports the neighbours without data (`OutMissingNeighborMask`), and the cook keeps them
  (`FChunkCollisionData::MissingNeighborMask`).
- The chunk manager's `OnChunkGenerationComplete`, the one place a chunk's voxel data arrives, calls
  `UVoxelCollisionManager::OnChunkVoxelDataAvailable`. For each cooked chunk that read the new one as air it classifies
  both sides of their boundary: the arriving chunk's slab facing it (the planes a cook reads across a boundary: one at
  stride 1, 2 × stride deeper) and the cooked chunk's own (two strides: the gradient normal of a crossing a stride inside
  the face reaches across it).
  - All air on both sides: no sign change across the boundary either way, so the cook is already exact; nothing to do.
    The air layers over the terrain that load near the viewer arrive this way.
  - All solid on both sides: the cook put a wall along the boundary (solid against the air it read), now inside the
    rock where nothing from the open reaches it; nothing to do. The layers under the terrain arrive this way.
  - Otherwise the arrival is noted (`ArrivedNeighborMask`), and `ProcessNeighborRecooks` marks the chunk for a re-cook
    once none of its other missing neighbours is still being generated, so the arrivals around a chunk fold into one
    re-cook. The re-cook queues below every first cook (`bNeighborRecookOnly`, `GetDirtyPriority`): the old body stays
    live until it is replaced and only its boundary cells toward the arrival are off, while a chunk without collision
    has nothing.
- **Edits.** A cook reads its edge and corner neighbours too, but an edit marked only the edited chunk and its six face
  neighbours. `MarkNeighborsDirtyForEdit` now also marks the edge and corner neighbours whose box the edit's sphere
  reaches (within stride + 2 voxels; all of them for an undo or redo, radius 0). That is what keeps a buried wall from a
  solid-on-both-sides arrival from ever being exposed: the dig that opens the rock there re-cooks it. It also fixes edge
  and corner cells going stale after an edit.
- `voxel.Collision.NeighborRecook` (1; 0 = the behaviour before, for A/B), `voxel.Collision.AuditNeighbors [n]` (cooked
  chunks, cooked with a neighbour missing, stale, re-cooks pending, re-cooks so far, arrivals needing none, and up to n
  stale chunks), and the collision manager's `GetDebugStats`.

**Design choices made while building.**

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| When to re-cook | On the neighbour's arrival, once the others on their way are in, queued after first cooks | Re-cooking at once at the edits' priority re-cooked a chunk once for each neighbour arriving late (88 re-cooks for 44 chunks in the test) and competed with first cooks; folding the arrivals brought the test to 16 |
| Which arrivals | Only those with a surface able to cross the boundary | With every arrival re-cooked, about one re-cook per cooked chunk at the spawn; skipping air on both sides left about 475 a bench run, still frame P95 +19% and manager P95 +20% against the old behaviour. Of the arrivals left, 71% had solid on both sides (the layers under the terrain): skipping those too, 104-122 a run |
| A buried wall | Kept until an edit reaches it | Unreachable inside the rock; the edit rule re-cooks it before a dig opens it, and a reload cooks the chunk afresh |
| Deferring first cooks until the neighbours exist | Not done | A first cook gives collision where there was none (the pawn's path coverage depends on it); waiting would delay it for a correction that most arrivals do not need |

**Tests** (`VoxelWorlds.Collision.*`, new):

| Test | Check | Result |
|------|-------|--------|
| `NeighborArrival` | A streamed plane (voxel 50, chunk 32, view 3,000) cooking every loaded chunk. The window's edge chunks are cooked while their +X / +Y neighbours are not loaded; the viewer moves two chunks along +X +Y and those neighbours load. Down-traces inside the last voxel cell along each such face, at every voxel, against the same traces after re-cooking those chunks from scratch; and the audit. Once with `NeighborRecook 0`, once with 1 | 0: 6 of 64 probes miss the ground a fresh cook has, the audit finds 13 of 44 cooked chunks stale (G32 reproduced). 1: 0 of 64 differ, 0 stale, no trace hits a buried wall; 7 re-cooks, with 40 arrivals with air and 46 with solid on both sides needing none |
| `EditNeighbors` | `MarkNeighborsDirtyForEdit` with a two-voxel edit mid-chunk, by a face, by an edge, by a corner, and with radius 0 | 0, 0, 1 (the edge neighbour), 4 (three edge neighbours and the corner one) and all 20 |

Suites `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: on P6.4's base 541/541
headless and in the editor; rebased on P6.5, 552/552 headless and 552/552 in the editor with the GPU tests running,
no device loss, the 108 GPU parity lines CRC-identical to P6.4's (collision only; no generation or meshing change).
On the rebase the live audit with the re-cook on: 0 stale on `VoxelDemo` at the spawn and after the teleport, and on
`Review_Planet` at the spawn and at 45°N 20°E.

**A/B on `VoxelDemo`.** The cvar in one build, a fresh PIE per run, input blocked, a throwaway run, then five pairs of
`voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500 40000 warmup=30 catchup=90` from the spawn, interleaved (tags `g32c_demo_*`), and the
audit after each run:

| | Frame P50 / P95 ms (median) | Manager P95 ms (median) | Collision section mean / P95 ms | Catch-up s | Re-cooks a run | Stale after the run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Re-cook on** | 16.7 / 27.1 | 7.73 | 0.27 / 1.05 | 0.17-0.19 | 104-122 (2,100-2,400 arrivals needing none) | 0 |
| Off | 16.7 / 27.4 | 7.91 | 0.24 / 0.94 | 0.17 | 0 | 60-75 |

The means over the five: frame P95 30.4 against 27.4 and manager P95 8.51 against 7.71, one pair's on run (a frame P50
of 27 ms, 42.3 ms at P95) carrying the difference: without that pair, +3% and +3%. Peak loaded chunks, LOD re-meshes and
catch-up are the same; the collision section's mean rises by 0.03 ms.

**Left as they were** (§19.8's other observations): a stride-2 collision mesh (`CollisionLODLevel` 1) still cracks along
chunk faces (every world cooks at LOD 0); the bottom layer of the window keeps the wall toward the layer under it, which
never loads; the thrash of a collision radius smaller than the chunk under the viewer.

### 19.11 G33: system edits re-extract the chunks that read them (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `b63f908`, UE5_PluginDev `099f3c2` (G32 merged). Branches `fix/g33-scatter-edit-readers`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g33-scatter-edit-readers` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program
Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8092), background throttling off. Live runs on `VoxelDemo`
and on `PlanetTest` with `/Game/PluginTesting/Review/Review_Planet` through `voxel.ConfigOverride`; planets extract
scatter on the CPU.

**What happened before** (checked in the code; the row overstated it). On a system or editor edit the chunk manager's
edit handler (`EditManager->OnChunkEdited` in `UVoxelChunkManager::Initialize`) called `RegenerateChunkScatter` for the
edited chunk and its six face neighbours and marked all seven dirty; `RegenerateChunkScatter` only drops the caches, and
the re-extraction came with each chunk's re-mesh hand-off. The chunks whose extraction reads an edited chunk's voxels
(`MakeExtractionContext`) are others:

- **Heightmap and cubic:** the chunk below, whose top layer's voxel above is the edited chunk's bottom layer
  (`AboveLayerEdits`, G26). It is a face neighbour, so it was never missed. The other five face neighbours
  re-extracted for nothing.
- **Planets:** the seven chunks at -X / -Y / -Z, whose last cells read one layer past their +X / +Y / +Z faces
  (`TouchingEdits`, G29, G31): a face neighbour reads the layer facing it, an edge neighbour the column along the shared
  edge, the corner neighbour the corner voxel. The three face readers were covered. The three edge readers and the corner
  reader were not, unless they were edited themselves or were a face neighbour of an edited chunk (and then they
  re-extracted for that broadcast, not for later ones). The +X / +Y / +Z face neighbours re-extracted for nothing.

So a heightmap never kept a stale view, and a planet kept one only where an edit reached a chunk's edge column or corner
voxel without reaching the chunks that share it. A convex region that reaches an edge column almost always reaches one of
those chunks too, whose face neighbour the edge reader is. A region whose min corner is chunk-aligned on two axes does not,
nor does a second edit that lands after the first one re-extracted its readers (the live repro below).

**G53 (found while tracing).** `UVoxelEditManager::CurrentEditCenter` / `CurrentEditRadius` were set by `ApplyBrushEdit`
and never reset. Every later operation of single-voxel edits (a POI's terraform, a dungeon stamp, water propagation: a
`BeginEditOperation` / `ApplyEdit` / `EndEditOperation` batch) broadcast `OnChunkEdited` with the last brush's centre and
radius. In a session where the player had dug once:

- the surface navigation invalidated around that dig instead of the terraform (P6.5 had made centreless edits use the
  chunk's bounds, but these were not centreless);
- G32's edge and corner collision re-cook judged the old dig's sphere and re-cooked none of them;
- water propagation rescanned the old dig for seeds on each of its own batches.

A sphere could not have bounded G33's re-extraction either, for the same reason.

**What changed.**

- **VoxelCore.** `UVoxelEditManager::GetBroadcastEditBounds` gives, during each `OnChunkEdited` broadcast, the chunk-local
  bounds of the voxels the edit changed in that chunk (`FVoxelEditedVoxelBounds`; every broadcast site goes through
  `BroadcastChunkEdited`):
  - operations from the voxels their edits touched (removals included);
  - undo and redo from the voxels they revert or re-apply;
  - a clear from the cleared layer, a load from the loaded edits.

  `EndEditOperation` and `CancelEditOperation` reset the centre and radius, so only a brush's operation reports one (G53).
- **VoxelScatter.**
  - `UVoxelScatterManager::GetEditReaderOffsets` (pure) and `GetEditReaders`: the inverse of what `MakeExtractionContext`
    reads, under the same conditions, by the layers the edit reached. A planet's reader at -D needs the edit to reach
    local 0 on every axis where D is 1; a heightmap's chunk below needs local Z 0.
  - `CompareWithFreshExtraction`: every cached chunk's surface points against an extraction run now from its edit-merged
    voxels and a context made now. It skips chunks queued or in flight and chunks with a cleared volume (a player edit
    only clears, by design).
  - `ExtractChunkSurfacePoints`: the one extractor dispatch, used by the async pass and the comparison.
  - Counters `GetTotalExtractionsLaunched` and `GetTotalRegenerations`.
- **VoxelStreaming.**
  - The edit handler: for a system or editor edit it regenerates the edited chunk as before (its re-mesh re-extracts it) and
    collects its readers. `UVoxelChunkManager::ProcessEditScatterReaders`, each tick before the scatter manager's update,
    re-extracts each reader once from its voxels (`RegenerateChunkScatter`, then `HandOffChunkScatter`, the hand-off a
    mesh completion makes), with no re-mesh.
  - Readers edited in the same tick are folded: their own re-mesh re-extracts them, after every edit of the tick.
  - Readers without voxel data are skipped: their extraction reads the edit when they load.
  - Player edits are unchanged: they clear in a radius and never re-extract.
  - `voxel.Scatter.EditReaders` (1; 0 = the rule before, the six face neighbours, for A/B) and
    `UVoxelChunkManager::GetEditScatterStats`.
- **G54 (found by the tests).** A re-extraction that finds no surface (a system edit that dug a chunk's ground away)
  completes without a result, so the instances `RegenerateChunkScatter` keeps for the replacement stayed, standing on the
  removed terrain until the chunk unloaded. `ProcessCompletedAsyncScatter` now removes a chunk's instances when its pass
  finds no surface and it has no scatter cache (a supplemental pass keeps what it has).
- **Tooling** (kept):
  - `voxel.Scatter.EditAudit [maxLines]` runs `CompareWithFreshExtraction` and logs the stale chunks with a `vox.TP` to
    each and whether each reads an edited chunk, has edits itself, or neither. It also logs the edit statistics and the
    rule, and writes `Saved/VoxelAudit/EditAudit_<world>_<time>.csv`. It takes 2 to 4 s for 150 to 250 chunks.
  - `voxel.Edit.System <x y z | pawn> <radius> [dig|fill] [none|edge|corner]` (a sphere brush with System source,
    optionally on the nearest chunk edge along local up or the nearest corner).
  - `voxel.Edit.SystemLayers <x y z | pawn> [dig|fill] [axes] [depth]` (the min-face layers of the chunk holding the
    point).

  Both log the chunks they edited and, for each, the chunks that read it.

**Design choices made while building.**

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Which chunks | The inverse of `MakeExtractionContext`'s reads, beside it in the scatter manager | The rule cannot drift from what extraction reads; a face-neighbour list was both too wide and too narrow |
| How far an edit reaches | The bounds of the voxels it changed, from the edit manager | System edits are batches of single-voxel edits with no centre (and until G53 a stale one); a sphere bounds nothing for them |
| How a reader re-extracts | From its voxels in the next tick, no re-mesh | Its voxels did not change; the rule before re-meshed the face neighbours for it, and a re-mesh whose state changed in flight hands nothing to scatter |
| Duplicates | One set drained per tick; readers edited in the same tick folded | One edit spans many chunks, and several share readers |
| The face neighbours' re-mesh | Kept | Meshing and collision are not G33's (see below) |

**Tests** (`VoxelStreaming/Tests/VoxelScatterEditReadersTests.cpp`, new):

| Test | What it checks | Result |
|------|------|------|
| `Scatter.EditReaders.Rule` | `GetEditReaderOffsets` by the layers an edit reached; the bounds and centre `OnChunkEdited` reports for a batch across two chunks, a brush, a batch after a brush, an undo and a clear | Heightmap: none for an edit inside a chunk or on its -X layer only, the chunk below for its bottom layer or unknown bounds. Planet: one reader for a face layer, three for an edge column, seven for the corner or unknown bounds. Exact bounds per chunk; the batch after a brush reports radius 0 and no centre (the brush's 150 before, G53) |
| `Scatter.EditReaders.Planet` | A streamed small planet (R 20,000, voxel 50, chunk 32, rays a voxel apart) at the equator (local up +X): a system edit digs the three min-face layers of a surface chunk (2,977 voxels), no other chunk edited. Its seven readers' re-extraction after the edit (`OnChunkScatterReady`), every cached chunk against a fresh extraction, and the regenerations for it and for an edit inside the chunk, with the rule before and after | Rule 0: the edge reader beside it is not re-extracted and is stale (G33 reproduced); 7 regenerations (the chunk and its six face neighbours), 7 for an edit inside. Rule 1: every reader with points re-extracted, their points changed, 0 of 13 cached chunks stale; 8 regenerations (the chunk and its seven readers), 1 for an edit inside |
| `Scatter.EditReaders.Plane` | A streamed plane (voxel 50, chunk 32): a system edit digs a chunk's bottom layer where the ground lies within G26's band over the chunk below's top (1,024 voxels), then an edit inside the chunk, then a dig of the whole chunk | Both rules: the chunk below re-extracted, its points changed, 0 of 27 stale. Regenerations 7 → 2 for the bottom layer and 7 → 1 inside. The whole chunk dug: 11 instances before and 11 after without G54's fix, 0 after with it |

Suites `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 555/555 headless and 555/555 in
the editor with the GPU tests running, no device loss (G32's 552 and the three above); the 108 GPU parity lines CRC-identical
to G32's (scatter and the edit notification only; no generation or meshing change). The A/Bs below ran on the build before
G54's fix, which removes an empty pass's instances and changes no surface point or spawn point the audit and the digests
compare; the suites ran on the final code.

**A/B on `VoxelDemo`.** The cvar in one build, a fresh PIE per run, input blocked, the clock and NPC AI frozen, a
throwaway run, then three runs per rule, interleaved. Each run:

2. Two system edits beside the pawn: `voxel.Edit.System pawn 700 dig edge` (a sphere on the nearest chunk edge, eight

3. `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower and the City, 60 s each, the audit and the digest at each.

| Stop | Stale chunks, rule 0 / 1 | System broadcasts so far | Scatter regenerations so far, rule 0 / 1 |

- The Village's POI terraform made 20 broadcasts on chunks not loaded yet. Rule 0 had no tracked face neighbour to

**A/B on `Review_Planet`.** The same script. The edits beside the pawn are at the spawn, the north pole (the sphere on the

|------|------|------|------|

- **G33 reproduced, in all three rule-0 runs:** chunks (0, -1, 51), (-1, 0, 51) and (-1, -1, 52) held 57, 8 and 2 changed
  points against a fresh extraction. They are the layers edit's edge readers, edited themselves by the sphere a second
  earlier, so the rule before re-extracted them for the sphere and not for the layers edit. The corner reader
  (-1, -1, 51) held the same points either way.
- **Rule 1:** 0 stale at every stop. The layers edit re-extracted its seven readers, and the sphere's readers were folded.
- **Digests and map:** of the chunks every run holds (157, 157, 182, 176, 180, 193) one differs between the rules, the

- **The tiled dungeon's stamp:** 11 broadcasts on loaded chunks. Rule 0 regenerated 66 face neighbours; rule 1 one reader,
  with 8 folded.
- **The 45°N stop:** 18 broadcasts on chunks not loaded yet, which neither rule re-extracts.

**The scatter work per edit.**

- **On loaded chunks** rule 1 regenerates the edited chunk and the readers the edit reached that were not edited in the
  same tick. Rule 0 regenerated the edited chunk and its six face neighbours.
- **Over the runs:** 10 against 63 regenerations for the demo's two edits, 16 against 63 for the planet's, 12 against 77
  for the dungeon stamp.
- **In worker time:** a planet extraction costs 16.5 ms per 64³ chunk (§19.9), so the dungeon stamp saves about a second
  of worker time.
- **Unchanged:** the face neighbours' re-mesh hand-off still runs. It re-extracts nothing for a chunk whose types are done,
  and as before relaunches an extraction for a chunk that never had a surface (no types are recorded for an empty pass).

**Left as they were** (noticed, not fixed):

- The edit handler still re-meshes the edited chunk's six face neighbours (render) and re-cooks their collision. Since
  seam ownership a chunk's mesh reads no neighbour data, so the render re-mesh is probably unneeded. Removed since as G56
  (§19.13; the collision re-cook stays), with G57 found on the way.
- `UVCMovementComponent`'s embed check after an edit (`OnVoxelChunkModified`) goes by the edit's centre and radius, which
  a system edit does not have (a stamp at the pawn arms no check). The bounds would serve it. Fixed since as G55 (§14.1).
- `UVoxelScatterManager::GenerateChunkScatterFromPending` is not called and has no planet branch.
- A chunk whose extraction finds no surface records no completed types, so each re-mesh hand-off relaunches it.

### 19.12 G34: the flat ceilings are the demo cave layer's roof (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `99c9253`, UE5_PluginDev `f1b8573` (G55 merged). Branches `review/g34-cave-roof` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g34-cave-roof` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree
editor (Claudius on 8093), background throttling off. Live runs on `VoxelDemo` as it is, with GPU generation (the asset's
setting) and with CPU generation (`voxel.GPUGeneration.Enable 0`).

**The finding** (§19.5's things to know). Wide flat ceilings at about Z 0, the plane the chunk layers 0 and −1 share,
under ground around Z 1,350 near every `VoxelDemo` stop: the lower layer's top voxels air, the upper layer's bottom voxels
solid. Not checked then: whether the cave configuration means them.

**Not an artefact.** They are the roof of the demo's one cave layer, and Z 0 is not special to them. In detail:

- **The configuration.** `DemoCaveConfig` (read from the asset by a temporary probe test, not committed) has three
  layers. Only one is enabled: a `Spaghetti` layer with frequency 0.0002, 3 octaves, threshold 0.5, carve strength 1,
  falloff 0.1, `MinDepth` 20, `MaxDepth` 45, `DepthFadeWidth` 4 and `VerticalScale` 0.5. The Cheese layer (threshold
  0.33, `MinDepth` 27) and the Noodle layer (threshold 0.16, depths 2 to 15) are disabled. `UnderwaterMinDepth` is 25,
  and biome 3 has cave scale 0.
- **A tunnel layer that fills its window.** A Spaghetti layer carves where both its noise fields lie within ±threshold.
  At 0.5 (the struct's default, tuned for Cheese; `CAVE_SYSTEM.md` gives 0.15 for Spaghetti) that is most of space. Over
  the Tower's 3 × 3 chunk columns the layer alone carves more than half at 77 to 84% of sample points, at every Z from
  −40 to +40 voxels. The disabled Cheese and Noodle layers would carve 3 to 9% and 8 to 12%. So the tunnels merge into
  one cavern with pillars that fills the layer's depth window under all land.
- **The roof.** The window fades in over `DepthFadeWidth`: the carve is multiplied by a smoothstep over depths 16 to 20
  voxels, and a voxel stays solid while the carve is under about 0.5 (density 255 − 255 × carve against 127). Where the
  noise carves fully, the roof therefore lies 18 voxels (1,350 uu) under the generated terrain, and 23 voxels (1,725 uu)
  under a seabed, where `UnderwaterMinDepth` replaces `MinDepth`. The floor lies at 47 voxels (3,525 uu). The roof
  follows the terrain, so it is flat under flat ground. It lies on Z 0 wherever the ground is at 1,275 to 1,350, and on
  Z −4,800 wherever the seabed is at −3,150 to −3,075.

**Tooling** (kept). `voxel.Gen.LayerAudit [maxLines=10] [regen=4]` (`UVoxelChunkManager::AuditLayerBoundaries`, new file
`VoxelChunkManagerLayerAudit.cpp`) works over every loaded chunk with voxel data:

- **Per plane.** Ceilings (air under solid) and floors per Z plane: the 63 planes inside a chunk, and the plane against
  the chunk below. It counts the generated voxels and the voxels with the edit layer applied. Compressed and uniform
  chunks are decoded into a copy, so their residency does not change.
- **The same chunks.** Over the chunk pairs (a chunk with the one below loaded), the boundary plane against the plane
  under it (the lower chunk's top two voxels), the plane over it (the upper chunk's bottom two) and the upper chunks'
  planes.
- **The worst pairs.** The chunks with the most boundary ceilings, each with a `vox.TP`. For the first `regen` of them:
  - the chunk and the one below regenerated with the CPU generator from the request the streaming sends
    (`BuildChunkGenerationRequest`, moved out of `ProcessGenerationQueue` unchanged) and compared voxel by voxel;
  - for each ceiling column, the generated terrain height there (conditioning zones applied) and the cave carve at the
    voxel under the plane and the voxel on it (`FVoxelCaveQuery`, the generator's formula);
  - one column's profile across the plane: streamed and CPU density and the carve, 8 voxels each side.


**Every suspect, checked.** Three runs of the A/B route (the spawn after 60 s, then `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower and
the City with 60 s each), with the audit at each stop, streaming frozen: two with GPU generation (the second for the
same-chunk counts, added after the first) and one with CPU generation. The finding's own
pair, (−45, −24, 0) over (−45, −24, −1) near the Tower, is in the Tower stop's list.

| Suspect | Check | Result |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Something at the chunk boundary | Ceilings on the boundary plane against the planes either side, over the same pairs | No step: the boundary holds as many as its neighbours at every stop (table below). The finding's chunk has 827 boundary ceiling columns and 1,651 on one of its own interior planes. §19.5's 1,700 counted cells with any sign change; a ceiling column touches up to four cells of the layer |
| The cave configuration | Terrain height and carve at each boundary ceiling column of the worst pairs | Over land the terrain is 1,275 to 2,120, mean 1,310 to 1,347 per chunk (the first GPU run). Under the sea (the Z −4,800 plane) it is −3,150 to −2,284, mean −3,118 to −3,056 (12 pairs each). The carve falls from a mean of 0.64 to 0.73 under the plane to 0.28 to 0.37 on it: the fade crossing 0.5. The minima are the prediction: a roof in the plane's voxel band needs terrain at least 1,350 − 75 (land) or −4,800 + 1,725 − 75 (sea) |
| GPU generation of the lower layer's top rows | The worst pairs regenerated on the CPU | First GPU run, 24 pairs: solid differs in 0 voxels of every upper chunk and in 0 to 3 of a lower one, at most one in its top layer (one pair counts 572 boundary ceilings against the CPU's 571); density differs in 2 to 61 and 11 to 384 voxels (by one step where the profiles show it: 116 against 115). CPU run, 12 pairs: no difference at all |
| Slab culling, a uniform-air shortcut | The code, and the pairs the audit reads | The chunk manager has no generation shortcut. 760 to 807 pairs per stop had the chunk below loaded and generated, and it equals the CPU regeneration |
| Far-chunk compression, uniform collapse | The same comparison on the pairs' storage | Compressed pairs (LOD 2) and resident ones (LOD 1) alike: no solid difference |
| The edit layer | Ceilings from the generated voxels against the edit-merged ones | No chunk had edits at any stop; the counts are equal |

One column, (−200,805, −58,479) in the finding's chunk, terrain 1,346: carve 1.00 up to Z −150, 0.83 at Z −75, 0.48 at
Z 0, 0.14 at Z 75 and 0 above. The streamed density (GPU and CPU alike) goes 0, 43, 132, 218, 255, so the surface is at
Z ≈ −4, 1,350 under the ground.

Ceilings over the chunk pairs, the second GPU run (the CPU run's boundary counts are within 3 of these):

| Stop | Pairs | Boundary plane | The plane under it | The plane over it | The upper chunks' planes, mean / max |
|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Spawn | 760 | 11,550 | 10,827 | 11,274 | 14,049 / 22,135 |
| Village | 807 | 16,021 | 15,992 | 15,648 | 13,783 / 23,791 |
| Tower | 780 | 16,680 | 16,611 | 15,714 | 13,773 / 23,183 |
| City | 800 | 16,032 | 15,314 | 16,490 | 14,245 / 19,548 |

**The planes follow the configuration.** Counted over every chunk, the planes vary with height. Their one sharp feature
is planes 22 to 26, which hold a quarter to a third of their neighbours' ceilings at every stop. In layer −1 those planes
are Z −3,150 to −2,850. A full-carve roof never lies there:

- over land (terrain at least −1,500) the roof is at −2,850 or higher;
- under the sea it is at −3,225 or lower.

That is `UnderwaterMinDepth` switching per column at the waterline: the roof steps 375 uu (5 voxels) down along every
coast.

**Live look** (screenshots in the worktree's `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius`, not committed):

- The hill over the finding's chunk (`vox.TP -202600 -58479`, ground at 1,365). A camera inside the layer at Z −1,300
  (`g34_cave_y180.png`) sees one cavern: a flat roof overhead, the floor, and pillars where the noise leaves rock.
- A pit dug from the ground through the roof with 24 system-edit spheres of radius 800 (`voxel.Edit.System`) beside the
  pawn. `g34_pit_wall.png`, the pit's wall: grass, about 1,350 uu of rock, the roof's flat edge, and the cavern with a
  pillar below. `g34_pit_section.png` is a camera inside the rock between the ground and the roof, whose back faces do
  not draw: a thin slab of ground over the cavern.

**What changes.** Nothing generated, meshed, collided or extracted: the audit is a console command, and the request
builder is the same lines moved. No `GenerationVersion` change, no test (there is no defect), and no A/B (no output
changes).

Suites `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 557/557 headless and 557/557 in
the editor with the GPU tests running, no device loss (main's tests; none added). The 108 GPU parity lines are
CRC-identical to G33's.

**Left as they were:**

- **Whether the demo means one cavern under all its land, 1,350 to 3,525 uu down, rather than Spaghetti tunnels.** That
  is a content decision. A Spaghetti threshold near 0.15, or the Cheese layer, would make the caves `CAVE_SYSTEM.md`
  describes. It would change the demo's terrain under the ground and its scatter (cave floors and underground types), so
  it needs its own A/B. Not changed here. `CAVE_SYSTEM.md` now explains a layer that fills its window. Decided the same
  day: tunnels and caverns, with that A/B (§19.15).
- **The 375 uu step in the roof along the coast** (above), the same configuration's (with the tunnels, a step in the
  depth where caves begin, §19.15).

### 19.13 G56 and G57: an edit re-meshes the chunks it changed (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `1c4531d`, UE5_PluginDev `f3c6cc5` (G52 merged). Branches `fix/edit-neighbour-remesh` (VoxelWorlds)
and `claude/nice-curie-086c9f` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8093), background throttling off. It takes up the follow-up §19.11 left: the edit handler
re-meshed the edited chunk's six face neighbours "so they re-extract boundary data".

**What a face neighbour's re-mesh did** (checked in the code). On every edit the chunk manager's edit handler
(`EditManager->OnChunkEdited` in `UVoxelChunkManager::Initialize`) called `MarkChunkDirty` on the edited chunk E and on
each tracked face neighbour N, and re-cooked their collision. For N that meant:

- **Its mesh:** the same mesh again. A chunk mesh is the interior domain, built from the chunk's own voxels and edit
  layer at its LOD and local up; the request carries no neighbour data (`ProcessMeshingQueue`,
  `EVoxelMeshCellDomain::Interior`). N's voxels and edits had not changed.
- **Its seams:** `MarkChunkDirty(N)` calls `FVoxelSeamRegistry::UpdateChunkContent(N)`, which restales all 26 of N's
  incident seams even when N's content version is unchanged. A seam job reads only its participants' edit-merged
  snapshots and rendered LODs (`DispatchSeamJob`: two for a face seam, four for an edge, eight for a corner), and every
  seam that reads E's voxels has E among them, so `MarkChunkDirty(E)` restales it. N's other seams were rebuilt
  unchanged: 25 to 75 more seam jobs for a one-chunk edit in the tests, 93 to 102 live, 226 to 255 for an eight-chunk
  brush (below).
- **Its mesh completion:**
  - `OnChunkLoaded`: the surface navigation re-reads the cells it had estimated analytically over the chunk, of which
    none are left after its first load; no Blueprint binds it.
  - The scatter hand-off: its types are done, so nothing re-extracts (since G33 the chunks that read an edit re-extract
    directly).
  - `UpdateWaterTileContribution`: from its own generated voxels, unchanged. The far-compression idle timer resets.
  - `PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`: it pulls water flags across the chunk's faces from its neighbours' generated voxels.
    Edits never reach a chunk's generated voxels (they live in the edit layer), so after an edit that pull finds only
    flags the chunk's first pull missed for load order (a neighbour that arrived after it). None did in the tests below:
    the two rules' water flags are the same after every edit, and a full re-mesh of every chunk changed no chunk's flags
    in 80 checks.
- **Its collision:** a cook reads the 26 neighbours' voxels (G32), so the face neighbours' re-cook stays.

The seam-ownership design says the same (`Research/SEAM_OWNERSHIP_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1: interior meshes are never
invalidated by neighbour edits). So the re-mesh changed nothing but the work, with one exception, G57.

**G57 (found while tracing).** `MarkChunkDirty` acted only on a `Loaded` chunk. An edit that reached a chunk on its way to
a mesh (`PendingMeshing`: queued; `Meshing`: on a worker or waiting for its upload) did nothing more:

- **Its seams:** none restaled. A seam built since the chunk's last restale kept the content from before this edit, while
  the chunk's next mesh showed it.
- **Its interior:** a queued mesh reads the edit layer when it is dispatched, so it had the edit. One already on a worker
  had been built without it and landed as the chunk's mesh, and nothing re-meshed it (no content check at completion).
  The edit stayed invisible until the chunk re-meshed for another reason.

That follows any edit made within a mesh's round trip of another on the same chunk: a held brush, water propagation's
batches, a system batch or stamp over chunks still meshing (the tiled dungeon's stamp on `Review_Planet`, below). The face
neighbours' incident seams cover all of the edited chunk's (every seam with E among its participants has a face neighbour
of E too), so the old re-mesh restaled them, but only when the neighbours were `Loaded` at the second edit. Their own
re-mesh for the first edit was usually still on its way, so in practice neither rule covered it: the tests below found the
same stale geometry under both.

**What changed** (VoxelStreaming).

- **G56.** The edit handler no longer re-meshes the face neighbours; it still re-cooks their collision.
  `voxel.Edit.NeighbourRemesh` (0; 1 = the rule before, for A/B). `voxel.Scatter.EditReaders 0` keeps the re-mesh for
  system and editor edits: that rule's face neighbours re-extract their scatter through it.
- **G57.** `MarkChunkDirty` on a chunk that is `PendingMeshing` or `Meshing` restales its seams (`UpdateChunkContent`: a
  seam job reads the edit-merged snapshot when it is dispatched). A `Meshing` one is marked
  (`FVoxelChunkState::bRemeshAfterMeshing`, cleared when a mesh is dispatched, since that mesh reads the edit layer), and
  `RemeshIfEditedWhileMeshing` re-queues it when the mesh on the worker lands. This holds for every caller: edits, water
  propagation, the dungeon stamper and entrance stitcher, a save's edit load, `voxel.RemeshAll`.
- **Counters** (kept): `UVoxelChunkManager::GetMeshWorkStats` (`FMeshWorkStats`: chunk mesh jobs and seam jobs with their
  worker time; edit broadcasts, edited chunks re-meshed, edits that reached a chunk on its way to a mesh, re-meshes after
  a mesh landed, face-neighbour re-meshes) and `voxel.Edit.MeshWork [reset]`, which logs them since the last reset.

**Tests** (`VoxelStreaming/Tests/VoxelEditRemeshTests.cpp`, new): `VoxelWorlds.Streaming.EditRemesh.Plane` and `.Planet`.
A real chunk manager streams a small world (voxel 50, chunk 32, view distance 3,000; with LOD, two bands to 3,600) into a
renderer that records the chunk meshes and seam buckets. Cases: DC, MC and cubic on the plane (cubic is terrain-only, and
planets are smooth), DC and MC on the planet, with and without LOD, and with a sea. The edits are at the chunk edge along
local up nearest the base point, where the surface crosses it (a few voxels under the sea for a water case):

1. A system dig of chunk E's voxels within 3.5 voxels of the edge, its min edge: the seams there are owned by E's -A,
   -B and -A-B neighbours, which it does not edit.
2. A system fill of the chunk across the edge, whose max edge it is: the seams there are its own.
3. A player brush (radius 2.5 voxels) across the edge.
4. Two system edits of a chunk by E's -B face with mesh dispatch held: the first edit's seams are built before the
   second lands, while the chunk waits for its mesh.
5. Two system edits by E's -A face, the second while the chunk's mesh is on a worker (dispatched in the tick after the
   first, whose seams are scheduled in that tick too).

After each edit settles, every chunk mesh and seam bucket is compared, as sorted triangles (position, normal, both UV
sets, colour), with a full rebuild made then: every loaded chunk re-meshed, every seam rebuilt. The rebuild also gives the
next edit a clean start. Each case runs under both rules, and the two runs are compared after every edit: geometry, the
edit-merged voxels' shape (material, density, biome) and their water flags.

| Case | Before the fix (the build with the cvar, without G57's change): stale after edits 4 / 5, under both rules | After |
|------|------|------|
| Plane DC | 1 seam bucket (104 triangles) / 1 chunk mesh and 2 seam buckets (198) | 0 |
| Plane DC, LOD | 2 buckets (78) / 1 mesh, 2 buckets (164) | 0 |
| Plane MC, LOD | 1 bucket (48) / 1 mesh, 2 buckets (154) | 0 |
| Plane cubic | 1 bucket (48) / 1 mesh, 2 buckets (114) | 0 |
| Plane DC, sea | 1 bucket (106) / not reached (that run's edit dug only air) | 0 |
| Planet DC | 1 bucket (130) / 1 mesh, 1 bucket (222) | 0 |
| Planet DC, LOD, sea | 1 bucket (130) / 1 mesh, 1 bucket (222) | 0 |
| Planet MC, LOD | 1 bucket (112) / 1 mesh, 1 bucket (132) | 0 |

- **Edits 1 to 3** matched a full rebuild under both rules before the fix as after it: removing the re-mesh changes no
  chunk mesh and no seam. The first edit changed the seam buckets of 3 owners it did not edit (2 for cubic) in every
  case.
- **The two rules** give the same geometry, voxel shape and water flags before the edits and after each of them, in every
  case (48 comparisons). The sea cases have 12 (plane) and 16 (planet) chunks with water flags, and E has 1 and 4 face
  neighbours with them.
- **Edits 4 and 5** reach their target: the chunk is `PendingMeshing` at edit 4's second edit and `Meshing` at edit 5's
  (on the first attempt, every case). With the fix the chunk re-meshes once after the mesh on the worker lands (the rule
  before also re-meshes the face neighbours that were on a worker: 6).
- **The meshing work** of the edits (the final build):

| Edit | Chunks edited, demo / planet | Chunk meshes, rule 0 / before: demo; planet | Seam jobs: demo; planet | Meshing worker ms (chunks + seams): demo; planet |

- The counts are the same in all three runs of a rule; the worker times are medians.

- Stream-in, one run per rule, 60 s after a teleport: the tiled dungeon's stamp on `Review_Planet` (`vox.TPPOI Dungeon`,

  rule before: 1 loaded, 6 queued (its neighbour re-meshes had queued them), 11 face-neighbour re-meshes. The Village's
  terraform on `VoxelDemo`: 20 broadcasts, all on chunks not loaded yet. The stream-in's own meshing (1,000 to 1,100
  chunk meshes and 9,400 to 10,300 seam jobs in the minute) dwarfs the edits'.
- An edit deep inside one chunk still restales all 26 of its seams (26 seam jobs for 27 voxels). The edit's bounds
  (`GetBroadcastEditBounds`) could pick the seams it reaches; not taken here.

**Suites** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 558/558 headless and 558/558 in the editor with the GPU tests running, no device loss (G52's 556 and the two above); the 108 GPU parity lines CRC-identical to G52's (no generation change).

**G58 (found while checking water; fixed in §19.14).** Edit-driven water propagation (`UVoxelWaterPropagation`) reads voxels with
`UVoxelChunkManager::GetVoxelAtWorldPosition`, the generated voxels without the edit layer. Its seed scan looks for air
next to water, and a voxel the player dug still reads solid there, so a dig under the sea never floods. A throwaway probe
on the plane (a seabed 301 uu under the sea, a player brush): of 11 voxels dug to air, 8 touched water-flagged air, none had
a water flag once settled, and no seed was logged. Its flood would be wrong too: `ProcessPropagation` sets each voxel to
the generated voxel plus the flag, which undoes an edit there (a fill in a dry cave under the sea). It does not depend on
the face neighbours' re-mesh; recorded for a fix of its own (read the edit-merged voxel, and keep the edit's density and
material when setting the flag).

**Left as they were:** the face neighbours' collision re-cook (G32's reads); `PropagateWaterFromNeighbors` pulling only
when the chunk itself meshes, so a neighbour that arrives later does not push its flags into a chunk already meshed (not
seen in the tests).

### 19.14 G58: edit-driven water propagation reads the edit-merged voxels (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `29b9588`, UE5_PluginDev `bf9ec16` (G56 and G57 merged). Branches `fix/g58-water-propagation-edits`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/serene-visvesvaraya-7331a4` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program
Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8095), background throttling off.

**What it did** (checked in the code). `UVoxelWaterPropagation` floods the voxels an edit opens to the sea: the chunk
manager's edit handler calls `OnChunkEdited` for every broadcast, which looks for seeds, and `ProcessPropagation` (each
tick) runs a bounded BFS from them.

- **Its reads** were `UVoxelChunkManager::GetVoxelAtWorldPosition`, the generated voxels without the edit layer, in the
  seed scan, in `CanReceiveWater` and for the voxel it wrote. A voxel the player dug still read solid, so it was never a
  seed; nothing after the scan ran (the G56 probe: no seed logged).
- **Its write** was `ApplyEdit(position, generated voxel + flag, Set)`: a flood reaching an edited voxel would have put
  the generated voxel back, a dig's rock or a fill's air (the variant run below shows both).
- **Its seeds** were scanned only for an edit with a radius, over the brush's sphere, once for every chunk the brush
  reached (an eight-chunk brush eight times). Since G53 an operation of single-voxel edits (a POI's terraform, a dungeon
  stamp, `voxel.Edit.System`), an undo, a redo, a clear and a load report radius 0, so none of them seeded. Any
  water-flagged neighbour counted as water, a filled one too: `Add` keeps the voxel's metadata, so a fill in the sea is
  solid with the sea's flag.
- **Unloaded chunks** read as air through the same call, so a flood that reached one would have written air with the
  flag into it, carving its ground away when it loaded.
- **Its keys** were world positions floored without `WorldOrigin` (the chunk manager and the edit manager subtract it),
  and the chunks it then marked dirty (`MarkChunkDirty` of `WorldToChunk` without the origin) were shifted by the origin
  on a world like the demo's; the batch's own broadcast marked the right ones anyway. Its sea test took the cell's
  centre, where generation's fill pass takes the voxel's sample point (the cell's min corner).
- **Its batches** set the edit manager's source to System and left it there (an editor's or test actor's brush that
  sets none was broadcast as System afterwards), and came back to its own `OnChunkEdited` (radius 0 since G53; before
  it, a brush's radius, so each batch rescanned the old dig).

**What changed** (VoxelStreaming).

- **Reads.** Every read is edit-merged (`GetEditMergedVoxelAtWorldPosition`), and the flag is set on the voxel as it is:
  `Set` of the merged voxel plus the flag, so a dig keeps its density and material and no voxel goes back to its
  generated value.
- **Seeds** come from the voxels each edit changed in the chunk (`UVoxelEditManager::GetBroadcastEditBounds`, G33), so
  every edit seeds alike: a brush, an operation of single-voxel edits, an undo, a clear, a load. The box is clipped to
  below the sea (the plane cuts its top, a box wholly outside the sphere is dropped), kept per chunk (a chunk broadcast
  again joins its box) and scanned at the start of the next `ProcessPropagation`, within `MaxScanReadsPerFrame` reads
  (32,768). A seed is a changed voxel that can take water with a water-flagged **air** neighbour.
- **A chunk's water must be in place.** `UVoxelChunkManager::IsChunkWaterSettled` (`FVoxelChunkState::bWaterSettled`):
  the chunk has voxel data and has submitted a mesh since it arrived, which pulls its water flags across its faces
  (`PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`); a chunk wholly under a heightmap sea has no flags before that. An edit of a chunk
  that is not settled (most system edits land before their chunks load, a save's edits before any) keeps its box until
  it is (`UVoxelWaterPropagation::OnChunkWaterSettled`, called at that mesh submit). The flood reads and writes only
  settled chunks: it stops at one that is not.
- **Its own batches** are not scanned (their voxels took the flag, their neighbours are its frontier; a seed restarts the
  flood's budget, so a capped flood would never stop). It restores the edit source the caller had, waits while another
  edit operation is open, and keys voxels by their index relative to `WorldOrigin` (the explicit `MarkChunkDirty`
  removed); below the sea is the generation's test.
- **Tools.** `UVoxelWaterPropagation::GetStats` (scans queued and deferred, reads, seeds, floods, flooded voxels, refused
  edits, cap hits), the log line `Water propagation done: N voxels flooded from M seeds` at a flood's end,
  `UVoxelChunkManager::GetWaterPropagation`.

**Tests** (`VoxelStreaming/Tests/VoxelWaterPropagationTests.cpp`, new): `VoxelWorlds.Streaming.WaterPropagation.Plane`
and `.Planet`. A real chunk manager streams a small world with a sea (voxel 50, chunk 32, view distance 3,000; the
plane's sea at Z 0 with `WorldOrigin` (3112.5, -1937.5, 0), a quarter voxel off the voxel grid in X and Y; the planet
of radius 20,000 with its sea at the datum). Three seabed sites 5 to 10 voxels under the sea where the ground is within
75 uu of the site's altitude 150 uu either way, and one 12,000 uu off:

- **A.** A player dig on the seabed (sphere brush, radius 2.5 voxels, `Sharp`: its change falls off as (1 - t)², so it
  digs the rock near its centre to air with densities of its own).
- **B.** A system edit digs a pocket 8 voxels under the seabed (radius 2.2 voxels: air of density 40, dirt), another
  fills its bottom (sandstone, 220); the sealed pocket must stay dry. A system shaft (single-voxel edits, radius 0) from
  the pocket into the sea then opens it.
- **C.** A player fill (`Smooth`, radius 7: the sea within about 3.5 voxels of its centre turns solid, keeping the flag)
  plugs the sea over the seabed, and a system edit digs a cavity across the seabed into the plug's core, touching the
  plug's flagged voxels.
- **D.** A system dig of a seabed chunk 12,000 uu away that has no voxel data yet (a POI's terraform at stream-in); the
  viewer then moves there.

Around each site no voxel may change but by taking the flag, and only air below the sea may take it. The rule before and
a variant were run as throwaway builds of the same tests: "before" emulates the old rule (generated reads and write,
brush-only seeding, any flagged neighbour as water); the variant has the new reads and seeding with the old write
(generated voxel + flag) and the old water test (any flagged neighbour).

| Case (plane / planet) | Before | Variant: new reads and seeds, old write and water test | After |
|------|------|------|------|
| A: 6 / 7 rock voxels dug to air (5 / 6 with a density above 0) | 0 seeds, 0 flooded | 6 / 7 seeds; every one written back as generated rock with the flag | all flooded, density and material kept (6 / 7 seeds, 143 / 132 reads) |
| B: pocket 44 voxels (32 air, 12 fill), shaft 36 / 20 | sealed pocket dry; the shaft (radius 0) not scanned: 0 flooded | pocket refilled with rock (0 of 32 as air), 12 / 6 shaft voxels as air; 60 / 48 voxels' density or material changed | sealed pocket dry, no seed; then pocket and shaft all flooded (68 / 52), the fill solid and dry |
| C: plug 156 / 152 voxels solid with the flag, cavity 8 / 7 voxels | dry (radius 0, not scanned) | the cavity flooded through the plug (1 / 4 seeds), every voxel written back as generated (rock, or the sea the plug filled) | dry, no seed, nothing changed |
| D: dig 36 / 37 voxels (23 / 28 rock) before the chunk loaded | not scanned (radius 0), 0 flooded | 17 / 13 seeds; all written back as generated | scan deferred, then all flooded with the dig's density and material (17 / 13 seeds) |

D failed on the plane in a first build, which deferred the scan only until the chunk's voxel data arrived: a chunk wholly
under the plane's sea gets its water flags at its first mesh, after that scan had found no water. Hence
`IsChunkWaterSettled`.

**Live** (`VoxelDemo`, a fresh PIE: sea at Z -1,500, chunks of 64 voxels of 75 uu). Over the lake by the spawn the
seabed lies at Z -3,615. `voxel.Edit.System 3600 -4875 -3615 300 dig` (a system brush, `Sharp`) touched 179 voxels; in
the next tick the propagation seeded 13 of those it dug to air and flooded 14 (`Water propagation done: 14 voxels flooded
from 13 seeds`).

**Suites** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 561/561 headless and 561/561
in the editor with the GPU tests running, no device loss (G56's 558, G55's `VoxelCharacter.Edit.SystemEditArmsEmbedCheck`
merged since, and the two above); the 108 GPU parity lines identical to G56's (no generation change).

**G59 (traced here; fixed in §19.16).** The 2D water tiles (`UpdateWaterTileContribution`) and the cross-chunk pull at a chunk's mesh
completion (`PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`) read and write the chunk's generated voxels only. A flood's water lives in the
edit layer, so it draws no tile: a channel dug inland from the shore below sea level is flagged but shows no water
surface (swimming there goes by the analytic sea, as before). And a flood that stops at a chunk not settled does not
continue into it when it loads. Before G58 no flood reached the edit layer, so neither showed.

**Left as they were:**

- A flood's batch is an edit like any other: the chunk manager re-meshes the chunks it touched, restales their seams,
  re-cooks their collision and re-extracts their scatter (the underwater class reads the flag; the meshes and the
  collision do not). A dig under the open sea floods in one batch.
- The batches enter the undo history (the demo test actor's Z): undo restores a Set's previous `NewData`, and for a voxel
  a brush dug (a relative edit, which keeps none) that removes the edit, so the first Z after a dig under the sea undoes
  the flood and, at the voxels it reached, the dig. Fixed in §19.17 (G60): the flood stays out of the history, and undo
  and redo restore the edit layer exactly.
- The cave flag: generation keeps cave air dry under the sea; a dig that opens a cave to the sea floods it, up to
  `MaxPropagationVoxels` (8,192).

### 19.15 The demo caves: tunnels and caverns instead of one cavern (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `29b9588`, UE5_PluginDev `bf9ec16` (G56 and G57 merged); rebased onto main after G58 (§19.14).
Branches `docs/demo-cave-tunnels` (VoxelWorlds, docs only) and `claude/demo-cave-tunnels` (UE5_PluginDev, the asset).
Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8094), background
throttling off. It takes up the content decision §19.12 left open.

**The decision** (the user, 2026-10-20). The options were to keep the cavern; Spaghetti at 0.15 alone; Spaghetti at
0.15 with the Cheese layer; or both with the Noodle layer too (its depths 2 to 15 open caves at the surface). The user
chose tunnels and caverns: Spaghetti at 0.15 with the Cheese layer, enabled as configured. The Cheese layer had no
`MaxDepth`, and the first round of measurements found what that costs (item 4): its caverns went on under the tunnels
and gave about 180 more chunks a mesh. The user then asked for a floor: `MaxDepth` 60.

**The change** is content only, in UE5_PluginDev: `DemoCaveConfig`'s layer 1 (Spaghetti) threshold 0.5 → 0.15 (the
Spaghetti default in `CAVE_SYSTEM.md`), and layer 0 (Cheese) enabled: threshold 0.33, frequency 0.00025, 3 octaves,
falloff 0.2, `MinDepth` 27, `MaxDepth` 0 → 60, fade 6, `VerticalScale` 0.6. Its caverns therefore fade in from 21 voxels
and out between 60 and 66. The Noodle layer stays off. `UnderwaterMinDepth` 25 and the one biome override (biome 3,
cave scale 0) are unchanged, so nothing carves within 16 voxels (1,200 uu) of the ground. No code changes.

**Which worlds.** 24 world configurations reference `DemoCaveConfig`, and 16 of them have caves enabled, so all 16 get
the tunnels: `VoxelDemo`'s `DemoSmoothWorldConfig`, `DemoCubicWorldConfig`, `DemoWorldConfig_LOD0Ext`,
`PlanetWorldConfig`, the five `Review_Cubic*`, the four `Review_Island*` and the three `Review_Planet*` configurations.
They all had the same one cavern. The eight seam and verification test configurations reference it with caves off.
Changing only `VoxelDemo` would have needed a second cave asset and `DemoSmoothWorldConfig` pointed at it.

**Saves are not refused.** `FVoxelWorldModeFactory::MakeFingerprint` leaves terrain tuning out on purpose (WM-A4), and
`GenerationVersion` is for code that generates different terrain from the same configuration. A save made before loads
its edits onto the new rock. Edits are stored per voxel and applied over the generated voxels (Set, Add, Subtract), so
only edits that reach 16 voxels under the ground meet different rock: a pit dug into the old cavern, or a voxel-carved
dungeon's jacket where it crossed the cavern.

**Measured.** "Before" is the old tuning, "no floor" the first round (Cheese without `MaxDepth`), "after" the change as
it stands.

1. **Air by depth** (a temporary probe test, not committed). CPU generation of 3 × 3 chunk columns at each A/B stop (the
   spawn, the Village, the Tower and the City), with the request `BuildChunkGenerationRequest` builds (no conditioning
   zones), and each voxel's depth under the analytic surface. 123,454 land and 24,002 sea columns. The window the
   Spaghetti layer carves, with the variants the decision weighed:

   | Configuration | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-34 | 35-44 | 45-49 | Air over 16-49 | Columns with a cave in 16-49 | Mean cave height | Sea, air over 16-54 |
   |---------------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|----------------|------------------------------|------------------|---------------------|
   | Before: Spaghetti 0.5 | 31.7% | 80.8% | 81.2% | 80.9% | 31.2% | 68.8% | 95.3% | 23.3 voxels | 48.3% |
   | Spaghetti 0.15 alone | 4.6% | 12.2% | 12.8% | 11.9% | 4.2% | 10.4% | 34.4% | 9.6 | 7.2% |
   | Cheese alone | 0 | 0.8% | 6.6% | 5.9% | 6.1% | 4.7% | 14.2% | 10.8 | 5.5% |
   | **After: Spaghetti 0.15 + Cheese** | 4.6% | 13.0% | 18.6% | 17.3% | 10.1% | **14.6%** | **43.9%** | **10.2** | 12.1% |
   | Spaghetti 0.10 + Cheese | 2.1% | 6.4% | 12.0% | 11.0% | 7.9% | 9.2% | 33.1% | 8.6 | 8.6% |
   | Spaghetti 0.20 + Cheese | 7.8% | 21.6% | 27.1% | 25.9% | 13.2% | 21.8% | 54.8% | 12.1 | 16.7% |

   Depths in voxels under the ground; the mean cave height is the mean length of a column's vertical air runs in 16-49.
   The Cheese layer's floor at 60 changes nothing above 60 voxels. Under the window, over 120 chunks from the ground to
   128 voxels down:

   | Configuration | 50-59 | 60-65 | 66-79 | 80-127 | Chunks with cave air | Chunks wholly below 66 voxels with cave air | CPU generation |
   |---------------|-------|-------|-------|--------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------|----------------|
   | Before | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 66 | 0 of 33 | 194-197 ms a chunk |
   | No floor | 6.2% | 6.4% | 5.9% | 6.1% | 107 | 30 of 33 | 228-231 ms (+17%) |
   | **After (`MaxDepth` 60)** | 6.2% | 2.6% | 0 | 0 | **70** | **0 of 33** | **211-214 ms (+8%)** |

   CPU generation of 64³ chunks, each configuration measured twice in one run. `VoxelDemo` generates on the GPU; the CPU
   generator serves `-VoxelForceCPU`, the headless benches, tests and point queries.

2. **The A/B** on `VoxelDemo`: three runs per tuning, interleaved, the route of §19.11 (the spawn after 60 s, then
   `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower and the City, 60 s each). At each stop, streaming frozen: `voxel.Map.Capture 6`,
   `voxel.Gen.LayerAudit 3 2`, `voxel.Scatter.Digest file`, the renderer's totals (`UVoxelChunkManager::GetDebugStats`)
   and `voxel.FarCompression.Stats`. `DemoCaveConfig` was set in memory to the old tuning or the new one before each run

### 19.16 G59: the water tiles and chunk arrival read the flood's water (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `6d9c8f9`, UE5_PluginDev `a4ada60` (G58 merged). Branches `fix/g59-water-tiles-edits` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g59-water-tiles-edits` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8096), background throttling off.

**What it did** (checked in the code). Since G58 a flood's water is in the edit layer (`Set` of the edit-merged voxel
plus the flag). Two consumers read only the chunk's generated voxels (`FChunkDescriptor`):

- **The 2D water tiles.** `UpdateWaterTileContribution` (each mesh submit) built the chunk's column mask from
  `Descriptor.GetVoxelDataForRead()`. A channel dug inland below the sea flooded, but its columns stayed dry in the tile:
  no water surface over it. Swimming there goes by the analytic sea, and scatter's underwater class reads the edit-merged
  flags, so only the surface was missing.
- **Chunk arrival.** A flood reads and writes only chunks whose water is in place (G58), so it stops at one that is not,
  and a dig's seed scan finds no water in one. When that chunk arrives, `PropagateWaterFromNeighbors` pulls flags across
  its faces from the neighbours' generated voxels into its own: a flood next to it in the edit layer is not seen, nor are
  its own edits, and nothing looks at the neighbour's side. G58's deferred scan covers only edits made while the chunk was
  not settled. So a flood that stopped at a chunk did not continue into it when it loaded (when the voxels across were
  edited while that chunk was loaded before, or are generated cave air), and a pocket dug beside a chunk that was not
  loaded stayed dry once that chunk loaded with its sea.

**What changed** (VoxelStreaming).

- **Tiles.** A chunk with edits builds its column mask from the edit-merged snapshot (`GetEditMergedSnapshot`, the one
  the seam jobs read for its content version); a chunk without edits reads its generated voxels as before.
  `PropagateWaterFromNeighbors` writes flags into the voxel array without a `ContentVersion` bump, so when it writes any it
  now drops the chunk's snapshot, and the tile's rebuild has them.
- **Chunk arrival.** The chunk manager calls `UVoxelWaterPropagation::OnChunkWaterSettled` once per arrival (the first
  mesh submit since the chunk's voxel data came; before, at every submit). Besides the deferred edit box (G58), it queues
  the faces the chunk shares with chunks whose water is in place, where either chunk has edits and a voxel of the two face
  layers is below the sea. `ScanPendingFaces` (after the edit boxes, within the same 32,768 reads a frame) takes each pair
  of voxels across a queued face with an edit on either side: one dry air below the sea and the other water-flagged air
  makes the dry one a seed, and the flood runs as for an edit. A pair neither edit touched is left to the generated pull,
  so generated water and caves are as they were.
- **Why not an edit-aware pull.** The pull writes the generated voxels, which are not saved and are rebuilt at every load
  in whatever order the neighbours arrive. The flood's water is an edit (saved, undone, re-meshed like any), so its
  continuation at a chunk's arrival is one too.
- **Tools.** `FStats::FaceScansQueued` and `FaceSeeds`; the seed log line counts the face seeds; `voxel.Water.Stats
  [x y | pawn]` logs the propagation's counters and the water tile's column there (the chunk layers that mark it wet,
  `UVoxelChunkManager::GetWaterTileColumn`) and the scans' game-thread time (`FStats::ScanSeconds`,
  `MaxFrameScanSeconds`); the test renderer (`VoxelTesting::FRecordingMeshRenderer`) keeps water tiles.

**Tests** (`VoxelStreaming/Tests/VoxelWaterPropagationTests.cpp`, G58's file; the same worlds: voxel 50, chunk 32, view
distance 3,000, the plane's sea at Z 0 with `WorldOrigin` off the voxel grid, the planet of radius 20,000 with its sea at
the datum):

- **`Streaming.WaterPropagation.ChunkArrival.Plane` / `.Planet`.** Two footprints 8 to 20 voxels apart on one chunk face
  (on the planet a face across Y at the +X equator), A this side and N the other, in the sea at least 5 voxels deep over
  the footprint's highest seabed. (i) With both chunks loaded, a pocket of 12 voxels is dug to dry air in N against the
  face (2 x 3 x 2), walled in on N's side, and a door of 6 voxels on A's side is filled: the sealed pocket stays dry, no
  seed. The viewer moves 2,400 uu from A's centre away from the face, so N (4,000 away) unloads and A stays. (ii) A pocket
  of 12 voxels is dug in A against the face, walled in on A's side: no seed with N not loaded. (i)'s door is dug open: A's
  sea floods it (6 voxels), the flood stops at the face. The viewer comes back, N loads.
- **`Streaming.WaterPropagation.Tiles.Plane`.** A shore near the origin (three columns of sea, then land up to 12 voxels
  high for 11 columns and 4 rows either side); a channel from 3 columns out in the sea to 7 inland, 3 wide, down to 3
  voxels under the sea (only rock dug, system `Set` to air). The channel's inland columns 3 to 7 (15) lie beyond the tiles'
  3-column dilation of the sea's wet columns.

The rule before was run in the same build behind a throwaway cvar (the tile mask from the generated voxels, no face scans):

| Case (plane / planet) | Before | After |
|------|------|------|
| (i) a flood that stopped at a chunk not loaded: N's pocket (12) beside the door A's sea flooded (6) | pocket dry (0 / 0 of 12), no face scanned | pocket flooded (12 / 12) |
| (ii) a pocket dug in A (12) beside N while N was not loaded | dry (0 / 0 of 12) | flooded (12 / 12) |
| Faces scanned and seeds once N loaded (both cases) | 0, 0 | 6 / 5 faces, 12 / 12 seeds, 24 / 24 voxels flooded |
| Tiles (plane): channel of 231 rock voxels at the shore column (-39, 18), 118 under the sea | 118 flood (G58); inland columns under the tile 0 of 15 | 118 flood; 15 of 15 |
| G58's cases A-D (`.Plane`, `.Planet`) | as in §19.14 | the same numbers |

**Live** (`VoxelDemo`, a fresh PIE: sea at Z -1,500, chunks of 64 voxels of 75 uu). The lake by the spawn has its west
shore along x 2,100 at y 1,500, the ground rising about 0.5 uu per uu inland (-1,526 at x 2,100, -1,369 at 1,800, -1,204 at

### 19.17 G60: undo and redo restore the edit layer; the flood stays out of the history (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `5907e2d`, UE5_PluginDev `98b2a85` (G59 and the demo caves merged). Branches `fix/g60-water-undo`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/nifty-nash-4063d7` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8095), background throttling off. It takes up the second item §19.14
left: the flood's batches entered the undo history.

**What it did** (checked in the code).

- **The flood in the history.** Each frame's flood is one edit operation (`ProcessPropagation`, G58), and
  `EndEditOperation` put every operation on the undo stack and emptied the redo stack. A dig under the sea took two undo
  steps, the dig and its flood (one more for each frame a flood takes).
- **The undo record.** An operation kept its edits as applied, each with `FVoxelEdit::OriginalData`: the `NewData` of the
  edit the voxel held before, or air when it held none. Undo wrote that value into the `NewData` of the edit the layer
  held at the voxel and removed the edit when the value was air; the edit's mode stayed. A relative edit (a dig, a fill,
  a paint) keeps no `NewData` (it is air), so:
  - The flood, a `Set` of the dug voxel plus the flag over the dig's `Subtract`, recorded air, and its undo removed the
    edit: the voxel went back to the generated rock. So the first undo after a dig under the sea (the demo test actor's Z)
    took the flood back and the dig at every voxel the flood had reached. The voxels the dig had only softened (still
    solid) kept it; the second undo took those.
  - Any edit over a relative edit went the same way: a dig over a dig (the two deltas sum into one `Subtract`, recorded
    as air: its undo removed both), and a fill cancelling a dig (the edit is removed, and its undo found no edit to set).
  - A `Set` over a `Set` to air (a wall over a dungeon stamp's air) recorded air: its undo removed both.
- **The chunk.** The record kept each edit's position in its chunk but not the chunk. Undo took the first of the
  operation's chunks whose layer held an edit at that position, for an operation over several chunks possibly another
  chunk's voxel. Redo wrote every edit into the operation's first chunk and broadcast only that chunk: a brush across a
  chunk face came back with all its voxels in one chunk, at the others' positions, and the others were not re-meshed.
  Cancel wrote every edit into every chunk of the operation.
- **Redo's broadcast** carried the edit manager's current source with no centre or radius: Player after any system edit
  restores it. The chunk manager does nothing to scatter for a Player broadcast with no radius, so a system edit's redo
  re-extracted no scatter (neither the chunk nor its readers, G33), and a player dig's redo left the scatter its undo had
  regenerated (a System broadcast) standing over the hole.
- The path that removes an edit (cancelling deltas) read the edit after removing it from the layer's map.

**Decision: the flood stays out of the history.** The alternative, the flood joining its dig's undo step, needs to know
which operation each of its batches follows from. A flood runs over frames, waits for chunks whose water is not in place
(G58) and continues when a chunk arrives (G59), by which time other operations can be on the stack, and adding to an
operation under the top breaks the stack's order (its undo would restore voxels a later operation changed). Out of the
history, undoing the dig restores its voxels as they were before it, the flood there with them, once the record
restores whole previous edits; a redo of the dig floods again through the propagation, which re-meshes, re-cooks and
re-extracts as any edit's broadcast. What it does not do: water the flood put beyond the dig's own voxels (a cave or a
sealed pocket the dig opened) stays after the dig is undone, since nothing drains water, as when a fill seals a flooded
hole.

**What changed** (VoxelCore, VoxelStreaming).

- **Outside the history.** `UVoxelEditManager::BeginEditOperation(Description, bAddToUndoHistory = true)`: an operation
  begun with false takes no undo step and leaves the redo stack as it is; it is broadcast like any other. Water
  propagation's operations begin with false.
- **The undo record** (`FVoxelEditOperation::Changes` of `FVoxelEditChange`, replacing its edit list): for each voxel
  change, the chunk, the position, and the whole edit the voxel held before and after it (or none). Undo restores
  Before last change first (an operation can change a voxel twice), cancel the same, redo After first change first
  (`RestoreOperation`), each voxel in its own chunk, and each chunk changed is broadcast with the bounds of its own
  restored voxels. `OriginalData` is still written to the edits file; undo no longer reads it.
- **Redo broadcasts** the source, brush centre and radius the operation broadcast when it ended
  (`FVoxelEditOperation::Source`, `EditCenter`, `EditRadius`): a player brush clears scatter in its sphere again, a system
  edit re-extracts its readers. Undo still broadcasts System with no radius (the restored voxels regenerate).
- The removal path records the edit before removing it.
- The history holds about 130 bytes per voxel change against about 40 before (at most 100 operations).

**Tests** (new `VoxelCore/Tests/VoxelEditUndoRedoTests.cpp`; G58's `VoxelWaterPropagationTests.cpp`, G56's
`VoxelEditRemeshTests.cpp` and G33's `VoxelScatterEditReadersTests.cpp` extended).

- **`VoxelWorlds.Edit.UndoRedo.Records`** (the edit layer alone): every edit of every chunk (mode, delta, material, new
  voxel) against the state an undo or redo should give. A brush across a chunk face (57 voxels in two chunks); a dig
  over a dig; a `Set` to stone over a `Set` to air; a fill cancelling a dig; an operation outside the history (no undo
  step, the redo stack kept; undoing the dig before it removes its edit on the dig's centre and keeps its other voxel);
  a cancel.
- **`VoxelWorlds.Streaming.WaterPropagation.Undo.Plane` / `.Planet`**: G58's worlds (voxel 50, chunk 32, view distance
  3,000, a sea; the plane's `WorldOrigin` off the voxel grid). For each edit: the region's edit-merged voxels and every
  edit in the world before it; the edit, settled (and flooded); one undo, settled; a redo, settled; and both again. The
  edit must take one undo step and its flood none, one undo must give back the region's voxels and the world's edits as
  they were before the edit, and a redo the flooded state. A: a player dig on the seabed (sphere brush of radius 2.5
  voxels, `Sharp`) inside a chunk, then that flooded dig through `SaveEditsToFile` and `LoadEditsFromFile` (a save's
  `.edits.bin`). B: the same dig centred on a chunk face (two chunks). C: a player dig on land, 4 to 12 voxels over the
  sea. D: a system stamp (one operation of single-voxel `Set`s to air, as the dungeon stamper's) opening a shaft from 4
  voxels under the seabed into the sea. E: a sealed pocket (dirt of density 40) 7 voxels under the seabed, then a system
  shaft opening it: undoing the shaft must put the shaft's voxels back and leave the pocket's water, undoing the pocket
  the region as before, and redoing both the dry pocket, then the flood.
- **`Streaming.EditRemesh.Plane` / `.Planet`** gain edits 6 and 7: a second player brush across edit 3's four chunks,
  settled and undone, then its redo; both against a full rebuild like the other edits, and the redo must broadcast every
  chunk the brush did.
- **`Scatter.EditReaders.Plane` / `.Planet`** (rule 1): the pass's two system edits undone, then redone, each followed by
  the audit (every cached chunk against a fresh extraction).

"Before" is the base build's edit manager, edit types, water propagation and chunk manager with the new tests (the
operation outside the history needs the new parameter, so that case ran after only).

| Case (plane / planet) | Before | After |
|------|------|------|

One undo: 49 / 47 voxels and 52 / 53 edits differ from before the dig (the softened voxels still dug, the flooded ones back to rock), 1 step left; the redo then redoes the flood | 1 step. One undo: 0 voxels and 0 edits differ; the redo floods again (0 differ from the flooded dig); both again: 0 |

100) on the lake bed at (3600, -4875, -3615) changed 251 voxels in one chunk and flooded 6 (`Water propagation done: 6
voxels flooded from 6 seeds`); the history held one step. `TestUndo` (what the Z key calls) undid `Dig` (251 edits): no
edit left, and the undo's scan found no seed. `TestRedo`: the 251 edits again, and the same 6 voxels flooded; a second
undo and redo did the same. Then `vox.Save` with the flooded dig (251 edits in the `.edits.bin`, 6,554 bytes) and a new
PIE, which loads the save: 251 edits loaded, no undo step. Once the pawn was back, the deferred scan of the loaded edits
and 5 chunk faces on arrival (15,959 reads in 0.6 ms) found no seed and flooded nothing: the flooded voxels kept their
flag (without it, those 6 dug voxels beside the sea would have seeded again). `vox.DeleteSave` after.

**Suites** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 567/567 headless and
567/567 in the editor with the GPU tests running, no device loss (G59's 564 and the three above); the 108 GPU parity
lines identical to G59's (no generation change).

**Left as they were:**

- Water does not drain: water the flood put beyond the voxels of the edit that let it in (a cave, a pocket) stays when
  that edit is undone (case E). Draining would need the flood to know what is still connected to the sea.
- System edits are undo steps like a player's: a POI's campsite, a dungeon stamp and its entrance (`Dungeon Stamp`),
  `voxel.Edit.System`, a test's batch. The demo test actor's Z after a dungeon streamed in undoes its stamp (as before;
  now exactly). `bAddToUndoHistory` false would keep them out; not changed here.
- A clear (`ClearChunkEdits`, `ClearAllEdits`) is outside the history and leaves it as it is: an undo after a clear puts
  the operation's previous edits back on its voxels (before, it found no edit there and did nothing). A load clears the
  history, and nothing else calls them.

## 20. Spherical Phase 6: big planets and orbit (planned 2026-10-17, done 2026-10-19)

The requirements doc's optional Phase 6 ([SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md](SPHERICAL_PLANET_REQUIREMENTS.md) §4): SP-H1
(precision), SP-C5 (the far band) and SP-C6 (orbit), with SP-C3 (a doc fix). Phases 1-5 made a small planet (R 250,000
