### 20.0 What the survey found (2026-10-17)

Three read-only passes over precision, streaming and orbit, with file and line references in the session's notes; the
figures below come from the code's own formulas (re-run for the streaming numbers, which match the Phase 2 benches).

**Precision.** Float spacing (ULP) is about 1.2 × 10⁻⁷ of a value: 0.5 uu at 5 × 10⁶, 1 uu at 10⁷, 8 uu at 10⁸ (1,000 km),
64 uu at Earth's 6.4 × 10⁸. The uint8 density step is about 0.6-0.8 uu.

| Area | Today | First visible at |
|------|-------|------------------|
| The terrain SDF (CPU and GPU) | `FSphericalPlanetWorldMode::CalculateRadialDistance` returns a float, `GetAltitude` subtracts two floats of size R, `TerrainRadius` is float R + altitude; the GPU does the same (`SphericalPlanet.ush:110-135`). "Planet-relative" removes only the centre's offset: with the centre at the origin the SDF still cancels at magnitude R | One density step at ~8 × 10⁶; terraces 5-10 steps tall and normals off by 2-5° at 10⁸ |
| Noise inputs | `FBM3D` and the 3D noises cast their position to float (`VoxelCPUNoiseGenerator.cpp:533`, `:578`); the GPU noise is float3. Terrain, continentalness and climate sample at direction × R; caves and ore at absolute positions | Ore jitter 5% of feature size at 10⁷; cave facets at 10⁸ |
| Noise period | A 256-entry permutation (CPU and GPU): every field repeats every ~222-256 noise units. Continentalness at its default frequency repeats every ~120 km, so about 50 times around a 1,000 km planet's equator | From ~2 × 10⁶ (a scale issue, on the plane too) |
| Mesh vertices | Chunk-local `FVector3f`, exact; but the scene proxy adds the absolute chunk offset as `FVector3f` (`VoxelSceneProxy.cpp:1028`, `:1236`, `:1902`, `:2304`) with the component at the origin; the GPU MC mesher builds absolute float corners. Collision is chunk-local with a double transform (safe) | 1 uu at 10⁷ (seams, the crossfade): the documented ~100 km ceiling |
| Scatter | One HISM per type at the origin, instances in world space | ~10⁷ (inferred) |
| Materials | The triplanar custom node takes Absolute World Position as float3 (per `MATERIAL_SYSTEM.md`; assets not checked) | ~10⁶-10⁷ |
| GPU specifics | The ore `Rarity` key is exact only while the planet-relative position is under 2²⁴ (1.68 × 10⁷); the GPU's great-circle distance and sea test are float while the CPU's are double (pad edges and shorelines drift between them) | 1-2 × 10⁷ |
| Safe at any size | The cube sphere (`FVoxelCubeSphere`, `FVoxelCubeSphereGrid`), conditioning on the CPU, `FVoxelSeaSurface`, collision, gravity, movement, camera and AI, world items, pad space, the dungeon lattice, navigation frames, the PCG grid, CPU scatter extraction, chunk, voxel and save integers (int32 to ~2 × 10¹¹ uu), KillZ, the LOD window and horizon | — |

`WorldOrigin` is both the planet centre and the chunk grid's origin; three sites assume they coincide (water propagation,
`GetChunkLocalUp`, the LOD window), and the save fingerprint records both. Nothing in the project uses UE's world origin
rebasing.

**Scale (not precision).** The ocean sphere caps at 160 segments a face edge, so its sag passes 8 uu past R 3.3 × 10⁵
(240 uu at 10⁷, 2,400 uu at 10⁸); the world map's zoom range shows a whole globe only up to R ≈ 5 × 10⁵; POI registration
surveys every cell of the planet (363,000 at 10⁷, `int32` overflow and gigabytes at Earth) and `voxel.Map.ExploreAll`
enumerates every tile (an `int32` counter overflows at ~5 × 10⁷); relief is clamped at 500 m (`PlanetMaxTerrainHeight`,
`PlanetMaxTerrainDepth` and `PlanetHeightScale`, `ClampMax` 50,000 uu). `FChunkDescriptor::GetUniqueID` packs coordinates
into 16 bits (no callers).

**Streaming.** The planet loads the whole shell (datum ± 6,500 plus half a chunk, 3.7 chunks thick on `Review_Planet`)
inside a 40,000 uu 3D sphere around the viewer: about 1,000 chunks, over 90% of them LOD 2 and compressed, **whatever the
radius** (1,004-1,094 at R 2.5 × 10⁵, 5 × 10⁶ and 10⁸). A literal surface ± margin slab saves only 10-20% on today's
planet (mostly uniform chunks that cost no memory), but with km-scale relief the shell becomes hundreds of chunks thick and
a per-chunk slab is required. Voxels to the horizon are out of reach (58,000 chunks at R 5 × 10⁶ on the ground, 1.15
million at 10⁸). Climbing, the window shrinks rather than grows: 884 chunks at 10,000 uu up, 92 at 40,000, none from
~50,000 (the viewer-Z clip and the 3D distance, the planet's version of G13, which M4's D8 fixed for heightmaps only).
Nothing is drawn past the view distance except the sea sphere. Frustum culling in the strategy is a no-op
(`FLODQueryContext::FrustumPlanes` is never filled; the proxy culls at draw time).

**Orbit.** Above about 0.2 R every chunk unloads and only the sea sphere draws (a world without water draws nothing).
The voxel LOD cannot reach orbit: every chunk has the same world size, generation is always 64³ at full resolution (LOD
is a meshing stride), and a whole shell is about 126,000 chunks. Other hazards: KillZ is a world-Z plane, so a player high
over a planet's southern hemisphere is killed (on `Review_Planet`, whose KillZ stays at the engine default, at an altitude of 10 R every latitude south of about −22°); there are no flight controls
(input is yaw only outside swimming); gravity keeps full strength at any distance; the load budget counts horizontal speed
only; the SkyAtmosphere keeps its 60 km default height (24 times this planet's radius); a second SkyAtmosphere would not
render. Reusable: the thread-safe analytic surface (`GetConditionedTerrainAltitude`, `QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions`), the
cube sphere, `FVoxelPlanetOcean`'s mesh builder, the far ocean's window-and-hole pattern (`FVoxelFarOcean`), the map's
per-direction tile worker, the planet branch of the GPU generator, the appearance fades, `SetBenchmarkView` and the settle
hold.

**Decided before planning** (asked 2026-10-17; recorded in §8):

| ID | Question | Decision |
|----|----------|----------|
| D17 | How big should Phase 6's planets get? (revises SD1) | **Up to about 1,000 km** (R 10⁸ uu): the precision track is in scope (double and chunk-relative terrain math on the CPU and the GPU, chunk-relative vertices and instances, relative noise, LWC-safe materials) as well as the scale items. Earth scale stays out |
| D18 | How far off the surface? (revises SD5) | **Orbit and back:** fly up until the whole planet is in view and come back down, voxels fading in over the far field. Other bodies (moons, distant planets) stay out |
| D19 | The far band (SP-C5) | **An analytic far mesh** beyond the voxel window, with a hole where voxels are loaded; the voxel window keeps its size, its shell tightened to the terrain's bounds. With km-scale relief (D17) the near window also needs the per-chunk radial slab |
| D20 | How the player gets to altitude | **QA tooling only:** debug flight and an orbit camera, with streaming and the out-of-world checks behaving at altitude. No gameplay flight; gravity stays constant |

**Design (written before building).**

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Double math on the CPU | Every quantity of size R kept in double from the centre to the final altitude or signed distance; float only for values of size altitude, chunk or voxel | The cancellation at magnitude R is the root cause; the CPU already holds double positions |
| The GPU without doubles | A chunk-relative formulation: the CPU sends what is large (the chunk origin's direction and altitude, the split noise origins, zone positions relative to the chunk) and the shader computes only small quantities in float. No `double` in HLSL (not portable, slow) | Keeps the planet on the GPU (Phase 2's default) at any size; the same small-value algebra on the CPU keeps parity |
| Noise at scale (D22) | Split-origin sampling with a hashed integer lattice for planets: exact positions at any radius and no 256-unit period | A planet of 1,000 km at continental frequencies would otherwise repeat its continents about 50 times around the equator, and its noise inputs would jitter by 8 uu |
| Rendering at scale (D23) | (a) **Region primitives:** the voxel component split into one primitive per region of N³ chunks (e.g. 16³ chunks, 76,800 uu at 4,800 uu a chunk), vertices relative to the region origin, each region's transform in double (UE5's large-world coordinates); (b) one primitive re-based to a render origin near the camera, every chunk re-baked when the camera moves far | (a) costs a few dozen primitives and no re-bake hitch; (b) keeps one primitive but re-uploads every chunk at each re-base |
| The near window at scale | The heightmap M4 rules on a sphere: a per-chunk surface slab (the analytic altitude range over the chunk's cap, cached per cube-sphere cell), the viewer's layer ± 2 near it, keep the whole shell near it, edits pinned; distances measured from the viewer's ground point | One rule for both world kinds; km relief makes the shell hundreds of chunks thick, so the slab is what keeps the count bounded |
| The far field | A separate cube-sphere quadtree of analytic-surface patches, not an `IVoxelLODStrategy`: patches are heightfields with their own primitives, split by screen-space error | The voxel LOD has one chunk size and full-resolution generation, so it cannot reach the horizon or orbit; the analytic surface is thread-safe and cheap per sample |
| The voxel edge | Patches inside the loaded cap are skipped; a band along its edge is drawn sunk about a voxel under the voxel surface; the hole follows the window (window-and-frame) | Holes and caves dug near the edge never show a far-field floor; the sunk band hides the seam without z-fighting |
| What the far field does not show | Caves, overhangs and edits beyond the voxel window (the map's edit overlays could adjust heights later) | The far field is seen from far away; G-style follow-up if it matters |
| Orbit | The far field is the planet from orbit; voxels unload above a cut-over altitude (the window would hold only LOD-2 chunks under a high viewer) and stream back on descent, fading in | A whole shell of voxels (~126,000 chunks) is out of reach; the fade already exists |
| Getting up (D20) | `vox.Fly` and `vox.Orbit` for QA; KillZ and an outer bound safe in space; constant gravity | No gameplay flight in this phase |

**Decisions** (asked 2026-10-17; **each decided as recommended**, recorded in §8):

| ID | Question | Options | Recommendation (accepted) |
|----|----------|---------|---------------------------|
| D21 | Does Phase 6 bump `PlanetGenerationVersion`? | Bump 4 → 5: every planet save is refused and kept on disk (the hashed noise of D22 and the double SDF change every planet's terrain, slightly on today's planet, completely in its noise pattern); heightmap saves keep loading. Or no bump | **Bump.** Planet saves hold only test data; the terrain changes |
| D22 | The planet noise lattice | (a) **Hashed integer lattice** (no period) with split-origin sampling, planets only: today's small planet changes its look once; (b) keep the 256-entry permutation and split-origin sampling only: exact positions, but continents repeat around big planets | **(a).** Repetition is the most visible scale artefact after precision, and the hash is already the pattern the ore `Rarity` key uses on both CPU and GPU |
| D23 | Rendering precision | (a) **Region primitives** (above); (b) a re-based single primitive | **(a).** No re-upload hitch, a bounded number of primitives, and the same split works for scatter |
| D24 | Relief and test-planet sizes | The relief clamps raised to (a) **10 km** (1,000,000 uu) for height and depth; (b) 5 km; (c) unclamped. Test planets M = 50 km, L = 1,000 km | **(a), with M and L as above.** Mountains of a few km on a 1,000 km planet; the slab (WM-BP8) bounds the cost |

| Walk and edit | Pole, 45°, the equator, a cube corner on L | No fall-through; dig and place; no seam cracks, shimmer or terraces; scatter seated |

| Climb to orbit and back | The pole and the equator on M and L, `vox.Fly` / `vox.Orbit` | The planet drawn at every altitude up to 2 R; voxels unload and come back on descent with a fade; landing on cooked ground; never killed by KillZ |
| Systems | L | The QA world, map, POI, save and NPC rows that Phases 4-5 passed, at L |
| Budgets | Benches on M and L against `Review_Planet` | Frame, manager and memory within the small planet's thresholds (D3: 1.5 GB peak, 0.6 GB settled); the far field's cost reported |
| Heightmap worlds unchanged | `VoxelDemo` A/B against a base build | Identical: map image, scatter digest, POIs, NPCs, paths, dungeon stamps |

**Left for later.** Earth scale (D17); other bodies and a landable second planet (D18); gameplay flight and gravity
falloff (D20); edits, caves and overhangs in the far field; frustum culling in the LOD strategy (a no-op today).

### 20.2 P6.1 results: guardrails and baseline (2026-10-18)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `82a9f6a`, UE5_PluginDev `2ebdad5` (G31 merged). Branches `feat/spherical-p6-1-guardrails`
(VoxelWorlds, VoxelCharacterPlugin) and `claude/spherical-p6-1-guardrails` (UE5_PluginDev), one commit per work item.
WM-BP11's two POI bounds were brought forward into this milestone (below): `Review_Planet_L` was unplayable without them.

**WM-BP1: the test planets.** `Scripts/setup_planet_test.py` (`SCALED_ONLY`) builds `Review_Planet_M` and
`Review_Planet_L` from `Review_Planet`, each with its own copy of the biome configuration (`Review_Planet_<X>_Biomes`).
The relief grows without steepening the ground: the terrain noise's base wavelength and `PlanetHeightScale` grow by the
same factor K and the noise gains log2(K) octaves, so its K-th octave is the demo's first (the same slope per octave, the
same walking-scale detail) under larger landforms; continentalness carries the km-scale offsets
(`UVoxelBiomeConfiguration::ScaleContinentalnessHeights`), and continents and climate zones grow with the planet. The
shells are the terrain's extent (`UVoxelWorldConfiguration::GetPlanetTerrainExtent`, the settings check's numbers) plus
10%, under D24's clamps (`PlanetMaxTerrainHeight`, `PlanetMaxTerrainDepth` and `PlanetHeightScale` now clamp at
1,000,000; the noise and climate frequencies clamp lower, UI metadata only).

| Continentalness offsets | ±3,000 | ±150,000 (x 50) | ±500,000 (x 166.7) |
| Continents / climate wavelength | 500 m / 200 m and 140 m (the demo's) | 60 km / 15 km and 11 km | 1,200 km / 250 km and 180 km |
| Terrain extent / shell | ±6,000 / 6,500 | ±198,000 / 218,000 | ±692,000 / 762,000 |
| Sea under the datum | 500 | 25,000 | 83,333 |

**The baseline, as shipped.** Live on `PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride` (screenshots
`Saved/Screenshots/Claudius/p6_base_{M,L}_{45N,equator,corner,pole}_{ground,above}.png` in the worktree), with the precision
probe below and the benches further down.

- *Getting onto a big planet.* The map's PlayerStart sits over the small planet's pole (z 254,500), inside M's and L's
  cores, and the spawn search (`FindSpawnablePosition`, by direction) looks for land within 50,000 uu of arc: M's and L's
  north poles are open sea with no land that close, so the pawn waits in the core for terrain that never streams (G36).
  Every survey started with `vox.TPLatLon`. L's cube corner and pole are open sea too (the pawn swims there).
- *L would not run* (before the POI bounds below): PIE start spent 120 s generating the planet's 8.2 million POIs for a log
  line, and then each frame took 30 s to 3 min, because the planet map markers and the claim streaming generated their POIs
  over a cap that grew with the query origin's height over the datum (the pawn in the core: 1,000 km; at 2 R: 2,000 km)
  (G37). With the bounds, L starts in seconds and runs at the frame rates below.
- *The voxel window.* With km-scale relief the shell is thicker than the view distance, so the window is the whole sphere
  of 40,000 uu around the viewer: 2,800-3,000 chunks on M and L (radial layers from −25 to 34 depending on the site; LOD 0/1/2 about 18/110/2,600),
  against about 1,000 on the small planet, whose shell is 3.7 chunks thick. Nothing is drawn past it but the sea sphere:
  from 115 m over M's ground the window ends in a chunk staircase against that sphere, and on L, where the sea lies 83,333
  under the datum, the 400 m window floats about 1.5 km over the sea sphere (`p6_base_L_45N_above.png`). The horizon from
  the ground is 5.8 km on M (14 times the window's reach) and 37 km on L.
- *Precision on L.* Visible from the ground: straight dark lines along chunk faces (the vertices' absolute float offsets)
  and striped ground material (the triplanar node's absolute world position). The probe's numbers are below.
- *Altitude.* Up to 2 R over the south pole of every planet the pawn lives (KillZ and the outer bound, WM-BP2); from the

  small planet's 60 km atmosphere, with a thin limb on L. The voxel window is empty from about the view distance up.
- *The exact north pole* (G35, fixed): a pawn teleported there from elsewhere on the planet kept its old tilt (54.7° off

  the north pole's.

The terrain noise's own inputs are fine at L (its top octave's float spacing is 2.4 × 10⁻⁴ of a feature, since the
position is multiplied by the frequency before the float cast), but a 100 uu feature sampled at an absolute position (caves,
ore) jitters by 8% of itself, and the 256-unit period repeats the terrain's top octave 61 times around L's equator (its base
octave once, continents and climate under once). The SDF's cancellation at magnitude R is what shows: 13 density steps of
terraces and normals off by up to 8° on L. WM-BP4 to WM-BP7 take each of these.

**WM-BP2: guardrails at altitude.**

- *KillZ and the outer bound.* `UVoxelWorldConfiguration::PlanetOrbitCeiling` (0 = 3 R) →
  `FSphericalPlanetParams::OrbitCeiling` → `FVoxelWorldBounds::OrbitRadius` (the datum plus the ceiling).
  `ComputePlanetKillZ` puts KillZ a chunk below the centre minus the orbit radius (−4 × 10⁸ − 4,800 on L), and
  `AVCCharacterBase::IsOutOfWorld` counts a pawn past the orbit radius as out of the world (it falls out and respawns).
- *Flight* (D20, QA only). `UVCMovementComponent::SetDebugFlight` / `SetFlightClimb`: `MOVE_Flying` with the movement
  input across local up, a climb along it (hands-free, or the jump / crouch keys held) at up to `MaxFlySpeed`, and with no
  climb the distance from the centre held, so a flight across a planet keeps its altitude (straight lines rise off a
  sphere; the hold takes that back each frame). A flyer stays upright (`ShouldRemainVertical`) and never turns into a
  swimmer; stopping drops it into a fall. `vox.Fly [0|1] [climb] [speed]` drives it (the speed raises the acceleration too,
  restored on landing); `vox.TPLatLon lat lon alt 0 1` holds an altitude.
- *The orbit camera.* `vox.Orbit <altitude|0> [period] [lat lon]`: a transient camera on the great circle through the point
  heading east, or a fixed look-down, looking at the centre. It is the view target and so the streaming viewer; the pawn is
  held, and settles onto the ground when the camera is released.
- *The load budget* counts the viewer's 3D speed on a planet (`ViewerLoadSpeed`; heightmap worlds keep the horizontal one),
  so a climb at a pole or a flight north raises it as a walk east does.
- *`vox.Planet`* adds the orbit radius, the streaming viewer's altitude, the voxel window
  (`UVoxelChunkManager::GetResidencySnapshot`: tracked and ready chunks, per LOD, per radial layer, the farthest chunk from
  the viewer and from its ground point) and the far field's state (`GetFarFieldStats`, inactive until WM-BP9), and the
  pawn's flight.
- `FChunkDescriptor::GetUniqueID` (16-bit packing, no callers) is gone; `LOD_SYSTEM.md`'s planet section (SP-C3) now
  describes the shell window, the 3D load horizon and the tangent-sum cull as the code has them.

Live, on the small planet, M and L: hold 2 R over the south pole for 20 s (flying, gravity +Z, alive), descend for about 20 s at
R/40 a second (125,293 uu on the small planet, 2,506,301 on M, 50,133,440 on L), the orbit camera

**WM-BP11, brought forward: POI work bounded on big planets.** `FPOIPlacement::GetPlanetCapAngleWithin`: the cap a query
by distance generates is the set of directions holding a point of the terrain shell within the range of the origin (the

the chord of the range plus the origin's height, which opened a cap of tens of degrees for an origin inside the planet or
high above it; on the datum the new cap is the chord's angle, far above with the minimap's range it is empty.
`GetPlanetSurveyAngle`: registration's statistics survey covers a cap of about 100,000 cells around the north pole (all of
the small planet and of M, 6° of L: 5,368 POIs in 0.2 s, where all of L was 8.2 million in 120 s). The rest of WM-BP11 (the
world map's zoom range, `ExploreAll`, NPC densities, the spawn search) stays in P6.5.

### 20.3 P6.2 results: precision (2026-10-19)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `daf78e0`, UE5_PluginDev `e90d8bd` (P6.1 merged). Branches `feat/spherical-p6-2-precision`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/spherical-p6-2-precision-27fdaf` (UE5_PluginDev), one commit per work item. On
`Review_Planet_L` (R 10⁸) the SDF, normals, noise and vertices are within the thresholds on the CPU and the GPU;
heightmap generation is bit for bit as before.

**WM-BP4: double CPU planet math.** Every quantity of size R stays in double from the centre to the final altitude or
signed distance: `FSphericalPlanetParams::PlanetRadius`, the shell radii and `FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest::WaterRadius`
are double; `CalculateRadialDistance`, `GetAltitude`, `GetDensityAt`, `ShellSignedDistance` and
`CalculateSignedDistance` subtract in double; `ShellSignedDistanceAtAltitude` writes the SDF as the terrain's altitude
minus the voxel's (the form the GPU uses since WM-BP6). `GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet` takes the voxel's planet-relative
position, distance and direction in double, and its SDF, depth, height rules and sea test read altitudes (the sea as
`WaterRadius − R`, formed in double). `GetSurfacePoint` and `GetConditionedSurfacePoint` build the point as centre +
direction × (R + altitude) in double, so the normal's central differences no longer see R + h rounded to 8 uu.
`QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions` and the LOD strategy's radii likewise.

**WM-BP5: split-origin hashed noise for planets (D22, D21).** `FVoxelPlanetNoise` (`VoxelPlanetNoise.h`) and its GPU
twin `PlanetNoise.ush`, with the same float algebra on both sides:

- a hashed integer lattice (the ore `Rarity` hash's mixing) instead of the 256-entry permutation table, so no period
  (the table repeated L's top terrain octave 61 times around its equator);
- split-origin sampling: an origin split in double, per octave, into an integer lattice cell (wrapping) and a float
  fraction, plus a small float offset, so every float is of the size of a cell at any radius (simplex splits in the
  skewed lattice; Perlin, cellular and Voronoi in the cube lattice). The CPU splits each sample at the point itself;
  the GPU splits a per-chunk origin (`PlanetNoiseOrigins`, uploaded per dispatch) and adds the voxel's offset from it;
- every planet field samples it: terrain and continentalness (`SampleRadialDisplacement`,
  `ComputeEffectiveTerrainParams`), temperature and moisture (generation, `SampleClimate`, the surface queries, the map's
  fallback climate, the editor's field preview; the heightmap's 2-octave fields, same seeds and frequencies),
  caves at the planet-relative position with the altitude scaled (`ScaleAltitudeRelative`), and ores at the
  planet-relative position with one streak direction per ore type (a direction that depends on the position turns into
  white noise far from the origin).

Heightmap noise is untouched. `PlanetGenerationVersion` 4 → 5 (D21): planet saves are refused and kept, heightmap saves
load (`VoxelWorldSave`'s planet test at `PlanetGeneration=5`).

**WM-BP6: the GPU planet branch chunk-relative.** The GPU has no doubles, so the CPU reduces every R-sized value in
double and the shader computes only small quantities in float, in the chunk's frame (`PlanetFrame.ush`, shared with the
post-passes). With the chunk centre as the anchor (distance r0, direction n0), a voxel at anchor + D lies
dR = r0·e / (√(1+e) + 1) farther out, e = (2 n0·D + D·D / r0) / r0, and its direction moves by (D − n0·dR) / (r0 + dR).

- The voxel's altitude is the anchor's (formed in double) + dR; the SDF, depth and the shell's quick reject read
  altitudes (`PlanetShellSignedDistance` mirrors `ShellSignedDistanceAtAltitude`).
- The sea is an altitude for the underwater column and materials; the post-passes test dR ≤ `WaterRadius` − |anchor|
  (a float |P − C|² against `WaterRadius`² jittered by 8 uu at R 10⁸).
- Conditioning zones are uploaded as their datum points relative to the anchor's (double); the shader measures the short
  chord to the voxel's datum point, arc = 2R·asin(chord / 2R) (R·atan2 of float directions was 10 uu off at L).
- The ore `Rarity` key is the chunk's integer base (the chunk origin relative to the centre, floored in double) +
  floor(fraction + local + 0.5).
- `PlanetCenter`, `PlanetChunkOffset` and the radius parameters are gone from the generation shader.

**WM-BP7: rendering precision (D23).** Region primitives (`FVoxelRenderRegions`, VoxelCore): on a planet the terrain is
split into regions of `voxel.Render.RegionChunks`³ chunks (16 by default: 76,800 uu), each its own
`UVoxelWorldComponent` at the region's origin in double. Heightmap worlds keep one component at (0, 0, 0), as before.

- `FVoxelCustomVFRenderer` routes every chunk, seam, water tile and fade to its region's component, creating it on demand
  (material, RVTs, water material, atlas, LOD collection, distances and viewer replayed), and retires a region whose
  component holds nothing (`UVoxelWorldComponent::HasRenderContent`); the primary component is region (0, 0, 0) and stays.
- `FVoxelSceneProxy` stores vertices relative to its component's location (`RenderOrigin`, `ToRenderOffset`) on the CPU
  path, the GPU path, seams, water tiles and batches.
- The GPU MC mesher writes chunk-local corners (`ChunkWorldPosition` zero).
- Scatter: one HISM per type and region (`FVoxelScatterHISMKey`), each at its region's origin; released instances park
  at local zero.
- The voxel master materials (`M_VoxelMaster`, `M_VoxelMaster_Fade`) feed both triplanar calls an LWC-safe position:
  Period = max(1, round(65,536 × `TriplanarScale`)) / `TriplanarScale` (a whole number of texture tiles), tiled =
  frac(absolute world position / Period) × Period. The custom nodes received the absolute position demoted to float
  (8 uu steps at 10⁸: P6.1's streaked ground); the tiled UV differs from the true one by whole tiles, and the nodes
  sample with `SampleLevel`, so no seam shows at a period boundary.

Live on M, 1 to 5 region components drew the window as it moved (`Render regions: 16^3 chunks, N primitive(s)` in the
chunk manager's status).

**The precision probe after P6.2** (`VoxelWorlds.WorldModes.Planet.PrecisionProbe`, headless, against §20.2's table; it
now reports the SDF error of generation's own form next to Phase 5's float formula, and a vertex relative to its render
region next to an absolute `FVector3f`). The surface altitudes differ from §20.2's (the new noise pattern), so the
vertex columns are at different points than P6.1's:

| Planet, site | Voxels within 2 of the surface with another density (P6.1 → P6.2) | SDF error: Phase 5's float formula / as generated | Density-gradient normals off, max (P6.1 → P6.2) | A surface vertex: absolute `FVector3f` / relative to its region |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small, all four | 0.4% (1 step) → 0 | 0.01-0.02 / 0.0000 uu | 0.6° → 0.00° | 0.00-0.01 / 0.0002-0.006 uu |
| M, all four | 14% (1) → 0 | 0.49-0.50 / 0.0000 | 0.7-1.15° → 0.00° | 0.07-0.14 / 0.0000-0.0024 |
| L, pole | 47% (14) → 0 | 7.99 / 0.0000 | 5.9° → 0.00° | 0.54 / 0.0000 |
| L, 45° | 47% (14) → 0 | 7.84 / 0.0000 | 6.5° → 0.00° | 1.81 / 0.0019 |
| L, equator | 48% (14) → 0 | 7.94 / 0.0000 | 8.2° → 0.00° | 0.99 / 0.0020 |
| L, cube corner | 48% (13) → 0 | 7.37 / 0.0000 | 4.0° → 0.00° | 0.36 / 0.0048 |

The probe ran after WM-BP4 (already 0 density steps and 0.00° gradient normals everywhere: the CPU part was done) and after WM-BP7
(the same, with the region column). It is CPU-only: the GPU's side is the parity test below, and the vertex column's
rendering side `Rendering.Planet.RegionPrecision`.

**Tests against the thresholds.**

### 20.4 P6.3 results: streaming at scale (2026-10-19)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `2f3dadd`, UE5_PluginDev `85a6d41` (P6.2 merged). Branches `feat/spherical-p6-3-streaming` (VoxelWorlds)
and `claude/spherical-p6-3-streaming-94d677` (UE5_PluginDev). P6.3 is WM-BP8 alone: one commit with its tests, and the
docs. On `Review_Planet_L` (km relief) the window is the surface slab: 1,100-1,260 chunks against P6.1's 2,860-3,010 and
the small planet's 1,250-1,310; a climbing viewer keeps its ground disk; nothing loads off the slab but near the viewer
and edits.

**WM-BP8: the near window at scale.** The heightmap M4 rules (D8, §14.8) on a sphere; a planet streams by chunk
(`FDistanceBandLODStrategy::IsInPlanetWindow`), not by column:

- *The horizon along the ground* (the planet's D8). On a planet `GetHorizonDistance` is the arc between the viewer's
  direction from the centre and the chunk centre's, on the sphere through the viewer's ground point
  (`GetPlanetGroundDistance`; the ground point is the analytic terrain under the viewer, `GetPlanetGroundRadius`, one
  sample when the viewer moves). The horizons are a cone around the viewer's up-line, as a heightmap world's are a
  cylinder, and the viewer's altitude never takes the ground out of range. The viewer-Z clip is gone from
  `GetPlanetShellWindow`. The chunk manager's queue eviction, edit pins, residency audit and the residency snapshot's
  ground reach (vox.Planet, the bench's `GroundReachUU`) follow through `GetHorizonDistance`. LOD bands stay 3D from the
  viewer (SP-C3), so a high viewer's ground disk sits at the coarsest band.
- *The shell from the terrain's real bounds*: `FSphericalPlanetWorldMode::GetDisplacementBounds` within the configured
  `PlanetMaxTerrainHeight` / `Depth` (past which terrain is cut off), + half a chunk; the horizon cull's peaks likewise.
  M's and L's configured shells are their extents + 10%, so their shell windows shrink by that.
- *The per-chunk radial slab.* A chunk loads when its radial extent (its box's nearest point and farthest corner from the
  centre) meets its slab: the surface's altitude range over the cube-sphere cells its eight corner directions span
  (`FVoxelCubeSphereGrid::GatherSpanned`), ± 1.5 chunks (`SlabSlackChunks`, the heightmaps' slack). Cells are about a chunk
  across on the datum sphere (`CellsPerEdgeFor(R, chunk size)`: 82 a face edge on the small planet, 1,637 on M, 32,725 on
  L), a cell's range five samples of `GetTerrainAltitude` (its corners and centre, as a heightmap column's five heights).
  Cells and chunks are memoized (`PlanetCellSurfaceCache`, `PlanetChunkSlabCache`, each starting over past a million
  entries).
- *Near the viewer* (within `GetNearWindowRadius` along the ground: band 0 + two chunks, 16,600 uu): off its slab a chunk
  loads within the viewer's altitude ± 2 chunks inside the shell and is kept while within the unload distance (3D), as a
  heightmap world streams the viewer's layer ± 2 within its height bounds and keeps the whole range near it. Edits off
  the window stay pinned by the chunk manager.
- *Candidates* (`ForEachPlanetCandidate`): the chunk columns along the grid axis closest to the viewer's up inside the box
  of the horizon's cone, crossing the spherical shell of the slab's envelope over the disk (`GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope`,
  memoized by the viewer's cell; `GetShellCrossing`, the old column crossing along any axis), plus the near window's
  cone and band. Load, unload and the balanced LOD cache use the same window.
- `bFarBandSurfaceSlabCulling` off: the whole shell inside the cone (the heightmaps' whole height range).

**Design choices made while building** (none changes a decision):

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| "Distance from the ground point": 3D, or along the ground? | Along the ground (the arc at the ground point's radius) | A ball around the ground point would drop a mountain beside a flyer, which is high above the ground point; the arc is a heightmap world's horizontal distance on a sphere |
| A sea column's slab | The seabed's, with no extension to the sea surface | Planets draw the sea with the ocean shell, not voxel water tiles (`UsesWaterTiles`), so no consumer needs the water volume's chunks; heightmap slabs reach the water plane for their tiles |
| The near window above the slab | Loaded, within the shell (the plan's rule) | A first build left air above the slab out ("no air around a flyer"). In the live survey the settle over L's open sea then held the pawn at the datum for good, waiting on its own chunk's collision, and the spawn's terrain wait counts the chunks around the pawn too. The air costs a flyer inside a thick shell up to about 450 uniform chunks (the climbs below; the first build's climbs held 1,062-1,085) |
| Keep near the viewer | The shell within the unload distance (3D) | A heightmap world keeps its whole height range near the viewer (8 layers on the demo); a planet's shell needs a bound |
| Cell size and samples | About a chunk, five samples | As a heightmap column; the 1.5-chunk slack covers the surface between samples and conditioning's deltas (a Tower pad on M loads whole) |

### 20.5 P6.4 results: the far field (2026-10-19)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `ea3d454`, UE5_PluginDev `4e43e99` (P6.3 merged). Branches `feat/spherical-p6-4-far-field` (VoxelWorlds)
and `claude/spherical-p6-4-far-field` (UE5_PluginDev). P6.4 is WM-BP9 alone: one commit with its tests, and the docs. On
`Review_Planet_M` and `_L` the planet is now drawn to the horizon from the ground and from altitude, where P6.3's shots
showed the voxel window's ragged edge against the sea sphere; at scale the sea is the far field's (G40 fixed); the small
planet keeps its ocean shell and looks as before.

**WM-BP9: the far field** (`FVoxelPlanetFarField`, VoxelStreaming; owned by the chunk manager on planets):

- *Patches.* Six face quadtrees on the cube sphere's surface coordinate (`FVoxelCubeSphere`'s faces and tangent warp):
  level 0 is a face, each level halves a patch along U and V (`FVoxelFarFieldPatchKey`, packed into a `uint64`). A patch
  is 16 x 16 quads (`voxel.World.FarFieldQuads`) of the conditioned analytic surface (`GetConditionedTerrainAltitude`,
  the zones gathered for patches up to 32 chunks in radius) drawn one voxel under it (`Sink`), every patch at every
  level. Normals come from the grid (a ring of samples past the patch's edges, so neighbours agree), the material and
  biome from what generation writes at the surface (`FVoxelSurfaceQuery::QueryPlanetSurfaceConditionsAt`, factored out
  of `QueryPlanetSurfaceConditions` with the same math), one material per quad (the corners' majority, vertices
  duplicated where materials meet). Vertices follow the voxel vertex factory's conventions (UV1 = material and face type
  against local up, colour = material and biome, the tangent cross(Z, N), UV0 the position on the normal's dominant plane
  in voxels relative to the patch), so the terrain material draws a patch as it draws a chunk.
- *Skirts.* Each edge hangs a skirt as deep as the worst gap to a neighbour up to three levels finer (the edge against
  its decimations by 2, 4 and 8) or coarser (the true surface sampled eight times along each edge quad), x 1.25 plus a
  margin; the skirt's bottom vertices are shared along the edge.
- *Selection.* A patch splits while its error (the drawn triangles against the surface at its quad centres, and the
  sea's chord sag) projects to more than `voxel.World.FarFieldError` pixels (2) from the camera, and merges under 0.7 of
  it; a patch whose cap lies wholly under the camera's horizon over the lowest terrain is neither drawn nor split. A
  patch keeps drawing until its children are built, so refining never opens a hole. Builds run on the thread pool, six
  in flight (`voxel.World.FarFieldMaxBuilds`), the roots first and then nearest first; the game thread applies them by a
  serial, so a stale build is dropped.
- *The hole.* Within the window's reach of the viewer's ground point (the unload distance plus a chunk's half diagonal,
  along the ground as WM-BP8 measures its horizons) patches split down to the band level, one to two chunks across
  (`ComputeBandLevel`: 64 a face edge on the small planet, 1,024 on M, 16,384 on L). A band patch hides its terrain once
  every voxel chunk its surface passes through is drawn (`SurfaceChunks`: its vertices', its quad centres' and a vertex
  spacing around each), after the chunks' fade-in (`voxel.MeshFade.Duration` + 0.1 s). A chunk counts as drawn when it
  is loaded, or re-meshing with its old mesh shown (`IsChunkDrawnForFarField`). A patch partly covered stays drawn a
  voxel under the voxel surface: no gap and no overlap along the window's ragged edge, and no far-field floor in a hole
  or a cave wherever the chunks are drawn. Patch geometry never depends on the window: the hole follows it by
  visibility alone, re-evaluated when a chunk changes state (`ChunkStateVersion`).
- *Residency.* One procedural mesh component per resident patch at its origin (its centre's point on the datum, in
  double), vertices float offsets of the patch's size (the render regions' rule, D23): section 0 the terrain, 1 the sea,
  2 its underside, shown and hidden with `SetMeshSectionVisible`. A patch hidden for 10 s releases its mesh and
  component (its subtree draws meanwhile), except the roots and the band patches near the window's edge (beyond 0.75 of
  the load distance), which stay built while covered so they show the moment their chunks unload. A band patch inside
  that with every chunk drawn and no sea is never built (its 9 x 9 surface samples' chunks stand in for its mesh).
- *The sea at scale.* Where the ocean shell's 160 segments a face edge would sag past 8 uu (`ShouldDrawSea`: from about
  R 3.3 x 10^5, so M and L) the far field draws the sea and the chunk manager builds no shell: each patch adds a sea
  section at sea level over its cells whose terrain lies under the sea or within two voxels of it, on an 8 x 8 grid with
  its own UVs (wrapped per patch); the sea sections stay drawn inside the voxel window, which has no water tiles on a
  planet, and the underside is added for patches four levels above the band and finer (seen from under the sea near
  the viewer). The sea's sag counts in the patch's error, so it refines with the terrain.
- *Reporting.* `voxel.World.FarField` (1; off: no far field and the ocean shell as before), `voxel.World.FarFieldStats`,
  `vox.Planet` (patches drawn, terrain, sea, hidden by the window, builds pending and built, ms, MB), and the bench:
  `FarFieldMs`, `FarFieldPatchN`, `FarFieldMB` and `FarFieldBuiltN` per sample, and in the JSON the far field's peak and
  end memory, the patches built and their mean build time, and its end state.

**Design choices made while building** (none changes a decision):

| Question | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Patch size | 16 x 16 quads (17² vertices), not the plan's 33² | Selection is by screen error, so smaller patches draw about as many triangles where they are needed and fewer elsewhere: on L at 45°N 112 → 41 MB and builds about 1 ms instead of 2.4-3.2 |
| Which patches sink | Every patch a voxel under the surface, not only a band at the window's edge | The band's geometry never depends on the window, so the hole moves with no rebuild, and neighbours at different levels meet at one sink (smaller skirts) |
| Where the hole is | Per band patch, hidden when every chunk its surface passes through is drawn | A cap test on the window's disk opens gaps where the disk's edge chunks are still loading or unloading; here a partly covered patch stays drawn under the voxel surface |
| Covered patches' meshes | Released after 10 s hidden (roots and the edge ring kept); covered band patches inside the edge ring with no sea never built | The first live build kept every patch it had ever built (277 MB at L 45°N) |
| The sea | The far field's at scale only; the small planet keeps the shell | The shell is within its budget there (8 uu), and its tests and look stay as they were |
| The sea's grid | 8 x 8 cells a patch, only over the cells near or under the sea | Ocean is flat; the terrain's grid on L's pole took 190 MB, the 8 x 8 grid 88 MB before the patch-size change |
| Face edges | The gnomonic coordinate exactly ±1 at a face edge, so both faces sample the same directions there | The planet terrain steps across the face-edge planes (G43): two faces' patches sampling 10⁻⁸ rad apart split by up to 136 uu on L |
| Normals | The analytic surface's (the grid's) | They equal the planet's `GetConditionedSurfacePoint` normals; the voxel window's LOD 2 ring is the one that is off (G44, fixed in §20.8) |

with `Review_Planet_L`'s noise and ±192,000 relief, with synchronous builds and a coarse view, 300 pixels a radian (a 600-pixel view at 90°) and 4 px):

| `Quadtree` | From 300 uu over the ground at the pole, 45°, the equator and a cube corner, the selection settles; no drawn patch over the error bound; along every edge between drawn patches (sampled at the finer side's vertices and between them) the gap is covered by the skirts; neighbours differ by at most the skirts' three levels | Settled in 10 updates (small) and 17 (1,000 km), 0.26 and 0.51 ms a build; 381-466 and 241-504 patches drawn (levels 2-6 and 3-14, 320-396 and 128-192 of them in the band); worst 3.73-3.99 px against 4, none over; 59,724-125,874 edge samples, the gaps up to 1,073 uu (small) and 75,947 uu (far, coarse levels on the 1,000 km planet), 0 past the skirt; level differences up to 2 |

The first `MatchesSurface` found the terrain stepping across the cube-sphere's face-edge planes, 10-136 uu between two
directions 10⁻⁸ rad apart (G43): the far field now samples a face edge on its plane from both faces, and the test checks the
two faces' vertices along x = z.

### 20.6 P6.5 results: orbit and back, and game systems at scale (2026-10-19)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `6b35d64`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `c7252f6`, WorldClockPlugin `0ce2ce2`, UE5_PluginDev `e6691f1` (P6.4
merged). Branches `feat/spherical-p6-5-orbit` (VoxelWorlds, VoxelCharacterPlugin, WorldClockPlugin) and
`claude/spherical-p6-5-orbit` (UE5_PluginDev, with VoxelWorldPOI and the game module). P6.5 is WM-BP10 and WM-BP11. On
`Review_Planet_M` and `_L` the player can now fly from the surface to 2 R and back to a landing, at the pole and the
equator, with the planet drawn at every altitude. Above a cut-over altitude the voxel window unloads and the far field
alone draws the planet. The window streams back ahead of the descending camera. Landing is on cooked ground or in the
water. The sky and its clouds are scaled to the planet. The spawn, the map, the NPC cells, navigation and scatter work on
the 1,000 km planet. Fixed on the way: G36 and G41 (planned), plus G46-G48, G50 and G51, found during the surveys (G47 and G50 had made a
dungeon stamp and the world map on L hold the game thread for minutes). G49 and G52 are recorded (G52 fixed since, §20.7). G45 stays open.

The cut-over's default changed during the milestone: from the view distance to three view distances, after the descent
benches. Budgets hold (D3: at most 964 MB peak, 491-543 MB settled with the far field). In orbit the voxel systems hold
14-77 MB, against 253-309 kept. A descent at 5,000 uu/s from 200,000 lands with the window ready within 0.2-3.7 s.

**WM-BP10: orbit and back** (D18):

- *The cut-over* (`FDistanceBandLODStrategy`, `IVoxelLODStrategy::IsWindowSuspended` / `GetCutoverAltitude` /
  `GetViewerSurfaceAltitude`). From high up the voxel window holds nothing the far field does not draw as well, so a
  planet's window is suspended while the streaming viewer is more than the cut-over over the surface under it (the
  analytic terrain along its direction, or the sea where that is higher: a flyer skimming a deep sea keeps its window)
  and resumes below 0.85 of it (`CutoverResumeFraction`; a flyer hovering at the cut-over does not churn). The cut-over
  is `UVoxelWorldConfiguration::PlanetVoxelCutoverAltitude` (new; 0 = three view distances,
  `FDistanceBandLODStrategy::DefaultCutoverViewDistances`, 120,000 uu on the review planets; one view distance at first,
  raised after the descent benches below), overridden by `voxel.World.VoxelCutover` (-1 the configuration's, 0 never: the window keeps its ground disk at
  any altitude, as WM-BP8 made it). Suspended, the strategy offers no candidate and unloads every chunk, its balanced
  LOD cache empty; the chunk manager evicts its queues (`ReprioritizeQueues`), stale-culls what finishes generating, and
  neither pins nor keeps edited chunks (their edits stay in the edit layers and load with the window). On M the window's
  1,263 chunks unload in about 2 s.
- *The far field without a window.* While chunks are held the far field cuts its hole as in P6.4; once the window holds
  none it refines by its screen error alone (`BandRadius` and `PrebuildRadius` 0: no band patches forced around an empty
  window). When the window resumes the band returns, its patches build while their parents draw, and the chunks appear
  over them with the appearance fade.
- *The camera and the streaming viewer.* The chunk manager now keeps both: the camera (`GetCameraPosition`) and the
  streaming viewer (`GetStreamingViewerPosition`), equal except under the descent prefetch. The window, the LOD bands and
  the cut-over are the streaming viewer's; the far field's error and horizon culling, its sea test and the appearance
  fade (`MeshRenderer->SetViewerPosition`) the camera's; `BuildStreamingContext` gives every other caller (the bench's
  backlog, the debug draw) the same context.
- *The descent prefetch* (`UVoxelChunkManager::ApplyDescentPrefetch`, `ComputeDescentLead`). Under a camera descending
  faster than `voxel.Stream.DescentMinSpeed` (1,500 uu/s) the streaming viewer goes ahead of it along local down by what
  it covers in `voxel.Stream.DescentLead` seconds (3), at most half its altitude over the surface and never within two
  chunks of it. The camera's radial speed is smoothed (`FInterpTo`, 4/s) and starts over after a jump of ten chunks in a
  frame (a teleport or a change of view target). The first version led by speed alone: an exponential descent at
  hundreds of thousands of uu/s put the viewer at the ground from 3.5 × 10⁶ uu and the window resumed and suspended
  every few frames; the half-altitude cap keeps the lead proportional.
- *The sky at scale* (WorldClockPlugin, `ADayNightController::ApplyPlanetSky`). The engine's atmosphere is Earth's: 60 km
  over a 6,360 km ground, a glowing ball 24 times the small planet's size from orbit. With `bScalePlanetSky` (on) it is
  scaled by K = clamp(max(R / 6,360 km, 4 × the terrain's top / 60 km), 10⁻⁴, 1) (`ComputePlanetSkyScale`,
  `PlanetAtmosphereOverTerrain` 4): the height, the Rayleigh and Mie scale heights, the ozone tent and the aerial
  perspective's distance by K, the scattering and absorption by 1/K, so a column of air holds what the authored one
  holds and the sky looks as authored from the ground. The terrain's top comes from the planet clock bridge
  (`UWorldClockSubsystem::SetPlanetFrame(Centre, SeaRadius, TerrainTop)`, VoxelWorldPOI: the world mode's altitude
  bounds over the sea). The volumetric cloud layers go with it (`ComputePlanetCloudLayer`: the thickness by K, the floor
  the authored floor by K but at least the terrain's top; G46). Small planet K 0.0047 (0.28 km of air), M 0.162 (9.7 km),
  L 0.563 (33.8 km). A space exposure (`bPlanetSpaceExposure`, a second unbound post-process,
  `SpaceExposurePostProcess`): auto-exposure meters the brightest part of the view (histogram 70-98%) with a weight
  that rises from half the atmosphere's height to one and a half (`ComputeSpaceExposureWeight`), so the sunlit planet
  keeps its daylight exposure from orbit instead of washing out against black.
- *Landing* (the game module's debug flight, `UVoxelDebugSubsystem`). `vox.Fly 0` arms a landing hold: while the pawn
  falls within max(2 chunks, its descent speed × 1 s) of land whose chunk has no cooked collision, it is held
  (`MOVE_None`) until the chunk cooks, then let go (`Landing hold: ...`, `Landing: on the ground / in the water after N
  landing hold(s)`); a timeout lets go for good. It never engages while the window is suspended: with the cut-over
  under its two chunks (a test at 2,000 uu) it held the pawn where nothing could load, until the timeout. The settle
  (`vox.TP`, `vox.TPLatLon`, the orbit camera's release) already held until collision; a settle with no land within
  reach goes onto the sea's surface and says so.
- *G36: land at scale* (VoxelCharacterPlugin). `FVCVoxelNavigationHelper::FindPlanetSpawnPointAtScale`: rings around the
  start direction at a quarter of their angle (at most 3.5°), at most 4,096 samples, out to the antipode;
  `FindSpawnablePosition(..., bAnywhereOnPlanet)` uses it for the character's first spawn. A planet with no land above
  its sea spawns the pawn at the sea's surface (`bSpawnAtSea`, swimming). The debug settle with no land within reach
  settles onto the sea's surface along the direction instead of hanging (`TeleportPawn: no land within reach ...`).
- *G48: a held pawn in water* (VoxelCharacterPlugin). The movement component's water check switched a pawn with movement
  disabled back to swimming, so the orbit camera's hold did not hold a swimmer: it sank through the seabed the window had
  unloaded. No swimming transition from `MOVE_None` now.
- *G41: the camera's teleport sweep* (VoxelCharacterPlugin). `UVCThirdPersonCameraMode::ComputeLaggedPivot`: the lagged
  pivot snaps to the ideal one when that jumps more than `TeleportSnapDistance` (5,000 uu) in a frame, so a teleport no
  longer sweeps the camera, and the streaming viewer with it, through the planet.
- *Tooling.* `vox.FlyTo <altitude> [seconds]` (an exponential climb or descent to an altitude over the surface in debug
  flight, holding there; progress at each quarter with the window's state and the far field's patches and memory),
  `vox.Planet`'s window line (active or suspended, the streaming viewer over the surface, the cut-over, the lead), the
  bench's descent route (`descend=Lat:Lon:Alt`) and its `Suspended`, `LeadUU`, `SurfAlt` columns and `voxelCutover`
  summary. The capture's fall-through comparison skips flight, the landing hold and the orbit camera's hold.

**WM-BP11: game systems at scale:**

- *The world map's zoom range from R* (VoxelCharacterPlugin, `UVCWorldMapWidget::GetPlanetZoomRange`): the outermost
  zoom shows the whole globe on any planet (0.9 of the panel), the innermost a tile at its size, so the wheel reaches
  both on L (where the old fixed minimum, 0.25, showed about 12 km across). `vox.Map [zoom|min|0]` opens it at a zoom.
- *A coarse globe albedo* (VoxelMap, `UVoxelMapSubsystem::GetGlobeAlbedo`): 256 cells a face edge of the analytic
  surface's colour (the far field's surface queries, `FVoxelFarFieldSurface`; built once on the thread pool, 0.04 s on L)
  with the tiles' colouring rules, explored by cell (`IsGlobeCellExplored`). The globe
  samples it below half a texel per tile (`FVCPlanetMapProjection::bUseGlobeAlbedo`), where per-tile images would be
  millions of tiles on L.
- *`ExploreAll` at scale* (`ExploreAllTiles` returns `int64`; `voxel.Map.ExploreAllMaxTiles`, 1,000,000): on a planet
  it marks the tiles nearest the pawn first (`FVoxelCubeSphereGrid::GatherWithinAngle`) up to the cap and queues images
  for the nearest 65,536; L's atlas is 32,725 tiles a face edge, 6.4 × 10⁹ tiles (an `int32` count overflowed).
- *G50: markers on a zoomed-out globe* (VoxelWorldPOI, `UPOIMapMarkerSubsystem::GetPlanetMarkersNear`): the globe asks
  for the markers of all it shows, and P6.1's cap (G37) is the whole planet for such a range: L's 36 million POI cells,
  the game thread held about 1 min 45 s. The far markers now come from at most `PlanetMarkerMaxCells` (20,000) cells
  around the query's direction (the small planet's 294 whole, a fifth of M's 90,774), and the half-second refresh
  reuses the last cap's POIs; the map draws at most 64 markers.
- *The globe's redraws* (VoxelCharacterPlugin, `UVCWorldMapWidget`): at the albedo's zoom the tile images do not show,
  so a tile's arrival no longer redraws the globe at once (at most every 2 s, for the exploration they carry): after an
  `ExploreAll` on M (16 million tiles, 65,536 images queued) a redraw per arrival held the open map at 6.5 FPS; it holds
  60. `ExploreAllTiles` sorts the whole atlas by precomputed keys (52 s for M's 16 million with the cap raised, from 79;
  the default cap takes about 1 s on any planet).
- *NPC cells* (VoxelWorldPOI): the population cells keep `CellSize` at any radius, their atlas coordinates fit
  `MakeNPCId`'s 20-bit fields up to L (94,248 a row), and the members planned per cell match the small planet's.
- *Navigation, scatter and the surface queries on the precise altitude*: P6.2's double CPU math and noise already carry
  them; the planet path and the scatter along local up now also run on a 1,000 km planet.
- *G47: edits without a centre* (VoxelNavigation). System edits (dungeon stamps, region edits, edit loads) broadcast the
  zero vector and radius 0, and the navigation invalidated a box there; on a planet that is the centre, whose box
  projected into every cached region's frame spanned the planet: on L a dungeon stamp near the pawn held the game thread
  for minutes. Such an edit now invalidates the edited chunk's bounds (on every world mode), corners deep inside the
  planet project into no frame, and a rectangle larger than the cache visits only its cached tiles.
- *Saves*: the fingerprint is unchanged in shape (world mode, radius, shell, centre, grid, `PlanetGenerationVersion` 5);
  P6.5 changes no generation.

  keeps its ground disk at any altitude.

new and ctl on every route, interleaved. Means of three runs (catch-up per run). JSON and CSV are in `Saved/VoxelBench`
of the worktree.

- **The great circle** never nears the cut-over, so new and ctl run the same code but the prefetch's per-frame check:
  - S: identical.
  - L: the runs overlap (frame P95 31.8-41.1 against 31.5-34.6 ms).
  - M: two of the new runs were slower in every section alike, scatter, seams, meshing and the LOD update 10-15% each
    (frame P95 34.7-40.3 against 34.1-34.8). That is the machine, not one terrain query a frame.
- **The climb through the cut-over:**
  - The window unloads at 40,000. At the top (60,200) the voxel systems hold 9-74 MB against 262-487 kept.
  - Frame and manager P95 stay equal or lower.
  - Peak memory is the same (it peaks on the ground).
- **The descent from above the cut-over:**
  - The window, unloaded at 100,000, resumed only with the camera about 48,000 over the ground (the lead is at most half
    the altitude: 15,000 at 5,000 uu/s), 10 s before arrival.
  - M's and L's windows (about 1,300 chunks on km relief) stream back at 65-160 chunks a second, so they touched down
    with half of it loaded. LOD 0 and 1 were complete; the far field drew the outer ring under the appearance fade.
  - Catch-up was 5.2 s on M and 5.5 s on L, against 0.36 and 0.26 kept. On the small planet it was 0.30 against 0.17.
  - Peak memory was 1,128-1,230 MB (fresh, uncompressed chunks), against 860-905: still under D3's 1.5 GB.
  - The control's frame P95 on the way down was the worse one, 35.6-37.4 ms against 29.6-30.2: it re-meshed its 1,500
    chunks' LOD 1,226-1,250 times under the descending viewer.
  - This is why the default became three view distances (above): from there a descent at 5,000 uu/s has about 20 s.

### 20.7 G52: the near band reaches no higher than the slab (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `2dc80ac`, UE5_PluginDev `5f6a8f2` (P6.5 merged). Branches `fix/g52-near-band-air` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g52-near-band-air` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8091), background throttling off.

**The cause.** P6.3's near band (`IsInPlanetWindow`, Load) adds, within `GetNearWindowRadius` (16,600 uu) of the viewer
along the ground, the chunks off their slab that meet the viewer's altitude ± 2 chunks: caves, dungeons and digging
under the surface, and the chunks a terrain wait reads around the viewer. It followed the streaming viewer at any
altitude inside the shell, and the shells of `Review_Planet_M` and `_L` reach about 2 km over the datum. Every chunk it
added there was air. It cost three things:

- **Descending.** At 5,000 uu/s the viewer crosses a chunk layer a second, and the band loaded a new layer of air around
  it each second. These chunks were the nearest to the viewer, so they generated first. The queue evicts by the horizon
  alone (along the ground, where they are at 0), so layers the viewer had passed still generated. The descent from
  200,000 peaked at 1,331-1,356 loaded chunks against 1,081-1,105, re-meshed 1,220 chunks for LOD changes against about
  160, and the window touched down 1.7-2.8 s behind the camera (the clean runs below; 0.8-12 s in P6.5's and this
  session's busier runs).
- **Climbing.** The same layers went up with a climbing viewer to the cut-over: a climb to 200,200 peaked at 1,534-1,547
  chunks against 1,090-1,123, with 1,320-1,338 LOD re-meshes against 78-80 and a frame P95 of 23.5-23.8 ms against 16.7.
- **With the window kept** (`voxel.World.VoxelCutover 0`, P6.4's behaviour and P6.5's control), both, all the way down
  and up.

**The fix** (`FDistanceBandLODStrategy`):

- **The band's ceiling** (`GetPlanetNearBandCeiling`): the top of the surface slab over the near disk, plus
  `SlabSlackChunks` (1.5). That is the highest analytic surface the near chunks' slabs read: `GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope`
  over the near radius's widest angle (at the shell's inner radius, plus half a chunk diagonal, `PlanetNearBandAngle`),
  memoized by the viewer's cell. Where the sea's surface is higher, the ceiling is the sea's surface plus the same slack.
- **The rule.** The band reaches no higher than the ceiling: its Load top is the viewer's altitude + 2 chunks or the
  ceiling, whichever is lower. A viewer above the ceiling takes no band (`IsPlanetNearBandActive`).
  `ForEachPlanetCandidate` enumerates the band's Load to the ceiling only.
- **Why nothing is lost.** Every near chunk's slab reads cells inside the envelope, so its slab top is at most the
  ceiling. A chunk off its slab that lies wholly above the ceiling therefore lies above its own slab: air, unless edited,
  and the chunk manager pins edited chunks. With the viewer above the ceiling, no band chunk can lie below its slab
  either (the band's bottom, 2 chunks under the viewer, is over every slab bottom in the disk), so the whole band is air.
- **What keeps the band:**
  - viewers inside or below the slab (caves, dungeons, a flyer near the ground);
  - the spawn's terrain wait: its 3 × 3 grid in the tangent plane at the pawn and the chunk under its feet lie under
    the ceiling;
  - the settle onto the sea, which waits for the chunk at the sea's surface to cook. This is why the sea is in the
    ceiling.
- **The keep window is unchanged:** a viewer crossing the ceiling unloads nothing near it, so the band does not churn
  there.
- **The first version** dropped the band above the ceiling but did not cap it. The benches showed the band switching back
  on at the ceiling about 1.5 s before landing and queueing 55-65 chunks of air at its top (the chunks between the slab
  top and the viewer + 2 chunks), which the old band had loaded on its way down: on the busy first batch L touched down
  1.0-1.6 s behind, the window kept as well (it ran the same rule), and on the quiet machine 0.28-0.44 s (the "no cap"
  rows below). Hence the cap.
- `GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope` takes the caller's memo (the load disk's and the near disk's are kept apart), and
  `GetDebugInfo` prints the band's state and ceiling.

Heightmap worlds are unchanged: their near window is already clipped to the terrain's height bounds.

### 20.8 G44 and G25: vertex normals at a stride and at chunk faces (2026-10-20)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `5907e2d`, UE5_PluginDev `98b2a85` (the demo caves merged). Branches `fix/g44-lod2-normals`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g44-lod2-normals` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8094), background throttling off.

**The cause** (G44). Not the far field, the scene proxy or the vertex factory: generation does not depend on the LOD
(every chunk holds its voxels at voxel resolution), and every chunk and seam mesh in the game comes from the CPU Dual
Contouring mesher. Its crossing normals are central differences with taps `Stride` voxels either side
(`CalculateGradientNormalLOD`, and each seam sampler's `GradientNormal`). Generated density saturates a voxel either
side of the surface: `SignedDistanceToDensity` clamps the signed distance to ±1 voxel. At stride 4 every tap the surface
does not pass within a voxel of reads 0 or 255, so each component of the gradient is a sign, and the cell's normal (the
average of its crossings') snaps toward one of the 26 cube directions. On a planet, local up at 45°N 20°E is about
(0.66, 0.24, 0.71), and LOD 2 leaned toward the diagonal (1, 1, 1) / √3: the near-white ring in P6.4's normal buffer,
and under the noon sun a ring 16% brighter than the LOD 0 centre (the window's mean grey 118 against 102,
`g44f_L_45N_top_n0`). LOD 1 (stride 2) leaned less, the dimmer square inside the ring. On a heightmap flat ground shows
nothing (up is an axis), but slopes snap: bright streaks on `VoxelDemo`'s rocky hills from above (`g44f_demo_top_n0`)
and a light line across a far hill's slope (`g44f_demo_oblique_n0`). A simulation of the estimator on a plane at 45°N
20°E put LOD 2's mean normal 16° off, LOD 1's 5° off, and LOD 0's 1° off.

**G25 on the way.** With G44's normals in, the seams along every Z chunk face of the LOD 2 band lit up as bright dashed
strips one cell wide, there in a fresh PIE too (`g44_L_close_fresh_n1`). They had been there all along, faintly
(`g44_L_45N_top_n0`: the same rows, 3.5 grey levels over the background against 10.7 with G44's normals alone). Their
cause is the clamp that makes a mesh job independent of its neighbours: the gradient's taps clamp into the job's voxels
("the terrain continues"), so at a chunk face the clamped axis's difference is one-sided and has up to half the weight
of the other two. The normals of the cells along the face lean away from it. At 45°N, under the noon sun, losing X or Y
darkens and losing Z brightens: P6.4's dark dotted diagonal lines along the X and Y faces and the faint bright ones
along the Z faces, at every LOD. That is G25 (the lines across the City's flat pad, §19.2.3), which this measures on
natural terrain.

**What changed** (`VoxelCPUDualContourMesher.cpp`; no change to generation, positions or seam ownership):

- **Vertex normals at a stride** (`VoxelDCShading`). The QEF keeps the stride-scale crossing normals, so no vertex moves
  and every seam, closure and collision mesh is the same. Only the cell's vertex normal changes. For each strided edge
  with a crossing, the cell finds where the surface crosses it at voxel resolution (`FindVoxelCrossing`, the first of
  its `Stride` voxel steps that changes sign). Its vertex normal is the normal LOD 0 gives the voxel cell inside the
  strided cell next to the crossing nearest the vertex (`VoxelCellNormal`: the stride-1 gradient normals at that voxel
  cell's crossings, averaged in `CellEdges` order): LOD 0's estimator with LOD 0's footprint. `SolveCellVertices` and
  the seam template (`ComputeCellVertex`) run the same op sequence through each view's density and gradient, and every
  voxel read lies inside the strided cell, so ring recomputes stay bit-identical. `voxel.Mesh.VoxelShadingNormals` (1; 0
  = the stride-scale normals before G44).
- **Clamped gradients** (`VoxelDCGradient::ClampedGradientNormal`), used by the interior pass and the face, edge and
  corner seam samplers: a clamped axis's difference is scaled back to the full span (`2 · Stride / span`). Where nothing
  clamps the result is the old central difference, bit for bit. `voxel.Mesh.ScaleClampedGradients` (1; 0 = before).
- **The estimator.** Three were measured on the test worlds below (before the clamp fix) on the ±800 relief:
  - Averaging the voxel-scale gradients of all the strided cell's crossings smooths the normals over the 4-voxel cell
    and lights brightest. LOD 2 is +7.4% against the analytic surface at 45°N and +21.6% on the plane, where LOD 0 is
    +1.0% and +8.0%.
  - One gradient sample at the crossing nearest the vertex lights less bright (+6.8%, +12.8%) but scatters most. LOD 2's
    mean angle is 15.4° and 32.4°.
  - LOD 0's cell normal at that crossing (chosen) lights like the single sample (+6.5%, +15.8%) with less scatter
    (11.7°, 26.0°).

**Tests** (`VoxelStreaming/Tests/VoxelPlanetStreamingTests.cpp`, the closed-surface tests' worlds: the planet of radius
20,000 with voxel 50 and chunk 32, the plane with voxel 100 and chunk 16, three LOD bands, CPU generation, a fresh world
per case with the cvar set before it streams). For every vertex and triangle of the chunk meshes and seam buckets, by
the LOD of the chunk it lies in, against `GetSurfacePointAt`'s normal on its up-line: the mean angle, the tilt (the mean
of normal minus analytic normal across local east and north) and the brightness (triangle area × the Lambert term with
the interpolated normal at the centroid against the analytic normal's, under the local noon sun; overhead on the plane).

- **`Streaming.Planet.LODNormals`** (new): 45°N 20°E and the equator. With gentle relief (±200, two octaves of 50 and 25
  voxels; LOD 2 resolves them) LOD 1 and 2 must tilt at most 1.5° more than LOD 0, light within LOD 0's brightness error
  + 2%, and stay within 1.5 × LOD 0's mean angle + 5°. The stride-scale normals must fail that bound. With the streaming
  tests' relief (±800, three octaves; the finest, 12.5 voxels, is finer than LOD 2 resolves) the mean angle must fall.
- **`Streaming.Plane.LODNormals`** (new): the same on the plane (gentle: one octave of 25 voxels).
- **`Streaming.Planet.ChunkFaceShading`** (new, G25): 45°N 20°E and the equator, gentle relief. Triangles within 1.5
  cells of an X, Y or Z chunk face must light within 3% of the interior's at LOD 0, 1 and 2. The unscaled clamp must
  fail at one of the places.

The vertex counts are the same with either normals (no vertex moves). On the default relief what is left of the
brightness difference is the coarse triangles interpolating normals across 4 voxels, not the estimator; the far field's
quads near the window do the same with the analytic normals. The plane's LOD 2 keeps a 7° mean angle on gentle hills:
its vertex normal is a voxel cell's up to a cell away on 27° slopes. Its tilt (0.58°) and brightness (+0.17%) are LOD
0's.

| Place (ChunkFaceShading), LOD | Interior | X faces | Y faces | Z faces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 45°N, LOD 0, unscaled → scaled | +1.76% → +1.79% | -7.28% → +1.37% | +0.96% → +1.71% | +7.69% → -0.23% |
| 45°N, LOD 1 | +1.63% → +1.63% | -2.13% → +2.36% | +1.45% → +1.78% | +5.02% → +0.67% |
| 45°N, LOD 2 | +1.22% → +1.21% | -3.17% → +0.96% | +0.95% → +1.18% | +3.20% → +0.24% |
| Equator, LODs 0-2 | -1.0 to -1.5% | within 1.2% of the interior either way | | |

On the equator the surface's normal is along X, so no face clamps a component that matters. The clamp fix also brings
LOD 0's normals closer to the analytic ones wherever the surface crosses chunk faces obliquely: the mean angle at 45°N
falls from 3.29° to 1.90° (gentle) and 4.35° to 3.73° (±800), and on the plane's two-octave gentle hills from 7.16° to
2.46°.

**New finding** (in §14.1):

| ID | Finding | Status |
|----|---------|--------|
| G61 | Marching Cubes' LOD normals use the same stride-scale taps (`FVoxelCPUMarchingCubesMesher::CalculateGradientNormalLOD`, and the GPU shader's `CalculateGradientNormalLOD`), so an MC world's LOD 1 and 2 would lean the same way. No shipped configuration uses MC (the planets and `VoxelDemo` are DC) | Fixed in §20.9: an MC edge vertex at stride > 1 takes LOD 0's normal at the voxel crossing on its edge, CPU and GPU |

**Left as they were:**

- Cubic meshing has face normals and no gradients.
- The retired GPU DC mesher's shader keeps its stride-scale normals; it meshes nothing
  (`voxel.Seam.CPUInteriorRouting`).
- What is left at LOD 2 on rough terrain is the coarse mesh's own smoothing: its triangles interpolate normals across 4
  voxels. The far field does the same across its quads, with the analytic normals.
- The clamp's one-sided difference leaves LOD 0's Z faces at 45°N 2% darker than the interior (from 6% brighter), under
  the 3% bound; a neighbour's voxels would close it, at the cost of the neighbour independence seam ownership relies on.

G44 and G25 are fixed.

### 20.9 G61: Marching Cubes' vertex normals at a stride (2026-10-21)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `fed44dc`, UE5_PluginDev `93e7812` (G44 and G60 merged). Branches `fix/g61-mc-lod-normals`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g61-mc-lod-normals` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The cause.** G44's in Marching Cubes. An MC vertex at stride > 1 took its normal from a central difference with taps
`Stride` voxels either side of it (`FVoxelCPUMarchingCubesMesher::CalculateGradientNormalLOD`, and the GPU shader's
`CalculateGradientNormalLOD` in `MarchingCubesMeshGeneration.usf`). The generated density saturates a voxel either side
of the surface, so at stride 4 each component read 0 or 255 and the normal snapped toward one of the 26 cube directions.
That covered both the regular cells (`ProcessCubeLOD`, interiors and the seam bands, which drive the same function) and
the transition ribbon (`ProcessTransitionCell`, its outer face at the coarser neighbour's stride). An MC world showed the
same ring as DC's on a planet and the same snapped slopes on a heightmap. No shipped configuration meshes with MC.

**What changed** (`VoxelCPUMarchingCubesMesher.cpp`, `MarchingCubesMeshGeneration.usf`; no change to generation,
positions, seams or the geomorph):

- **An edge vertex's normal at a stride** (`CalculateEdgeShadingNormal`). An MC vertex lies on one cell edge. At stride >
  1 the edge is walked in voxel steps from its min end, and the step whose crossing lies nearest the vertex gives the
  normal: LOD 0's own (`CalculateGradientNormal`, taps one voxel apart) at that crossing. That is the normal LOD 0's vertex
  there has. The normal is a function of the edge alone, so every cell and ribbon that shares the edge gives its vertex the
  same normal, and the boundary geomorph (which moves vertices, not edges) does not change it. The walk reads voxels on the
  edge and the gradient reads one voxel around the crossing, which is less than the old taps' `Stride`, so no mesh job
  reads past the data it held before. `ProcessCubeLOD` now computes one normal per cell vertex instead of three per
  triangle. In `ProcessTransitionCell` each vertex uses its own normal stride: the coarser neighbour's on the outer face,
  where the coarse MC cell has the same edge, and this chunk's on the inner face.
- **The GPU shader** has the same function (`CalculateEdgeShadingNormal`, `UseVoxelShadingNormals`, parameter
  `VoxelShadingNormals` set by `FVoxelGPUMarchingCubesMesher` from the cvar) in `MainCS` and `TransitionCS`. The GPU MC
  mesher meshes nothing in the game (`voxel.Seam.CPUInteriorRouting`); it is kept consistent for its tests.
- **One switch for both smooth meshers.** `voxel.Mesh.VoxelShadingNormals` (1; 0 = the stride-scale normals) was G44's
  (DC only). It is now shared: `CVarVoxelShadingNormals` lives in the DC mesher and the MC CPU and GPU meshers use it
  through an `extern`. With 0, and at LOD 0 in either setting, MC's normals are the old ones bit for bit.
- **Left on the stride-scale gradient:** the transition cell's folded-triangle check (debug only). A coarse triangle's
  centroid can lie more than a voxel off the surface, where LOD 0's taps all read saturated density; the snapped
  direction is enough for a test against a fold of more than ~95°.

**Tests.**

- **`Streaming.Planet.LODNormalsMC`, `Streaming.Plane.LODNormalsMC`** (new): G44's `LODNormals` places, reliefs and
  bounds on MC worlds (`FPlanetStreamingWorld::MeshingMode`; `RunLODNormalsPlace` takes the meshing mode). On gentle relief
  LOD 1 and 2 must meet G44's bound, and the stride-scale normals must fail it. On the streaming tests' relief the mean
  angle must fall. Every vertex of the chunk meshes and seam buckets is measured, with the vertex counts equal in both
  settings.
- **`Meshing.MarchingCubes.LODNormals`** (new): a plane tilted 23° whose density saturates a voxel either side, at LOD 0, 1
  and 2 on one chunk. LOD 1 and 2 must stay within a degree of LOD 0's error, LOD 0 must be the same in both settings, and
  the old LOD 2 must be off by more than 3° over LOD 0's. With a real RHI it also meshes each case on the GPU and matches
  every GPU vertex to the CPU vertex at its position to compare their normals. Before → after, LOD 0/1/2: 3.34° / 12.50° /
  23.75° → 3.34° / 3.64° / 3.31°. GPU against CPU: every GPU vertex is at a CPU vertex, with normals 0.03-0.06° apart on
  average and at most 0.13°, at every LOD in both settings.

| Place, LOD | Mean angle before → after (LOD 0) | Tilt before → after | Brightness before → after (LOD 0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Planet 45°N, gentle, LOD 1 | 7.51° → 2.15° (2.46°) | 3.89° → 0.92° | +5.08% → +1.75% (+1.72%) |
| Planet 45°N, gentle, LOD 2 | 13.40° → 2.15° | 6.18° → 0.62° | +3.46% → +1.18% |
| Planet equator, gentle, LOD 1 | 9.27° → 2.93° (2.69°) | 1.24° → 0.39° | -5.11% → -1.47% (-1.16%) |
| Planet equator, gentle, LOD 2 | 20.29° → 3.29° | 3.10° → 0.57° | -16.65% → -1.78% |
| Plane, gentle, LOD 1 | 10.53° → 3.79° (4.30°) | 0.83° → 0.33° | -6.29% → -1.74% (-2.56%) |
| Plane, gentle, LOD 2 | 18.08° → 4.45° | 1.85° → 0.06° | -12.06% → -0.49% |
| Planet 45°N, ±800, LOD 1 / 2 | 11.69° / 17.44° → 5.01° / 5.94° (5.22°) | 0.56° / 0.73° → 0.20° / 0.01° | +4.48% / +10.30% → +2.16% / +4.74% (+0.81%) |
| Planet equator, ±800, LOD 1 / 2 | 10.21° / 16.61° → 4.31° / 5.42° (4.41°) | 0.51° / 1.38° → 0.20° / 0.19° | -4.47% / -5.40% → -0.71% / +1.90% (-1.96%) |
| Plane, ±800, LOD 1 / 2 | 19.34° / 30.16° → 11.38° / 13.18° (11.94°) | 0.49° / 2.18° → 0.21° / 0.67° | +21.9% / +24.1% → +10.4% / +14.7% (+4.7%) |

The stride-scale normals fail the gentle bound on the tilt at 45°N (LOD 1 3.89° against LOD 0's 1.13°), on the mean
angle on the equator (LOD 1 9.27° against 2.74°) and on the brightness on the plane (LOD 1 -6.29% against -2.56%). LOD 0's
own figures move a little between the two settings: its chunks' transition ribbons carry outer-face vertices at the
coarser neighbour's stride, which the old estimator snapped too (on the gentle plane LOD 0's mean angle 4.53° → 4.30°).
MC's LOD 1 and 2 now match LOD 0 more closely than DC's do in §20.8 (gentle plane LOD 2 4.45° against LOD 0's 4.30°, DC
7.11° against 2.55°). An MC vertex sits on the edge whose crossing it takes its normal from, while a DC vertex can be a
cell away from its voxel crossing.

**Meshing cost.** `Review_Planet_L` in MC at 45°N 20°E, pawn held, `voxel.RemeshAll` (1,267 chunk meshes, 6,564 seam
jobs) with `voxel.Edit.MeshWork`'s worker times, the two settings alternated three times in one PIE. Chunk meshes took

run-to-run spread). A strided vertex's normal now reads `Stride` + 5 voxels once per cell vertex, where the old one read 6 for
each triangle using the vertex. Seam jobs took 50.3-51.6 s with either setting; that is MC's own seam cost
(G63, below), not G61's.
