CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change). The MC seam and closure tests pass unchanged:
`Meshing.MarchingCubes.*` (30, including `SeamClosure.MCS0-MCS3`, `LODBoundary.T1-T13`, `CPUvsGPU` and
`PlanetGeomorph`), `Streaming.EditRemesh.{Plane,Planet}` (MC LOD cases) and `Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.ClosedSurface`.
The DC `LODNormals` figures are §20.8's to the hundredth.

**New findings** (in §14.1):

| ID | Finding | Status |
|----|---------|--------|
| G62 | The stride-1 gradient both smooth meshers use (`CalculateGradientNormal`: the crossing floored to a voxel, taps one voxel either side on the one-voxel density ramp) bands along voxel layers. With the surface a fraction f of a voxel above the floored voxel, the vertical difference is 1 - f/2 instead of 1, so a slope's normal tilts by 1.0-1.8 times the slope (5°: 5.0-9.1°; 15°: 15.0-22.9°) depending on where the surface crosses the voxel layer. MC's LOD 0 has the bands a voxel layer apart, too fine to see from altitude. DC's LOD 0 uses the same gradient, averaged over a cell's crossings (not measured here). Since G61, MC's LOD 1 and 2 sample the same estimator sparsely, which shows from altitude as faint broad rings around hills. A gradient taken at the crossing point itself (trilinear taps, as the geomorph's steepness gate does) has no such dependence | Fixed in §20.12: both meshers' shading normals at voxel resolution are the density gradient fitted to the voxels on the ramp around the point |
| G63 | Marching Cubes seam jobs cost about 23 times Dual Contouring's on `Review_Planet_L` at 45°N 20°E: 6,564 MC seam jobs took 50-52 s of worker time (7.7 ms each) against 5,673 DC seam jobs in 1.7-2.0 s (0.33 ms each, §20.8). MC's chunk meshes cost about the same as DC's (1.6 ms each). Not traced; the seam path builds a synthetic request per participant (`InitFrameRequest` copies the volume, `FillFacePlanes` fills the neighbour planes) and meshes its band cells through `ProcessCubeLOD` | Open (not traced): MC is unshipped |

**Left as they were:**

- The GPU MC mesher's neighbour data is one plane deep, so taps past a chunk face read that plane. They did before as
  well, and the GPU mesher meshes nothing in the game.
- MC's LOD 0 estimator (G62).

G61 is fixed.

### 20.10 G42: scatter's HISM writes, batched (2026-10-21)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `fed44dc`, UE5_PluginDev `93e7812` (G44 merged). Branches `fix/g42-planet-scatter-cost`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g42-planet-scatter-cost` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8096), background throttling off. This follows G61's §20.9
(draquel/VoxelWorlds#130, merged first; main merged into this branch).

**Profiling.** Instruments first, kept in the build:

- The bench's CSV gained the scatter section's steps: `ScatEditMs` (edit readers), `ScatApplyMs` (completed
  extractions), `ScatLaunchMs`, `ScatDistMs` (the distance spawn), `ScatFlushMs` (the renderer's instance flush). It also
  gained the extractions applied and launched, the HISM instances placed and released (`ScatAddN`, `ScatRelN`), and the
  engine's game-thread, render-thread and GPU times (`GTMs`, `RTMs`, `GPUMs`, `stat unit`'s).
- `TRACE_CPUPROFILER` scopes on the scatter manager's and renderer's steps, and a trace region over the bench's traverse
  (`VoxelBench Traverse`).
- `voxel.Scatter.Stats hism`: the HISMs by size.

Insights traces of the great circle (`voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500 40000 gc=45:20:90 follow=300`, the editor run with
`-statnamedevents`, `Trace.File`) were exported headless (`UnrealInsights.exe -OpenTraceFile=... -AutoQuit -NoUI
-ExecOnAnalysisCompleteCmd=...`, `TimingInsights.ExportTimingEvents` / `ExportTimerStatistics`), and every game-thread
event of the traverse was folded per frame.

- **The small planet is not a like-for-like control.** Its 45°N 20°E is sea (the settle lands at 46.1°N, §20.4), and
  65% of the great circle's samples lie under the sea surface; M's and L's routes are land throughout. Scatter there is
  mostly seabed plants, and the HISM instance churn is a quarter of M's (35 instances placed and 26 released a frame
  against 132 and 121 in the benches below). A land route on the small planet is measured below.
- **Where M's and L's frames go.** In the slowest 5% of frames, the chunk manager's own time is the same on all three
  planets (6.7-8.3 ms). On M and L (against the small planet) there are three extra costs:
  - HISM cluster tree builds on the game thread (`UHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent::BuildTreeAsync`): 3.5-5.1
    ms against 0.8;
  - the game thread waiting for the render thread: 4.1-4.6 ms against 0.1;
  - HISM scene proxies (`Foliage Create Proxy`): 1.2-1.4 ms against 0.5.

  On the render thread the distance-field scene's object updates (`UpdateDistanceFieldObjectBuffers`) take 3.6-3.7 s of
  the 26 s traverse against 0.4 s, single frames up to 51 ms, and ray tracing's instance gathering 1.2-1.6 s against 0.2.
  The scatter section's own P95 (3.4-3.8 ms) is its distance spawn and instance flush, which trigger the same HISM work.
- **The mechanism** (engine source, 5.8.3). A UE 5.8 HISM keeps its instances in legacy mode
  (`FPrimitiveInstanceDataManager::EMode::Legacy`). An instance change that is not in place (an add, a move) marks its
  cluster tree out of date and starts `BuildTreeAsync`, which copies every instance's transform on the game thread. A
  change while the build runs sets `bConcurrentChanges`, and the finished build is thrown away and started again. An
  applied build calls `MarkForRebuildFromLegacy` and `MarkRenderStateDirty`: the scene proxy is recreated, and the
  render thread removes and re-adds every instance's distance-field object (and Lumen and ray-tracing entries). The
  scatter renderer also marked the HISM's render state dirty after every release and every frame's flush, and parked
  released instances at the HISM's origin (a move, so not in place). So each frame the streaming touched a HISM, it paid
  for all its instances. On L after one traverse:
  - 60 HISMs held 250,440 instances, 53% of them pooled (zero-scaled, waiting for reuse).
  - The grass HISMs held up to 37,000 instances each.
  - Pooled instances are in every tree build, proxy and distance-field update of their HISM.
- **Not it:** extraction (on workers, as §19.9 measured), applying completed extractions (P95 0.01 ms), launches (0.03
  ms), edit readers (none on these routes), and the GPU (P95 7.6-7.7 ms on all three).

**What changed** (`UVoxelScatterRenderer`, VoxelScatter; the bench and `voxel.Scatter.Stats` in VoxelStreaming; no
change to extraction, placement, spawn points or generation):

- **Batched HISM writes** (`voxel.Scatter.HISMBatchSeconds`, 0.1 s). The pools and chunk indices change at once, as
  before (`GetChunkInstanceCount`, the cache audits and the tests see no delay). The HISM writes are held per HISM
  (`FPendingHISMWrites`: an index's new transform, the last write winning, and the new instances, numbered after the
  HISM's count and those already held). `Tick` applies a HISM's writes at most once per interval, and not while its
  tree builds, unless they have waited `voxel.Scatter.HISMMaxHoldSeconds` (0.5 s). No `MarkRenderStateDirty`: the HISM
  sends in-place changes to its proxy itself, draws placements and new instances unbuilt until its build lands, and
  then recreates the proxy once. 0 = every write at once, releases parked at the origin, the render state marked dirty:
  the behaviour before G42, for A/B runs.
- **In-place releases.** A release zero-scales each instance where it stands. The HISM takes that without rebuilding
  its tree (`bDoInPlaceUpdate`), so unloads, the distance cleanup and edits no longer rebuild anything.
- **Compaction** (`voxel.Scatter.HISMCompactMinPooled`, 1,024). A HISM taking a batch whose pooled instances are at
  least that many and outnumber its live ones is rewritten with its live instances only (`CompactHISM`: each chunk's
  instances with the held writes applied, renumbered; one `ClearInstances` and `AddInstances`).
- **Smaller regions on a planet** (`voxel.Scatter.RegionChunks`). The scatter HISMs keep their own regions: 4 chunks
  on a planet by default (-1), the render regions' 16 with 0 (as before), N chunks in any world mode with N > 0.
  Heightmap worlds keep one region. Smaller regions only gain precision.
- Queries see held writes: `FindNearestInstance` (harvest) reads instances through them and scans held placements and
  new instances; `GetTotalInstanceCount` counts held new instances; `FlushHISMWrites` applies everything now.
  `voxel.Scatter.Stats hism` lists the HISMs by size; the bench logs `ScatBatchN` and `ScatCompactN`.

**What each part bought** (L's great circle, one profiled run each on a quiet machine, `-statnamedevents`):

| Before (write-through, regions of 16) | 30.0 | 3.45 | 1,209 / 1,272 | 2.6 / 0.67 / 6.9 | 3.5 |
| Batched + compacted, regions of 16 | 24.4 | 2.43 | 678 / 416 | 1.3 / 0.10 / 4.7 | 2.6 |
| **Batched + compacted, regions of 4** | 23.5 | 1.79 | 422 / 429 | 0.19 / 0.15 / 3.3 | 1.7 |

With compaction L's HISMs end the traverse at 108,000-125,000 instances, 5,000-17,000 pooled, against 253,000 and

### 20.11 G66: the great circle's peak was the window before far compression (2026-10-21)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `4a4df99`, UE5_PluginDev `ebf888d` (G42 merged). Branches `docs/g66-peak-memory` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g66-peak-memory` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8098), background throttling off. G52's build is the G52 session's own worktree (VoxelWorlds
`1c4531d`, UE5_PluginDev `469cb83`, built there), run with the same scripts. No code changes.

**The finding.** §20.10's great circles peaked 300-400 MB over §20.7's: M 755 → 1,068-1,072 MB of systems memory, L
831 → 1,213-1,215, the voxel data's peak 812-859 MB, in both of its A/B's modes. Peak loaded chunks and the settled
figures had not moved, so it read as more voxel data per chunk, or more held in flight, from something merged since G52.

**Not a regression: §20.10's benches started earlier.** The bench reports settle it without a build:

- **Where the peak was.** Every one of §20.10's 18 great-circle runs peaks in its first 1.5 s. At the first sample M's
  window has 690-822 of its 1,076 chunks resident (697-829 MB of voxel data), with 109-160 uniform and 93-145
  compressed. Far compression brings it down within about 5 s, and the traverse runs as in §20.7.
- **The traverse is unchanged.** Over the traverse after its first 7 s the voxel data peaks at 375-391 MB on M and
  404-411 on L, against §20.7's 381-400 and 407 (`g52b_{M,L}_new_gc_*`).
- **§20.7's runs started from a compressed window.** M's first sample: 120.5 MB, with 108 resident, 526 uniform and 442
  compressed chunks, a settled world's split. Their peak was the traverse's.
- **The scripts' timing differs.** From the editor logs, §20.10's script started each bench 10.7 s after the settle
  (15.5 s after PIE started), and §20.7's 21.5 s after it (32 s after PIE started: it waited 15 + 2 s and read the whole
  log every 1.5 s).
- **Why it matters.**
  - Far compression (§12.7, §12.8) compacts a chunk only after it has sat `voxel.FarCompression.IdleFrames` (300)
    frames unchanged at LOD 2 or coarser. It starts at most 4 encodes a tick, with 8 in flight.
  - Uniform chunks collapse in the same sweep, so they also stay resident (1 MB for a 64³ chunk) until then.
  - A teleport streams the whole window at once.
  - The bench's memory peaks count every sample from the first, warmup included (`VoxelStreamingBenchmark.cpp`).
- **§20.10's other planet rows are the same.** The climbs to 60,200 (1,057-1,237 MB, against 488-544 for §20.7's
  climbs to 200,200) and the small planet's land route began with 718-843 of their chunks resident (728-850 MB of voxel
  data). `VoxelDemo`'s runs began 45 s after the spawn, settled (127 MB).
- **One build, both states.** G44's L runs (§20.8) came after the demo caves and G56-G60, and also started 10 s after the
  settle. They began with 124-529 MB of voxel data and peaked at 781-855 MB, 784 when the window had compressed.

**The window after a teleport.** `voxel.FarCompression.Stats` once a second after `vox.TPLatLon 45 20` and its settle,
with the benches' PIE setup on a warm editor (`course_*` in the session's scratchpad):

| Build, planet | Chunks with data at the settle | Window loaded | First compaction | Peak voxel data (resident / uniform / compressed chunks) | Settled at | Settled split (resident / uniform / compressed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current, small | 48 of 1,079 | +16.3 s | +6.3 s | 565 MB at +14.5 s (550 / 21 / 408) | +21.5 s | 103 / 68 / 908 |
| Current, M | 63 of 1,076 | +11.4 s | +6.3 s | 787 MB at +10.4 s (779 / 149 / 136) | +16.3 s | 108 / 494 / 474 |
| Current, L | 40 of 1,102 | +11.3 s | +6.2 s | 813 MB at +11.3 s (805 / 159 / 138) | +16.3 s | 107 / 502 / 493 |
| G52's, M | 52 of 1,076 | +10.2 s | +6.2 s | 837 MB at +10.2 s (830 / 138 / 108) | +15.4 s | 108 / 526 / 442 |

- **The settle comes early.** It releases as soon as the chunk under the pawn has collision, with 4-6% of the window
  holding data. The window fills over the next 10-16 s, and far compression's first compactions come 6 s after the
  settle.
- **Which state a bench starts in.** A bench started 10 s after the settle starts at the window's peak; one started 21
  s after starts settled.
- **The small planet settles last.** Its window is sea and seabed, with 908 chunks to encode against M's 474.
- **G52's build behaves the same.** Its peak is 837 MB, and it settles 0.9 s sooner. The transient predates every merge
  since G52.

**The A/B.** One build at a time, the bench started 10 s or 21 s after the settle (`bench_run.ps1 -IdleSec`). The rest
is §20.10's protocol:

- PIE on `PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride`, a fresh world per run;
- `vox.TPLatLon 45 20` and its settle, local noon, move and look input blocked;
- a fresh editor and a throwaway run, then three repetitions alternating which goes first;
- `voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500 40000 gc=45:20:90 follow=300 warmup=30 catchup=90`.

Tags `g66a_{S,M,L}_i{10,21}_gc_r{1,2,3}` (the current build, in this session's worktree's `Saved/VoxelBench`) and
`g66b_{M,L}_i{10,21}_gc_r{1,2,3}` (G52's build, in the G52 session's worktree's). Ranges over three runs:

|  | 21 s | 126-130 (103) | 736-738 | 375 | 375 | 186-187 / 100-102 | 67 | 1,282-1,289 |
| Current, M | 10 s | 748-775 (741-768) | 1,048-1,061 | 768-783 | 375-378 | 198-199 / 100-101 | 48 | 1,239-1,244 |
|  | 21 s | 121 (108) | 675-683 | 376-380 | 376-380 | 198-204 / 99-101 | 48 | 1,229-1,244 |
| Current, L | 10 s | 746-847 (741-840) | 1,194-1,241 | 805-852 | 404-406 | 194 / 95-97 | 49-51 | 1,266-1,269 |
|  | 21 s | 120 (107) | 832-833 | 404-405 | 404-405 | 193-194 / 94-96 | 49 | 1,265-1,269 |

| G52's, L | 10 s | 728-788 (723-781) | 1,168-1,189 | 800-816 | 410-418 | 227-228 / 110-114 | 49 | 1,264 |

- **When the bench starts decides the peak.**
  - Started 10 s after the settle, systems memory peaks at 1,028-1,241 MB on every planet, in both builds.
  - Started 21 s after, it peaks at 675-836 MB.
  - G52's build started at 21 s reproduces §20.7's figures: M 742-779 MB against 747-769, L 830-836 against 830-837.
- **Nothing after the start differs.** The traverse's voxel data after its first 7 s, scatter, collision, the far field
  and peak loaded chunks are the same both ways.
  - One exception: G52's first M run at 10 s. Another session's headless tests started during it, so its traverse ran
    at a lower frame rate. 300 frames then took longer, and the traverse held up to 491 MB.
  - The current build's batch ran on a quiet machine.
- **Between the builds, started settled:** M 675-683 MB against 742-779, L 832-833 against 830-836.
  - Scatter and collision peak lower on the current build: M 198-204 and 99-101 MB against 232-234 and 114-116; L
    193-194 and 94-96 against 227-228 and 112-113.
  - L's edit memory is higher: 122.0 MB against 61.6 (G68, below).

**Content.** The settled split moved between the two builds:

- M: 526 uniform and 442 compressed → 494 and 474. L: 538 and 457 → 502 and 493.
- So 32-36 chunks that were all solid now hold cave. The most likely cause is the demo caves' Cheese layer (§19.15),
  which carves down to 66 voxels where the old cavern stopped at 45. Not isolated.
- A compressed chunk holds about 0.03 MB here, so settled voxel data moved by 0.3-0.8 MB (M 120.5 → 120.8 MB, L 119.0
  → 119.8).

**L's edit memory (G68).** The bench counts the edit manager with the voxel systems. On L it holds 122.0 MB on the
current build against 61.6 on G52's. M and the small planet have no edits around the site.

- **Measured live** on L, 25 s after the settle (a Python probe through Claudius: the edit manager's `GetDebugStats`
  before and after `ClearHistory`):
  - 4 operations in the undo history, all from POI placement around 45°N 20°E (a fresh world, no player edits);
  - 420,713 edits in 18 chunks;
  - 122.0 MB, and 28.0 MB with the history cleared. The history holds 94.0 MB.
- **What changed.** System edits enter the undo history: the POI subsystem's stamps (dungeons, their entrances,
  campsites, brush edits) begin their operations with the default `bAddToUndoHistory`. Since G60 (§19.17) each voxel change there is an `FVoxelEditChange`: its chunk, its position,
  and the whole edit before and after, 112 bytes. Before G60 it was an `FVoxelEdit` of 40 bytes.
- **The old size.** At 40 bytes the same history is 33.6 MB, and the edit memory 28.0 + 33.6 = 61.6 MB: G52's exactly.
- **What it costs.** L's systems memory, settled and peak, is 60 MB higher since G60. It did not cause G66.
- **What else follows.** These are the history's only entries, so an undo (the demo test actor's Z) would take back
  the last of them.

**D3.**

- **The peak after a teleport is real, and counts against D3's 1.5 GB.** In these runs it is at most 1,241 MB of
  systems memory plus 51 MB of far field (L), and 1,159 + 67 on the small planet. D3 holds.
- **Earlier streaming peaks were under-reported.** The transient is the same on G52's build, so §20.7's benches, and
  any earlier bench that started settled, under-reported the streaming peak by 300-400 MB. Their traverse figures
  stand.
- **The settled budget (0.6 GB) is unaffected.** The settled figures are §20.10's: 440-571 MB with the far field. L's
  571 includes G68's 94 MB of undo history.
- **§20.10's frame and manager times stand.** They are traverse statistics, and both of its modes started the same way.
  Here, frame P95 (22.5-26.4 ms) and manager P95 (6.4-7.9 ms) do not depend on when the bench starts. Only the far
  compression step's own P95 rises during the catch-up (0.54-0.80 ms against 0.46-0.49).

**Benches from now on.**

- **To start settled,** a planet bench waits 25 s after the settle (the small planet's window settles at +21.5 s). Or it
  checks that the CSV's first row has the settled split (`ResidentN` about 100-110 on the review planets).
- **To include the teleport's peak,** a bench starts at once.
- **Either way, the report should say which.** `peakVoxelSystemsMB` counts every sample from the first.

**New findings** (in §14.1):

| ID | Finding | Status |
|----|---------|--------|
| G67 | After a teleport or a spawn the window streams in at once, and stays resident until far compression catches up (`IdleFrames` 300, then at most 4 encodes a tick): on M and L, 779-830 of about 1,100 chunks are resident 10-11 s after the settle (787-837 MB of voxel data, systems 1.05-1.24 GB) for about 5 s, in G52's build too. About 340 of them are uniform (all air or all solid), which the sweep collapses for free but only after the same wait. Collapsing a uniform chunk when it is generated would take about 340 MB off that peak, given reads that do not re-expand it (meshing and seams read through `EnsureResident`). Under D3 either way | Fixed in §20.18 |
| G68 | System edits (POI and dungeon stamps, campsites) enter the undo history, and since G60 each voxel change there is an `FVoxelEditChange` (its chunk, its position and the whole edit before and after: 112 bytes, against `FVoxelEdit`'s 40). On L, 4 POI operations around the site hold 94.0 MB of the edit manager's 122.0 (the edit layer: 420,713 edits, 28.0 MB). The same history took 33.6 MB before G60, so L's systems memory, settled and peak, rose 60 MB with it. An undo would take back the last of them | Open: keep system edits out of the history (as G60 did for water propagation), slim the record (it repeats the position and keeps two timestamps), or cap the history by memory; a design decision (undoing a stamp) |

G66 is dismissed: not a regression. No code changes; no suites were run.

### 20.12 G62: the voxel-resolution gradient, fitted (2026-10-21)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `4a4df99`, UE5_PluginDev `ebf888d` (G61 and G42 merged). Branches `fix/g62-crossing-gradient`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g62-crossing-gradient` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098), background throttling off.

**The cause.** Both smooth meshers took their normals at voxel resolution from a central difference about the voxel the
point floors to (`FVoxelCPUDualContourMesher::CalculateGradientNormal`, `FVoxelCPUMarchingCubesMesher::CalculateGradientNormal`
and `CalculateGradientNormalLOD(…, 1)`, DC's seam samplers' `GradientNormal(…, 1)`, the GPU MC shader's
`CalculateGradientNormalLOD(…, 1)`). The generators' density is a one-voxel ramp of the signed distance along local up that
saturates beyond it (`SignedDistanceToDensity`), and for a surface a fraction f of a voxel above the floored voxel the tap
below it lies in the saturated rock: the difference along up was 1 − f/2 of the ramp's, so a slope's normal tilted by
1.0-1.8 times the slope with the surface's phase in the voxel layer. On a planet every grid axis crosses the ramp, so even
flat ground erred by a degree or more depending on where the voxel grid met it.

**DC's share, measured first.** G62 left open how much Dual Contouring shows, since its LOD 0 vertex normal is the sum of a
cell's crossing normals. An offline model of the estimators on exact ramp planes (random phases, uint8 densities) gave DC
nearly MC's error: on a 5° plane a mean of 1.52° against MC's 1.57° (standard deviations 1.11° and 1.24°), on flat ground at
45°N 20E 1.17° against 1.26°. A cell's vertical-edge crossings all lie in its own voxel layer, so they share the phase and
summing them does not cancel it. In the engine (the band metric below, on the streaming tests' gentle relief), DC's LOD 0
banded by 2.3-3.8° over the voxel phase and erred 1.9-2.6° on average, MC's by 4.2-4.5° and 2.5-4.3°. DC is the shipped
mesher on planets and `VoxelDemo`, so it changes too; only its shading normals do (below).

**The estimator.** The model compared the floored difference with trilinear taps one voxel either side of the point (the
geomorph's steepness gate's way, which the finding suggested), taps half a voxel either side, an edge-exact difference along
the crossing's edge, a crossing-displacement fit and least-squares fits. Trilinear taps at ±1 only cut the error by about a
third (5° plane: MC 0.94°, DC 0.92°): they still reach the ramp's saturated knee. The fit chosen is exact for any plane and
the best on curved surfaces:

- **Weighted linear least squares over the voxels on the ramp** (`VoxelCrossingGradient::FitNormal`, new private header
  `VoxelCrossingGradient.h`): the voxels of the 3×3×3 block around the point's nearest voxel with 0 < density < 255 (a
  saturated voxel only bounds the ramp) that the caller's view holds, tent weights centred on the point (the product over
  the axes of 1.5 minus the distance in voxels), and a free offset, so a point off the surface (a geomorphed MC vertex) is
  fitted too. Model: 5° plane 1.8° → 0.05° (MC) and 0.03° (DC), 30° 3.9° → 0.06° / 0.03°, flat at 45°N 1.2° → 0.09° /
  0.06°; spheres of 8 voxels 3.4° → 0.26°, sine hills 3.7-6.1° → 1.3-2.9°; a point 0.3 voxel off a plane 0.05°, where a
  fit held to the iso value at the point erred 2.3°.
- **The guard.** Where the voxels on the ramp do not span three directions (det M under 0.02 (trace M / 3)³: the surface
  through a voxel layer leaves a single layer on the ramp; or too few voxels held), the fit reports failure and the old
  difference is used. That is where the floored difference is exact (f ≈ 0), so there is no visible switch.
- **What a view holds.** Voxels outside the view are skipped, never clamped (a clamped duplicate at the wrong place would
  bias the fit). DC: the interior pass's box (the chunk in the Interior domain, one voxel past it in the Full domain, where
  missing neighbours read as Air, which the fit skips) and each seam sampler's own box (`GetBox`, shared with
  `GradientNormal`), so a ring recompute runs the interior pass's op sequence. MC: `IsVoxelHeld`, inside the chunk or one
  voxel past it where the request carries that face's plane, edge's strip or corner (`GetVoxelAt` clamps elsewhere); the
  GPU shader's `IsVoxelHeld` is the same rule over its flags. Within those, the fit reads the 3×3×3 block around the
  point's nearest voxel.

**What changed** (`VoxelCPUDualContourMesher.cpp/.h`, `VoxelCPUMarchingCubesMesher.cpp/.h`, `VoxelGPUMarchingCubesMesher.cpp`,
`MarchingCubesMeshGeneration.usf`; no change to generation, positions, seams, the QEF or the geomorph):

- **Dual Contouring's shading normals.** LOD 0's vertex normal is the sum of the fitted normals at the cell's crossings
  (`FDCEdgeCrossing::ShadingNormal`, computed once per crossing in `DetectEdgeCrossings`; `ComputeCellVertex` the same per
  sampler), and at a stride G44's voxel-cell normal sums them (`CalculateShadingNormal`, the samplers' `ShadingNormal`),
  as does G17's boundary fallback vertex. The QEF keeps the central difference (`Crossing.Normal`), so no vertex moves and
  every ring stays bit-identical.
- **Marching Cubes' normals.** LOD 0's vertex normal (`ProcessCubeLOD` at stride 1, the transition ribbon's stride-1
  vertices) and G61's normal at a strided edge's voxel crossing (`CalculateEdgeShadingNormal`) are the fitted gradient
  (`CalculateShadingNormal`); the GPU shader the same (`CalculateShadingNormal`, `IsVoxelHeld`, parameter
  `CrossingGradientNormals`).
- **One switch:** `voxel.Mesh.CrossingGradientNormals` (1; 0 = the floored central difference, bit for bit), defined in the
  DC mesher beside `voxel.Mesh.VoxelShadingNormals` and read by the MC CPU and GPU meshers.
- **Left as it was:** the stride-scale gradients with `voxel.Mesh.VoxelShadingNormals 0`, the transition cell's
  folded-triangle check (debug) and the geomorph's steepness gate.

**Tests.**

- **`Meshing.CrossingGradient.Planes`** (new, `CrossingGradientTests.cpp`): fifteen exact ramp planes (heightmap planes at
  5°, 15° and 30° in nine directions and three phases; a planet's tangent planes at 45°N 20°E, flat and 15°, three phases)
  meshed by DC and MC at LOD 0, 1 and 2 in both settings. Per vertex, the angle from the plane's normal and the **band**:
  the spread of the mean angle over eight bins of the vertex's phase in the voxel grid along the normal's dominant axis. With
  the fit every LOD of both meshers is within a quarter degree on average with no band; the central difference bands LOD 0 by
  more than a degree; positions and indices are bitwise the same in both settings. With a real RHI the GPU MC mesher's normals
  match the CPU's. Before → after (mean, band, largest), LOD 0/1/2:

  | Mesher | Mean angle | Band | Largest |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | DC | 2.36° / 2.32° / 2.29° → 0.03° / 0.03° / 0.03° | 2.44° / 2.11° / 0.84° → 0.02° / 0.01° / 0.01° | 6.4° → 0.19° |
  | MC | 2.48° / 2.52° / 2.38° → 0.05° / 0.05° / 0.05° | 3.61° / 3.22° / 1.53° → 0.01° / 0.01° / 0.02° | 8.4° → 0.28° |

  GPU against CPU (MC): every GPU vertex of LOD 1 and 2 and 148,328 of 148,380 of LOD 0 at a CPU vertex, normals 0.064-0.067°
  apart on average and at most 0.156° with the fit (0.051-0.052° and 0.156° without it).
- **`Streaming.Planet.GradientBands`, `Streaming.Plane.GradientBands`** (new): the `LODNormals` places with gentle relief
  (45°N 20°E and the equator; the plane's hills), in DC and in MC, chunk meshes and seam buckets, both settings.
  `FLODNormalStats` gains the angle's standard deviation and the band (bins of 50 vertices). LOD 0 must band at most 0.5° with
  the fit and more than 1° without it, every LOD's mean angle must fall, and the vertex counts must agree. LOD 0, before →
  after:

  | Place | DC mean / band | MC mean / band |
  |---|---|---|
  | Planet 45°N 20°E | 1.90° / 2.63° → 0.17° / 0.05° | 2.46° / 4.41° → 0.14° / 0.06° |
  | Planet equator | 2.49° / 3.79° → 0.18° / 0.05° | 2.69° / 4.23° → 0.13° / 0.04° |
  | Plane | 2.55° / 2.33° → 0.59° / 0.21° | 4.30° / 4.45° → 0.52° / 0.28° |

  LOD 1 falls as far (DC 2.09-3.49° → 0.74-2.05°, MC 2.15-3.79° → 0.16-0.68°). At LOD 2 a vertex's phase is not that of the
  crossing its normal comes from, so the band there is reported, not bounded; its mean falls (DC 2.94-7.11° → 2.01-5.83°, MC
  2.15-4.45° → 0.31-1.23°).
- **`Streaming.Planet.ChunkFaceShading`** (G25's): its A/B of the clamp scaling now runs on the central difference
  (`voxel.Mesh.CrossingGradientNormals 0`), since the fit skips the voxels a job does not hold and cannot draw G25's lines;
  a third run with the defaults must light chunk faces like the interior too. It does, and evenly: LOD 0's interior lights
  +0.04% against the analytic surface at 45°N (+1.79% with the central difference) and +0.05% on the equator (−1.02%).
- **The existing normal tests** pass with the new default, closer to the analytic surface than G61's run of them (LOD 0,
  same places and reliefs): DC gentle 45°N 1.90° → 0.17° (tilt 1.07° → 0.01°, brightness +1.61% → +0.04%), DC gentle
  equator 2.49° → 0.18°, DC gentle plane 2.55° → 0.59°; on the streaming tests' relief (±800) DC 45°N 3.73° → 1.34°, the
  plane 9.18° → 7.37°; MC gentle 45°N 2.46° → 0.14°, MC ±800 45°N 5.22° → 0.99°, the plane 11.94° → 7.13°. The central
  difference's LOD 0 tilted systematically on a planet (1.07° at 45°N), which the fit does not.

**Live** (one worktree editor, `PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride` and `VoxelDemo`; in each PIE the central
difference first and then the fit, each after `voxel.RemeshAll` from the same cameras at local noon, eye adaptation and the
vignette off; shots `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius/g62_*` in the worktree, `_n0` before and `_n1` after). The ripple is the
standard deviation of the shot's grey level band-passed between Gaussian blurs of 4 and 16 pixels, the scale of G61's rings;
on G61's own shots it reads 0.79 on the hill's rings and 0.68 with the hill at LOD 0.

- **`Review_Planet_L` in MC, 45°N 20°E** (G61's site and cameras; MC duplicate made in the worktree by G61's
  `g61_make_mc_configs.py`, not committed, deleted after), from 60,000 uu over the ground: the band-passed central difference
  shows G61's picture, concentric rings around the hill east of the site and fine voxel-layer bands ("fingerprints") over the
  LOD 0 centre; with the fit both are gone and only the texture's grain is left (`g62_Lmc_45N_top_n*_band`). Ripple on the
  hill 0.786 → 0.562, over the frame 0.625 → 0.535, the centre 0.545 → 0.532. The oblique look is the same but a shade darker.
- **`Review_Planet_L` (DC), 45°N 20°E**: from 60,000 uu nothing bands in either setting (hill 0.569 → 0.539); the frame is
  1.9% darker with the fit, the brightness bias the tests measured going away. From 8,000 uu over the ground, at LOD 0, the
  central difference draws regular diagonal stripes a voxel layer apart and a dark line along a chunk face; the fit draws
  neither (ripple over the frame 0.642 → 0.566, `g62_Ldc_45N_low_top_n*_band`).
- **`VoxelDemo` (DC, its own config)**, a lake shore straight down from z 8,000 over the world origin (the script's pawn
  query found no pawn, so the cameras stayed there) and the oblique look: the grass and
  material borders bury any band at this scale in both settings (ripple on grass 9.20 → 9.18); the fit changes the frame by
  1.8 grey on average, on the slopes. Nothing new along shores, cliffs or material borders (the oblique's difference is clouds,
  water and moving deer).

**Meshing cost** (`voxel.Edit.MeshWork`'s worker times, pawn held, `voxel.RemeshAll`, the two settings alternated three times
in one PIE; the re-mesh's wall time was the same in both settings everywhere, 9.7-14.0 s):

| World | Chunk meshes, before → after | Seam jobs, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| `Review_Planet_L` DC, 1,102 chunks, 5,673 seam jobs | 2,005 / 2,004 / 2,239 → 2,442 / 2,694 / 2,530 ms (+13-34%) | 1,924 / 1,960 / 2,093 → 2,297 / 2,405 / 2,305 ms (+10-23%) |
| `VoxelDemo` DC, 979 chunks, 5,290 seam jobs | 2,120 / 2,185 / 2,276 → 2,569 / 2,639 / 2,621 ms (+15-21%) | 1,871 / 1,828 / 1,900 → 2,181 / 2,182 / 2,196 ms (+16-19%) |
| `Review_Planet_L` MC | 1,116 / 1,113 / 1,124 → 1,609 / 1,697 / 1,722 ms (+44-53%) | 35.7 / 35.2 / 35.1 → 35.0 / 35.7 / 35.2 s (G63's) |

The fit reads 27 voxels and solves a 3×3 system where the central difference read 6. DC computes it once per crossing at LOD
0 and per voxel-cell crossing at a stride; MC once per cell vertex (a vertex shared by four cells is fitted four times).

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 579/579 headless (576 + the
three above) and 579/579 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines are
CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change). The DC seam and closure suites (`Meshing.DualContour.*`: the ring bit-match
tests SC2, ES2, CS2, MS2 and MT2 compare positions, which the QEF keeps; `InteriorDomain.ID1-ID3`) and the MC ones
(`Meshing.MarchingCubes.*`, `Streaming.EditRemesh.*`, `Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.ClosedSurface`) pass unchanged.

**Left as they were:** the QEF's normals (DC), the stride-scale gradients with `voxel.Mesh.VoxelShadingNormals 0`, the
transition cell's folded-triangle check (debug), the geomorph's steepness gate, and the retired GPU DC shader.

G62 is fixed.

### 20.13 G65: far-compressed chunks read off the game thread (2026-10-21)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `7a5e605`, UE5_PluginDev `570ba32` (G62 and G66 merged). Branches `fix/g65-gt-decode` (VoxelWorlds)
and `claude/g65-gt-decode` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.10): far-compressed chunks were decoded on the game thread when something read their voxels
(`FChunkDescriptor::EnsureResident`, Oodle): single frames up to 28.9 ms on the small planet's great circle and 8.8-11.7
ms on M and L.

**Instruments first**, kept in the build:

- `VoxelResidencyStats` (VoxelCore, new): every expansion of a compact chunk (uniform or compressed) with its reader, its
  thread, its time and the chunk. Readers name themselves with a `FReadScope` (the outermost scope wins): collision,
  collision neighbour arrival, water pull, water tile, water propagation, seam job, chunk mesh, scatter, surface query,
  point query, map overlay, snapshot, prefetch. The game thread's waits for a decode on a worker are counted apart (an
  expansion inside a wait is not counted twice). `voxel.FarCompression.Decodes [reset]` lists them;
  `EnsureResident` has the trace scopes `VoxelChunk_ExpandUniform` and `VoxelChunk_Decompress`.
- The bench's CSV gained `DecodeN` and `DecodeMs` (the game thread's expansions and waits in the frame) and `SnapMB`; its
  JSON gained `decodeGTCount`, `decodeGTMsP99`, `decodeGTMsMax`, `decodeGTSamplesOver2Ms`, `peakSnapshotMB` and
  `endSnapshotMB`.
- `GetVoxelMemoryStats` counts the seam snapshot cache (`SnapshotBytes`), apart from the voxel data's total.

**The cause.** On the small planet's great circle (the protocol below), with the reads as before, the game thread
expanded 2,959 times over the bench, 1,279 distinct chunks, 923 ms in all:

| Reader | Expansions | Chunks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collision cooks (`PrepareCollisionMeshRequest`, the chunk and its 26 neighbours) | 1,024 | 891 | 313 ms |
| Water pull (`PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`, at a chunk's mesh completion) | 924 | 463 | 270 ms |
| Seam jobs (`DispatchSeamJob`, the participants' snapshots) | 740 | 578 | 253 ms |
| Chunk meshes (the meshing request's copy of the voxels) | 241 | 241 | 79 ms |
| Surface and point queries, collision neighbour arrival | 30 | 25 | 8 ms |

Each took 0.29-0.34 ms on average at 64³ (at most 1.6 ms; expanding a uniform chunk fills 1 MB too). A chunk compacted
while far is read again as the viewer comes near: by its own re-mesh at a finer LOD, its neighbours' seam jobs, the
collision cooks of its 27-chunk neighbourhood and the water pull. Every one of those readers gathers its voxels on the
game thread and expanded the chunk in place there. The sweep then compacted it again at once (the seam pipeline reads
through its snapshot cache, so nothing holds the chunk resident, and the sweep re-applies the cached compact form without
encoding), so the next reader expanded it again: 57% of the expansions were repeats.

**Tried first and dropped: expanding ahead on workers.** Expanding the descriptors of chunks about to be read on worker
tasks and keeping them resident while they were read took the game thread's decodes to 21 ms on the small planet but held
the streaming front resident: the peak of voxel data rose from 375 to 1,118 MB. With a short hold instead (30 or 60
ticks), the chunks went back and forth: 13,000-17,000 worker expansions per traverse.

**The fix: the readers use a snapshot decoded on a worker, and the chunk stays compressed.**

- `FVoxelCompactSource` (`ChunkDescriptor.h`): a copy of a compact chunk's form (its uniform value, or a shared reference
  to the compressed buffer) that expands into an array off the descriptor (`FChunkDescriptor::CopyCompactSource`,
  `IsCompact`). The descriptor is not touched.
- `UVoxelChunkManager::GetSeamVoxelSnapshot`: for a far-compressed chunk without edits the snapshot is an array that a
  worker task (`UE::Tasks::Launch`, `BackgroundHigh`) fills from the compact source; the cache entry holds the task
  (`FSeamVoxelSnapshot::Ready`). A caller that passes `OutReady` receives the task and waits for it on its own worker;
  any other caller (the game thread) waits for it at once, which counts as a game-thread wait.
- Seam jobs, collision cooks (`PrepareCollisionMeshRequest`'s `OutSnapshotsReady`) and chunk mesh jobs
  (`LaunchAsyncMeshGeneration`: the meshing request copies its chunk's snapshot on the worker) wait for their decodes
  on their workers.
- The water pull's seed search reads snapshots and takes the chunk's array for writing only where water flows in; the
  water tile and the scatter hand-off read the snapshot.
- **Prefetch.** A chunk queued for a mesh (`AddToMeshingQueue`) or a collision cook (`RequestCollision`) starts the
  snapshots of the compact chunks without edits in its 27-chunk neighbourhood (`PrefetchVoxelSnapshotsAround`,
  `BlueprintCallable`), so they are usually ready when read.
- Resident chunks, chunks with edits, and the surface and point queries read as before.
- **One switch:** `voxel.FarCompression.SnapshotReads` (1; 0 = every read expands the chunk in place on the game thread,
  as before). The benches ran it under its first name, `voxel.FarCompression.ExpandAhead`; nothing else changed.

**Tests.**

- **`Compression.Codec.CompactSource`** (new): a compact source expands to the descriptor's voxels, uniform and compressed,
  and the descriptor stays compact.
- **`Streaming.Planet.FarReadsOffGameThread`, `Streaming.Plane.FarReadsOffGameThread`** (new, `VoxelPlanetStreamingTests.cpp`):
  a place streams, far compression compacts the far band (`IdleFrames` 5), and the viewer moves 3,000 uu (the planet's
  45°N 20°E eastward, the plane's (23,000, 7,000) along +X), so its LOD bands sweep over compressed chunks; with each
  setting in turn. The move's game-thread decodes: plane 82 (0.7 ms) → 0, planet 111-127 (4.3-5.3 ms) → 0, with 30-70
  snapshots decoded on workers. The second setting must take at least ten times fewer; every chunk's voxels (the water flag
  masked) and every chunk mesh's CRC must be the same in both. The planet's water flags differ in 0-1 of 195 chunks, run
  to run with either setting: G70.

**Benches.** One build, the setting by cvar; per run a fresh PIE on `PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride`
(`Review_Planet`, `_M`, `_L`), `vox.TPLatLon 45 20`, the bench 25 s after the settle (§20.11), `voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500
40000 gc=45:20:90 follow=300 warmup=30 catchup=90`; three runs per planet and setting, interleaved, the order alternating.
The decode figures are the traverse's frames (1,437 a run); memory as the bench reports it (systems: voxel data, edits,
renderer, collision, scatter), the snapshot cache apart. Before → after (ranges over the three runs):

| | Small planet (S) | M (50 km) | L (1,000 km) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Game-thread decode, traverse | 536-548 → 15-18 ms | 364-410 → 23-27 ms | 397-436 → 11-12 ms |
| Expansions and waits on it | 1,781-1,837 → 59-74 | 1,238-1,328 → 95-101 | 1,318-1,436 → 53-54 |
| Worst frame's decode | 7.8-9.1 → 1.8-3.3 ms | 7.7-9.5 → 2.8-3.9 ms | 7.6-10.7 → 1.8-3.0 ms |
| Frames with over 2 ms of it | 58-75 → 0-3 | 53-60 → 3-5 | 54-64 → 0-1 |
| Frame P95 / P99 | 26.0-27.4 / 31.6-34.0 → 24.9-25.8 / 29.7-30.9 ms | 23.8-24.5 / 30.2-31.3 → 23.0 / 27.3-29.8 ms | 24.1-24.7 / 30.3-31.4 → 22.7-23.9 / 28.1-28.8 ms |
| Manager P95 | 6.8-7.6 → 5.3-5.4 ms | 6.6-7.2 → 5.6-6.0 ms | 7.1-7.7 → 5.7-6.1 ms |
| Catch-up | 0.17-0.18 → 0.17-0.18 s | 0.17 → 0.17 s | 0.17 → 0.17 s |
| Peak voxel data / systems | 377 / 737-743 → 288 / 642-646 MB | 376-377 / 679-684 → 307-314 / 597-606 MB | 405 / 831-833 → 292-293 / 702-703 MB |
| Voxel data at the end | 348-350 → 230-234 MB | 283-295 → 163-168 MB | 335-345 → 189-195 MB |
| Snapshot cache, peak | 1,061-1,085 → 1,084-1,095 MB | 688-701 → 708-713 MB | 730-745 → 740-753 MB |

What is left on the game thread is the surface and point queries (36-114 small expansions a traverse, 11-28 ms) and a
few waits by the collision neighbour arrival. The voxel data falls because the read chunks stay compressed. The workers
take about 1.0-1.1 ms a decode (contended, against the game thread's 0.3), 2.0-2.5 s of worker time a traverse, with no
change to the catch-up. The snapshot cache is the same size in both settings and is not part of the systems figures: G69.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 582/582 headless (579 + the
three above) and 582/582 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss), both on the final build
(the cvar renamed). The 108 GPU parity lines are CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change).

**New findings** (in §14.1):

| ID | Finding | Status |
|----|---------|--------|
| G69 | The seam snapshot cache (`UVoxelChunkManager::SeamSnapshotCache`: one full array per chunk, 1 MB at 64³, kept for 128 seam ticks after its last use) holds 1,061-1,095 MB at the small planet's great-circle peak and 688-753 MB on M and L, in both settings, 590-750 MB at the end. Nothing counted it before G65 (its comment says tens of MB). Counted with the systems and the far field, the traverse peaks at 1.75-1.83 GB on S, 1.34-1.42 on M and 1.48-1.61 on L (the lower ends with G65), over D3's 1.5 GB on S | Fixed in §20.15: collision cooks read their neighbours' boundary shells, uniform chunks share one array |
| G70 | The water pull's result at a chunk corner depends on the order in which the neighbouring chunks finish meshing: in `Streaming.Planet.FarReadsOffGameThread` 9 air voxels below the sea at chunk (6, 0, 9)'s +Y+Z corner are flooded in some runs and not in others, with either setting | Open (not traced) |

**Left as they were:** the surface and point queries' expansions (small, on the game thread), chunks with edits (read

### 20.14 G68: system edits outside the undo history, and a memory budget for it (2026-10-22)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `63c171a`, ProceduralDungeonPlugin `fe9232e`, UE5_PluginDev `8b3e119` (G62, G66 and G65 merged).
Branches `fix/g68-system-edit-history` (VoxelWorlds, ProceduralDungeonPlugin) and `claude/g68-system-edit-history`
(UE5_PluginDev, which holds VoxelWorldPOI). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8098), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.11): system edits entered the edit manager's undo history. The dungeon stamp, its entrance and the
campsites began their operations with the default `bAddToUndoHistory`, and since G60 each voxel change there is an
`FVoxelEditChange` of 112 bytes. On `Review_Planet_L` four POI operations around 45°N 20°E held 94.0 MB of the edit
manager's 122.0, and an undo (the demo test actor's Z) would have taken back the last of them.

**The decision** (the user's, 2026-10-22): the world's own generation stays out of the history, as G60 did for water
propagation's flood, and the history gets a memory budget as a safety net. Keeping stamps undoable with a slimmer record, or
a budget alone (which on L would drop the stamps again), were not taken. Undo exists in the game only through the demo test
actor; the player controller has none.

**What changed:**

- **Out of the history** (`BeginEditOperation(…, /*bAddToUndoHistory=*/false)`): `UDungeonVoxelStamper::StampDungeonInFrame`
  (ProceduralDungeonPlugin), `UDungeonEntranceStitcher::StitchEntranceInFrame` (ProceduralDungeonPlugin), and both paths of
  `UVoxelWorldPOIPlacement::PlaceCampsite` (VoxelWorldPOI; heightmap and planet). They are broadcast as before (System
  source: re-mesh, re-cook, scatter re-extraction, water), take no undo step and leave the redo stack. Whether an operation
  enters the history stays the caller's choice: other System operations (the debug `voxel.Edit.System` and
  `voxel.Edit.SystemLayers`, and the ones the undo tests build on the edit manager) are still undo steps.
- **The history's memory budget** (`UVoxelEditManager`): `voxel.Edit.UndoHistoryMB` (32 MB; 0 = no budget, the
  100-operation limit only). When an operation enters the history, the oldest operations are dropped while the undo and redo
  history is over the budget, down to the newest, which is always kept. A player brush of radius 8 voxels takes about 0.25
  MB. `GetHistoryMemoryUsage()` (BlueprintCallable) reports it; `GetDebugStats` prints it.
- **What follows:** as with the flood, undoing a player's edit made before a stamp puts that edit's voxels back as they were
  before it, the stamp's there with them. Only the demo test actor can undo, so this is a debug-tool corner.

**Tests.**

- **`VoxelWorlds.POI.SystemEditsOutsideHistory`** (new, VoxelWorldPOI): on a small plane a player dig (81 voxels, one undo
  step, 9,798 bytes of history), then a dungeon stamp (28,832 voxels), its entrance (5,321) and a campsite: still one undo
  step and 9,798 bytes, and an undo takes back the dig and leaves the POIs' 28,276 edits. Before, the three would each have
  been an undo step, about 3.8 MB of history, and the undo would have taken back the campsite.
- **`VoxelWorlds.Edit.UndoRedo.MemoryBudget`** (new): twelve digs (972 edits, 114,872 bytes of history) are all kept with
  no budget; with a budget of a third of that, 3 of 12 are kept in 30,434 bytes, each undo restores the layer after the dig
  before it, nothing older can be undone and redo restores the twelfth dig's layer; under a budget smaller than one
  operation the newest is still kept and undoes.
- **Unchanged and green:** `Edit.UndoRedo.Records`, `Streaming.WaterPropagation.Undo.{Plane,Planet}` (their system stamp is
  an operation the test builds on the edit manager, still an undo step), `Scatter.EditReaders.*`, `Streaming.EditRemesh.*`, `Dungeon.Stamp.*`,
  `Dungeon.Stitch.*`, `POI.Planet.PlaceCampsite`.

**Live** (`Review_Planet_L` on `PlanetTest`, a fresh world, the pawn settled at 45°N 20°E and probed 25 s later through
the edit manager's `GetDebugStats` and `GetHistoryMemoryUsage`, as in §20.11): the same 420,713 edits in 18 chunks (a
dungeon of 289,574 voxels and 4,563 for its entrance, and a campsite), no undo step and 0.00 MB of history; the edit manager
holds 28.0 MB against 122.0 before. L's systems memory, settled and peak, is back by the 94 MB G60 added.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 584/584 headless and 584/584
in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines are CRC-identical to G44's.

G68 is fixed.

### 20.15 G69: the seam snapshot cache, bounded (2026-10-22)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `63c171a`, UE5_PluginDev `8b3e119` (G65 merged). Branches `fix/g69-snapshot-cache` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g69-snapshot-cache` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree
editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.13): the seam snapshot cache (`UVoxelChunkManager::SeamSnapshotCache`: one ChunkSize³ array per chunk,
1 MB at 64³, dropped 128 seam ticks after its last read) peaked at 1.06-1.10 GB on the small planet's great circle and
0.69-0.75 GB on M and L, uncounted until G65. Counted, the small planet's peak was over D3's 1.5 GB.

**Instruments first**, kept in the build: every entry records how it was made (copied from a resident chunk, with edits,
decoded from a compressed or a uniform chunk), when, its reads, the readers that made it and last read it, and a bitmask of
every reader that took it (a seam job, a chunk mesh, a collision cook's own chunk or a neighbour, the water, scatter);
session counters (made, read, replaced, evicted by age and how many never read again, removed, made again within 600 ticks
of an eviction). `voxel.Snapshot.Stats [reset]` (`DescribeSnapshotCache`) lists them with the entries' age, reads and
distance from the viewer's chunk. The age is a cvar, `voxel.Snapshot.MaxAgeTicks` (128).

**What the cache holds.** Probes on the bench's great circle (the protocol below; the stats logged 4, 8, 12, 20 and 28 s in):

- **The working set, not stale entries.** On the small planet 700-1,070 entries, 75-96% read ten times or more (145,000
  reads in a traverse, 39 per entry), most last read under 64 ticks ago, 4-7 chunks from the viewer. A shorter lifetime
  does not lower the peak: at 128, 64 and 32 ticks the 8 s sample holds 1,035, 1,072 and 1,001 entries; it only makes them
  again (1,484, 2,854 and 4,067 made again within 600 ticks of an eviction) and slows the frame (P95 28.9, 29.6, 35.5 ms).
- **Collision cooks.** The cache jumps from 0 to 914 MB in the bench's first two seconds, with no re-mesh: collision's
  decisions re-run when the viewer starts moving, and its radius is half the view distance (20,000 uu here) plus a speed
  lead, so hundreds of chunks are cooked. A cook reads its chunk and its 26 neighbours' snapshots
  (`PrepareCollisionMeshRequest`), but of a neighbour the slice extraction (`VoxelNeighborSlices::Extract`) reads only the
  planes next to the shared face, edge or corner: one at collision LOD 0 (`CollisionLODLevel`), stride + 1 above it. With
  the reader bits: 191-218 entries (182-206 MB) taken only by cooks as a neighbour, 42-182 (40-178 MB) by a cook as its own
  chunk and as a neighbour.
- **Uniform chunks.** On M and L a third of the entries are uniform chunks (all air or all rock, 204-212 of 568-699), each
  expanded on a worker into its own 1 MB array.
- **Copies of resident chunks** are a quarter to a third of the entries (144-289), the rest decoded from compressed chunks.

**The fix.**

- **Neighbours as boundary shells** (`voxel.Collision.NeighborShells`, 1). `FVoxelChunkShell` (VoxelCore, new) holds a
  chunk's voxels within a depth of each of its six faces: six slabs, `Get(X, Y, Z)` for any voxel within the depth of a face
  (at an edge or a corner any slab holding it answers). `VoxelNeighborSlices::GetNeighborDepth` (new, the rule `Extract`
  used) gives the cook's depth. `UVoxelChunkManager::GetChunkShell` keeps one per chunk (`ShellCache`, per ContentVersion and
  depth, the same age sweep, dropped with the snapshot on unload and on the water pull's flags): cut on a worker from the
  chunk's cached snapshot if there is one; for a far-compressed chunk without edits decoded on a worker with only the shell
  kept (the chunk stays compressed, as in G65); for a uniform one the shared shell of its value and depth; for a resident one
  cut on the game thread (its faces only); with edits cut from its edit-merged snapshot. `PrepareCollisionMeshRequest`
  hands the cook the neighbours' shells (`OutNeighborShells`); the cook's worker reads them in the slice extraction
  (`ensure`: no read outside the depth). At 64³ a depth-1 shell is 96 KB.
- **A cook's own chunk is read once.** The cook cuts its chunk's shell from the snapshot (for its neighbours' cooks) and then
  drops the snapshot, unless another reader took it (the reader bits). Collision's prefetch (`PrefetchCollisionInputs`, from
  `RequestCollision`) starts the far-compressed neighbours' shells and not the chunk's own snapshot: after the bench's
  teleport back, a queue of 408 cooks held 377 MB of their own prefetched snapshots.
- **Shells while they are small:** taken while 8 × depth ≤ ChunkSize (`ShouldUseCollisionShells`: a shell is 6 × depth /
  ChunkSize of a chunk, overlapping at the edges; at 64³ one plane is 9%, collision LOD 2's five planes 47%). A deeper one
  holds about as much as the chunk, and the cook reads whole snapshots as before.
- **Uniform chunks share one array per value** (`voxel.Snapshot.ShareUniform`, 1): `GetUniformSnapshotArray`, counted once.
- **Memory stats:** `FVoxelMemoryStats::ShellBytes` (in `SnapshotBytes`); the bench's CSV gained `ShellMB`.

**Tests.**

- **`Compression.ChunkShell.Extract`** (new): random chunks of 8³, 16³ and 64³ at depths 1, 2, 3, 5, half and the whole
  chunk: `Contains` is the within-depth rule and every voxel held reads as the chunk's; a chunk of the wrong size makes no
  shell; a uniform shell (96 KB at 64³ and depth 1).
- **`Streaming.Planet.CollisionNeighborShells`, `Streaming.Plane.CollisionNeighborShells`** (new): a place streams, far
  compression compacts the far band and a dig makes chunks with edits (resident, compressed, uniform and edited chunks); every
  loaded chunk's collision request is prepared and meshed with its neighbours' snapshots and then with their shells, at LOD
  0 and 1, the caches emptied between. Every collision mesh (and the neighbours read as air) is the same. On the planet (32³
  chunks) 158 chunks, 2,684 neighbour reads, all from shells: the cache 14,208 → 2,920 KB at LOD 0 and 14,256 → 8,296 KB at
  LOD 1 (depth 3). On the plane (16³) 207 chunks: 2,128 → 830 KB at LOD 0; at LOD 1 a depth-3 shell would be bigger than the
  chunk and none is taken. The memory must be within 1.25 times the shells' share of the snapshots'.
- The G65 tests (`Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.FarReadsOffGameThread`) still find no game-thread decode in the move.

**Benches.** One build, the settings by cvar: before = `voxel.Snapshot.ShareUniform 0`, `voxel.Collision.NeighborShells 0`
(the cache as on main after G65), after = both 1. The protocol of §20.13 (a fresh PIE on `PlanetTest` with
`voxel.ConfigOverride`, `vox.TPLatLon 45 20`, the bench 25 s after the settle, `voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500 40000 gc=45:20:90
follow=300 warmup=30 catchup=90`, three runs per planet and setting, interleaved), after a throwaway warm-up run. The peak
with the cache is one sample's systems (the bench's: voxel data, edits, renderer, collision, scatter) plus snapshot cache plus
far field. Before → after (ranges over the three runs):

| | Small planet (S) | M (50 km) | L (1,000 km) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Snapshot cache, peak (shells included) | 1,087-1,093 → 669-706 MB (72-73) | 709-760 → 464-508 MB (20) | 743-754 → 484-504 MB (21) |
| Peak with the cache and the far field | 1,760-1,776 → 1,299-1,361 MB | 1,340-1,406 → 1,100-1,142 MB | 1,485-1,489 → 1,231-1,235 MB |
| Snapshot cache at the end | 637-702 → 503-534 MB | 622-673 → 289-439 MB | 726-754 → 458-472 MB |
| Peak voxel data / systems | 288-300 / 644-648 → 288-291 / 644-648 MB | 307-308 / 597-599 → 309-313 / 599-603 MB | 292 / 703-704 → 290-291 / 702-704 MB |
| Frame P95 / P99 | 27.4-33.0 / 38.2-43.5 → 26.7-32.9 / 32.7-43.2 ms | 24.0-30.1 / 31.1-38.0 → 23.7-30.6 / 29.0-41.0 ms | 23.5-30.2 / 29.4-38.3 → 23.4-26.5 / 28.0-35.0 ms |
| Manager P95 | 5.4-6.5 → 5.2-6.3 ms | 5.7-6.9 → 5.6-7.1 ms | 5.9-7.6 → 6.1-6.6 ms |
| Catch-up | 0.17-0.21 → 0.17-0.22 s | 0.17 → 0.17 s | 0.17-0.54 → 0.17 s |
| Game-thread decode, traverse | 14-24 → 16-20 ms | 20-26 → 20-30 ms | 12-16 → 12-13 ms |

D3 is met on every planet with the cache counted. Worker decodes: on the small planet 2,387 → 3,607 a traverse (a chunk read
by a seam job and by cooks is decoded once for its snapshot and once for its shell when no snapshot is cached), 2.60 → 2.43 s
of worker time; on L 1,917 → 1,498, 1.97 → 0.81 s (no uniform chunk decodes). The frame times of this session ran 25-35%
over §20.13's in both settings and in every manager section alike, those G69 does not touch included (the far field +37%,
LOD +40%, the GPU +6%), and the first repetition was the slowest in both: the machine's, not the change's; compare within
the table.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 585/585 headless (582 + the
three above) and 585/585 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss, no ensure). The 108 GPU parity lines
are CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change). After merging main (G68, §20.14): 587/587 headless.

**New findings** (in §14.1):

| ID | Finding | Status |
|----|---------|--------|
| G71 | Seam jobs and chunk meshes still read their participants' whole snapshots: with shells, 540-607 of the small planet's mid-traverse entries (518-579 MB). A seam reads its participants only near the seam, but each side's ring is recomputed with its own samplers, which reach a stride-scale depth, and the rings must stay bit-identical | Open (an improvement): D3 is met without it |

**Left as they were:** seam jobs and chunk meshes on whole snapshots (G71), the cache's lifetime (128 ticks: shorter only
re-makes), the collision radius, and copies of resident chunks for seam jobs.

G69 is fixed.

### 20.16 G70: the water pull, again when a neighbour's water rises (2026-10-22)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `45fbf28`, UE5_PluginDev `a6ccc2b` (G68 and G69 merged). Branches `fix/g70-water-pull-order`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g70-water-pull-order` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8`; tests headless and in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.13): in `Streaming.Planet.FarReadsOffGameThread` 9 air voxels below the sea at chunk (6, 0, 9)'s
+Y+Z corner flooded in some runs and not in others, with either setting of `voxel.FarCompression.SnapshotReads`, so the
test compared the water flags apart.

**The cause.** A chunk pulls the water flags across its six faces from its neighbours once, when its mesh lands
(`UVoxelChunkManager::PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`, at the mesh submit), and floods its own dry air below the sea from
those seeds. A chunk wholly under the sea has no water of its own (generation's fill pass seeds the chunk the sea's surface
crosses), so it gets all of it that way. Nothing pushed: a neighbour whose water rose after the chunk pulled (its own pull,
or its generated water arriving with its data) never passed it on. Water that reached a chunk only through a neighbour that
flooded later never came, and which voxels flooded depended on the order the chunks finished meshing in. A seabed chunk
meshed before the chunk above it stayed dry.

**What changed** (`VoxelChunkManager.cpp/.h`; no change to generation, meshes, the edit-driven flood or the water tiles'
rule):

- **The pull again** (`QueueWaterRepulls`, `ProcessWaterRepulls`). When a chunk's water rises, its face neighbours that
  have already pulled (`bWaterSettled`) and reach below the sea are queued to pull again: across every face when its water
  first settles (its generated water arrived with it), else across the faces its pull flooded
  (`PropagateWaterFromNeighbors` now reports them). The queue runs each tick within about a millisecond (at least one
  pull), first in first out, on Loaded chunks only: a chunk queued for a mesh or meshing pulls when that mesh lands, and its
  voxels are not written while a job may read them. A pull that floods refreshes the chunk's water tile (heightmap worlds)
  and queues on. The flood so reaches every dry air voxel below the sea connected to the sea through loaded chunks,
  whatever the order they mesh in.
- **One switch:** `voxel.Water.PullAgain` (1; 0 = one pull each, the rule before). `voxel.Water.Stats` reports the second
  pulls (`GetWaterRepullStats`: queued, run, flooded, voxels, skipped, pending).
- **Left as they were:** scatter is handed a chunk's voxels before its pull (its cave points are classified by the
  underground flag, so the pull's flags rarely reach it), and an unloaded chunk's water is pulled again from its neighbours
  when it reloads.

**Tests.**

- **`Streaming.Water.PullOrder.Plane`, `.Planet`** (new, `VoxelWaterPullOrderTests.cpp`): a sea two chunk layers deeper than
  the seabed's top (the small plane under a sea at 2,900; the small planet under one 2,300 over the datum), streamed from a
  viewer 1,200 under the datum, so the chunks under the sea mesh from the bottom up. Afterwards the flags must be closed
  under the flood: from every flagged voxel, no dry air below the sea in a loaded chunk is reachable through such air, in
  its own chunk or across a face. With the fix there is none; with one pull each, many:

  | | Before (one pull each) | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Plane, 48 chunks | 202,034 dry voxels the flood reaches, in 18 chunks (512,075 flagged) | 0 (714,109 flagged; 119 second pulls, 17 flooded 139,514 voxels) |
  | Planet, 40 chunks | 103,345, in 10 chunks (500,869 flagged) | 0 (604,214 flagged; 79 second pulls, 4 flooded 39,055 voxels) |

- **`Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.FarReadsOffGameThread`** (G65's) compare every chunk's water count between their two runs
  now: 0 of 195 planet and 0 of 231 plane chunks differ in three runs of each (six worlds each). With one pull each
  the three runs of the planet's showed no difference either: the miss was intermittent there (0-1 of 195 chunks in
  §20.13's runs), and the `PullOrder` tests are the deterministic check.
- **What stays history-dependent:** a chunk's flags persist until it unloads, so water a neighbour passed on before it
  unloaded stays, and a neighbour that unloads before its mesh lands passes its water only to chunks that pulled while it
  had data. The flood is the same whatever order the chunks mesh in, given the chunks that were loaded together.
- **Unchanged and green:** `Streaming.WaterPropagation.*` (the edit-driven flood, its chunk-arrival scans, tiles and undo),
  `Streaming.EditRemesh.*`.

**Live** (a worktree editor, `voxel.Water.Stats` after streaming): `VoxelDemo` from the spawn, a minute: 1,350 second
pulls queued and run, 2 flooded 124 voxels one pull each would have left dry. `Review_Planet` settled at 45°N 20°E: 2,178
run, none flooded. A second pull without seeds reads only its chunk's six faces; the queue's millisecond a tick was not
reached.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 589/589 headless and 589/589 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device
loss). The 108 GPU
parity lines are CRC-identical to G44's.

### 20.17 G64: the minimap fills its texture only when it changed (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `45fbf28`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `c34a8d9`, UE5_PluginDev `a6ccc2b` (G69 merged). Branches
`docs/g64-minimap` (VoxelWorlds), `fix/g64-minimap-tick` (VoxelCharacterPlugin) and `claude/g64-minimap-tick` (UE5_PluginDev).
Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background
throttling off. The code is VoxelCharacterPlugin's (`UVCMinimapWidget`, `VCPlanetMapProjection`); this plugin has the
write-up.

**The finding** (§20.10): the minimap widget's tick took over 2 ms in about 18% of PIE frames on every planet alike.

**Instruments first**, kept in the build: the refresh's phases are timed (tile requests, texture fill, texture upload,
markers, the refresh; trace scopes `VCMinimap_*`), and `vc.Minimap.Stats [reset]` logs refreshes, fills, refreshes skipped
and over 2 ms, and each phase's mean and maximum.

**The cause.** The refresh runs every 0.1 s (`UpdateInterval`), one frame in six, and each refresh filled the 284 × 284
texture on the CPU. Standing for 14 s at 45°N 20E: on the small planet and on L every one of 138-140 refreshes took over
2 ms; the texture fill took 2.6-2.8 ms (the tangent-plane sampler, `FVCPlanetMapSampler`), the tile requests 0.05 ms, the
upload 0.08 ms (`UpdateResource`) and the markers 0.02 ms. On `VoxelDemo` (a plane) the fill took 2.5 ms: it blitted every
pixel of every tile in view at its near corner, about 300,000 pixels to draw 80,000 texels.

**The fix** (VoxelCharacterPlugin):

- **Fill only when something changed** (`vc.Minimap.SkipUnchanged`, 1). A refresh still requests the tiles, rotates the
  image and places the markers. `NeedsRefill` fills only when:
  - there is no texture yet, or its size changed;
  - the player moved `RefillShiftTexels` (2) from the last fill's centre;
  - an image of a tile the last fill read changed (`ComputeTileSignature`: each tile's entry, its pixel buffer and its
    resolution; the samplers report the tiles they read, `VisitedTiles`);
  - `MaxRefillSeconds` (2) passed.
- **The shift.** Between fills the image is shifted back by the player's movement since the last fill
  (`GetFillOffsetTexels`, rotated with the map), so the terrain stays under the player. The texture gets a margin for it
  (289 × 289 at the defaults; 160 uu a texel, shown 1:1).
- **The display frame.** On a planet the heading and the markers are taken on the tangent plane the texture was drawn in
  (`GetDisplayFrame`), because neighbouring planes turn against each other near a pole.
- **A plane is filled texel by texel** (`FVCPlaneMapSampler`, `vc.Minimap.TexelFill`, 1). Each texel shows the tile pixel
  just inside its far corner, which is the pixel the blit wrote last. The columns' and rows' tiles and positions are worked
  out once. Where tile pixels are coarser than texels every texel is drawn; the blit left gaps there.
- **The planet sampler** steps its interpolation along a row and truncates instead of flooring.

**Tests.**

- **`VoxelCharacter.Map.PlaneMapSampler`** (new): on a small plane's tiles, off the tile grid, with 1.6 tile pixels a texel
  the texel fill draws the blit's image (100% of 16,384 texels here). With 0.4 the blit leaves 36% of the texels as
  background and the texel fill draws them all.
- **`VoxelCharacter.Planet.MinimapShift`** (new): a texture filled two texels away, shifted, with the heading on its own
  plane, shows terrain across the visible square within 0.017 texels of a fresh fill, at 0-89.9° on planets of 250,000 and
  5,000,000 uu. With the heading on the player's own plane it would be off by 1.03 texels at 80°, 2.07 at 85° and 113 at
  89.9° on the small planet.
- The planet sampler tests (`VoxelCharacter.Planet.MapSampler`, `MapZoomAtScale`) pass unchanged (99.36-99.77% exact
  texels).

**Benches.** These are in-session A/Bs by cvar, because this machine's speed swung three- to fourfold between sessions.
Old = `vc.Minimap.SkipUnchanged 0` and `vc.Minimap.TexelFill 0` (as before); new = both 1. The pawn was stepped 60 uu
every 0.1 s by teleports, 7,200 uu in 18-21 s (about 380 uu/s), at 45°N 20E on the planets and along X on `VoxelDemo`:

| | Fills | Refreshes over 2 ms | Fill, mean | Refresh, mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small planet, old → new | 173-183 → 20 | 158-176 → 18-19 | 2.13-2.46 → 2.03-2.34 ms | 2.35-2.73 → 0.36-0.42 ms |
| L, old → new | 174-185 → 20 | 66-120 → 3-12 | 1.91-2.27 → 1.72-2.29 ms | 2.14-2.55 → 0.34-0.41 ms |
| `VoxelDemo`, old → texel fill → new | 177 → 190 → 20 | 177 → 20 → 0 | 2.54 → 1.09 → 0.90 ms | 2.74 → 1.34 → 0.21 ms |

`VoxelDemo`'s second repetition is left out: its runs' settings did not take (its new run filled at every refresh). Standing
still the texture is filled 7-14 times in 138-140 refreshes (every 2 s, more where tiles were still drawing), with 0-11
refreshes over 2 ms against all of them.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 589/589 headless (587 + the
two above) and 589/589 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines are
CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change).

**Left as they were:** a planet's fill (about 2 ms; while moving, once a second at this speed and more often faster), the
texture upload (`UpdateResource`, under 0.15 ms), and the world map widget, which draws only while it is open.

G64 is fixed.

### 20.18 G67: uniform chunks collapse as they are generated (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `fdd2310`, UE5_PluginDev `9369a37` (G64 merged). Branches `fix/g67-uniform-collapse` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g67-uniform-collapse` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.11): after a teleport or a spawn the whole window streams in at once. It stays resident until far
compression catches up, and about 340 of its chunks are uniform (all air, all rock or open sea). The sweep collapses
those at no cost, but only after the same wait.

**The cause, confirmed.** Generation stored every chunk resident (`SetResidentVoxelData`), and the sweep looks at a chunk
only after it has been idle for `IdleFrames` (300). A uniform chunk therefore held its whole array (1 MB at 64³) for
those frames, near the viewer too. At the bench's start (10 s after the settle) M had 475-479 resident chunks and 21-26
uniform, and L had 504-511 and 4-14. Over the traverse the sweep brought the uniform count up to 485-502.

**The fix** (VoxelWorlds; `voxel.FarCompression.UniformAtGeneration`, 1; 0 = as before):

- **Generation finds a uniform result** where it makes the voxels (`FAsyncGenerationResult::bUniform` / `UniformValue`):
  - the CPU generation worker;
  - the tree-injection worker, after it injects;
  - GPU readbacks as they land (`ProcessPendingGPUReadbacks`), with the tick's landed readbacks scanned in parallel
    (`ParallelFor`).

  `FChunkDescriptor::ComputeUniformValue` compares whole voxels as words in 64-voxel blocks and stops at the first block
  that differs, so a chunk with any surface costs next to nothing. A fully uniform chunk is read whole.
- **The result is stored collapsed**: `ProcessCompletedAsyncGenerations` stores the data and then
  `FChunkDescriptor::CollapseToUniform` collapses it (no second scan, no content version change), before
  `OnChunkGenerationComplete`. `UVoxelChunkManager::GetUniformAtGenerationCount` counts these.
- **Nothing expands it again.** Its snapshot is the shared array for its value (G69, `voxel.Snapshot.ShareUniform`; that
  sharing applies only to a collapsed chunk). A point read (`GetVoxelResident`) now answers with the chunk's value; before,
  it expanded the array.

**Designs dropped on the way** (benches as below, three runs per planet):

- **A worker task per GPU readback for the scan** held each GPU chunk's generation slot for one more tick. Catch-up went
  from 0.22-0.29 to 0.48-0.53 s on the small planet and from 0.42-0.60 to 0.87-0.99 s on L (M unchanged).
- **The scan inline on the game thread**, one readback after another, brought catch-up back. But the generation poll's
  P95 rose from 0.03 to 0.60-0.68 ms on M and L (max 1.88-3.40 ms).
- **Scanning the tick's readbacks in parallel** (kept): P95 0.40-0.44 ms on M and L (max 0.96-2.52) and 0.12-0.14 ms on
  the small planet (max 0.59-1.38).

**Tests.**

- **`VoxelWorlds.Compression.CollapseToUniform`** (new): a chunk found uniform collapses with no scan and keeps its
  content version, a point read answers its value without expanding it, a chunk already collapsed does not collapse
  again, and expanding it gives the value at every voxel.
- **`VoxelWorlds.Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.UniformAtGeneration`** (new): one place is streamed twice with the sweep held
  off (`IdleFrames` 1,000,000), first with the setting at 0 and then at 1.
  - At 0 no chunk is collapsed.
  - At 1, on the plane 121 of 207 chunks are collapsed as generated and the voxel data falls from 3.3 to 1.4 MB; at 45°N
    20E on the small planet 75 of 158 are, and it falls from 19.8 to 10.4 MB.
  - In both runs every chunk's voxels and every mesh and seam are the same, and the stream expands nothing on the game
    thread.
- **`VoxelWorlds.Compression.Uniform.RoundTrip`** now expects a point read to leave a uniform chunk collapsed.

**Benches.** In-session A/B by the cvar, old = 0 and new = 1, with a fresh PIE for each run. Each run teleported to 45°N 20E
with a settle, waited 10 s (inside the post-teleport transient, §20.11) and then ran P6.4's great circle
(`1500 40000 gc=45:20:90 follow=300 warmup=30 catchup=90`). Three runs per planet and mode, interleaved, with the order
alternating per repetition:

| | Small planet, old → new | M, old → new | L, old → new |
|---|---|---|---|
| At the start: resident / uniform chunks | 467-476 / 2-4 → 436-446 / 31-32 | 475-479 / 21-26 → 242-246 / 254-262 | 504-511 / 4-14 → 255-260 / 271-289 |
| Peak voxel data | 524-532 → 490-494 MB | 522-523 → 291-294 MB | 576-590 → 294-338 MB |
| Peak voxel systems | 795-798 → 761-766 MB | 797-798 → 567-569 MB | 866-882 → 584-629 MB |
| Peak snapshot cache | 692-700 → 666-679 MB | 547-552 → 361-372 MB | 598-624 → 379-384 MB |
| Peak systems + snapshot cache + far field | 1,515-1,549 → 1,462-1,471 MB | 1,332-1,343 → 887-903 MB | 1,465-1,500 → 955-1,000 MB |
| Catch-up | 0.23-0.27 → 0.20-0.30 s | 0.18-0.22 → 0.17-0.20 s | 0.47-0.59 → 0.46-0.55 s |
| Frame P95 | 34.5-36.1 → 34.2-38.1 ms | 35.5-36.4 → 34.7-35.8 ms | 35.6-35.8 → 35.3-35.7 ms |
| Manager P95 | 9.3-9.6 → 9.3-10.9 ms | 9.4-9.7 → 9.1-9.3 ms | 9.9-10.3 → 9.1-9.6 ms |
| Generation poll P95 (max) | 0.03 (0.12-0.48) → 0.12-0.14 (0.59-1.38) ms | 0.03 (0.08-0.25) → 0.40-0.43 (0.96-1.00) ms | 0.03 (0.21-0.39) → 0.41-0.44 (1.25-2.52) ms |

This machine ran at about 35 ms a frame in both modes in this session. The small planet's 38.1 ms frame P95 (and its
10.9 ms manager P95) comes from one run; its other two match the old runs. The small planet's window holds few uniform
chunks: at most 74-75 over the traverse, against 485-502 on M and L. With G67, M and L's traverse peaks about 440-500 MB
lower with everything counted, and D3 (1.5 GB) is met with room on all three planets.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 594/594 headless (591 + the
three above). In the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss), 593 of 594 passed: the round trip's old assertion
failed. With its update, the compression tests and the two streaming tests above pass in the editor too. The 108 GPU
parity lines are CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change).

**Left as they were:** the cost of the generation poll above, a fully uniform chunk read whole as its readback lands, and
non-uniform far chunks, which still wait for the sweep's idle frames and encode budget (§20.11).
