### 20.19 G71: resident chunks' snapshots share the chunk's array (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `fdd2310`, UE5_PluginDev `9369a37` (G64 and G70 merged); VoxelWorlds `93efb5c` (G67, §20.18) merged in
before the PR. Branches `fix/g71-seam-snapshots`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g71-seam-snapshots` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic
Games\UE_5.8`; tests headless and in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.15): with G69's shells, seam jobs and chunk meshes still read their participants' whole snapshots,
540-607 of the small planet's mid-traverse entries (518-579 MB), and a seam shell would have to be stride-deep.

**Measured first** (a `voxel.Snapshot.Stats` line kept in the build: the seam and mesh entries by the chunk's rendered LOD,
by who took them, and what a seam shell would hold). The small planet's great circle (the protocol below, one run, the
stats 6-40 s in): the cache held 476-651 entries (450-628 MB), 82-93% of them taken by a seam job or a chunk mesh. Of
those:

| | LOD 0 | LOD 1 | LOD 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entries (seam jobs only / with their chunk mesh) | 0-19 / 1-19 | 6-61 / 33-96 | 323-435 / 3-51 |
| What a seam shell would hold of them | 36% | 52% | 76% |

A seam ring is recomputed on each side with that side's samplers: about 2 × stride + 2 voxels deep from a face on the
neighbour's side and 3 × stride + 2 on the owner's (at 64³ and stride 4 that is 10 and 14 of 64). Most entries are far LOD 2
chunks read only by seam jobs, and a shell deep enough for their rings keeps three quarters of each, so shells would have
saved about 30% (150-180 MB) for a bit-identical rewrite of every seam mesher (DC face, edge and corner, same and mixed
LOD, Marching Cubes' and cubic seams). No chunk mesh read an entry that a seam job did not. Another 35-47% of the cache
(167-297 entries, the same in MB) were copies of chunks that were still resident: each one a second copy of a 1 MB array
the chunk held anyway. The user chose to share those instead (2026-10-23).

**What changed** (`ChunkDescriptor.h`, `VoxelChunkManager.cpp/.h`, `VoxelResidencyStats`; no change to generation,
meshing, seams, collision or the water rules):

- **A chunk's resident array is shared copy-on-write** (`FChunkDescriptor::VoxelArray`, a
  `TSharedPtr<TArray<FVoxelData>>` instead of the array). `ShareVoxelData` hands it to a reader. `GetVoxelDataMutable`,
  `SetVoxel` and `SetVoxelByIndex` clone it first while anything else holds it (`DetachVoxelArray`), so a reader's
  voxels never change under it; installing new data, clearing, collapsing and compressing drop only the chunk's
  reference. `EnsureResident` and the read accessors return a const array. A copy of the descriptor shares the array the
  same way.
- **Snapshots of resident chunks without edits share it** (`GetSeamVoxelSnapshot`, a new kind `SharedResident`): seam
  jobs, collision cooks and the water pull read the chunk's own array, with no game-thread copy. A chunk with edits
  still gets its edit-merged copy. The water pull, the one write that keeps the `ContentVersion`, drops the chunk's
  snapshot and shell before it writes (it dropped them after), so the write clones only while a job holds the array.
- **The far-compression encode reads the chunk's array too** instead of a copy into a pooled scratch array.
- **Counted once.** A shared entry holds nothing of its own while the chunk still holds the array
  (`GetSnapshotOwnBytes`); the memory stats and `voxel.Snapshot.Stats` count it in the voxel data, and once the chunk
  compacts, unloads or clones it, in the cache. `voxel.Snapshot.Stats` lists the shared entries and the copy-on-write
  clones (`VoxelResidencyStats::GetSharedArrayClones`).
- **One switch:** `voxel.Snapshot.ShareResident` (1; 0 = copies, as before).

**Tests.**

- **`Compression.SharedArray.CopyOnWrite`** (new): sharing hands out the chunk's own memory; each write path clones a
  shared array once and leaves the reader's voxels, and clones nothing when unshared; new data, clearing, collapsing and
  compressing leave the reader's array whole; a copy of a descriptor shares and writes apart.
- **`Compression.SharedArray.WorkerReads`** (new): eight workers read a shared array while the game thread writes the
  chunk 400 times; 919-1,137 reads (three runs), every one the voxels as taken.
- **`Streaming.Planet.SharedResidentSnapshots`, `Streaming.Plane.SharedResidentSnapshots`** (new): the far-reads test's
  places (45°N 20°E with a sea at the datum, and the plane), the far band compacted, a 3,000 uu move, with
  `ShareResident` 0 and 1: every chunk's voxels (water included) and every mesh and seam the same; every resident
  snapshot shared (310-320 on the planet, 373 on the plane) where 321-324 and 373 were copied; the snapshot cache's peak
  20,992-21,376 → 15,232-15,872 KB on the planet and 3,216 → 2,256 KB on the plane, with the voxel data 28,713-29,552 →
  22,256-22,896 and 4,822 → 3,309 KB (three runs); no clones.
- **`Streaming.{Planet,Plane}.CollisionNeighborShells`** (G69's) compare the shells with whole snapshots as the cache
  held them for cooks, so they run with `ShareResident 0`.

**Benches.** One build, the setting by cvar: copies = `voxel.Snapshot.ShareResident 0` (the cache as on main), shared = 1.
G69's protocol (a fresh PIE on `PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride`, `vox.TPLatLon 45 20`, the bench 25 s after the
settle, `voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 1500 40000 gc=45:20:90 follow=300 warmup=30 catchup=90`), three runs per planet and setting,
interleaved, after a throwaway warm-up. The peak with the cache is one sample's systems (voxel data, edits, renderer,
collision, scatter) plus snapshot cache plus far field. Copies → shared (ranges over the three runs):

| | Small planet (S) | M (50 km) | L (1,000 km) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Snapshot cache, peak (shells included) | 658-692 → 491-496 MB | 478-494 → 314-331 MB | 503-511 → 317-335 MB |
| Peak with the cache and the far field | 1,283-1,302 → 1,067-1,079 MB | 1,104-1,118 → 876-882 MB | 1,158-1,170 → 896-915 MB |
| Snapshot cache at the end | 519-562 → 389-393 MB | 369-450 → 257-322 MB | 448-488 → 283-304 MB |
| Peak voxel data / systems | 296-325 / 593-619 → 304-307 / 599-602 MB | 308-310 / 596-601 → 305-307 / 594-596 MB | 293-295 / 610-615 → 286-289 / 605-607 MB |
| Resident snapshots copied → shared, a traverse | 1,389-1,646 → 1,640-1,685 | 1,278-1,557 → 1,525-1,582 | 1,626-1,653 → 1,609-1,749 |
| Seam scheduler P95 | 1.86-2.01 → 1.40-1.47 ms | 1.86-1.93 → 1.33-1.43 ms | 1.81-1.92 → 1.25-1.29 ms |
| Far-compression sweep P95 | 0.59-0.65 → 0.10-0.11 ms | 0.50-0.57 → 0.09-0.10 ms | 0.53-0.58 → 0.09-0.10 ms |
| Frame P95 / P99 | 28.0-31.5 / 34.1-35.9 → 28.0-29.4 / 34.5-36.2 ms | 25.5-26.3 / 30.6-33.0 → 24.3-25.6 / 29.1-31.8 ms | 25.9-27.5 / 30.6-34.9 → 25.2-26.8 / 30.1-32.0 ms |
| Manager P95 | 7.1-7.6 → 6.3-6.9 ms | 6.4-6.7 → 5.7-6.1 ms | 6.5-7.2 → 6.1-6.4 ms |
| Catch-up | 0.17 → 0.17-0.18 s | 0.17 → 0.17 s | 0.18-0.68 → 0.17-0.22 s |
| Game-thread decode, traverse | 37-41 → 42-46 ms | 22-25 → 21-27 ms | 13-19 → 12-17 ms |

Run by run, the traverse's peak with the cache and the far field fell by 204-229 MB on S, 222-239 on M and 243-274 on L
(16-23%), and the cache at the end by 16-43%: what is left of it is mostly far-compressed chunks decoded for seam jobs
and cooks (seam shells would still save about 30% of those), the shells and the uniform values. Each copy was a 1 MB
game-thread copy, about 1.3-1.6 GB of them a traverse: the seam scheduler's P95 fell by about half a millisecond and the
manager's by 0.3-0.9 ms. The far-compression sweep no longer copies each chunk into a scratch array for its encode. No
run cloned an array: the water pull drops a chunk's snapshot before it writes, and no seam job or cook held a chunk the
pull wrote. The small planet's game-thread decode is 5-7 ms higher over a 26.7 s traverse, M's and L's overlap (not
traced; sharing changes no read of a compressed chunk); the rest is within run-to-run spread. D3 is met with more room:
the largest peak with the cache and the far field is 1.08 GB.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 595/595 headless (591 on
main + the four above) and 595/595 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines
are CRC-identical to G44's (no generation or meshing change). After merging main (G67, §20.18; its `CollapseToUniform`
drops only the chunk's reference): 598/598 headless and 598/598 in the editor, the parity lines the same.

**Left as they were:** seam jobs and chunk meshes on whole snapshots of far-compressed chunks (shells would save about 30%
of those), a chunk mesh's own copy of a resident chunk (`MeshRequest.VoxelData`, held while its job runs) and scatter's
(`FPendingScatterGeneration::ChunkVoxelData`, held while it waits), and the edit-merged copies of chunks with edits.

G71 is fixed.

### 20.20 G19: one sea plane in heightmap worlds (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `6cf8973`, VoxelCharacterPlugin `1d84e16`, UE5_PluginDev `b992fe5` (G71 merged). Branches
`fix/g19-sea-plane` (VoxelWorlds, VoxelCharacterPlugin) and `claude/g19-sea-plane` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor
5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8`; tests headless and in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098).

**The finding** (§17): heightmap water consumers disagreed on the water plane. Generation, scatter, the map and PCG used
`WaterLevel`; navigation, the character and the NPC spawner used `WaterLevel + WorldOrigin.Z`. They agree whenever
`WorldOrigin.Z` is 0. Since Phase 3 both conventions had been named in `FVoxelSeaSurface` (`FromConfig`,
`FromConfigOriginRelative`).

**Which plane is the sea.** `WorldOrigin` moves the chunk grid, not the ground: the terrain's heights are world Z
(`SeaLevel` + `BaseHeight` + the noise, `FVoxelWorldModeFactory::MakeTerrainParams`), and generation's water fill (CPU and
GPU) floods air at world Z ≤ `WaterLevel` (`GetChunkWorldPosition` is `WorldOrigin` plus the grid position). The water tiles
are drawn there too (built relative to `WorldOrigin.Z` and placed at it by both renderers), and so is the island's far
ocean. So the sea is `WaterLevel`, wherever `WorldOrigin` is.

**The audit.** Every plane test in the code, by the plane it used:

| Plane | Consumers |
|---|---|
| `WaterLevel`, world Z | generation's water fill and underwater materials (CPU, GPU), the water tiles' height, the far ocean, scatter's underwater class, the map and its edit overlay, PCG, POI placement |
| `WaterLevel + WorldOrigin.Z` | navigation (`FVoxelSurfaceNavParams::WaterLevel` and `Sea`), the character (swim and breath depth, the spawn search, the sea spawn on a planet), the NPC spawner, the debug commands, `GetSeaDepthAt` (Blueprint), the LOD slab's water term (`SlabWaterLevel`) |
| grid Z against `WaterLevel` (the same as the row above) | the chunk manager's water pull and its second pulls (`PropagateWaterFromNeighbors`, `QueueWaterRepulls`), the edit-driven flood (`UVoxelWaterPropagation::IsBelowSea` and its plane clip), the water tiles' chunk filter (`UpdateWaterTileContribution`) |

The last row was not in G19: those tests passed the voxel's grid position to the sea, not its world position, which on a
plane is the origin-relative plane again. With `WorldOrigin.Z` ≠ 0 each origin-relative consumer was off by it: a pawn
reads its swim depth from the wrong surface (clamped to 0 under a negative origin) and spawns on the seabed or finds no
land; navigation walks under the sea or treats land as water; the LOD slab drops the layer the water's surface is in, or
streams layers of air above it; a chunk holding the sea's surface gets no water tile under a negative origin; a dig under
the sea floods up to the wrong height, or not at all.

**What changed** (one plane, generation's):

- `FVoxelSeaSurface::FromConfigOriginRelative` is gone and `UVoxelChunkManager::GetSeaSurface` takes no parameter: every
  consumer reads `FromConfig`, the `WaterLevel` plane in world Z (the sphere on a planet, unchanged). Navigation, the
  character, the NPC spawner, the debug commands and `GetSeaDepthAt` with it.
- Navigation's `WaterLevel` is the sea's plane; the LOD slab's water term is `WaterLevel`.
- The water pull, its second pulls, the edit-driven flood and the water tiles' chunk filter test the voxel's world position
  (`WorldOrigin` + grid) on the plane, as they already did on a planet.

**No world in the project changes.** All 25 `UVoxelWorldConfiguration` assets have `WorldOrigin.Z` 0 (listed headless: the
demo and review worlds at (12,345, 54,321, 0), the rest at the origin), and at Z 0 every changed line computes what it did.

**Tests.** Each new test fails before the change and passes after:

- **`Streaming.Plane.OneSeaPlane`** (new, `VoxelSeaPlaneTests.cpp`): the small plane with its sea at 0, `WorldOrigin.Z`
  -3,000 and 2,600, streamed. Generation's highest water-flagged voxel is at Z 0. Every one of the 22,309 flagged voxels
  must be under the chunk manager's sea (before: 0 of them at -3,000), a voxel above the highest above it (before: under
  it at 2,600), and every chunk column holding water must have a water tile (before: 0 of 12 at -3,000).
- **`LOD.VerticalWindow.WaterPlaneWithOrigin`** (new): every far column's slab must be its surface ± the slack, raised to
  the water plane, in the grid's layers. Before: 93 of 252 columns wrong with the origin 20,000 down and the sea at 6,000
  (the water's surface layer dropped), 107 with it 9,000 up and the sea at 1,000 (a layer of air added).
- **`Navigation.Plane.SeaWithOrigin`** (new): navigation's sea is the `WaterLevel` plane and ground a wade deeper under it is
  water. Before: its plane at -3,000 and 2,600.
- **`VoxelCharacter.Plane.SpawnAboveSeaWithOrigin`** (new, VoxelCharacterPlugin): from a seabed start the spawn search finds
  dry land, from a land start it stays. Before: the seabed accepted at -3,000; no spawn from either start at 2,600.
- **The edit-driven flood's suite** (`Streaming.WaterPropagation.*`: digs, pockets, chunk arrival, tiles, undo) now runs on a
  plane whose origin is off the voxel grid on every axis, Z included ((3,112.5, -1,937.5, -2,187.5)); its helpers test the
  plane in world space (`SeaGridZ`), as does `Streaming.Water.PullOrder`'s measure.
- `Streaming.Planet.SeaQueries` and `WorldModes.Planet.SeaDepth` check the one plane instead of the two.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 602/602 headless (598 on main
+ the four above) and 602/602 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines are
CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change).

G19 is fixed.

### 20.21 G28: the voxel over a buried chunk's top layer, caves included (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `6cf8973`, UE5_PluginDev `b992fe5` (G71 merged), with main's G19 (§20.20) and G39 (§20.22) merged in after the runs below.
Branches `fix/g28-buried-top-face` (VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g28-buried-top-face` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§19.4): a heightmap chunk's column and cubic scans cannot see the voxel over the chunk's top layer, which
belongs to the chunk above. G26 decided it within 1.5 voxels of the generated ground, where no cave reaches. Deeper, a cave
can open it, so it was still taken for air. A buried chunk's whole top face therefore carried a row of points inside the
rock. The buried-chunk test classified them underground, and underground-only scatter spawned on them.

**The cause, measured** with `voxel.Scatter.TopFaceAudit` on `VoxelDemo` before the fix (three runs, the A/B below):

- At each of the five stops, 450,763-586,088 of the cached chunks' top-face points were copies under the rock, against
  5,845-9,440 real crossings at the boundary (the surface, or a cave floor there).
- 378-756 spawn points of the underground-only types stood on the copies.
- Half of the surface points extracted over a run were copies: 5.15-5.18 million of them, against 2.56-2.57 million with
  the fix. They kept 32-43 MB in the surface cache.

**The fix** (VoxelWorlds; `voxel.Scatter.BuriedTopFace`, 1; 0 = before):

- `FScatterExtractionContext::GetVoxelAboveChunk` makes the voxel as generation makes it at any depth:
  - the generated height's signed distance at the chunk's top;
  - less the cave carve where that voxel is solid and under the ground. This is `FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::CalculateCaveDensity`
    at its depth under the generated ground, for the column's biome (the chunk's own voxel there carries it: a column has
    one biome), with the sea's minimum depth when the ground is under the sea. Generation's
    `GenerateChunkInfinitePlane` and `IslandBowl` apply the carve the same way;
  - with the chunk above's edit there applied, as before.
- The context carries the world's cave configuration when its caves are on (`CaveConfiguration`, set in
  `MakeExtractionContext`). With no caves the voxel is the terrain's alone.
- The column scan and the cubic scan decide that voxel for every column (`bDecideVoxelAboveAtAnyDepth`), not only in
  G26's band:
  - **solid:** the top voxel is no surface and the rest of the column is covered;
  - **air:** the point is a cave floor at the boundary, underground by the buried-chunk test.
- A buried chunk with no cave at its top face now finds no point there. When it finds none anywhere it caches no surface
  data, as any chunk without a surface.
- Planets, generation and the band's rule are unchanged; no `GenerationVersion` bump.

**Tooling.** `voxel.Scatter.TopFaceAudit` counts the real crossings at the boundary from both chunks' edit-merged voxels,
over the columns the scan reads (`realCross`), and those with no point (`missedReal`, `missedRealDeep`). A rule deciding
the voxel above wrongly would lose real floors, and this shows it. A top voxel at exactly the surface density puts its
crossing at its own height, so a point there counts too. `voxel.Scatter.Stats` reports the worker extraction since the
last `voxel.Scatter.Stats reset`: chunks, surface points, and extraction and placement time
(`UVoxelScatterManager::ResetExtractionTiming`).

**Tests.**

- **`VoxelWorlds.Scatter.TopFace.BuriedCaves`** (new): real InfinitePlane terrain with biomes, a sea at 0 and the
  default cave layers. Nine chunk pairs are generated on the CPU, each boundary at least 12 voxels under the lowest ground
  of its chunk column. Over every column of the lower chunk's top layer, on both heightmap paths:
  - 8,307 columns with a solid top voxel, 95 of them under a cave at the boundary;
  - with the fix: 95 points, all underground, no copy, no crossing missed;
  - taken for air: 8,307 points, 8,212 of them copies.
  - **Edits on the upper chunk's bottom layer** (1,187 voxels dug over rock, 136 filled over caves): 2,526 crossings, no
    copy, none missed.
  - **Biome overrides** (caves only in the commonest of two biomes, from a shallower minimum depth): 80 crossings, no
    copy, none missed.
- `Scatter.TopFace.Contour`, `FlatGround` and `EditsAbove` (G26's) pass unchanged.

**A/B on `VoxelDemo`** (in-session, by the cvar). Six runs of one script, three per rule, interleaved. Each run: a fresh
PIE with the world's save deleted, the spawn (60 s), then `vox.TP` to the Village, the Tower, the second village and the
City, 45 s each. At each stop streaming was frozen for the audit, a per-chunk digest (`voxel.Scatter.Digest file`) and the
scatter statistics. GPU generation, CPU extraction (the demo's settings).

| Stop | Copies under the rock | Underground spawns on them | Real crossings (missed) | Surface cache |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spawn | 586,088 → 0 | 611 → 0 | 5,944 (0 → 0) | 129.3 → 86.0 MB |
| Village | 564,824 → 2 | 415 → 0 | 8,457 (0 → 1) | 128.7 → 86.7 MB |
| Tower | 459,661-482,908 → 1 | 482-756 → 0 | 7,703-7,996 (0 → 0) | 119.1-122.8 → 87.2-89.2 MB |
| Second village | 450,763 → 0 | 677 → 0 | 9,538 (0 → 0) | 119.6 → 86.6 MB |
| City | 520,293 → 0 | 378 → 0 | 7,653 (0 → 0) | 122.0 → 81.3 MB |

- **Scatter changed only where underground spawns stood on copies.** Within each stop, 173-188 chunks were in every run
  and gave the same digest in all three runs of each rule. Of them, 10-15 changed between the rules, and every one had
  underground spawns on copies in the old runs' audit. Their spawn points went 4,569 → 4,017 (spawn), 4,536 → 4,175, 6,547
  → 6,114, 4,937 → 4,609 and 486 → 109.
- **The three underground-only types** (15-17, the cave mushrooms) keep 18-22% of their spawn points, those on real cave
  floors: at the spawn 280, 250 and 248 → 65, 50 and 52. The 14 surface types are unchanged.
- **Cost:** over each run 1,899-1,915 chunks were extracted on workers. Extraction took 4.06-4.75 ms a chunk on the mean
  before and 3.87-4.31 after (the cave carve's cost is within the run-to-run spread). Placement halved, 0.150-0.169 →
  0.085-0.091 ms, on half the points. 221-247 chunks cached surface data before and 173-190 after.
- **The leftover:** under GPU generation 1-3 columns a stop disagree, the same in all three runs (three at the Village, one at the Tower, each a single column at a cave boundary): the GPU generator's density there differs from the CPU formula the rule uses. A fourth run of the fix with CPU generation (`voxel.GPUGeneration.Enable 0`) had 0 copies and 0 missed at every stop.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 599/599 headless (598 + the one above) and 599/599 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). The 108 GPU parity lines are CRC-identical to G44's (no generation change). With G19 merged, 603/603 headless; with G39 (§20.22) too, 609/609.

**Left as they were:** planets. A planet chunk's rays read the voxels past its +X, +Y and +Z faces as the generator makes
them without the cave carve (`GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk`, G29, G31). Deep under the ground that voxel is rock, so no copy
is made, but where a cave opens it the floor crossing in that cell is missed. That is G72, recorded below. Deeper digs keep
the buried-chunk test's edit-blindness, as G26 left them.

**G72 (new, open, low): planets.** `FScatterExtractionContext::GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk` makes the voxels past a planet
chunk's +X, +Y and +Z faces from the generated altitude alone. Where a cave opens such a voxel under the ground, a ray
crossing the face there reads rock and misses the cave floor's point, so underground scatter has no point in those cells.
Not measured. The same carve (`CalculateCaveDensity` with the planet's local up) would fix it; it changes planet scatter,
so it needs its own `Review_Planet` A/B. Fixed in §20.23.

G28 is fixed.

### 20.22 G39: biome blend zones dithered in patches, not along the voxel grid (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `50f96cd`, UE5_PluginDev `0a6dd79` (G19 merged). Branches `fix/g39-blend-dither` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g39-blend-dither` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8`; tests headless
and in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098). The user chose patches over a per-voxel hash, and no version bump.

**The finding** (§20.3): a voxel in a biome blend zone (no weight over 0.9) takes one biome's material, the first biome
whose cumulative weight passes a "random" value. That value was frac(W0 × 17.3 + W1 × 31.7 + depth × 0.1), with no hash of
the voxel's position. Across a zone the weights change slowly, so the value followed the voxel's depth under the surface,
which on a slope cycles with the voxel grid: the two materials alternated in bands along the grid. Every world mode had it;
planets showed it widest, the grid being tilted against local up everywhere and climate zones km across (`Review_Planet_L`'s
equator, M's 45° and equator from above). The same formula ran in four places: `FVoxelBiomeSnapshot::SelectBlendedMaterial`
and `SelectBlendedMaterialWithWater` (generation on the CPU), `FVoxelBiomeRegistry::GetBlendedMaterial` (the map's
fallback) and the GPU's `GpuBlendedMaterial`.

**The dither** (`FVoxelBiomeBlendDither`, `VoxelBiomeBlendDither.h`; mirrored bit for bit by `GpuBiomeBlendDither` in
`BiomeMaterial.ush`):

- *Key.* The voxel's integer position in voxels counted from the world's origin of space, round(WorldPos / VoxelSize), and
  the world seed. Generation adds the local index to the chunk's first voxel (`GridBase(ChunkCoord, ChunkSize,
  WorldOrigin, VoxelSize)`; the GPU gets it as `BlendDitherBase`); the analytic readers (`FVoxelSurfaceQuery`'s surface and
  planet conditions, the map's registry fallback) take `KeyAt` at the point they read. A planet uses the same key: its
  voxel's world position, as the ore `Rarity` hash does.
- *Value.* 3D value noise over a lattice 4 voxels apart. Each lattice point gets a 16-bit hash (the ore `Rarity` hash's mix
  on the lattice coordinates and the seed + 0x5D1A3). The eight corners are blended trilinearly with smoothstep weights
  (0, 5, 16 and 27 of 32 at the voxel's offset in its cell), all in integers (the sum stays under 2^31). The result goes
  through a fixed 257-entry table of the noise's distribution (`Cdf`, a 256-million-sample Monte Carlo over the 64 offsets),
  interpolated in integers. The value is a multiple of 2^-24, uniform on [0, 1), and the same on the CPU and the GPU.
  Without the equalisation, smoothed noise piles up around 0.5: a biome at weight 0.10 would cover 0.9% of the voxels and
  one at 0.25 9.8%.
- *Order.* The walk goes over the blend's biomes in BiomeID order (the GPU sorts its four entries with a five-comparator
  network). The blend sorts its biomes by weight, so a walk in that order changes biome in every voxel where the leading
  biome changes inside a zone: a seam down the middle of each zone. In BiomeID order the cumulative bounds do not move
  there.

The 0.9 shortcut stays: a weight over 0.9 takes its biome's material outright, so a zone's visible edge is where the leading
weight crosses 0.9, as before. `voxel.Biome.BlendDither` (default 1; 0 = the old value and weight order, for A/B) is read
wherever a pick is made, on any thread; the GPU gets it as `BlendDitherMode`.

**No version bump** (the user's decision): neither `GenerationVersion` nor `PlanetGenerationVersion` moved. Only generated
materials inside blend zones change, so a save from before loads; its edits apply over the new materials.

**Tests** (new, `BiomeBlendDitherTests.cpp` in VoxelCore, and one GPU test):

- `Biome.BlendDither.Uniform`: over 2 million voxels the value's 16 bins are within 0.61% of an even share, and a biome at
  weight 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 0.90 covers 0.1005 / 0.2507 / 0.5007 / 0.7505 / 0.9004 of the voxels.
- `Biome.BlendDither.Patches`: in a 50/50 blend, neighbours along each axis take the same biome 0.874-0.875 of the time
  (0.5 for independent picks); the value does not depend on depth.
- `Biome.BlendDither.Keys`: `GridBase` plus the local index equals `KeyAt` at the voxel's sample point for 60,000 voxels on
  three grids (two with origins off the voxel grid).
- `Biome.BlendDither.NoGridBands`: on a slope at weight 0.7, the leading biome's share by the surface's phase in the voxel
  layer (8 bins). Before: 0.000 to 1.000 (all of one biome in some phases, none in others: the bands). Now: 0.696 to 0.704.
- `Biome.BlendDither.DominanceFlip`: across a point where the leading biome changes (weights 0.501/0.499 to 0.499/0.501), the BiomeID
  walk changes 375 of 200,000 voxels; a walk in weight order would change all 200,000.
- `Generation.GPUvsCPUBlendDitherParity` (GPU): the default biomes with a wide blend (`BiomeBlendWidth` 0.5) on an off-grid
  origin. On the CPU the two settings pick differently in 4,179 of 32,768 voxels. GPU against CPU: 100.0% of the materials
  match with the dither and with the old pick, at LOD 0/1/2.
- `Biome.SnapshotParity`'s reference passes the same key as the surface query.

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 608/608 headless (602 on main
+ the six above) and 608/608 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). GPU parity, 36 cases at LOD 0/1/2:

- With `voxel.Biome.BlendDither 0`, all 108 lines are CRC-identical to G44's.
- With the dither (the default), 78 lines (26 cases) change CRC, the cases whose chunk holds a blend zone; 30 lines
  (10 cases) are identical: the ore variant and nine planet cases with no blend zone in their chunk.
- In every case the GPU's density differences from the CPU are the same counts as G44's, and its material differences the
  same or fewer (Simplex 2 → 0, L's coast 1 → 0).

**Live** (`PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride` and `VoxelDemo` with its own configuration; one PIE per world and
setting, the cvar set before the world generates; local noon; screenshots `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius/g39_*` in the
worktree, four pairs side by side in `g39_before_after.png`):

- *L and M at P6.2's equator site (0°, 100°E)*, from 12,000 uu up looking north (P6.2's framing). The old pick draws bands
  of the two materials along the voxel grid on the slopes, and wide strips of one material where the ground is flat (there
  the depth term is constant and the weights change slowly, so the value stays on one side of the leading weight). The
  dither draws the two materials in patches over the whole zone. Top-down at 2,500 uu on M: one material with the old
  pick, patches of the second biome over a share of the ground with the dither.
- *L at (0°, 0°)*: a blend zone the old pick draws in one material only; the dither draws patches. M at 45°N 20°E and at
  (0°, 0°) stand in one biome (the same either way; at (0°, 0°) a zone begins on the far ridge).
- *`VoxelDemo`*, from 6,000 uu over the world origin in four directions: with the old pick, strips of the second biome
  follow the terrain's contours through the forest's brown; with the dither they are patches. A zone's edge, where a weight
  crosses 0.9, looks as before.

G39 is fixed.

### 20.23 G72: the voxels past a planet chunk's faces, caves included (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `0da2b83`, UE5_PluginDev `5fb2245` (G28 merged). Branches `fix/g72-planet-face-caves` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g72-planet-face-caves` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a
worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§20.21): a planet chunk's rays (G31) read the voxels past its +X, +Y and +Z faces in their last cells.
`FScatterExtractionContext::GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk` made those voxels from the generated altitude alone. Where a cave
opens such a voxel under the ground, the extraction read rock there:

- the cave floor in that cell got no point;
- where the cave meets the face, the rock against the cave's air made a floor in the air (a point the neighbours' own
  voxels do not give).

It is the opposite of the heightmap's G28: no copies under the rock, but missed and misplaced cave floors.

**Measured first** with a new audit, `voxel.Scatter.PlanetFaceAudit`
(`UVoxelScatterManager::ComparePlanetFaceVoxels`). It extracts every cached chunk whose seven neighbours on those sides
have voxels twice: once with the voxels past its faces made, and once taken from the neighbours' edit-merged voxels
(`FScatterExtractionContext::OutsideVoxelSource`, the reference). It counts the reference points the made voxels miss and
the points they add, and which of each are underground.

On `Review_Planet` (`DemoCaveConfig`: Cheese 27-60 and Spaghetti 20-45 voxels down, no caves in biome 3, a 25-voxel
minimum under the sea), at four stops (45°N 20E, 0°N 100E, 30°S 60W, the cube corner), 173-201 chunks were compared at each:

- 8,793-11,243 reference points missed per stop (1.3-1.6% of 541,449-699,534), 92-97% of them underground;
- 284-46,141 points added, nearly all underground. The 46,141 are at 30°S 60W, where caverns meet many chunk faces;
- in 133-154 of the chunks.

**The fix** (VoxelWorlds; `voxel.Scatter.PlanetFaceCaves`, 1; 0 = before). `GetPlanetVoxelOutsideChunk` makes the voxel as
`GenerateChunkSphericalPlanet` does: the generated altitude's signed distance, less the cave carve where the voxel is solid
under the ground, with the neighbour's edit applied as before.

- The carve is `FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::CalculateCaveDensity` at the voxel's depth along local up, with the planet's
  vertical scale along local up (SP-B6) and the sea's minimum depth when the ground is under the sea.
- **The biome.** The cave configuration's biome overrides read it, and on a planet it is the direction's: the climate
  fields on the datum sphere and the continentalness the altitude samples, through the world mode's biome snapshot (the
  registry's blend without a biome configuration, 0 without biomes). It is found only when the configuration has
  overrides.
- **A depth pre-check.** The biome is found only when some layer can carve at the voxel's depth for some biome. That
  window is each layer's, using the shallowest of its own minimum depth, an override's and the underwater one
  (`CaveLayerReachesDepth`). Outside it the carve is 0 for every biome. Without the pre-check every solid voxel under the
  ground past a face paid two climate fields: 3.4 ms a chunk on the mean against 1.5-2.2 ms with it.
- The context carries `bEnableBiomes` and `bCarvePlanetFaceVoxels`; the cave configuration was already there (G28).
- Heightmap worlds, generation and the planet's surface (the shell's signed distance) are unchanged. No
  `PlanetGenerationVersion` bump: generation does not change.

**Tests.**

- **`VoxelWorlds.Scatter.Planet.FaceCaves`** (new): the planet of the line-top tests with biomes, a sea at the datum and
  the default cave layers. Chunks 15 and 35 voxels under the ground at four sites, each generated on the CPU with its seven
  neighbours on the +X, +Y and +Z sides.
  - Every chunk extracted with the voxels past its faces made matches, point for point (position to 0.1 uu and the
    underground class), the same extraction with the neighbours' own voxels there: 9,893 reference points (9,450
    underground), none missed, none added.
  - Without the carve: 878 missed and 451 added.
  - With biome overrides (caves only in the commonest biome, from 6 voxels down): 9,714 points, none missed, none added.
- The line-top tests (G29, G31) and G28's top-face tests pass unchanged.

**A/B on `Review_Planet`** (in-session, by the cvar). Six runs, three per rule, interleaved. Each was a fresh PIE on
`PlanetTest` with the config override and the world's save deleted, then `vox.TPLatLon` to the four stops with 45 s at
each. At each stop streaming was frozen for the audit, a per-chunk digest and the scatter statistics. GPU generation,
CPU extraction (the review planet's settings). The audit gave the same counts in every run of a rule:

| Stop | Reference points | Missed (underground) | Added (underground) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45°N 20E | 699,534 | 10,862 (10,179) → 36 (9) | 565 (537) → 37 (9) |
| 0°N 100E | 541,449 | 8,793 (8,097) → 15 (8) | 7,318 (7,311) → 15 (8) |
| 30°S 60W | 642,334 | 10,169 (9,897) → 42 (6) | 46,141 (46,105) → 42 (6) |
| Cube corner | 690,664 | 11,243 (10,512) → 49 (8) | 284 (243) → 49 (8) |

- **The leftover is the GPU generator.** With the fix, 15-49 points a stop are missed and as many added, the same
  positions in pairs: a point that moved by at least 0.1 uu because the GPU-generated neighbour's voxel there differs from
  the CPU formula by a density step. A fourth run of the fix with CPU generation (`voxel.GPUGeneration.Enable 0`) had 0
  missed and 0 added at every stop.
- **Scatter.** 178-213 chunks a stop were in every run and gave the same digest in all three runs of each rule. Of them,
  4-15 changed between the rules, in the underground types (15-17) and one point each in three
  surface types at the corner. Their spawn points went 212 → 217 (45°N), 2,323 → 2,331, 19,539 → 19,496 (30°S, where the
  added floors stood) and 1,817 → 1,825. Underground spawns gain where floors were missed and lose where floors in the
  air were added: at 30°S types 15-17 went 60, 57 and 46 → 50, 39 and 31.
- **Cost.** Over each run 1,588-1,592 chunks were extracted on workers. Extraction took 18.70-19.26 ms a chunk on the
  mean before and 20.73-20.88 after (+1.5-2.2 ms, 8-11%); placement was unchanged. The surface cache was within 1 MB at
  three stops and 4.7 MB smaller at 30°S (the added floors).

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 610/610 headless (609 + the one above) and 610/610 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). Of the GPU parity lines, the 78 that G39's dither changed differ from G44's baseline as G39 recorded, the other 30 are CRC-identical, and every case still matches the CPU (no generation change here).

**Left as they were:** the extraction cost above. M and L were not benched; their extraction is the same code, and their
chunks are the same size.

G72 is fixed.

### 20.24 G43: the planet Simplex noise continuous across the simplices (2026-10-23)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `b46375b`, UE5_PluginDev `187d9c5` (G72 merged). Branches `fix/g43-simplex-kernel` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g43-simplex-kernel` (UE5_PluginDev). Built with editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8`; tests headless
and in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8098). The user chose the tangent-corrected kernel and planets only (decision D27).

**The finding** (§20.5): `FVoxelPlanetNoise::Simplex` (and `PlanetNoise.ush`) weighted each simplex corner by Gustavson's
(0.6 − d²)⁴. A point's nearest corner outside its own simplex is √0.5 away, so that weight reaches past the simplex, and a
corner's contribution dropped out where a sample crossed into the next simplex: a step in the noise. The corner order's
planes x = y, y = z and x = z through the origin are a boundary in every octave at once, and on a planet they are the cube
sphere's face edges.

**Measured first** (a numpy model of the engine's simplex, then the tests below):

- The classic kernel steps by up to 0.0043 of the noise's ±1 range at an arbitrary boundary and 0.0064 on the planes
  through the origin, per octave; the slope jumps by up to 0.35 there.
- Across the 12 face edges (directions 2 × 10⁻⁹ rad apart), the altitude stepped by up to 6.6 uu on the small planet's
  terrain noise, 465 uu on `Review_Planet_L`'s (more than P6.4's first sample, 136), and as configured 13 uu on
  `Review_Planet`, 91 uu on `_M` and 300 uu on `_L` (about four voxels). Only the six edges on x = y, y = z and x = z
  step; the six on x = −y, y = −z and x = −z are not lattice boundaries.
- Heightmap worlds have the same kernel (`FVoxelCPUNoiseGenerator::Simplex3D`, `SimplexNoise.ush`). Estimated from the
  model with the demo's noise (three octaves, ±3,000 uu): at most about 20 uu, a quarter voxel, where every octave steps
  together (in the z = 0 slice the lines x = y, x = 0 and y = 0 of the noise's coordinates), less elsewhere.

**The kernels considered** (the classic sum scaled 32; each candidate scaled by least squares to the classic spread):

| Kernel w(d²), v = 0.5 − d² | Step | Slope | Correlation with the classic | Difference (rms / worst, of ±1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic (0.6 − d²)⁴ | 0.0064 | jumps | 1 | — |
| Value-corrected (0.6 − d²)⁴ − 0.1⁴ | 0 | a crease (a few percent) | 0.99999 | 0.002 / 0.010 |
| **Tangent-corrected** v²(v² + 0.4v + 0.06) | 0 | continuous | 0.9996 | 0.012 / 0.059 |
| v³(v + 0.4) (C2) | 0 | continuous | 0.996 | 0.036 / 0.18 |
| Textbook (0.5 − d²)⁴ | 0 | continuous | 0.985 | 0.074 / 0.35 |

They are one family: the classic weight less its Taylor expansion at d² = 0.5 to order 0, 1, 2 and 3 (the textbook kernel).
The user chose the tangent-corrected one (D27): no step, a continuous slope, and the same landscape.

**What changed** (planets only):

- `FVoxelPlanetNoise::Simplex` and its double reference: each corner weighs v²(v² + 0.4v + 0.06), v = 0.5 − d², and the
  sum is scaled by 33.25 instead of 32 (the classic spread). `PlanetNoise.ush` the same, from `PlanetSimplexContinuous`.
  Every planet field moves slightly with it: terrain, continentalness, temperature, moisture, caves and ores.
- `voxel.Planet.ContinuousSimplex` (default 1; 0 = the classic kernel, for A/B only: version 6 saves do not match it).
- `FVoxelWorldModeFactory::PlanetGenerationVersion` 5 → 6: earlier planet saves are refused and kept. Heightmap worlds keep
  the classic kernel and `GenerationVersion` 2.

**Tests:**

- **`Noise.PlanetSimplexContinuous`** (new): 3,000 random points on each kind of boundary (the corner order's planes
  x − y = k, y − z = k, x − z = k, the planes through the origin separately, and the skewed cells' faces x + s = n),
  with both kernels. Classic: steps up to 6.35 × 10⁻³, slope changes up to 0.35. Continuous: steps up to 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ in
  the double reference (the noise's own change over 2 × 10⁻⁷) and 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ in the float split-origin form (over
  2 × 10⁻⁵), slope changes up to 5.8 × 10⁻⁵. Over 40,000 points the spread is the classic's (std 0.4275 both, the largest
  value 0.969), correlation 0.99963, difference 0.0116 rms, worst 0.051.
- **`WorldModes.Planet.FaceEdgeContinuity`** (new): 300 directions on each of the 12 face edges, the altitude 10⁻⁹ rad
  either side, with both kernels, on the small planet's and L's terrain noise and on `Review_Planet`, `_M` and `_L` as
  configured (their assets loaded, skipped if absent). A control probes 3,600 random directions off the edges the same
  way. The face edges must step far beyond the control with the classic kernel, and with the continuous one stay under a
  tolerance or within 1.5 times the control.

  | Planet | Classic, at the edges | Continuous, at the edges | Control (continuous) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Small planet's terrain noise | 6.6 uu | 0.001 | 0.001 |
  | L's terrain noise | 465 uu | 0.18 (grows with the distance: the slope) | 0.14 |
  | `Review_Planet` | 13 uu | 0.003 | 0.003 |
  | `Review_Planet_M` | 91 uu | 0.10 | 0.17 |
  | `Review_Planet_L` | 300 uu | 0.45 | 0.32 |

  On the configured big planets a few tenths of a uu remain everywhere, not only at the edges, and do not grow with the
  distance at first: the float resolution of the continentalness field (its float fraction resolves about 7 uu of ground
  on L, and its height curve turns one step of it into 0.3-0.5 uu, under L's density step of 0.59 uu).
- `VoxelWorldSave.Document.PlanetKeys`: a planet fingerprint carries `PlanetGeneration=6`, and saves of versions 2 to 5
  are refused.
- `LOD.Planet.SurfaceSlab` and `LOD.Planet.NearBand` failed on the new terrain, by margins of their brute-force references,
  not of the window (no chunk missing in either):
  - `SurfaceSlab` sampled the true surface a chunk apart, and on L's km relief peaks between those samples are missed by
    about 100 uu: three cube-corner chunks came out 7,299 uu off the surface against 7,200. It now samples half a chunk
    apart.
  - `NearBand` bounded the near-band ceiling by the surface within four chunks past the near radius. The envelope
    (`GetPlanetSurfaceEnvelope`) reads the cells whose centres lie within the near angle plus two cell angles of π/N each
    (four cells) of the viewer's cell, and their samples reach a further cell, so up to about six chunks on L, where a
    cell is a chunk across. The bound is now that radius, from the strategy's own angle and grid.

  Both pass with either kernel (`LOD.Planet`, 7 of 7, with `voxel.Planet.ContinuousSimplex 0` too).

**Suites.** `VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`: 612/612 headless (610 on main
+ the two above) and 612/612 in the editor with the GPU tests running (no device loss). GPU parity, 38 cases at LOD 0/1/2,
against G39's lines (the latest; G28 and G72 changed no generation):

- With the continuous kernel, the 60 planet lines (20 cases) change CRC and the 54 heightmap lines are identical. The GPU
  still matches the CPU as closely as before: 0-22 voxels a case differ in density, none by more than 2 steps (0-53
  before), no material (one before) and one biome voxel at the small planet's equator.
- With `voxel.Planet.ContinuousSimplex 0`, 102 lines are identical. The 12 others (4 planet cases) differ from the CPU in
  one or two more voxels by a density step (3 → 4, 14 → 15, 53 → 55, 19 → 19): the shader compiler schedules the
  restructured corner function differently. The CPU's classic path computes what it did, operation for operation.

**Live** (`PlanetTest` with `voxel.ConfigOverride`, one PIE per planet and kernel, the cvar set before the world
generates; `vox.TPLatLon` and its settle at the face-edge site where the test logs the classic kernel's largest step on
land, local noon; screenshots `Saved/Screenshots/Claudius/g43_*` in the worktree, four pairs in `g43_before_after.png`):

- *`Review_Planet_L`, 41.667°N 27.135°W*, on the x = z face edge (the classic step there 300 uu). From 4,000 and 1,500 uu
  straight down, the classic kernel draws a straight light line across the terrain along the edge, the step's riser; the
  continuous kernel draws none.
- *`Review_Planet_M`, 41.994°N 25.813°W* (91 uu): the same line, fainter, with the classic kernel; none with the continuous
  one.
- The landscape is the same in both (the same patches, slopes and biomes); trees and other scatter stand slightly
  elsewhere where the ground moved.

G43 is fixed.

### 20.25 G16: the water's dark lines under the horizon (2026-10-24)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `b46375b`, UE5_PluginDev `187d9c5` (G72 merged), with main's G43 (§20.24) merged in. Branches `fix/g16-water-horizon-bands` (VoxelWorlds) and
`claude/g16-water-horizon-bands` (UE5_PluginDev). Editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8` in a worktree
editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off. No code change: the fix is a project setting.

**The finding** (§14.10): the water draws thin dark bands just under its horizon at grazing angles, at fixed screen rows
from any position. M6 ruled out the far ocean, fog, volumetric fog, anti-aliasing and the sky sphere.

**Reproduced** on island M (`Review_Island_M`, `WaterMeshMaterial` = `/DatasmithContent/Materials/Water/M_Water`, Epic's
translucent default-lit water: refraction of the scene colour, caustics and depth fog in a material function), with a
camera on the open sea past the coast looking out:

- **What they are.** Lines one or two pixels tall across the whole width, 1.0-1.5° under the horizon: 11,500-16,500 uu
  out at 300 uu over the sea, closer and more of them at 100 uu, none seen from 1,000 uu (the same angles lie past
  50,000 uu, where the height fog covers the water).
- **They follow the camera.** The same rows from 10,000 uu further out.
- **They are the water's, not the world's.** Weaker 90° along the coast, nearly gone looking back at the island (a shallow
  seabed brightens the water under them), and no line on the seabed with translucency hidden.

**Traced** by switching one thing at a time, at the same view:

| Switched | The lines |
|---|---|
| Fog, volumetric fog, sky atmosphere, volumetric clouds, anti-aliasing, mip bias, anisotropy | stay |
| Lumen reflections off (`r.ReflectionMethod 0`), Lumen translucency volume off, the translucency lighting volume off | stay |
| The sky light: lower hemisphere not black, cubemap 512 instead of 128, a static capture | stay |
| A copy of the material: flat normal (constant up), no emissive, roughness 0.3 | stay (fainter at 0.3) |
| The copy: specular 0; or `show Specular` off | **gone** |
| Lumen front-layer translucency reflections on (`r.Lumen.TranslucencyReflections.FrontLayer.Enable 1`) | **gone** |
| Lumen translucency reflections from the radiance cache off (`r.Lumen.TranslucencyReflections.RadianceCache 0`) | **gone** |
| `r.Lumen.TranslucencyReflections.MarkDownsampleFactor` 4 (the engine default) → 2 / 1 | **gone** (2: a faint line left at a swimmer's height) |

**The cause** is the engine's, not the material's. Without front-layer reflections, Lumen gives translucent surfaces their
reflections from its radiance cache, and marks the probes they need in a pass over the translucent surfaces at
1/`MarkDownsampleFactor` of the screen (`TranslucentSurfacesMarkPass`). At grazing angles kilometres of sea squeeze into a few
pixel rows, so at a quarter resolution the pass skips probe cells along the view. The water there reads no probe and its
reflection comes out dark. The rows are where those cells fall, so they follow the camera, and the water's own colour
hides them where a shallow seabed brightens it. The material's reflection is a mirror of the sky light even with its waves
flattened, which is why the normals, roughness and the cubemap did not matter.

**The fix** (UE5_PluginDev): `r.Lumen.TranslucencyReflections.MarkDownsampleFactor=1` in `Config/DefaultEngine.ini`
(`[SystemSettings]`). No scalability group sets it, so it holds at every quality level.

- Front-layer reflections also remove the lines, but they replace the water's look (mirror reflections of the scene) at a
  much larger cost, and the engine enables them only at Cine quality.
- Factor 2 still left a faint line at 50-100 uu over the sea.

**A/B on island M** (one PIE, by the cvar). Camera 100 and 300 uu over the sea (and 50 uu), pitch −1°, −3° and −8°,
heading out to sea and 90° along the coast. Counted: rows more than 3 pixels under the geometric horizon whose brightness
dips 15 or more under their neighbours (`g16_under.py`).

| | Factor 4 (before) | Factor 1 (after) |
|---|---|---|
| 300 uu | 2-6 dark rows a view, dips 17-71 | 0 |
| 100 uu | 5-10 dark rows a view, dips 18-84 | 0 |
| 50 uu | 0 in this run (an earlier sweep the same session: 7-10) | 0 |

After restarting the editor with the setting in `DefaultEngine.ini` (the cvar 1 at startup, nothing set by hand), the same
views have no dark row.

**Cost.** `ProfileGPU`, three frames each at 1280 × 722, looking out at 100 uu over the sea:

- `TranslucentSurfacesMarkPass`: 0.012-0.014 ms at factor 4, 0.016-0.018 ms at 2 and 0.033-0.034 ms at 1, a pass that
  scales with the pixels (about 0.3 ms at 4K by that ratio).
- `UpdateWorldRadianceCaches`, `RenderTranslucency` and `LumenReflections` were within their frame-to-frame spread.

**Tests.** No code change; the suites are untouched. The setting changes nothing that headless or in-editor tests read.

**Left as it was:** `M_Water` itself, an engine-plugin asset, is not edited.

G16 is fixed.

### 20.26 G14: the first PIE's LOD re-meshes were the bench's count (2026-10-24)

Bases: VoxelWorlds `7462223`, UE5_PluginDev `d4f786d` (G16 and G43 merged). Branches `fix/g14-first-pie-remesh`
(VoxelWorlds) and `claude/g14-first-pie-remesh` (UE5_PluginDev). Editor 5.8.3 from `D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8`
in a worktree editor (Claudius on 8097), background throttling off.

**The finding** (§14.8): the first PIE of an editor session counted far more LOD re-meshes than later runs on the same
route (533 against 287-304 on the control's 40,000 uu chord at v3000). Every bench batch since has started with a
throwaway PIE.

**Reproduced** on `VoxelDemo` (the control), with the save deleted, the clock at noon and input blocked:
`voxel.Bench.Run <tag> 3000 40000 start=0:0 dir=1:0 warmup=120` in three PIEs of a fresh editor gave 499, 259 and 257
LOD re-meshes. Frame and manager P95 were 37.3 / 10.7 and 37.8 / 11.2 ms in the first two; the third (53.7 / 14.9 ms)
ran while the machine was busy.

**Traced.** The streaming did the same work in every run; only the count differed.
- **The LOD evaluation queued the same.** Per sample, `LODQueued` summed over a run is 499-503 in every PIE, the first
  included.
- **The count started late in later PIEs.** In the first PIE, LOD re-meshes counted at about 40 a second from the
  traverse's first second. In the second, 0-4 a second for the first 3 s (to x ≈ 10,800) and 12-26 a second to
  x ≈ 28,800. Only then did it reach about 40 a second, once the viewer had left the ground loaded before the bench.
- **Why.** The bench counts a re-mesh when a mesh job launches for a chunk in `BenchEverMeshed`, the chunks with a mesh.
  That set was filled only while a bench ran, and `ResetBenchCounters` emptied it when one started. A chunk meshed before
  `voxel.Bench.Run` was not in it, so its LOD re-meshes went uncounted.
- **Why the first PIE differs.** The scripts start the bench about 8 s after PIE starts. In a later PIE most of the window
  is meshed by then; in a cold first PIE (shaders and assets loading) almost nothing is. The bench then saw 4-9 chunks
  loaded against 340-500 in later PIEs, so the first PIE counted every LOD re-mesh and a later one about half.

**The fix** (VoxelWorlds): the manager keeps `BenchEverMeshed` at all times. Every mesh submission adds the chunk,
`RemoveChunkState` (an unload, an eviction from the generation queue) drops it, and a world reset empties it. A bench
start no longer empties it. One set insert per mesh and one removal per unload; nothing else changes.
`voxel.Bench.CountPreBenchMeshes` (1) is the switch; 0 empties the set at a bench's start, the rule before. G10's rule
holds: a chunk that unloads and loads again meshes for the first time again.

**A/B on `VoxelDemo`** (the route above, two fresh editors, one build, by the cvar):

| Editor session | PIE | Rule | Chunks loaded at the bench's start | LOD queued | LOD re-meshes counted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 (cold) | 1 (fix) | 9 | 500 | 500 |
| 1 | 2 | 1 | 340 | 503 | 503 |
| 1 | 3 | 1 | 352 | 503 | 503 |
| 1 | 4 | 0 (before) | 454 | 503 | 266 |
| 1 | 5 | 0 | 460 | 503 | 265 |
| 2 | 1 (cold) | 0 | 6 | 499 | 499 |
| 2 | 2 | 0 | 464 | 503 | 264 |
| 2 | 3 | 1 | 448 | 503 | 503 |

With the fix the count equals what the LOD evaluation queued in every run, the cold first PIE included.
- **The old rule's count** depended on how much was meshed before the bench started: 499 cold, 264-266 later.
- **Frame P95** was 41-44 ms in most runs (manager P95 12.0-13.0 ms). Session 1's first two PIEs gave 62 ms (manager
  18.9 ms) and a 4.4 s catch-up, with 12.9-20.8 s warmups: the machine was busy, and the counts were not affected.
- **What the old counts meant.** Every LOD re-mesh count in this plan's PIE benches that followed a throwaway PIE left out
  the chunks meshed before its bench started (about half on this route). Comparisons inside one batch still hold, since
  their runs started from the same state. A bench started before the world had meshed (a cold first PIE) counted them
  all.
- **Throwaway PIEs.** A bench's re-mesh counts no longer depend on one. Where the machine was not busy, the first PIE's
  frame and manager P95 matched the next one's (37.3 / 10.7 against 37.8 / 11.2 ms, 42.7 / 12.3 against 44.2 / 12.3 ms),
  so nothing here says one is needed for the timings either.

**Tests.** `VoxelWorlds.Streaming.Bench.PreBenchMeshes` (new): a small plane with three LOD bands settles around a
viewer, the counters are reset as a bench start resets them, and the viewer moves 3,000 uu and settles again. The
recording renderer counts the re-meshes it receives (`FRecordingMeshRenderer::ChunkResubmits`).
- **With 1:** 48 re-meshes received, all 48 counted as LOD transitions.
- **With 0:** 0 counted.

Six suites (`VoxelWorlds+VoxelWorldSave+VoxelCharacter+WorldClock+InteractionPlugin+Dungeon`): 613/613 headless (G43's
612 and the new test) and 613/613 in the editor. The GPU parity lines are as on main: the 54 heightmap lines identical to
G72's run (§20.23), the 60 planet lines changed as G43 changed them (§20.24; its own run reported the same).

**Left as it was:** the bench still counts at a job's launch, and the reason it records (`BenchQueuedRemeshReason`) is
still taken from the queue only while a bench runs. A chunk queued for its LOD before the bench started and launched
after counts as "other"; every run above counted 0 "other".

G14 is fixed.
